This page specifies the Quader Bastion: a second, smaller deployment of Quader that is exposed to the internet, gives external
parties read access to the content of a main installation with the main installation's own tokens, keeps a cache of what it
served, and takes as much load as possible off the main installation. It covers:

- the deployment profile: a role of the Quader image, its own Helm chart `quader-bastion`, no PostgreSQL, no web interface, no
  settings outside the chart (*revised on 2026-11-26:* a Bastion's limits, throughput and switches come from its registration, R-BAS-093;
  not built);
- the trust between the Bastion and the main installation: the Bastion token an administrator of the main installation issues,
  what it can and cannot do, and its renewal by hand;
- the Bastion interface of the main installation: its routes and headers, its own version, the handshake, the check of a
  caller's credential and read, the marking of responses, the revocation feed and the intake of download events;
- how the Bastion serves a read without format knowledge: the URL space of the main installation mirrored, fetching with the
  caller's token, answers kept for a bounded time, shared documents for callers who read the whole repository, per-caller
  documents with conditional requests, a negative cache, a concurrency budget towards the main installation;
- the behaviour while the main installation is unreachable or speaks another interface version;
- the cache (an own bucket or a local volume per replica), the optional Valkey, and the blocking in two stages;
- audit, metrics, the PrometheusRule, the chart with its complete values, and the test suites.

Conventions on this page:

- `https://quader.example.com` is the main endpoint of the main installation *(example)*; `https://packages.example.com` is the
  base URL of a Bastion registered as `partners` *(example)*.
- The repositories are those of project `web` *(example)*: `npm-all` is a virtual repository over `npm-local` and `npm-remote`
  (upstream `https://registry.npmjs.org/`), `nuget-all` its NuGet counterpart; `npm-partner` is a local repository
  *(examples)*. Their addresses carry the project (`/api/npm/web/npm-all/`), and every wire value that names a repository is
  its qualified name (`web/npm-all`); a bare key in a sentence names the repository of `web`.
- Fixture principals *(examples)*: the service account `acme-full` of project `web` (`sa:web/acme-full`), whose project policy
  grants `read` on `npm-all`, `nuget-all` and every member, and whose token is `$FULL`; the service account `acme-part` of
  `web`, whose project policy grants `read` on `npm-all` and on `npm-local` with `packages.include: ["@acme/*"]` only, token
  `$PART`; `$NONE`, a token of a service account without grants; `$BST`, the Bastion token of `partners`.
- *Main installation* is the Quader installation whose content a Bastion serves; *caller* is a client of the Bastion; *answer*
  is something the main installation told the Bastion about a caller (R-BAS-020).

## Overview

```text
   external parties: npm, pnpm, yarn, dotnet, docker,        the internet, floods included
   podman, containerd, apt, ansible-galaxy, freshclam, curl
                │  https://packages.example.com
   ┌────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
   │ HAProxy Ingress of the Bastion            │  stage 1: coarse per-address limit (optional, wider, R-BAS-038)
   │ TLS Secret <fullname>-tls                 │  routing by path for local volumes (optional, R-BAS-033)
   └────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                │  Service <fullname>:8443 (TLS)
   ┌────────────▼───────────┐   ┌────────────────────────┐
   │ Bastion replica 1      │   │ Bastion replica n      │   quader serve --role bastion (R-BAS-001)
   │ stage 2: block list,   │   │ …                      │   answers, feed cursor, audit buffer,
   │ limits, failed-auth    │   │                        │   document copies (memory)
   └──┬────────┬────────┬───┘   └──┬─────────────────────┘
      │        │        └──────────┴───► cache backend: own bucket (shared)  |  local volume per replica (R-BAS-030)
      │        └───────────────────────► Valkey, optional: block list, counters, fetch locks, signed answers (R-BAS-034)
      │  https://quader.example.com, the main endpoint (default endpoint of the main installation)
      │  Quader-Bastion-Authorization: Bearer qdr_bst_…   Authorization: <the caller's own credential>
      │  X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host/-Port and Forwarded: the client address and the Bastion's host
   ┌──▼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ main installation: its ingress → web replicas, default endpoint               │
   │   /api/<format>/…, /files/…,  decided as the caller's own request,            │
   │   /v2/… (R-BAS-051)                                                           │
   │                               marked (R-BAS-013), writes refused (R-BAS-014)  │
   │   /api/v1/bastion/handshake | check | feed | downloads   (R-BAS-008)          │
   │   PostgreSQL, Valkey: never reached by the Bastion; the object store: only    │
   │   by a link handed for one blob (R-BAS-070)                                   │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

A read at the Bastion goes one of three ways. A **hit** is served from the cache after an answer of the main installation that
the caller may read it, kept for `bastion.answers.period`. A **check** asks the main installation about the caller, by a
conditional request through the real route or through the check operation, and serves the cached bytes on a yes. A **miss** is
fetched from the main installation with the caller's own credential; the main installation decides and serves it as it would
the caller's own request, marks the response, and the Bastion keeps what may be shared. The Bastion holds no users, tokens or
policies and knows no package format: every decision is the main installation's, and every protocol byte it serves was produced
by the main installation, except the few answers of its own of R-BAS-029.

## Roles and trust boundaries

| Party | Trusted with | Not trusted with | Where the boundary is enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Caller (anyone on the internet) | its own credential, and what the main installation lets that credential read | forwarded headers, any decision, any write | the Bastion's ingress and its stage 2 (R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037); the main installation's decision on every answer |
| HAProxy Ingress of the Bastion | the client address it writes, when its addresses are in the Bastion's `server.trusted_proxies` | anything else | R-BAS-019, [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-006 |
| Bastion replica | the Bastion token, the signing key, the cached bytes, the client address it reports; with the handover, for one read, the link of one object and, on an encrypted connection, that object's data key (R-BAS-076) | users, tokens, policies (it holds none); every write to the main installation except download events; any credential or key of the main installation's store above one object's data key | the Bastion interface (R-BAS-005, R-BAS-008); the main installation's serve point ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095) |
| Valkey of the Bastion | block list, counters, fetch locks, answers it stores but cannot forge (signed) | granting anything: a forged or altered answer fails its signature | R-BAS-034 |
| Cache backend (own bucket or volume) | bytes and signed entries | the main installation's object store, which the Bastion reads only by a link handed for one blob (R-BAS-070) | R-BAS-030, R-BAS-032 |
| Main installation | every decision about a caller, every rendered byte, the audit trail | — | — |
| Administrator of the main installation (`endpoints:write`) | issuing and revoking Bastion tokens | — | R-BAS-004, R-BAS-007 |

```text
   caller ──(1) TLS, own credential──► Bastion ──(2) TLS, Bastion token + caller's credential──► main installation
      ▲                                  │  ▲                                                       │
      │  decided by the main             │  └──(3) answers, marked responses, feed entries ─────────┘
      └──installation, replayed ─────────┘
   (1) crosses the internet boundary; (2) and (3) cross the trust boundary between a DMZ instance and the main installation.
```

## Deployment profile

### R-BAS-001 · The Bastion: a role of the Quader image behind its own chart
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

- The Bastion is the role `bastion` of the one `quader` image (INV-1, INV-2): `quader serve --role bastion`
  ([Q-BAS-22](#q-bas-22--the-bastion-is-a-role-of-the-quader-image)). The role enables the Bastion's client listener, its ops
  listener, the Bastion engine of this page and, when configured, the Valkey client. It enables no other subsystem: no
  PostgreSQL pool, no object-store client for the main installation's blobs (a link handed for one blob is read by a plain `https`
  client that holds no credential of the store, R-BAS-074), no job runner, no format plug-in route table, no
  management API, no UI, no login, no session, no remote repository. "Enables" is the operative word: the platform packages the
  role shares (the Valkey client in `internal/cluster`, the listeners in `internal/httpserver`, the S3 client in
  `internal/blob/s3`) import packages of the main installation (the PostgreSQL store, the audit types, the scope and CI claim
  types, the blob store interface, the format areas), which are in the role's binary and never started. The import rule of the
  role is transitive and lists those packages with their reason ([Q-BAS-129](#q-bas-129--the-import-rule-follows-the-dependency-closure-and-lists-what-it-cannot-narrow),
  [H-473](#h-473--the-roles-binary-contains-packages-of-the-main-installation-it-never-starts)); a test of the role proves that it
  opens no connection to a PostgreSQL address.
- The role is deployed only by the chart `quader-bastion` in `deploy/helm/quader-bastion` (R-BAS-045), never by the chart
  `quader`, and the chart `quader-bastion` renders no other role. Several Bastions in front of one main installation are several
  releases of that chart, each with a registration of its own (R-BAS-004).
- The configuration schema of the role is its own: `server.listen`, `server.ops_listen`, `server.base_url`,
  `server.trusted_proxies`, `server.forwarded_header`, `server.max_in_flight`, `server.tls`, the section `bastion` of this page,
  `valkey`, `log`, `tracing`, `runtime` and `ui` with `ui.legal` alone (R-BAS-100). A key of another section (`database`, `storage`,
  `auth`, `authz`, `ci`, `backup`, `audit`, `server.endpoints`, `server.additional_base_urls`, the main installation's `ui.readme`, …)
  stops startup with an error that names the key and the role.
  The role has `server.ops_tls` as well (R-BAS-044), is chosen by `--role bastion` and by nothing else, and takes `--log-level` as
  its one flag ([Q-BAS-50](#q-bas-50--the-role-has-a-configuration-tree-of-its-own-chosen-by---role-alone)).
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's statement on W-35 ([Q-BAS-14](#q-bas-14--no-web-interface-at-the-bastion), R-BAS-101 to
  R-BAS-103):* the role gains a read-only web interface for anonymous visitors, switched on per registration at the main installation
  (`gui`, `docs`), fed by the public catalogue the replica mirrors over the interface; it still has no management API, no login and no
  session. *Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7 and P9):* every replica mirrors the catalogue while `gui` is on (R-BAS-109 to R-BAS-113) and
  serves the web interface from it (R-BAS-116 to R-BAS-118); its bundle is the Bastion's own, not the main installation's.
- Horizontal replicas: every Bastion replica is identical and interchangeable (INV-2); a request may reach any replica, and
  nothing a request needs is held only by the replica an earlier request reached (INV-18): answers, document copies and a
  local cache volume are caches whose loss costs performance only. The Bastion has no PostgreSQL; what it must not lose lives
  at the main installation, and what it may lose lives in its cache backend and, optionally, Valkey.

```yaml
server:
  listen: ":8443"                       # default (proposed) for the role bastion
  ops_listen: ":8081"                   # default (proposed)
  base_url: ""                          # required; example: https://packages.example.com
  trusted_proxies: []                   # default (proposed); the chart requires it while its Ingress is on (Q-BAS-130); example: ["10.244.0.0/16"] (the Bastion's ingress pods)
  forwarded_header: x-forwarded-for     # default (proposed): x-forwarded-for | forwarded (R-ARCH-006)
  max_in_flight: 1024                   # default (proposed), per replica
```

Acceptance criteria:

- `quader serve --role bastion` with a file that holds `database.host` stops with an error naming `database.host` and the role
  `bastion`; with the keys above, `bastion.main.url` and the token file it starts, and `ss -ltn` in its pod shows `:8443` and
  `:8081` only.
- A Bastion pod opens no connection to any PostgreSQL port and makes no request to the main installation's bucket during the
  whole e2e suite (the object store's access log), whose registrations have the handover off (R-BAS-071). The role started with a trap listening where a
  PostgreSQL client of the process would look sees no connection and exports no database metric
  (`TestR_BAS_001_TheRoleOpensNoConnectionToPostgreSQL`).
- The import rule names every package of the main installation in the role's dependency closure, with the platform package that
  pulls it in; a new one fails `go test ./internal/archtest/...` with the chain.
- `GET /api/v1/system/ping`, `GET /ui/` and `GET /auth/oidc/corp/start` on the Bastion answer `404` without a request to the
  main installation (R-BAS-018).

### R-BAS-002 · Configuration only through the chart
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

*Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation):* what an administrator of the main installation decides
about a Bastion comes from its registration and reaches it with the handshake (R-BAS-093): the switches, the limits' mode and preset, the
rules of its place, the flood figures, the slots, the throughput, the anonymous ceiling and the egress addresses. The bullets below hold
for what stays in the chart; the second bullet's "state of the main installation" gains the configuration, which is the Bastion's own and
held at the main installation; W-35's switches `gui` and `docs` are members of it (R-BAS-102). *Built by E7:* the configuration travels in
the handshake (interface version 8). *Built by E8 (2026-11-26):* the main installation stores it on the registration and sends it
([Q-BAS-440](#q-bas-440--the-configuration-reaches-the-handshake-from-the-replicas-snapshot-in-one-statement-of-one-moment)). *Built by E9a
(2026-11-26):* the Bastion applies the configuration whole, its flood figures, slots and anonymous ceiling among it, and the chart no longer
holds `config.bastion.limits`, `failed_auth`, `blocking` and `main.max_concurrent`, `anonymous_share`, `queue_timeout`: the registration's
`PATCH` is the only place they are set.

- Every setting of a Bastion is a value of its chart: the main installation and the Bastion token, the cache, the periods, the
  limits, the blocking, the trusted proxies, Valkey, TLS and monitoring (owner,
  [Q-BAS-15](#q-bas-15--the-bastion-is-configured-only-through-its-chart)). The chart renders them into
  `/etc/quader/quader.yaml` and the mounted Secrets (R-BAS-046). The Bastion has no runtime settings, no settings API and no
  setting read from the main installation; a change of a value is a rollout.
- What the Bastion learns from the main installation is state of the main installation, not configuration of the Bastion:
  whether it serves anonymous reads at all (`anonymousReads`), whether downloads are recorded, the main installation's interface
  version (R-BAS-010).
- The two exceptions to "a change is a rollout" are file reloads of material the chart mounts: the Bastion token (R-BAS-006)
  and the TLS material (R-BAS-044), both picked up without a restart.

Acceptance criteria:

- `grep` of the Bastion's code finds no write of a `bastion.*` value at runtime; the chart test renders every value of
  R-BAS-046 into the configuration file or a Secret mount, and a value without a rendering target fails the test.
- Changing `config.bastion.answers.period` with `helm upgrade` rolls the pods (the configuration checksum annotation changes);
  replacing the token Secret's content rolls nothing and the new token is in use within `bastion.main.token_reload_interval`.

### R-BAS-003 · What the Bastion serves: the package clients' read paths, no web interface
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

- The Bastion serves package clients and raw downloads with tokens only (owner,
  [Q-BAS-14](#q-bas-14--no-web-interface-at-the-bastion)): the path families `/api/<format>/…` (every path below `/api/`
  except `/api/v1/…`) and `/files/…` of INV-6, and the registry root `/v2/…` at the host root of the Bastion's base URL, mirrored
  from the main installation (R-BAS-018), for every format (owner, 2026-11-22, [R-BAS-050](#r-bas-050--every-formats-read-paths-at-the-bastions-host),
  [R-BAS-051](#r-bas-051--the-registry-root-at-a-bastion)); on a host the main installation binds to one repository, also the
  bound-host prefixes its format declares ([R-BAS-057](#r-bas-057--format-facts-at-the-bastion-the-handshakes-format-table-and-bound-hosts)).
  *Superseded in place on 2026-11-22: `/v2/…` was in the list below and answered `404`.* Every other path answers `404`
  from the Bastion itself (R-BAS-029): `/`, `/ui/…`, `/auth/…`, `/api/v1/…`, `/-/…`, `/.well-known/…` (except a bound-host prefix of
  R-BAS-057). The main
  installation's router decodes every segment before it compares it, so `/api/%761/users` is `/api/v1/users` there: a path
  whose family, format, project or key segment contains a percent-encoding, and a path with a `.` or `..` segment, answer `404`
  from the Bastion as well ([Q-BAS-121](#q-bas-121--a-path-is-classified-as-the-main-installations-router-will-read-it-and-a-token-refusal-on-a-forward-is-no-statement-about-the-bastions-token)).
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-35, R-BAS-101 to R-BAS-103):* while its registration's switch `gui` is on, a Bastion also serves its read-only
  web interface below `/ui/`, `/` as a redirect to it, and `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` at the host root, from the catalogue it mirrors
  and never by a request to the main installation (W-35's packages P9 and P10). *Built by P9 on 2026-11-26:* `/`, `/ui` and everything
  below `/ui/` are the web interface's (R-BAS-116, R-BAS-117), whatever the switch says: off, they answer `404 not_found` as below.
  *Built by P10 on 2026-11-26:* `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and every path below `/sitemap/` are the web interface's too (R-BAS-122):
  `robots.txt` answers whatever the switch says, the sitemap `404` while it is off.
- There is no login, no session, no cookie and no browser flow. A `Cookie` header is ignored and never forwarded. A session
  token never reaches the Bastion from Quader, because Quader never sets a cookie for the Bastion's host.
- The ops listener serves `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` as on every Quader role ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)
  R-OPS-001, R-OPS-006).

Acceptance criteria:

- A table test sends every row of INV-6's path table to the Bastion: only `/api/<format>/…`, `/files/…` and `/v2/…` reach the read
  flow (the core routes of `/v2/` as R-BAS-051 says); the others answer `404` with `not_found` and the counting double of the
  main installation records no request.
- A request with `Cookie: __Host-qdr_session=…` and no other credential is treated as anonymous, and the request the Bastion
  forwards carries no `Cookie`.
- `/api/%761/users`, `/api/%76%31/bastion/handshake` and every other encoded spelling of a family, format, project or key segment
  answer `404 not_found`, reach the main installation never, and leave the replica reachable however often they are
  repeated (`TestR_BAS_003_R_BAS_018_APathIsClassifiedAsTheMainInstallationsRouterWillRouteIt`,
  `TestR_BAS_003_R_BAS_006_AnEncodedSpellingOfTheInterfaceRoutesCannotTurnTheReplicaUnreachable`).

## Trust between the Bastion and the main installation

### R-BAS-004 · Bastion registrations and the Bastion token on the main installation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-025

- **Registration.** A Bastion is registered on the main installation as a principal of the kind `bastion`, reference
  `bastion:<name>`, name `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,19}$` ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-002) other than `presets`, the path of the presets' list (R-BAS-093). It holds no grants, no
  roles, no group memberships and no package ownership: a policy entry, a role binding, an owner record or a membership that
  names it answers `422 principal_not_allowed` ([Q-BAS-60](#q-bas-60--a-bastion-registration-is-refused-by-every-write-path-with-one-top-level-422-principal_not_allowed)).
  It is not internal ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-030,
  [Q-AUTHZ-320](authorization.md#q-authz-320--a-bastion-registration-is-not-internal-a-bastion-reads-for-the-caller-it-forwards-for)):
  a Bastion reads nothing on its own credential, only for the callers it forwards for. Its token is refused by every route that
  could admit it, and the decision point gives the kind `bastion` an empty principal set (no grant, no role, no level but
  `public`), should any route ever decide for it. At most
  `bastions.max_registrations` registrations exist. A registration can be disabled soft or hard, which tells its Bastion over its
  connection to stop and leaves its tokens valid (R-BAS-133; *revised on 2026-11-27*, before it refused the tokens like a disabled
  service account's), and deleted, which revokes them.
- **Bastion token.** The Bastion's credential is a token of the type `bst`, prefix `qdr_bst_`, issued by an administrator of
  the main installation (owner, [Q-BAS-3](#q-bas-3--the-bastions-credential-is-a-token-issued-by-an-administrator-of-the-main-installation),
  [Q-BAS-23](#q-bas-23--the-bastion-token-is-a-token-type-of-its-own-on-a-bastion-principal)). It follows the format, storage,
  validation, caching and revocation bound of R-AUTH-022 and R-AUTH-023 and the revocation of R-AUTH-029; its owner principal
  is the registration. It has no scope: what it may do is fixed by its type (R-BAS-005). It always expires: `ttlSeconds` is at
  most `auth.tokens.bst.max_ttl`, defaulting to `auth.tokens.bst.default_ttl`; 0, a negative value, under 60 seconds and above the
  maximum are `400 invalid_ttl`, and a missing description becomes `Bastion <name>`
  ([Q-BAS-63](#q-bas-63--a-bastion-tokens-lifetime-is-ttlseconds-alone-every-violation-is-400-invalid_ttl-the-description-is-optional)).
  *Amended on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-127, [Q-BAS-466](#q-bas-466--the-declared-token-does-not-expire-its-lifetime-is-its-declarations)):* the
  token a registration's configuration declares does not expire and counts against no limit; every issued token still expires.
  At most `auth.tokens.max_active_per_principal.bst` unrevoked tokens exist per registration, so an overlap (R-BAS-006) fits and a
  forgotten token does not accumulate. The validation is the token service's, through its cache and revocation bound
  ([Q-BAS-62](#q-bas-62--the-bastion-token-authenticator-is-the-token-services-with-its-cache-gate-and-change-area)); disabling a
  registration revokes nothing, deleting it revokes every token first
  ([Q-BAS-61](#q-bas-61--the-registration-events-carry-no-journal-entry-a-bastion-tokens-events-name-the-registration-in-their-data)).
  Both are journaled ([ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-054): a restore to a point before a disable or a deletion disables the
  registration again, hard for a deletion, whose revoked tokens stay revoked
  ([Q-BAS-145](#q-bas-145--a-disabled-or-deleted-registration-is-journaled-and-replayed-as-disabled), R-BAS-133).
- **API** (management API conventions of [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md); capability in brackets,
  [Q-BAS-24](#q-bas-24--bastion-registrations-are-managed-with-the-endpoint-capabilities)):

| Operation | Capability | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/bastions` `{"name", "description"}` | `endpoints:write` | `201` with the registration |
| `GET /api/v1/bastions`, `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` | `endpoints:read`; `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` also `limits:read`, which reads `id`, `name`, `limits`, `status`, `state` and `running` only (R-BAS-093, R-BAS-133) | name, description, `disabled`, `state` and `running` (R-BAS-133), its tokens (ID, hint, `expiresAt`, `createdAt`, `lastUsedAt`), and the last contact of R-BAS-010: time, client address, Bastion release, interface version, reported base URL, replica |
| `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/{name}` `{"description", "disabled"}` | `endpoints:write` | `200`; `disabled` is `soft`, `hard` or `null` (R-BAS-133) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/bastions/{name}` | `endpoints:write` | `204`; revokes its tokens (`token.revoked`, journaled) |
| `POST /api/v1/bastions/{name}/tokens` `{"description", "ttlSeconds"}` | `endpoints:write`; a session needs a recent authentication ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-API-007) | `201` with the token secret, once (R-AUTH-022); `409 managed_by_config` for a declared registration (R-BAS-133) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/bastions/{name}/tokens/{id}` | `endpoints:write` or `tokens:revoke` | `204`; `token.revoked`, journaled (R-HA-054); the declared token's too (R-BAS-133) |

- `quader admin bastion create <name>`, `quader admin bastion disable <name> [--hard]`, `quader admin bastion enable <name>`
  (R-BAS-133), `quader admin bastion token create <name> --ttl <duration>` and
  `quader admin bastion token revoke <name> <id>` do the same from a `web` pod (R-AUTH-015's pattern). Every operation writes its
  audit event: `bastion.created`, `bastion.updated` (the description), `bastion.disabled` (with its way), `bastion.enabled`,
  `bastion.deleted`, and `token.created` / `token.revoked` with `resource_type: bastion`. `bastion.disabled` and `bastion.deleted` carry
  the journal entry `{principalId, name, mode}` (R-BAS-133), the others none; `token.revoked` keeps its flag and its entry (Q-BAS-145). At most
  `bastions.max_registrations` is held exactly, also when creates race
  ([Q-BAS-64](#q-bas-64--creating-registrations-is-serialized-by-an-advisory-lock-a-registrations-name-never-changes)).

```yaml
auth:
  tokens:
    bst:
      default_ttl: 8760h               # default (proposed): one year
      max_ttl: 9480h                   # default (proposed): one year and a month, so a yearly renewal fits its overlap
    max_active_per_principal:
      bst: 3                           # default (proposed)
bastions:                              # the main installation's section (the Bastion's own is bastion)
  max_registrations: 16                # default (proposed); bounds the bastion label of R-BAS-008's metrics
```

Acceptance criteria:

- `POST /api/v1/bastions {"name": "partners"}` then `POST /api/v1/bastions/partners/tokens {"ttlSeconds": 31536000}` returns a
  57-character `qdr_bst_` token that passes R-AUTH-022's checksum; `ttlSeconds` above `max_ttl` answers `400 invalid_ttl`, and a
  fourth unrevoked token answers `409 token_limit_reached` (the registry's code for the limit, [Q-BAS-53](#q-bas-53--unbuilt-operations-answer-501-bastion_not_implemented-three-codes-follow-the-existing-registry)).
- A policy entry for `bastion:partners` and a role binding of `admin` to it answer `422 principal_not_allowed`.
- A caller with `endpoints:read` only gets `403` on the token creation; `tokens:revoke` alone may revoke a Bastion token.
- Deleting `partners` revokes its tokens (a `token.revoked` with `resource_type: bastion` and a journal entry each), removes the
  registration and its contacts, and the revoked token is refused on every replica within `auth.revocation_bound`; disabling it
  leaves its tokens valid (R-BAS-133).
- A registration disabled or deleted after the point a restore returns to is disabled by the journal's replay, in the disable's way and
  hard for a deletion, whose tokens stay revoked; an enable after that point is not replayed
  (`TestR_BAS_004_ADisabledOrDeletedRegistrationStaysDisabledAfterARestore`).

### R-BAS-005 · What the Bastion token can do
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-025

The Bastion token identifies the Bastion and may only have tokens checked; it reads no package (owner,
[Q-BAS-7](#q-bas-7--the-bastion-fetches-with-the-callers-token-and-its-own-token-reads-no-package)).

- **Where it is accepted.** Only on the Bastion interface of the default endpoint: as `Authorization: Bearer` on
  `/api/v1/bastion/…`, and as `Quader-Bastion-Authorization: Bearer` on a request the Bastion forwards (R-BAS-008). Every other
  route of every endpoint refuses the type `bst` in `Authorization`, as Basic password and as API key with the `401
  invalid_token` of an unknown token, before any database lookup ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-010 step 2). `bst` is not a
  valid entry of an endpoint's `auth.token_types`: it stops startup and names the key. Further endpoints do not serve the
  Bastion interface.
- **What it grants.** Nothing in the decision point: it is never a subject of a read, a write or a management operation. On
  the interface it allows: the handshake, the check of a caller's credential and read (which tells the Bastion what the caller
  could find out by using its credential itself), reading the revocation feed (token and principal IDs, qualified repository
  names `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`), and
  submitting download events (R-BAS-016). It cannot issue tokens, change a Secret, read a package, write content, or read the
  audit trail.
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-35, R-BAS-101, [Q-BAS-7](#q-bas-7--the-bastion-fetches-with-the-callers-token-and-its-own-token-reads-no-package)):*
  the token also reads the public catalogue of its own registration through the catalogue routes (the change list, the documents and
  the public set): what an anonymous caller reads anyway, stripped of internal identities (W-35's B.10), and only while the
  registration's switch `gui` is on (`404 not_found` otherwise, documentation only while `docs` is on). It reads no other registration's
  catalogue and still no package. *Built by E7 with P5:* the routes, which answer an empty catalogue until W-35's builder (P6) lands.
- **Forwarded requests** are decided on the caller's credential alone. The Bastion token on a forwarded request only makes the
  main installation add the marking headers of R-BAS-013 and refuse writes (R-BAS-014); a forwarded request without a caller
  credential is anonymous, whatever the Bastion token is.

Acceptance criteria:

- `$BST` as `Authorization: Bearer`, as Basic password and as `X-NuGet-ApiKey` on `/api/npm/web/npm-all/lodash`,
  `/files/web/npm-local/x` and `/api/v1/repositories` answers `401 invalid_token`, and the token table records no query for it.
- `GET /api/npm/web/npm-all/@acme%2fsdk` with `Quader-Bastion-Authorization: Bearer $BST` and no `Authorization` answers exactly what
  an anonymous request answers, plus the marking headers.
- `server.endpoints.default.auth.token_types: [pat, bst]` stops startup naming the key.

### R-BAS-006 · Renewing the Bastion token by hand with an overlap
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-025

The renewal is manual (owner, [Q-BAS-19](#q-bas-19--the-bastion-token-is-renewed-by-hand-with-an-overlap)):

1. An administrator issues a second token for the registration before the first expires (R-BAS-004).
2. The new token reaches the Bastion's Secret (`secrets.mainToken`) through GitOps; the chart never writes it, and the Bastion
   holds no right to write a Secret or to issue a token (its ServiceAccount has no Kubernetes API access, R-BAS-045).
3. Every replica re-reads the token file every `bastion.main.token_reload_interval` and on a change of the file, and uses the
   new token from its next request to the main installation; requests in flight finish with the old one. No restart. A change
   of the file is noticed by a check of its identity (the file behind the link, its size and its time) every second, so a
   rotation of the mounted Secret does not wait for the interval
   ([Q-BAS-77](#q-bas-77--the-token-file-is-watched-by-a-one-second-identity-check-besides-the-interval-read)).
4. The administrator revokes the old token once the screen of R-BAS-007 shows the new token's `lastUsedAt` from every replica's
   contact. A replica that still uses a revoked token gets `401 bastion_token_invalid` to a call of its own (handshake, feed,
   check, download batch) and treats the main installation as unreachable (R-BAS-027; the same answer to a forward is not that statement,
   [Q-BAS-121](#q-bas-121--a-path-is-classified-as-the-main-installations-router-will-read-it-and-a-token-refusal-on-a-forward-is-no-statement-about-the-bastions-token)), `quader_bastion_main_token_refused` is 1 and `QuaderBastionTokenRefused` fires (R-BAS-041).

- **Remaining lifetime.** The handshake returns the expiry of the token in use (R-BAS-010). The Bastion exports
  `quader_bastion_token_remaining_seconds` and logs a warning at start and then once a day while the remaining lifetime is below
  `bastion.token.warn_before`, naming the registration, the token hint and the expiry. The PrometheusRule warns from the same
  threshold, read from the gauge `quader_bastion_token_warn_before_seconds` (R-BAS-041).
- An unreadable or malformed token file (wrong prefix, failed checksum) keeps the previous token in use, logs an error and
  counts `quader_bastion_token_reloads_total{outcome="refused"}`; at start it stops startup.

```yaml
bastion:
  main:
    token_reload_interval: 10s          # default (proposed)
  token:
    warn_before: 720h                   # default (proposed): 30 days (owner's proposal)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With two unrevoked tokens, replacing the Secret's value moves every replica to the new token within 70 s (the kubelet's
  Secret sync plus `token_reload_interval`), shown by `lastUsedAt` of both tokens; revoking the old one afterwards causes no
  failed request in a concurrent `npm ci` loop.
- A token that expires in 20 days makes the Bastion log `bastion token expires soon` at start, sets
  `quader_bastion_token_remaining_seconds` below 1,728,001, and fires `QuaderBastionTokenExpiresSoon` in `promtool test rules`.
- Revoking the token in use makes every replica report `quader_bastion_main_token_refused 1` within `feed.poll_interval` plus
  5 s.

### R-BAS-007 · Bastions in the main installation's screen, client setup and manual
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **Screen.** Administration → Bastions in the main installation's UI (capabilities of R-BAS-004): the list of registrations
  with the last contact, the interface version and release each replica reported, the token expiries with a warning mark below
  30 days, and the actions create, disable, delete, issue token (the secret shown once, as for every token) and revoke token.
  The screen uses only the operations of R-BAS-004 (INV-17). It is one page with a card per registration, which shows the
  registration's facts and actions, the last contact of every replica and its tokens ([Q-BAS-95](#q-bas-95--the-bastions-screen-is-one-page-with-a-card-per-registration)).
  *Amended on 2026-11-23* ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) [Q-UI-959](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-959--a-bastion-cards-tables-keep-one-form-at-the-wide-and-the-middle-width-what-most-rows-share-stands-under-the-rows-name)):
  the last contact is a table of **Replica**, **Time** and **Reported base URL**, with the client address, the release and the interface
  version under the replica's name; the tokens a table of **Token** (the hint and the creation under the description), **Expires**,
  **Last used** and **Revoke**; every time relative with its date and time as its title. Both keep this form at every width of a card
  but the narrow one, where their rows stack, whatever their values. *Amended on 2026-11-27 (W-39,
  [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1622--a-bastions-replicas-are-one-line-it-warns-when-the-bastion-is-silent-or-its-replicas-disagree)
  Q-UI-1622, [Q-UI-1623](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1623--a-bastions-tokens-are-one-line-the-mark-says-expires-soon-without-a-number)):* the
  two tables stand last on the card in the closed sections **Replicas** and **Tokens**, each with its count and one line ("Last contact 1
  minute ago · version 0.42.0", "The next expires in 12 months"), which turns into a warning and opens the section by itself when no
  replica made contact in 5 minutes while the registration is enabled, when the replicas heard in that time run more than one version or
  report more than one base URL, or when a token expires within 30 days or has expired; the interface version is no longer shown (every
  recorded contact shares it: a handshake with another one is refused); the column **Time** is **Last contact**; the warning mark is
  **Expires soon**, without a number beside the cell's relative time.
- **Client setup.** `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/repositories/{repoKey}/client-setup` ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-API-030) accepts
  `bastion=<name>`: the snippets are rendered on the base URL the Bastion reported at its last handshake, provided it is an
  entry of `server.additional_base_urls` (else `409 bastion_base_url_unknown`, also while it has reported none; a name that is no
  registration answers `404`; [Q-BAS-97](#q-bas-97--the-reported-address-is-matched-against-the-listed-addresses-and-the-setup-needs-no-base-url-of-its-own)),
  and carry no publish snippets, since the Bastion is read-only. The guide of each format (R-UI-049) and the setup page of
  R-UI-016 offer the Bastion as a target when a registration has reported a base URL
  ([Q-BAS-96](#q-bas-96--a-bastion-is-a-target-of-the-setup-page-and-of-the-guides-read-only-and-by-link-for-everyone)).
  For npm, the configure snippet sets `replace-registry-host=always`, so that a lockfile written against another host resolves
  through the Bastion.
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-34, W-35):* the card holds the registration's configuration (R-UI-240): the switches `gui` and `docs` beside
  the handover, the limits, and, while `gui` is on and a reporting replica's catalogue is not kept (`Quader-Bastion-Catalogue-Kept: false`),
  the sentence of W-35's B.2b; the client setup for a Bastion is rendered by the Bastion's own web interface as well, on its host and
  without publish lines (W-35's P9). *Built by E12 (2026-11-26):* the card's configuration, switches and sentence (R-UI-240). *Today,
  until P9 lands:* the client setup as below.
- **Manual.** The admin manual gains `docs/manual/admin/bastion.md`: register a Bastion, issue its token, the chart values of a
  minimal and of an HA install, the settings on the main installation (the registration's `egress`, R-BAS-017;
  `server.additional_base_urls`), verify with the handshake metric, renew the token, and what each alert of R-BAS-041 means.

Acceptance criteria:

- The browser test creates `partners`, issues a token, copies it once, and sees the last contact appear after the Bastion of
  the e2e cluster starts; a token expiring in 20 days shows the warning mark.
- `client-setup?client=npm&bastion=partners` on `web/npm-all` returns a registry URL
  `https://packages.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/`, `replace-registry-host=always`, and no `publish` tab
  (`TestR_BAS_007_ClientSetupRendersOnTheBaseURLTheBastionReported`, and through the stack
  `TestR_BAS_007_ClientSetupForABastionThroughTheStack`).

## The Bastion interface of the main installation

### R-BAS-008 · Interface routes, recognition and headers
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040

The main installation's side of the Bastion is one interface on its default endpoint
([Q-BAS-25](#q-bas-25--the-interface-lives-under-apiv1bastion-on-the-main-endpoint)). The Bastion connects to the main endpoint
(owner, [Q-BAS-4](#q-bas-4--the-bastion-connects-to-the-main-endpoint-and-replaces-the-customer-endpoint)), through the main
installation's ingress or its Service.

| Route | Purpose | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/bastion/handshake` | interface version, the Bastion's identity and token expiry, the main installation's state the Bastion needs | R-BAS-010 |
| `POST /api/v1/bastion/check` | a caller's credential and its read shape on repositories, with the answer's validity | R-BAS-011 |
| `GET /api/v1/bastion/feed` | the revocation feed | R-BAS-015 |
| `POST /api/v1/bastion/downloads` | download events served from the Bastion's cache, its usage and its status | R-BAS-016 |
| `GET /api/v1/bastion/catalogue`, `GET …/catalogue/document`, `POST …/catalogue/documents`, `GET …/catalogue/public` | the public catalogue of the registration (W-35) | R-BAS-101 |
| every `/api/<format>/…` and `/files/…` route | a forwarded read, decided as the caller's own request and marked | R-BAS-013, R-BAS-014 |

- **Headers of every request from the Bastion:** `Quader-Bastion-Interface: <n>` (R-BAS-009); `User-Agent:
  quader-bastion/<release>`; `Quader-Bastion-Replica: <pod name>`; W3C `traceparent` (R-BAS-042). On the interface routes the
  Bastion token is `Authorization: Bearer`. On a forwarded request it is `Quader-Bastion-Authorization: Bearer`, the caller's own
  credential stays in `Authorization` exactly as the caller sent it, and the forwarded headers of R-BAS-017 carry the client
  address and the Bastion's host.
- **Forward or interface call.** A request that carries `Quader-Bastion-Authorization` is a forward, whatever its path; a request
  without it whose path the router decodes to a route below `/api/v1/bastion/` is an interface call, with the Bastion token in
  `Authorization`. A forward of a path outside `/api/<format>/` and `/files/` answers `404 not_found` before authentication
  (R-BAS-014, [Q-BAS-115](#q-bas-115--a-request-with-quader-bastion-authorization-is-a-forward-and-a-forward-reaches-only-the-package-families)).
- **Recognition.** The main installation treats a request as a Bastion request only when `Quader-Bastion-Authorization` (or, on
  the interface routes, `Authorization`) carries a valid `bst` token of an enabled registration. A request with
  `Quader-Bastion-*` headers but no valid Bastion token is served as an ordinary request: the headers are ignored and no
  marking is added. A request whose Bastion token is invalid answers `401 bastion_token_invalid`; one whose interface version
  differs answers `400 bastion_interface_mismatch` (R-BAS-009). Both are problem details of the management API, also on a
  package route, because they concern the Bastion, never the caller; the Bastion never passes them on (R-BAS-027).
- **A recognized forward is decided as any other request.** The subject of a forward, and the caller the check of R-BAS-011
  decides, is the caller's own subject, the one the same request at the main installation's own door has: an internal caller
  reads by the level `internal` through a Bastion, a user flagged external does not, and the anonymous caller reads what is
  `public` ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-030,
  [Q-BAS-148](#q-bas-148--a-request-through-a-bastion-is-decided-as-any-other)). The subject carries no mark of the channel
  ([authorization.md](authorization.md) Q-AUTHZ-321).
- `Quader-Bastion-Authorization` is redacted like `Authorization` in every log, span and support bundle (R-OPS-013), and the
  main installation never echoes a `Quader-Bastion-*` request header.
- The operations are in the OpenAPI document under the tag `bastion`, marked `x-quader-bastion-interface: <n>` and declared
  `x-quader-permission: {bastion: true}` (`<n>` is 8 since the wire of [interface version 8](#the-interface-version-8-the-shared-wire)), which the shared authorization step admits on the recognition result alone
  ([Q-BAS-52](#q-bas-52--recognition-and-marking-are-one-chain-stage-before-authentication-the-dispatcher-tells-an-observer-about-the-route));
  they are not part of the management API's v1 promise but of the interface version (R-ARCH-025).
- Main side metrics: `quader_bastion_interface_requests_total{bastion, operation, outcome}`,
  `quader_bastion_forwarded_requests_total{bastion, class}` (`class` of R-BAS-013) and `quader_bastion_forwarded_bytes_total{bastion, class}`
  (the caller's class, `anonymous` or `authenticated`, R-BAS-090); `bastion` is the registration name, bounded by
  `bastions.max_registrations`.
- **Recognition in detail** ([Q-BAS-65](#q-bas-65--the-recognition-admits-an-interface-route-on-its-own-proof-throttles-tokens-it-cannot-place-and-counts-the-bastion-in-the-read-class)).
  The token is the Bearer credential of the first line of the header, and only a value that starts with `qdr_bst_` is looked at; any
  other credential leaves the request ordinary. The stages behind the recognition receive the request without the Bastion token. A
  rejected Bastion token counts as a failure of the address that sent it (the address before the Bastion's forwarded headers count,
  R-BAS-017) in a budget of its own; while that address is in throttled mode, a token the replica does not hold in its token cache, and
  whose marker does not say it was valid recently, is refused `429 rate_limited` without a lookup, as every other credential is
  (R-AUTH-038); a token the replica holds costs no read of the shared counters. A request whose token names no registration is counted
  under the registration `unknown`. `token.rejected` of a Bastion token names the request's source, and the last use of an accepted one
  records the address the Bastion connected from, never a caller's it forwards for. A recognized interface request is the registration's,
  not the address's: the request log names it, also on the check, which runs a caller's credential through the authentication stage
  without touching the line ([Q-BAS-119](#q-bas-119--the-check-runs-the-credential-through-a-stage-that-records-nothing-in-the-request-log)), and the general limits charge it to the class `read` under the bucket `token:<token ID>`,
  whatever the method.

Acceptance criteria:

- A forwarded `GET` with `Quader-Bastion-Authorization: Bearer <a revoked bst token>` answers `401 bastion_token_invalid` as
  `application/problem+json`; with `Quader-Bastion-Authorization: Bearer $PAT` (a valid token of another type) the request is
  served as an ordinary one without marking headers.
- The request log of the main installation shows `Quader-Bastion-Authorization` as `[REDACTED]`.
- A forward of `GET /api/%76%31/tokens` or `GET /api/%761/bastion/handshake` (the router decodes both to routes of `/api/v1/`) with a
  valid Bastion token in `Quader-Bastion-Authorization` answers `404 not_found` and runs no route, never `401 bastion_token_invalid`
  (`TestR_BAS_014_AForwardOutsideThePackageFamiliesReachesNoRoute`); the log line of `POST /api/v1/bastion/check` names the registration
  (`TestR_BAS_008_TheCheckLeavesTheRequestLogLineOfTheRegistration`).

### R-BAS-009 · The interface version
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The Bastion interface has a version of its own, separate from the release number (owner,
[Q-BAS-20](#q-bas-20--the-bastion-interface-has-a-version-of-its-own-equal-on-both-sides)).

- The version is a positive integer, `iface.InterfaceVersion` in `internal/bastion/iface`, starting at 1. It is raised by every change of the
  interface: a route, a request or response field, a header, a marking value, a feed entry kind, or the meaning of any of them
  ([Q-BAS-26](#q-bas-26--every-change-of-the-interface-raises-its-version)). Nothing is added "within" a version: equality is the
  rule, so neither side has to read a field it does not know.
- Main installation and Bastion talk only when both speak the same version. Every request of the Bastion carries
  `Quader-Bastion-Interface`; every answer of the main installation to a Bastion request carries its own version in the same
  header. A request with another version, or without the header, answers `400 bastion_interface_mismatch` with the problem
  member `"interfaceVersion": <main's>`, and is served in no other way.
- On a mismatch the Bastion treats the main installation as unreachable (R-BAS-027: the grace period, then nothing) and raises
  a Prometheus alert through `quader_bastion_interface_mismatch` and the rule of its chart (R-BAS-028, R-BAS-041).
- **Guard.** `internal/bastion/iface/testdata/interface.txt` holds the version on its first line and the interface surface
  (routes, headers, marking values, feed kinds, the JSON schema of every body) below it.
  `TestR_BAS_009_TheInterfaceChangesOnlyWithItsVersion` fails when the generated surface differs from the file;
  regenerating (`go test ./internal/bastion/iface -run TestR_BAS_009 -update-interface`) refuses to write a changed surface
  under an unchanged version.
- **Upgrades.** A release that raises the version is announced in its release notes, and main installation and Bastions are
  upgraded together, within the grace period of the Bastions (R-BAS-027). R-ARCH-025's table holds the interface as a surface
  of its own.
- **The raises so far**, each with the requirement that describes it: 4, the format table and the bound repository (R-BAS-057); 5, the
  read shapes per package (R-BAS-087); 6, the handover per blob (R-BAS-073); 7, the longest wait a format's client is told,
  `retryAfterMaxSeconds` of the format table (R-BAS-091); 8, the configuration, the subject's limits, the usage and status reports,
  the format table's `errorShape` and `readWithBody`, the renamed codes, the probe's headers gone, the contact's headers, the registry
  token's payload version 2 read, and W-35's catalogue ([the wire of interface version 8](#the-interface-version-8-the-shared-wire),
  [Q-BAS-322](#q-bas-322--both-topics-raise-the-interface-version-once-to-8); built on 2026-11-26 by E7 with W-35's P5); 9, the request
  header `Quader-Bastion-For-Head` of a `GET` that answers a `HEAD` and the status's `cache.shared`
  ([the wire of interface version 9](#the-interface-version-9-a-head-is-no-download-and-a-replica-says-whose-cache-it-reports), built on
  2026-11-26 by W34-E19); 10, the catalogue's document of a package's open findings per version, the public set's projects with their
  names and the configuration's `display` with the installation's form of a time (R-BAS-128, built on 2026-11-27 by W35-P9e); 11, the
  catalogue's state document with today's signatures of the malware scan and today's vulnerability database of the image scanning
  ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-042, [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-052,
  [Q-BAS-494](#q-bas-494--the-state-documents-shape-is-part-of-the-interface-version-11), built on 2026-11-27 by W-36's P8); 12, the
  catalogue of the project view: a public repository's description, a project's and a repository's index, an image's list by content,
  the set-up path of a package without a version, and the switch `hideRepositories` (R-BAS-130, R-BAS-131,
  [Q-BAS-506](#q-bas-506--the-project-view-raises-the-interface-to-version-12-and-the-bastions-state-record-to-form-3), built on
  2026-11-27 by W-40's P1, released in v0.166.0); 13, the disable of a Bastion: the configuration's `disabled`, the status's
  `operation` and the problem `bastion_disabled` (R-BAS-133, built on 2026-11-27 by W-41's A1, first folded into 12 while it was
  unreleased and raised to 13 at landing, since 12 had been released before it). The version is `iface.InterfaceVersion`;
  the comment beside it names the same list.

Acceptance criteria:

- An in-process main installation built with `InterfaceVersion + 1` and a Bastion with `InterfaceVersion`: the handshake
  answers `400 bastion_interface_mismatch` with `"interfaceVersion": <InterfaceVersion + 1>`, the Bastion sets
  `quader_bastion_interface_mismatch 1` and `quader_bastion_interface_version{side="main"} <InterfaceVersion + 1>` ([Q-BAS-106](#q-bas-106--the-main-installations-interface-version-is-the-series-with-side-main-of-quader_bastion_interface_version)), serves cached artifacts to callers with live answers for the grace period, and
  `503` afterwards.
- Adding a field to the check answer without raising the version fails `TestR_BAS_009_TheInterfaceChangesOnlyWithItsVersion`,
  and `-update-interface` refuses to regenerate.

### R-BAS-010 · Handshake
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040

`GET /api/v1/bastion/handshake`, with the Bastion token. The Bastion calls it at start, every `bastion.main.handshake_interval`,
after every reconnect, and after a feed entry of the kind `settings` (R-BAS-015). It sends its own host as the forwarded host
(R-BAS-017).

```json
{
  "interfaceVersion": 8,
  "bastion": {"name": "partners", "tokenId": "0192f1c4-…", "tokenExpiresAt": "2027-11-02T00:00:00Z"},
  "installation": {"baseUrl": "https://quader.example.com", "release": "0.14.0"},
  "responseBaseUrl": "https://packages.example.com",
  "anonymousReads": false,
  "recordDownloads": true,
  "feed": {"cursor": "MjAyNi0xMS0wMlQxMDowMDowMFp8MDE5MmYx…"},
  "serverTime": "2026-11-02T10:00:00.123Z"
}
```

*(example answer; the members `formats` and `boundRepository` are R-BAS-057's, `configuration` R-BAS-093's)*

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093, [the wire of interface version 8](#the-interface-version-8-the-shared-wire)):* the answer gains `configuration` and loses the top-level
`handover`, which moves into `configuration.switches`; the forwarded host counts only when the Bastion connected from an address of its own
registration's `egress` (R-BAS-017); the contact also records the edge figure the Bastion reports in `Quader-Bastion-Edge-Limit` and
W-35's `Quader-Bastion-Catalogue-Kept`. *Built by E7:* `configuration` replaces `handover`; the two contact headers are read when a
replica sends them, a malformed value answers `400`, and they go into the event `bastion.contact` and the contact's fingerprint
([Q-BAS-354](#q-bas-354--the-contact-headers-are-optional-and-recorded-in-the-contacts-event-until-e8)). *Built by E8 (2026-11-26):*
`configuration` is the registration's own, and the contact's row keeps both values (`bastion_contact.edge_limit`, `catalogue_kept`,
migration 00147), which `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` shows per replica as `edgeLimit` and `catalogueKept`; every replica sends the edge figure since
E9a (the chart's `bastion.edge_limit`), and the catalogue's since W-35's P7 (2026-11-26, R-BAS-111). The forwarded host counts from the registration's own `egress` since E13 (2026-11-26).

- `responseBaseUrl` is the response base URL the main installation derived for this request (R-OPS-005, R-EP-003), with the
  Bastion's forwarded host counted only when the Bastion connected from an address of its registration's `egress` (R-BAS-017). The Bastion
  requires it to equal its own `server.base_url`; otherwise it logs `bastion base URL not honoured by the main installation`,
  sets `quader_bastion_base_url_mismatch 1` and treats the main installation as unreachable, so that no client ever receives a
  document with the main installation's URLs from the Bastion.
- `anonymousReads` is true when the main installation serves any read without a credential: its default endpoint admits such
  requests (`endpoints.default.auth.anonymous`) and the artifacts of at least one repository are `public`
  ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033); it is `publicContent` of R-AUTH-009, read from the grant index of the
  answering replica ([Q-BAS-150](#q-bas-150--the-handshake-reports-whether-the-main-installation-serves-anonymous-reads-at-all)). `recordDownloads`
  is `audit.record_downloads` (R-BAS-039). `feed.cursor` is the feed position at the time of the answer (R-BAS-015).
- The main installation records the last contact of the registration (time, client address, `release` from `User-Agent`,
  interface version, `responseBaseUrl`, replica) at most once a minute per replica, and writes `bastion.contact` (asynchronous)
  when one of the reported values changes.
  The contact is bounded: a registration keeps at most 256 replica rows, the newest, and a failure to record it does not fail the
  handshake ([Q-BAS-69](#q-bas-69--the-last-contact-is-remembered-per-replica-bounded-per-registration-and-its-event-is-asynchronous)).

Acceptance criteria:

- With `https://packages.example.com` missing from `server.additional_base_urls`, the handshake answers
  `"responseBaseUrl": "https://quader.example.com"`, the Bastion sets `quader_bastion_base_url_mismatch 1` and answers a cold
  `npm view` with `503 unavailable`.
- *As built by E7:* `TestR_BAS_093_TheHandshakeCarriesTheConfigurationAndRecordsTheContact` (`internal/api/v1`): the configuration
  answered, valid, with the registration's revision and switches; a malformed `Quader-Bastion-Edge-Limit` or
  `Quader-Bastion-Catalogue-Kept` answers `400`.
- `GET /api/v1/bastions/partners` shows the replica names and the release of every Bastion replica within one
  `handshake_interval`.

### R-BAS-011 · Credential and read check
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040

`POST /api/v1/bastion/check`, with the Bastion token. The Bastion asks about a caller it has no usable answer for, when the
content is cached and no fetch is needed (R-BAS-022, R-BAS-023).

```json
{"credential": "qdr_pat_3kQ9…", "clientAddress": "203.0.113.7", "repositories": ["web/npm-all", "web/npm-partner"]}
```

```json
{
  "subject": {"kind": "token", "tokenId": "0192…", "principalId": "0191…", "expiresAt": "2027-01-31T00:00:00Z"},
  "repositories": {
    "web/npm-all":     {"read": "full"},
    "web/npm-partner": {"read": "none", "status": 404}
  }
}
```

*(example request and answer)*

- `credential` is the token string the caller presented (R-BAS-019), or `null` for an anonymous caller. The main installation
  runs R-AUTH-023's validation on it, including the failed-credential throttle of R-AUTH-038 for `clientAddress`, and records
  `token.rejected` with `source_ip = clientAddress` as for a direct request.
- `clientAddress` counts only when the check comes from an address of the registration's `egress` (R-BAS-017,
  [Q-BAS-432](#q-bas-432--the-callers-address-a-check-names-counts-only-from-the-bastions-own-networks-too)): from any other address, and with an empty list, the check is decided, throttled and recorded as a
  request from the address the Bastion came from (built with E13, `BastionCheck` in
  [bastion_check_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_check_api.go)).
- `subject.kind`: `token` (valid; `expiresAt` is the token's expiry), `anonymous` (no credential; the main installation serves
  anonymous reads), `anonymous_refused` (no credential; it serves none: `anonymousReads` is false), `invalid` (malformed, unknown, expired, revoked, owner disabled:
  R-AUTH-002 does not tell which, and neither does this answer), or `throttled` with `retryAfterSeconds` (the address is in
  R-AUTH-038's throttled mode and the credential is not exempt).
- `repositories`: at most `bastions.check.max_repositories` qualified names `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`, the addresses the
  Bastion classified (R-BAS-018); for each, the read shape of R-BAS-012 and, for `none`, the status the caller would receive
  for a read of the repository (`401` for an anonymous caller, otherwise `404` or `403` by R-AUTHZ-016 and R-AUTHZ-017). An
  unknown name, a project the caller cannot see included, answers `none` with the status of a missing repository for that
  caller, so the check reveals no more than the caller's own request would; a name without a project is refused with
  `400 malformed_request`.
- The check writes no `authz.denied` events: it asks about repositories, not about a request a client made; the request that
  follows a `none` is the Bastion's own refusal (R-BAS-029), and its audit is the request log of the Bastion.
- An answer has no lifetime of its own: the Bastion keeps it for its period (R-BAS-020), never beyond `expiresAt`.
- **How the check validates** ([Q-BAS-66](#q-bas-66--the-check-runs-the-credential-through-the-endpoints-authentication-stage)). The
  credential goes through the authentication stage of the default endpoint as a direct request from `clientAddress` would, so the
  endpoint's token types and bindings apply, a rejected Bastion token presented as the caller's credential is `invalid`, and the last use
  of the token names the caller's address. A subject that is not usable (`invalid`, `anonymous_refused`, `throttled`) carries an empty
  `repositories` object. A `none` always names a status, and `401` for an anonymous caller. A registry token is presented below `/v2/`
  and its shape capped at `partial` (R-BAS-052); the check's paths count as served on every replica, whatever families its role serves
  ([Q-BAS-190](#q-bas-190--the-checks-paths-count-as-served-on-every-replica)).
- **Packages** (R-BAS-083). The request gains `packages`, a list of `{"repository", "package"}` pairs whose
  repository is named in `repositories`, and the answer gains `packages`, one `{"repository", "package", "read"}` per requested pair in
  request order, `read` being the caller's package shape of R-BAS-080 (`full` or `partial`; a pair whose repository reads `none` reads
  `partial`), and an empty array for a subject that is not usable. Both members are always present. The Bastion sends a pair only for a
  cached entry that names a package, when it holds no usable shape answer for the repository (R-BAS-085).

```yaml
bastions:                              # the main installation's section (the Bastion's own is bastion)
  check:
    max_repositories: 16               # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- `$FULL` on `["web/npm-all", "web/npm-partner"]` answers `full` and `none` with `404`; `$PART` on `["web/npm-all"]` answers `partial`;
  a revoked token answers `"kind": "invalid"`; `null` while nothing is `public` answers `anonymous_refused`.
- 400 checks with random well-formed tokens for one `clientAddress` within a minute: from the 301st on the answer is
  `throttled` (R-AUTH-038's default), and a direct request from that address is throttled too.

### R-BAS-012 · Read shapes: what "reads the whole repository" means
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040

The read shape of a subject on an addressed repository is computed by the decision point
([Q-BAS-28](#q-bas-28--what-reads-the-whole-repository-means)):

- `full`: the subject may read every package and every version reachable through the repository, and its wiki, and every response
  of a read route of that repository is the same for it as for every other `full` subject. A subject that reads the artifacts in
  full but not the wiki is `partial`: its documents lack the wiki members ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034,
  [Q-BAS-149](#q-bas-149--a-full-read-shape-includes-the-wiki-so-a-shared-document-never-carries-a-readme-to-a-caller-without-it)). For a local or remote repository: `ReadAll` of
  `authz.ReadScoper` (an unrestricted read grant or `content:bypass`, a token scope that does not narrow, the endpoint's
  exposure `all`), and for a remote repository additionally the populate right of R-AUTHZ-008. For a virtual repository: the
  gate `read` on the repository itself (R-AUTHZ-009 rule 1) and `full` on every member, recursively.
- `none`: the subject may read nothing through the repository: no gate, `ReadNone` on every member, an anonymous subject on a
  repository whose artifacts are not `public`, an unknown repository or project.
- `partial`: every other case.

The shape is the answer to the owner's "the main installation confirmed a full read of the repository" (Q-BAS-18): a `full`
answer lets the Bastion share a marked document with that caller and serve it every cached artifact of the repository without
a per-artifact question (R-BAS-022, R-BAS-023). Content that the format refuses at serve time (a tombstoned version, a blocked
version) is not a matter of the shape; R-BAS-022's revalidation and R-BAS-015's content entries cover it.

A subject whose shape on the repository is `partial` may still read one package of it in full: that shape per package is
[R-BAS-080](#r-bas-080--read-shapes-per-package-at-the-decision-point). A `full` shape on the repository is `full` on
every package of it.

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_012_ShapeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint`: over every subject, repository, package and version of the R-AUTHZ fixture,
  a `full` shape never meets a refused read, and a `none` shape never meets an allowed one.
- `acme-full` without the populate right on `web/npm-remote` has shape `partial` on `web/npm-all`; with it, `full`.
- An exposure rule on the default endpoint makes every shape on the exposed repository `partial` at most.

The rules the list leaves open are decided in [Q-BAS-73](#q-bas-73--the-read-shape-is-computed-inside-the-decision-point-and-agrees-with-it-by-test):
the capability `content:metadata-read` alone never makes a shape `full` (it reads no artifact); the gate of a nested virtual
repository is asked as a member's read; a virtual repository without a readable member is `none`; and a `none` shape carries the
status a refused read gets (`401` for an anonymous subject, `403` or `404` as R-AUTHZ-016 says), taken from the decision point
itself. The tests are `TestR_BAS_012_ShapeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint` and `TestR_BAS_012_Shapes` in `internal/authz`.

### R-BAS-013 · Marking of responses to Bastion requests
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040, RMT-044

A forwarded request is served by the main installation's own route as the caller's own request: authentication, the
decision point, hidden existence, the format's serve-time checks, resolution, the populate right of a remote member (a request
through a Bastion fills a remote member exactly when the caller's own request would, RMT-044), rendering on the Bastion's host,
download statistics and `artifact.downloaded` of the main installation. The core adds the marking headers to the response of a
recognized Bastion request; no format code is involved, because the dispatcher knows the route's `RouteKind`
([Q-BAS-27](#q-bas-27--a-cached-artifact-is-checked-through-the-real-route)):

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Quader-Bastion-Class` | `artifact` for a `200` or `304` of a `Download` route or of a file under `/files/`; `shared` for a `200` or `304` of a `Metadata` or `Computed` route (or a `/files/` folder listing) when the caller's shape on the addressed repository is `full`; `private` for the same routes otherwise; `absent` for a `404` of a read route when the item does not exist in the repository for any subject (no member holds it, the remote's negative cache or upstream says so); `pass` for every other answer (`Volatile` and other routes, errors, redirects) |
| `Quader-Bastion-Repository` | the addressed repository's qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>` |
| `Quader-Bastion-Read` | the caller's shape on the addressed repository (R-BAS-012) |
| `Quader-Bastion-Subject` | `token=<token ID>; principal=<principal ID>; expires=<unix seconds>` (`expires` left out for a token that does not expire, [Q-BAS-49](#q-bas-49--the-interface-is-one-package-of-wire-types-four-details-of-the-contract-are-fixed-in-it)), or `anonymous`, or `invalid` on a `401` for a rejected credential |
| `Quader-Bastion-Interface` | the main installation's interface version |
| `Quader-Bastion-Counted` | `download` on a `200` whose serving counts a download at the main installation (R-BAS-059, Q-BAS-186); absent otherwise |
| `Quader-Bastion-Package` | the package the response belongs to (R-BAS-081), percent-encoded: every byte outside `A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~ @ /` as `%XX` with upper-case hexadecimal digits; decoded 1 to 512 bytes of valid UTF-8 without a control character. Present on a `200` or `304` of a `Download`, `Metadata` or `Computed` route, and on a handover's `200` (R-BAS-073), whose request named exactly one package; absent everywhere else, every refusal and every `404` included (R-BAS-082) |
| `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read` | `full` or `partial`, exactly when `Quader-Bastion-Package` is present: `full` when `Quader-Bastion-Read` is `full` or the caller's package shape (R-BAS-080, with a registry token's grant applied) is `full` (R-BAS-082) |

- `absent` is set only when the core's own lookups (the remote engine, through which a virtual repository's remote members
  answer, and the local lookup of a package or an item) know the item is missing for every subject; a refusal by the decision
  point, a hidden item and a serve-time refusal are `pass`, so a negative entry never stands for a hidden item (R-BAS-024). How
  the lookups tell the marking without format code, and why `absent` needs a `full` shape as well, is
  [Q-BAS-70](#q-bas-70--absent-is-derived-from-the-notes-of-the-cores-lookups-and-only-for-a-full-reader).
- `shared` follows from the shape and the route kind alone: a document of a `full` subject is the unfiltered rendition for the
  Bastion's host, and its ETag is the same for every `full` subject (R-NPM-013's inputs). A format whose document varies by
  anything but the repository's content and the request headers it names in `Vary` must render such a route as `Volatile`; the
  conformance kit has a check (check 12, [Q-BAS-72](#q-bas-72--the-conformance-kit-compares-documents-between-callers-as-check-12)) that
  sends one document request as a user, a service account and the anonymous caller - each with a request context of its own and request
  headers of its own (credential, client, session, forwarded address), except the headers the first answer names in `Vary`, which
  all send alike - and compares status, bytes and validators.
  npm's `-/whoami` and `-/ping` answer by who asks and are `Volatile` since that check found them.
  *Amended on 2026-11-22, built on 2026-11-22 (R-BAS-082):* `shared` is set for a `200` or `304` of a `Metadata` or `Computed` route
  when `Quader-Bastion-Read` is `full` **or** `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read` is `full`; kit check 21 (R-BAS-086) holds that a reader of
  only the response's package receives what a reader of the whole repository receives. `absent` stays tied to a `full` shape on the
  repository.
- The headers are added only to Bastion requests and stripped from every other response, so an ordinary caller never learns
  its own shape.
- Details the table leaves open ([Q-BAS-71](#q-bas-71--the-mark-stage-is-an-edge-package-and-learns-the-caller-from-the-authentication-stage)):
  the subject is `invalid` on every `401` but one whose challenge says `insufficient_scope` (R-BAS-052) and on a credential that is no
  token (a session cookie), and `anonymous` for a caller without a credential; on the registry's token service, whose credential the
  chain does not authenticate, it is the caller the token service accepted (Q-BAS-187); a response that no route matched or that the decision refused carries the repository when the route is
  known and no `Quader-Bastion-Read` (on `/files/` too: the raw file handler tells the marking the decision once the service allowed
  the read); a response on an interface route of the Bastion carries `Quader-Bastion-Class: pass` and
  `Quader-Bastion-Interface` only; a `/files/` path with a trailing slash, and the root, is a listing (`shared` or `private`
  like a document), any other `/files/` path a download.

Acceptance criteria:

- Through the in-process main installation: a tarball `GET` with `$FULL` carries `Quader-Bastion-Class: artifact`,
  `Quader-Bastion-Read: full`; the package document with `$FULL` carries `shared` and with `$PART` `private`; `-/v1/search`
  carries `pass`; a missing name in `web/npm-local` with `$FULL` carries `absent`, and a name `$PART` may not read carries `pass`
  with the same `404` body as a missing one.
- The kit check passes for npm and NuGet: two `full` subjects receive byte-identical documents and the same ETag on every
  `Metadata` and `Computed` route of the fixture.
- No response to a request without a valid Bastion token carries a `Quader-Bastion-` header (contract test over the route table).

### R-BAS-014 · Writes through a Bastion are refused by the main installation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Superseded on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-336](#q-bas-336--the-bastion-refuses-a-write-itself):* a Bastion refuses a write itself, before it reads the
body and without a request to the main installation, with `403 read_only` and a detail that names nothing of the main installation
([R-BAS-095](#r-bas-095--writes-are-refused-by-the-bastion-itself), R-BAS-099). The probe below, the main installation's admission of a
probe as the anonymous caller for routing (Q-BAS-118), the headers `Quader-Bastion-Probe` and `Quader-Bastion-Route` and the detail that
names the main installation's URL go; the main installation's refusal of a forwarded write stays as R-BAS-095's backstop with the neutral
detail, and the forward of a path outside the package families keeps answering `404`. *Built by E15 on 2026-11-26:* the probe below,
`bastionmain.IsProbe`, the probe's admission in `BastionRouteAuth` and the probes' replay cache at the Bastion are gone; the requirement is
R-BAS-095's. *Checked by W-35's P8 on 2026-11-26:* the Bastion's refusal and the main installation's backstop both answer
`errs.ReadOnlyDetail`, "This address is read-only: it serves downloads and accepts no uploads.", which names no address; the paragraphs
below that say the refusal points at the main installation describe the interface up to version 7. *Revised on 2026-11-26 by E7 (interface version 8,
[Q-BAS-351](#q-bas-351--until-e15-a-probe-is-recognized-by-its-form-and-a-read-route-with-a-body-is-the-format-tables)):* the headers
`Quader-Bastion-Probe` and `Quader-Bastion-Route` are gone. The Bastion forwards a request that matches a read route with a body of the
format table (`readWithBody`, R-BAS-095) at once, with its body and the caller's credential, and probes every other request of a method
other than `GET` and `HEAD`; the main installation recognizes a probe by its form, a forward of such a method without a body and without a
caller's credential (`bastionmain.IsProbe`), and refuses every probe at the route match, a read route's as well (H-2293), so it answers no
`204` any more. The bullets below that name the two headers or the `204` describe the interface up to version 7.

The Bastion is read-only for package content (owner, [Q-BAS-2](#q-bas-2--the-bastion-is-read-only-for-package-content)). It
answers a write in the client's protocol shape and points at the main installation, without format knowledge of its own
([Q-BAS-38](#q-bas-38--writes-are-refused-by-the-main-installation-from-a-bodiless-probe)):

- A request with a method other than `GET` and `HEAD` is first sent to the main installation as a **probe**: the same method,
  path and query, the request headers of R-BAS-021, `Content-Length: 0`, no body, no caller credential, and
  `Quader-Bastion-Probe: 1`. The Bastion reads none of the caller's body while it waits.
- The probe carries no credential of a caller by design. The authentication stage admits a recognized probe as the anonymous caller
  for routing only, whatever the anonymous switches say, so that it reaches the route match ([Q-BAS-118](#q-bas-118--a-write-probe-is-admitted-as-the-anonymous-caller-for-routing-only));
  every route below `/api/<format>/`, `/files/` and `/v2/` tells the marking stage its kind there first (the registry's version check
  answers `GET` and `HEAD` only and decides nothing), and the probe goes no further (H-469).
- The main installation's middleware answers a Bastion probe after routing and before any handler or body read:
  - a route whose `RouteKind` is `Upload`, `Delete` or `Admin`, or whose coarse action is not `read`: `403` with the problem
    code `read_only` in the format's error shape (R-ARCH-023), whose detail names no address: `This address is read-only: it
    serves downloads and accepts no uploads.` (R-BAS-099 row 1; until E16 it named the main installation's URL of the addressed
    repository);
  - a read route that takes a body (npm's `POST …/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk`): `204` with `Quader-Bastion-Route:
    read-with-body`;
  - no route: the format's or the core's `404`.
- The Bastion reads `Quader-Bastion-Route` of the probe answer before its client removes the `Quader-Bastion-` headers
  ([Q-BAS-108](#q-bas-108--the-route-of-a-probe-answer-is-read-before-the-marking-is-stripped)).
- The Bastion replays a `403` or `404` probe answer to the caller and keeps it per method and path for
  `bastion.cache.metadata_revalidate_after`. After a `204` it forwards the real request with its body (at most
  `bastion.main.max_forwarded_body`; a larger body answers `413` from the Bastion) and the caller's credential; the answer is
  `pass`. A request with a body above the limit is refused before the probe. The credential of the real request is checked after the `204` ([Q-BAS-81](#q-bas-81--a-write-is-decided-by-the-probe-first-its-credential-is-checked-only-if-the-real-request-is-forwarded)).
- A forward of any path outside `/api/<format>/`, `/files/` and the registry root `/v2/` (R-BAS-051) - judged on the path as the router decodes it, segment by segment, so
  `/api/%76%31/tokens` is `/api/v1/tokens` - answers `404 not_found` as problem details of the management API before authentication,
  whatever its method and credential: a forward reaches no route of the management API, the login tree or the UI ([Q-BAS-115](#q-bas-115--a-request-with-quader-bastion-authorization-is-a-forward-and-a-forward-reaches-only-the-package-families)).
- A forwarded non-probe write that reaches the main installation anyway (a defect) is refused the same way, since the
  Bastion token makes every write `read_only`.
- The test is the route's kind and action, not the method alone ([Q-BAS-74](#q-bas-74--a-write-is-a-route-of-a-writing-kind-or-a-coarse-action-other-than-read)):
  a `PUT`, `DELETE` or `POST` on an `Upload`, `Delete` or `Admin` route, or on any route whose coarse action is not `read`, is
  refused whoever sent it; npm's family of unimplemented endpoints (`Admin`, whatever the method) is therefore `403
  read_only` to a Bastion, where a direct client gets its `404` or `501`. The real request of a read route that takes a
  body (npm's audit) is served.

Acceptance criteria:

- `npm publish` against the Bastion prints `E403` with the read-only sentence and without the main installation's URL in the message,
  and `dotnet nuget push` exits non-zero with `403`; the main installation records no `package.published`, and the Bastion's byte counter shows that less than
  64 KiB of the upload body were read.
- `npm audit` through the Bastion returns the main installation's answer.
- 1,000 `PUT` requests to one path within a minute cause one probe to the main installation.
- With nothing `public`, the probe of `npm publish` answers `403 read_only` with the read-only sentence through the
  real authentication stage, the probe of `npm audit` `403` too (since interface version 8), a forward with a body is no probe, and no
  handler runs (`TestR_BAS_014_AProbeIsAnsweredThroughTheRealAuthenticationStage`).

### R-BAS-015 · Revocation feed
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040
