`GET /api/v1/bastion/feed?after=<cursor>&limit=<n>`, with the Bastion token. The feed is built on the revocation journal of
[authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-031 and [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-054: the journaled audit events, plus
the content events below ([Q-BAS-29](#q-bas-29--the-feed-reads-the-journals-events-from-the-audit-table),
[Q-BAS-30](#q-bas-30--the-feed-also-carries-withdrawn-content)).

| Audit event | Feed entry |
|---|---|
| `token.revoked`, `ci.token.revoked`, `token.rotated` | `{"kind": "token", "tokens": [<token ID>]}` (for `token.rotated`, the predecessor) |
| `user.disabled`, `user.deleted`, `serviceaccount.disabled`, `serviceaccount.deleted` | `{"kind": "principal", "principals": [<ID>]}` |
| `group.members.changed`, `user.groups.synced` | `principal` with every removed member |
| `authz.role.unbound` of a user or service account | `principal` with that principal |
| `group.deleted`, `authz.role.unbound` of a group, `authz.policy.deleted`, `authz.policy.updated`, `authz.settings.changed`, the `ci.issuer.*` and `ci.mapping.*` disables, deletions and updates, `endpoint.exposure.deleted` and `.updated` of the default endpoint | `{"kind": "grants"}`: every permission answer of every caller; `authz.settings.changed` that changed `visibility.artifacts` yields `settings` as well; one whose changed members are levels only (`visibility.artifacts`, `visibility.wiki`) and none of them lower than before yields no `grants`: a raise opens reads and makes no kept answer wrong |
| `settings.auth.changed` | `{"kind": "settings"}` |
| `bastion.configuration.changed` (R-BAS-093; built by E8) | `{"kind": "settings"}`: every Bastion handshakes again and applies its registration's configuration; a change of one registration costs every replica of every Bastion one handshake |
| `bastion.disabled`, `bastion.enabled` (R-BAS-133, *revised on 2026-11-27*: before, a disable yielded none) | `{"kind": "settings"}`: the disable is a member of the configuration, so the disabled Bastion applies it within one poll |
| `authz.project.visibility_changed` | `{"kind": "settings"}`, so the Bastion asks the handshake for `anonymousReads` again, and `grants` when the level was lowered ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-036) |
| `user.external_changed` | `principal` with the user when the flag was set: the user read by `internal` through a Bastion as at the main installation (Q-BAS-148), and the flag ends that, so every answer the Bastion keeps for the user's credentials goes; clearing the flag only widens and yields none |
| `npm.unpublish`, `package.deleted` | `{"kind": "content", "repositories": [<projectKey>/<repoKey>, …]}`: the repository and every virtual repository that includes it, recursively, at the time the feed is read, by their qualified names |
| from M4b: `vulnerability.finding.status_changed` and `vulnerability.finding.reopened` with `block: set` ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-013) | `content` for the finding's repository and its virtual repositories |
| `malware.found`, `malware.release.withdrawn` ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-021, R-MAL-026) | `content` for every repository that holds the blob when the feed is read, and their virtual repositories ([Q-BAS-164](#q-bas-164--the-malware-scannings-events-in-the-feed-a-find-and-a-withdrawn-release-are-content)) |
| `storage.download_links.changed` that switches the delivery by signed links off ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-014) | none: it changes how the main installation hands its own clients a download, never what it serves, and a Bastion's forward is never answered with a link (R-STOR-070 step 2) |
| `system.storage.keys_destroyed` ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-099) | none: it destroys the keys of a retired connection, which holds no copy and no live replica configures, so no download is served from it and no grant and no byte a Bastion keeps changes |
| `malware.settings.changed` that turns the switch on (R-MAL-019) | none: it changes which bytes the main installation serves in every repository, and a `content` entry for every repository would empty every Bastion's cache; the Bastion learns it at its next revalidation ([H-1102](#h-1102--the-bastion-serves-what-it-cached-for-up-to-ten-minutes-after-the-switch-is-turned-on)) |
| `signature.release.withdrawn` ([signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-070, R-SIG-075, [Q-SIG-94](signatures.md#q-sig-94--the-bastion-learns-a-narrowing-as-content-entries-for-the-gated-repositories)) | `content` for the release's repository and its virtual repositories |
| `signature.anchor.removed`, `signature.signer.blocked`; `signature.anchor.updated` that switched an anchor off or took a fingerprint from it; `signature.settings.changed` that switched project anchors off ([signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-039, R-SIG-075) | `content` for every repository whose signature gate is on (`signatures.onlyVerified`, R-SIG-061) when the feed is read, and their virtual repositories: a narrowing of trust changes which bytes those repositories serve and no other's; none while no gate is on, and none for an update that only widens or renames (details that do not read are read as a narrowing) |
| `repository.moved` | `grants`: the repository left its project's roles and policies behind and changed its address ([Q-BAS-120](#q-bas-120--unassigning-a-repository-from-a-project-drops-every-permission-answer-and-every-journaled-event-is-classified), [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md#r-repo-060--move-a-repository-to-another-project)) |
| `authz.project.member_removed`, `authz.project.member_changed` | `grants`: a member's role grants reads on every repository of the project ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-026), so a removal or a lower role narrows them |
| `repository.disabled`, `repository.deleted` | `grants`: the repository takes no part in resolution or download any more, and a `content` entry would keep its shape answers ([Q-AUTHZ-238](authorization.md#q-authz-238--disabling-a-repository-is-journaled-as-repositorydisabled-with-a-handler-of-its-own), [Q-AUTHZ-239](authorization.md#q-authz-239--a-deleted-repository-is-journaled-and-replayed-as-disabled)) |
| `repository.narrowed` ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-061) | `content` for the repository and its virtual repositories: patterns, members, pin rules and blocks change which bytes a URL may be answered with, not who may read the repository ([Q-BAS-146](#q-bas-146--a-content-narrowing-and-a-claim-of-scope-members-yield-a-content-entry-a-global-claim-yields-grants)) |
| `remote.examination.discarded` ([remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-016) | none: it removes what a remote stored and its delivery rules did not deliver, so no Bastion was ever served it; listed with that reason (`TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`). A narrowing of the delivery rules is a part of `repository.narrowed` (the parts `rules` and `deliveryMode`, R-REPO-061) and yields its `content` entry |
| `repository.claims_changed` with an added claim | `content` for the claiming repository and its virtual repositories when every added claim has scope `members`; `grants` when one has scope `global`, which is in effect in every virtual repository of the format and in remote refusal (Q-BAS-146); none when the change only removed claims |
| `authz.ownership.removed`, `authz.ownership.released`, `package.published`, `authz.project.updated`, `authz.project.deleted`, `bastion.deleted`, `group.updated`, `user.updated` | none: they bound publishing, reserve numbers, change a project's name and description, remove a project that holds no repository (a project's policies are deleted before it, each `authz.policy.deleted`), end a registration, which is no caller a Bastion answers and learns of its end from `401 bastion_token_invalid` (R-BAS-006, [Q-BAS-145](#q-bas-145--a-disabled-or-deleted-registration-is-journaled-and-replayed-as-disabled)), clear a group's auto-join flag, which removes no membership that exists, or remove a pending identity link, which no caller holds until a login completes it; each is listed with its reason, and every journaled event of the audit registry is either mapped or listed (`TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`) |
| `signing.identity.removed`, `signing.identity.retired` ([signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-057, R-SIG-059) | none: what a withdrawal changes on the wire, npm's keys document and the documents that carry the identity's signatures, reaches a Bastion as those documents' new revisions ([signatures.md](signatures.md) Q-SIG-154); listed with that reason (`TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`) |
| `oci.manifest.deleted`, `deb.package.deleted`, `deb.coordinates.removed`, `deb.signing_key.promoted`, `deb.signing_key.retired`, `ansible.version.deleted` | `content` for the event's repository and its virtual repositories, as `package.deleted`: a deleted manifest (and the tags and children its cascade took), a withheld package file, a package taken out of a suite, a new primary key and a withdrawn key each change which bytes a URL of the repository is answered with ([Q-BAS-175](#q-bas-175--the-withdrawals-of-oci-debian-and-ansible-galaxy-are-content-entries)). *Superseded in place on 2026-11-22: they yielded none, because a Bastion served neither the OCI registry nor the Debian format (Q-OCI-23, Q-DEB-26), and the code listed them and the two Ansible events in `noFeedEntry`, Ansible Galaxy with Q-ANS-25 as its reason. Built the same day: the six are mapped in `mappers` ([feed.go](../../internal/bastionmain/feed.go))* |
| `ansible.tombstone.cleared` | none: it frees the number of a deleted Galaxy version, which widens what may be published and changes no byte a Bastion holds; listed with that reason (`TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`) |

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {"id": "0192f2a0-…", "at": "2026-11-02T10:00:01.250Z", "kind": "token", "tokens": ["0192…"]},
    {"id": "0192f2a1-…", "at": "2026-11-02T10:00:02.900Z", "kind": "content", "repositories": ["web/npm-local", "web/npm-all"]}
  ],
  "cursor": "MjAyNi0xMS0wMlQxMDowMDowMi45MDBafDAxOTJmMmExLi4u",
  "more": false,
  "reset": false
}
```

*(example answer)*

- **Order and cursor.** Entries are read from `audit_event` by `(occurred_at, id)`. Because `occurred_at` is the start of the
  transaction, a later commit can carry an earlier time; the main installation therefore returns every entry with
  `occurred_at > cursor.at − bastions.feed.lookback`, and the Bastion skips the IDs it has applied. `cursor` names the last entry
  returned, or the request's cursor when there is none; `more` is true when `limit` (at most `bastions.feed.max_page`) cut the
  answer.
- **Entry IDs and paging** ([Q-BAS-49](#q-bas-49--the-interface-is-one-package-of-wire-types-four-details-of-the-contract-are-fixed-in-it)).
  An event that yields more than one entry gives the others the IDs `<event ID>:1`, `<event ID>:2`. A read is two queries: all
  entries within the lookback up to and including the cursor, and the entries after it, cut by `limit`, so a page always advances;
  when the entries behind the cursor exceed four times `bastions.feed.max_page`, the answer is `reset: true`.
- **Reset.** `reset: true` when the entry the cursor names no longer exists although its time lies within the audit retention
  (a point-in-time restore or a failover that lost commits), when the cursor's time lies after the main installation's clock by
  more than `lookback`, when it lies before the audit retention, or when it lies before the last restore (`system_state`
  `restored_at`): a restore re-applies the narrowings made after its restore point with a journal replay, which writes no audit
  event, so the feed carries none of them and the answers of a Bastion that has not seen the restore may predate them. The
  position of a handshake or a reset is then the database clock, so the Bastion settles after one reset. The Bastion then drops every answer (R-BAS-026) and takes the
  returned cursor.
- **History.** `after` may name a synthetic cursor `t:<RFC 3339>` up to the audit retention back, so a starting replica reads the
  entries of the whole lifetime of an answer (R-BAS-026,
  [Q-BAS-33](#q-bas-33--a-replica-starts-with-the-feed-history-of-an-answers-lifetime)).
- Entries carry IDs, never names or secrets. The feed costs one indexed query per poll and replica.
- **Cursor and cuts in detail** ([Q-BAS-68](#q-bas-68--the-feed-advances-over-every-event-it-consumed-is-cut-at-event-boundaries-and-resolves-member-names-when-it-is-read)).
  The cursor names the last audit event the read consumed, also one that yielded no entry; a page ends between events, so the two
  entries of one event are never separated; the member names of a membership event become IDs when the feed is read, and an event
  whose target cannot be read drops every answer (`grants`).

```yaml
bastions:                              # the main installation's section (the Bastion's own is bastion)
  feed:
    lookback: 5m                       # default (proposed); longer than any transaction (the replay_margin of R-HA-054)
    max_page: 1000                     # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- Revoking `$FULL` adds one `token` entry within the commit; a feed read with the earlier cursor returns it once, and the next
  read with the returned cursor returns it again only while it lies within `lookback`, with the same `id`.
- A point-in-time restore of the main installation to before the cursor's entry answers the next feed read with `reset: true`.
- `npm unpublish @acme/sdk@1.0.0` in `web/npm-local` yields a `content` entry naming `web/npm-local` and `web/npm-all`.
- Removing a member from project `web`, lowering its role, and moving a repository of `web` to another project each yield a
  `grants` entry.

### R-BAS-016 · Download intake
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-041

`POST /api/v1/bastion/downloads`, with the Bastion token: the downloads the Bastion served from its cache, in batches of at
most `bastions.downloads.max_batch` (owner, [Q-BAS-13](#q-bas-13--downloads-served-from-the-cache-are-reported-to-the-main-installations-audit)).

```json
{
  "events": [
    {"at": "2026-11-02T10:00:03.100Z", "tokenId": "0192…", "principalId": "0191…", "clientAddress": "203.0.113.7",
     "repository": "web/npm-all", "path": "/api/npm/web/npm-all/@acme/sdk/-/sdk-2.1.0.tgz",
     "sha256": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
     "userAgent": "npm/11.20.0 node/v24.0.0", "replica": "quader-bastion-7d9c-x2k4q"}
  ],
  "dropped": 0,
  "droppedSince": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z"
}
```

*(example request)*

- The main installation writes each event as `artifact.downloaded` (asynchronous, R-OPS-015) with `actor` from `principalId`
  (or `anonymous`), `token_id`, `source_ip = clientAddress`, `repository` (the qualified name) and `project`, `path` (the request path; the Bastion knows no item
  path), `details.sha256`, `details.origin: "bastion"`, `details.bastion: <registration name>`, `details.replica`, and
  `occurred_at = at`. An event whose `at` lies in the future is recorded at the time of receipt; one older than
  `bastions.downloads.max_age` is not recorded and is counted as dropped.
- `dropped` counts the events the Bastion lost since `droppedSince` (R-BAS-039); a non-zero value writes
  `bastion.downloads.dropped` with the count and the period, so the loss is in the audit trail itself.
- With `audit.record_downloads: false` the operation answers `204` and records nothing; the Bastion learns the switch from the
  handshake and does not send.
- Downloads the Bastion fetched from the main installation are recorded by the main installation itself as the caller's
  request; the Bastion reports only downloads it served from its cache, so no download is counted twice.
- **Events that cannot be recorded** ([Q-BAS-67](#q-bas-67--a-download-event-that-breaks-its-contract-is-dropped-and-counted-the-batch-is-refused-only-when-it-is-too-large)).
  An event that breaks its contract (no time, repository or path, a SHA-256 that is no digest) is dropped like one older than `max_age`;
  both are added to the count of `bastion.downloads.dropped`, which also names the parts (`reported`, `expired`, `invalid`). A batch above
  `max_batch` is refused `422`.
- **Budget** ([Q-BAS-117](#q-bas-117--download-events-are-charged-to-their-registration-by-their-count)). Every batch is charged to its registration by its events, in units of 100 rounded up, on a cluster limiter of R-ARCH-034
  (`bastion.download_events`, bucket the registration). A batch the budget does not hold answers `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`
  and records nothing; the Bastion keeps it and sends it again (Q-BAS-78), and what its bounded buffer cannot hold meanwhile is counted
  as lost (R-BAS-039). `events_burst` holds `max_batch`, so every batch can fit; the budget is per registration (H-468).
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-324](#q-bas-324--a-bastion-reports-usage-and-status-on-the-channel-of-its-download-events) ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-045):* a batch
  gains `usage` and `status` ([the wire of interface version 8](#the-interface-version-8-the-shared-wire)); the main installation writes the usage rows into its usage store at the place of
  the Bastion and the status into a transient table per replica, and the Bastion sends a batch every flush also while `recordDownloads` is
  false, then without events; a batch is charged to the registration's budget by its events, and its usage rows are bounded by their
  number and the body's size ([Q-BAS-442](#q-bas-442--a-batchs-body-is-sized-for-100000-usage-rows-and-its-usage-is-stored-after-every-refusal-was-decided)).
  *Built by E8 (2026-11-26):* the main installation stores both, also while `audit.record_downloads` is off, after every refusal of the
  batch was decided; the body of a batch is bounded at `max_batch` × 10 KiB, 640 bytes per usage row of 100,000 and 256 KiB for the rest.
  *Built by E9b (2026-11-26):* every flush of a replica sends one batch with the usage its budgets counted since the last one and its
  state, also without an event and while downloads are not recorded; a usage the main installation did not take is kept for the next
  flush (R-BAS-096, [Q-BAS-474](#q-bas-474--a-replica-reports-its-usage-as-deltas-with-every-flush-and-its-state-says-of-each-figure-whose-it-is)).

```yaml
bastions:                              # the main installation's section (the Bastion's own is bastion)
  downloads:
    max_batch: 1000                    # default (proposed)
    max_age: 720h                      # default (proposed)
    events_per_second: 200             # default (proposed): per registration, across the replicas
    events_burst: 2000                 # default (proposed): holds max_batch; the window is events_burst / events_per_second; units of 100
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With `audit.record_downloads: true`, a warm `npm ci` of 20 tarballs through the Bastion yields 20 `artifact.downloaded`
  events with `origin: bastion`, the callers' token ID and client address, within two `flush_interval`s; the cold run's 20 were
  recorded by the main installation without `origin`.
- A batch with `"dropped": 7` yields one `bastion.downloads.dropped` event with count 7.
- With the defaults, two batches of 1,000 events are recorded and a third within the window answers `429` with `Retry-After` and records
  nothing; another registration is not slowed down (`TestR_BAS_016_DownloadEventsAreChargedToTheRegistrationByTheirCount`).

### R-BAS-017 · The real client and the Bastion's host at the main installation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-334](#q-bas-334--a-bastions-egress-addresses-belong-to-its-registration):* the egress addresses belong to each registration
(`egress`, R-BAS-093, [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-243): a recognized forward's client address and host count only when the request
comes from an address of its own registration's list, and the configuration key `bastions.trusted_proxies` goes; the second acceptance
criterion loses its exception, since a refusal of a write names nothing of the main installation (R-BAS-099). *Built by E16:* the
exception is gone. *Read by W-35's P8 on 2026-11-26, not run:* no end-to-end test runs `npm view … dist.tarball` through the Bastion or
captures its bodies; the second criterion is held by the integration replays' scan (R-BAS-099 row 10), which since P8 also reads every
registry token a Bastion relays (R-BAS-115). *Built (package E13, 2026-11-26):* the list, its validation and its recognition as below ([Q-BAS-430](#q-bas-430--a-bastion-is-recognized-by-its-token-its-reports-about-its-callers-count-only-from-its-own-registrations-networks) to
[Q-BAS-433](#q-bas-433--the-networks-live-in-the-replicas-snapshot-of-the-registrations-with-a-change-area-of-their-own)).

The main installation counts the real client and renders documents for the Bastion's host (owner,
[Q-BAS-17](#q-bas-17--the-bastion-mirrors-the-main-installations-url-space), [Q-BAS-21](#q-bas-21--internet-exposure-limits-blocking-failed-sign-in-timeouts-and-a-configurable-cache)):

- **Client address.** The Bastion sends exactly one forwarded-for entry, the client address it determined with its own
  `server.trusted_proxies` (R-BAS-019), in both header families: `X-Forwarded-For: <address>` and `Forwarded: for=<address>`
  (quoted and bracketed for IPv6). It replaces whatever forwarded headers the caller sent. Each registration lists the networks its
  Bastion connects from (`egress`, at most 32, R-UI-243, [Q-BAS-431](#q-bas-431--a-registration-lists-at-most-32-networks-an-address-is-its-own-network-and-0-is-refused)), not `server.trusted_proxies`
  ([Q-BAS-116](#q-bas-116--the-bastions-forwarded-headers-count-only-for-a-recognized-request-from-an-address-of-bastionstrusted_proxies)). The
  Bastion is recognized by its token wherever it connects from; after the token was checked, a request whose address - as R-ARCH-006
  resolves it with `server.trusted_proxies`, which name the main installation's own ingress - lies in its own registration's networks is
  resolved again with those networks trusted as well, so the client address is the caller's, in whichever family
  `server.forwarded_header` selects; the rate limits, the failed-credential throttle and the audit then apply to the client, not to the
  Bastion ([Q-BAS-430](#q-bas-430--a-bastion-is-recognized-by-its-token-its-reports-about-its-callers-count-only-from-its-own-registrations-networks)). A recognized request from any other address - another registration's network
  included - and every request of a registration whose list is empty forwards nothing: it is served as the Bastion's own request, its
  client address is the address it came from, and its request line carries `bastion_egress: "unlisted"`. A request from the same address
  without a valid Bastion token - any workload that shares the Bastion's egress - forwards nothing either: its client address stays the
  egress address. The replica reads the networks from its snapshot of the registrations, which the change area `bastion_egress`
  refreshes within R-ARCH-018's bound ([Q-BAS-433](#q-bas-433--the-networks-live-in-the-replicas-snapshot-of-the-registrations-with-a-change-area-of-their-own)), never per request.
- **Host.** The Bastion sends its base URL's scheme, host and port as `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Host`,
  `X-Forwarded-Port` and as `proto=` and `host=` of the same `Forwarded` element; the main installation counts them by the same rule
  as the client address (behind its own ingress they are what the ingress reports, H-467). The main installation lists the Bastion's
  base URL in `server.additional_base_urls`, so every URL it renders for the Bastion is on the Bastion's host (R-OPS-005,
  R-EP-003); the handshake proves it (R-BAS-010). The Bastion therefore carries no format knowledge: it never rewrites a body.
- Main installation values for the example *(example)*:

```yaml
server:
  trusted_proxies: ["10.244.3.17", "10.244.5.9"]           # example: the main installation's own ingress pods, never the Bastion
  additional_base_urls: ["https://packages.example.com"]   # example
```

The registration's member *(example)*, set on its card (R-UI-243) or by `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/partners`:

```json
{"egress": ["198.51.100.20/32"]}
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A caller at `203.0.113.7` sending `X-Forwarded-For: 192.0.2.1` through the Bastion appears in the main installation's request
  log and audit as `203.0.113.7`, with either value of the main installation's `server.forwarded_header`.
- `npm view @acme/sdk dist.tarball` through the Bastion prints a URL on `packages.example.com`, and no body or header the e2e run
  captures at the Bastion contains `quader.example.com`; every answer of the integration replays is scanned the same way (R-BAS-099
  row 10).
- A request from the Bastion's egress address without a Bastion token that sends `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7` and
  `X-Forwarded-Host: packages.example.com` is served with the egress address as its client and on the main installation's base URL
  (`TestR_BAS_017_AnUnrecognizedRequestFromTheBastionsEgressForwardsNothing`,
  `TestR_BAS_017_TheBastionsForwardedHeadersCountOnlyForARecognizedBastionRequest`).
- Unit (`internal/bastionmain`, `internal/app`, `internal/api/v1`, milliseconds): a request with one registration's token from another
  registration's network is that registration's request and forwards nothing; a registration without networks forwards nothing, and the
  request line says `bastion_egress: "unlisted"`; a check from an unlisted address is decided for the Bastion's own address; the list's
  rules (`TestR_BAS_017_ARequestCountsAsComingFromItsBastionOnlyFromItsOwnRegistrationsNetworks`,
  `TestR_BAS_017_TheNetworksABastionConnectsFromAreValidated`, `TestR_BAS_017_ACheckFromAnUnlistedAddressIsDecidedForTheBastionsOwnAddress`).
- Integration (area `bastionreg`, about 3 s): two registrations with disjoint networks; a `PATCH` of one list raises the revision, records
  `bastion.updated` with the lists before and after and reaches the replica's snapshot; a forward with one token from the other's network
  is served with the address it came from (`TestR_BAS_017_EachRegistrationNamesTheNetworksItsBastionConnectsFrom`).
- A loop of failed credentials from one caller through the Bastion is throttled by the main installation per that caller's
  address, while a second caller through the same Bastion is not slowed down.

## Serving at the Bastion

### R-BAS-018 · Request classification at the Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The Bastion holds no repository list; every repository of the main installation is reachable under the same paths (owner,
Q-BAS-17). Each request passes these steps in order; the first that answers ends it:

1. **Host.** The effective host (R-EP-003 rules, with the Bastion's own trusted proxies) must be the host of
   `server.base_url`; any other host, an IP literal and a missing host answer `421 misdirected_request` (a port is not part of the host, [Q-BAS-83](#q-bas-83--the-engine-decides-the-host-and-takes-the-client-address-from-the-chain)).
2. **Block list** (R-BAS-037): a blocked address answers `429 address_blocked`.
3. **Path family.** `/api/v1/…` and every path outside `/api/<format>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…`,
   `/files/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…` and the registry root (`/v2/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…` and its three core routes, R-BAS-051;
   on a bound host the bound-host prefixes, R-BAS-057) answer `404 not_found` (R-BAS-003; below `/v2/` in the
   distribution's shape, Q-BAS-169): a protocol path needs four segments before its rest, a raw path three, a registry path three. `<projectKey>/<repoKey>` is the addressed repository's qualified name for the Bastion's
   bookkeeping (answer keys, the check, cache entries) until the main installation's `Quader-Bastion-Repository` confirms it; a
   project segment that does not match `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-+[a-z0-9]+)*$` or a key that does not match
   `^[a-z0-9]+(?:(?:[._]|__|-+)[a-z0-9]+)*$` (INV-5) answers `404` without a request, and so does `/api/npm/web` with one segment after
   the format. The Bastion reads no other part of a path. A family, format, project or key segment that is percent-encoded
   and a `.` or `..` segment are not classified: the path answers `404 not_found` (Q-BAS-121).
4. **Per-address limits** (R-BAS-035) and **credentials** (R-BAS-019), including the failed-authentication timeout (R-BAS-036).
5. **Method.** `GET` and `HEAD` go to the read flow (R-BAS-020 to R-BAS-024); `OPTIONS` answers `405`; a read route with a body of
   the format table is forwarded with its body; every other method is refused `403 read_only` by the Bastion itself (R-BAS-095). The
   credential of a write is not read ([Q-BAS-452](#q-bas-452--a-write-is-refused-before-its-credential-is-read)); the credential
   step of 4 is the read flow's and the forward's.
6. **Read flow**: the cache entry for the request's cache key and the caller's answers decide between a hit, a check and a miss.

- **Cache key**: the path and query exactly as received (percent-encoding kept), and the normalized values of the request
  headers the main installation's `Vary` named for that path (`Accept`, `Accept-Encoding` for npm documents). The host is
  constant. A replica learns the names from the responses it receives and, for a target it has not seen, from the entry that a peer
  also stored under the key without the values, so a document one replica kept is a hit on every replica that shares the backend
  (`TestR_BAS_023_AnotherReplicaServesTheDocumentAPeerKeptWithoutKnowingItsVary`).

Acceptance criteria:

- `curl --resolve quader.example.com:443:<bastion address> https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/lodash` answers `421`.
- `GET /api/npm/web/NPM-ALL/lodash`, `GET /api/npm/Web/npm-all/lodash`, `GET /api/npm/1web/npm-all/lodash`,
  `GET /api/npm/w%65b/npm-all/lodash` and `GET /api/npm/web` answer `404` without a request to the main installation;
  `GET /api/npm/npm-all/lodash`, which names project `npm-all` and repository `lodash`, is forwarded and answers the main
  installation's `404` of a missing repository; `GET /api/npm/web/npm-all/lodash` with
  `Accept: application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json` and without it are two cache entries.

### R-BAS-019 · Credentials at the Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Reads at the Bastion authenticate exactly as at the main installation (owner,
[Q-BAS-6](#q-bas-6--a-caller-reads-what-its-token-may-read-there-is-no-release-step)), with the client credentials of INV-8 and
without sessions:

- **Sources.** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or Basic with the token as password (any username). `X-NuGet-ApiKey` is
  never a read credential: NuGet sends it on pushes, which the Bastion refuses without reading it (R-BAS-095). The cookie is ignored
  (R-BAS-003). The credential key of every answer is the SHA-256 of
  the token string; the Bastion keeps no token in memory beyond the request, on disk or in Valkey.
- **Before any request to the main installation:** a token that fails R-AUTH-022's syntax and checksum answers `401
  invalid_token` with the challenge of R-AUTH-002 for the path family and counts as a failed authentication (R-BAS-036). The
  types `pat`, `sat` and `cit` are accepted; below `/v2/` also the registry token `rgt` by its own syntax, which has no checksum
  (R-BAS-052); `bst` and an unknown prefix answer the same `401` and count. On `/v2/_token` the credential is the one the token
  service reads: the Basic password of a `GET`, the form's `password` of a `POST` (R-BAS-051).
- **Anonymous.** A request without a credential is anonymous exactly when the main installation serves anonymous reads
  (owner, [Q-BAS-12](#q-bas-12--anonymous-reads-as-on-the-main-installation-with-misses-absorbed-at-the-bastion)): with
  `anonymousReads: false` from the handshake the Bastion answers `401 credentials_required` with the challenge itself, without a
  request; before the first successful handshake the setting is not known and an anonymous request answers `503 unavailable`
  ([Q-BAS-99](#q-bas-99--a-replica-that-has-not-handshaken-answers-an-anonymous-request-503)); with `true` the anonymous caller's answers are kept under the key `anonymous`, shared by every anonymous caller, since
  the main installation's decision does not depend on the client address ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-029).
- **Client address.** R-ARCH-006 with the Bastion's `server.trusted_proxies` and `server.forwarded_header`. For the limits and
  blocks of R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037 an IPv6 address counts as its `/64`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `qdr_pat_` with one flipped character answers `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="quader"` on `/api/npm/…`, and the
  main installation's counter records no request.
- With nothing `public` at the main installation, 1,000 anonymous `npm view` within a minute cause no request to the main
  installation after the handshake; after an administrator makes a project and one of its repositories `public`, the next
  anonymous request is
  checked within `feed.poll_interval` plus 5 s.

### R-BAS-020 · Answers and their validity
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

An answer is what the main installation said about a caller (owner,
[Q-BAS-1](#q-bas-1--the-bastion-asks-the-main-installation-and-keeps-no-copy-of-users-tokens-or-policies),
[Q-BAS-8](#q-bas-8--answers-are-kept-for-a-period-and-a-revocation-feed-drops-them-within-seconds)):

| Answer | Key | Holds | From |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credential | credential key | `kind`, token ID, principal ID, token expiry | the check, or `Quader-Bastion-Subject` of any marked response |
| Read shape | credential key, repository | `full`, `partial`, `none` with its status | the check, or `Quader-Bastion-Read` |
| URL | credential key, cache key | allowed, or the stored refusal (status, headers, body) | a forwarded or conditional request for that URL |
| Package (R-BAS-084) | credential key, repository, package | `full` or `partial` | the check's `packages`, or `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read` of a marked response whose `Quader-Bastion-Repository` is the request's repository; recorded only while the caller's shape on the repository is not `full` |

A repository in an answer's key, in a cache entry and in a feed entry is the qualified name `<projectKey>/<repoKey>` of the
address (R-BAS-018); the key of a read-shape answer is `<credential key>|<projectKey>/<repoKey>`, and its Valkey record is
`ans:v1:shape:<sha256 of that key>` (R-BAS-034). Two repositories of the same key in two projects never share an answer. The key of a
package answer is `<credential key>|<projectKey>/<repoKey>|<package>`, and its Valkey record is `ans:v1:package:<sha256 of that key>`.

- **Validity** ([Q-BAS-32](#q-bas-32--answers-validate-themselves-against-the-feed-and-are-signed-in-valkey)). An answer obtained
  at `o` (the Bastion's clock when it sent the request) is usable while all of these hold:
  1. `now < o + bastion.answers.period`, extended by `bastion.answers.grace_period` only while the main installation is
     unreachable (R-BAS-027);
  2. `now <` the token's expiry, never extended;
  3. no feed entry that matches the answer was received after `o − 15 s`: a `token` entry naming its token, a `principal` entry
     naming its principal, a `grants` entry for a read-shape, package or URL answer, a `content` entry naming its repository for a URL
     answer (a `content` entry leaves a package answer usable and makes the cache entry stale instead, R-BAS-022); 15 s covers the main installation's revocation bound (at most 10 s, R-AUTH-023) and the clock skew between Bastion
     replicas;
  4. `o` is not earlier than the start of the replica's feed history plus 15 s (R-BAS-026).
- A refused or invalid answer is kept like an allowed one, so a refused caller costs the main installation one request per
  period; a widening of a right may take the period to reach the Bastion (owner). A `403` is kept, unless it says `Cache-Control: no-store`
  (the refusal of a remote's delivery rules, `403 not_allowed_in_repository`, which an allow lifts without a feed entry:
  [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) Q-CUR-44); a `404` that is not marked `absent` never is,
  whether it answers a plain fetch or a conditional request, because it may be a missing name or a hidden one, and replaying it only
  for names the Bastion holds would show a narrowed reader which hidden names are cached
  ([Q-BAS-124](#q-bas-124--a-404-that-is-not-marked-absent-is-never-kept-as-a-url-answer), which replaces [Q-BAS-80](#q-bas-80--a-404-that-answers-a-plain-fetch-is-not-kept-as-the-callers-url-answer)).
- Answers live in the replica's memory (at most `bastion.answers.max_entries`, least recently used first) and, with Valkey, in
  Valkey as signed records (R-BAS-034). A replica may refresh an answer that a request uses in the last fifth of its period in
  the background, with one collapsed request (the shape answer, through the check; URL answers renew by use, [Q-BAS-84](#q-bas-84--the-background-refresh-renews-shape-and-credential-answers-url-answers-renew-by-use);
  package answers renew by use too, [Q-BAS-248](#q-bas-248--package-answers-renew-by-use)).

```yaml
bastion:
  answers:
    period: 5m                          # default (proposed); 30s to 1h
    grace_period: 15m                   # default (proposed; the owner's proposal); 0 to 24h
    max_entries: 200000                 # default (proposed), per replica
```

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_020_AnAnswerObtainedBeforeARevocationIsNeverUsedAfterIt`: an answer whose request left before a `token` entry
  arrived is not used, also when it reaches the replica (or Valkey) after the entry was applied.
- A token that expires 30 s after its answer was obtained is refused at the Bastion from its expiry on, also while the main
  installation is unreachable.
- With `period: 5m`, a policy that grants `$NONE` read on `npm-all` reaches the Bastion within 5 minutes and 5 seconds.

### R-BAS-021 · Fetching on a miss with the caller's credential
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040, RMT-044

On a miss the Bastion forwards the caller's request with the caller's own credential; the main installation decides and serves,
and the Bastion keeps what may be kept (owner, Q-BAS-7):

- **Request.** `GET` or `HEAD` with the path and query as received, the caller's `Authorization` unchanged, every end-to-end
  request header except `Cookie`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `Quader-*`, `Range`, `If-*` and the hop-by-hop headers, and the
  headers of R-BAS-008 and R-BAS-017. A conditional the Bastion sends is its own (R-BAS-022, R-BAS-023), never the caller's.
- **Response.** The marking decides what is kept: `artifact` (R-BAS-022), `shared` or `private` (R-BAS-023), `absent`
  (R-BAS-024), `pass` (nothing). `Quader-Bastion-Subject`, `Quader-Bastion-Read` and the status give the credential, shape and URL
  answers of R-BAS-020. The caller receives the main installation's status, headers and body, without the `Quader-Bastion-*`
  headers, `X-Quader-Replica`, `Cache-Status` ([Q-BAS-40](#q-bas-40--no-cache-state-in-the-bastions-answers)) and hop-by-hop
  headers.
- **Streaming.** An artifact is spooled while it is streamed to the caller, with R-REPO-041's withheld tail: the last 64 KiB
  are released only after the SHA-256 equals the content address of its `ETag` and the entry is committed; on a mismatch the
  transfer is aborted and nothing is kept. The spooling does not wait for the caller
  ([Q-BAS-123](#q-bas-123--the-fill-reads-the-main-installation-at-its-own-speed-and-no-client-holds-a-slot-or-a-waiter)): the fill reads the
  main installation's body into the spool at the main installation's speed and frees the budget slot when the body ends, and the
  caller is served from the spool at its own speed. A fill goes on when its caller goes away, so the next request is a hit. A spool that
  cannot take the bytes cuts the transfer; the bytes are never passed on unverified. A document is kept once it has arrived whole. An artifact without `Content-Length`
  or above `bastion.cache.max_object_bytes` is passed through and not kept. A document above 64 MiB is spooled like an artifact
  when its strong `ETag` is a content address and it is within `max_object_bytes` and `documents_max_bytes`, and passed through otherwise
  ([Q-BAS-173](#q-bas-173--a-shared-answer-above-the-memory-bound-is-spooled-by-its-content-address); *superseded in place on
  2026-11-22: every document above 64 MiB was passed through*). A caller's `Range` on a miss is served from the growing spool, and a
  second caller of a running fill follows it on its own permission (R-BAS-054). A `HEAD` miss is
  forwarded as `HEAD`; of an artifact it keeps answers only (*superseded in place on 2026-11-26: a `HEAD` miss of a document kept answers
  only as well, so a client that only `HEAD`s a tag cost the main installation one request per pull*). *Revised on 2026-11-26 by
  [Q-BAS-475](#q-bas-475--a-head-of-a-document-is-answered-from-what-the-bastion-keeps), built the same day (package W34-E18):* a `HEAD`
  of a document is answered from what the Bastion keeps, for every format. A `HEAD` miss is still forwarded as `HEAD`, since only the
  marking of the answer tells the Bastion what the path is; when it answers `200` marked `shared` or `private` with a `Content-Length`
  within the memory bound of the document's class (the smaller of 64 MiB and `documents_max_bytes`, or of `private_documents_max_bytes`
  for a copy, which for a caller with a token needs a validator), the Bastion sends the `GET` of the path with the caller's credential,
  keeps its answer as a `GET`'s answer is kept (an entry, the caller's copy or the anonymous caller's copy, R-BAS-023, R-BAS-094) and
  answers the `HEAD` from it, with the `GET`'s headers and no body ([Q-BAS-476](#q-bas-476--a-head-miss-learns-from-its-marking-that-it-addresses-a-document-and-then-sends-the-get),
  [Q-BAS-477](#q-bas-477--the-get-of-a-head-is-sent-only-for-a-document-the-bastion-keeps-in-memory)). That `GET` is a miss of the
  caller's address and an upstream request of its subject (R-BAS-035, R-BAS-096); when one of them, the link or the anonymous ceiling
  refuses it, the caller receives the `HEAD`'s answer the Bastion holds ([Q-BAS-478](#q-bas-478--a-refused-get-of-a-head-passes-the-heads-answer-on)).
  The conditional request of a `HEAD` for a kept document within that bound, or for the caller's copy, is a conditional `GET`, so a
  `304` renews what is kept and a `200` replaces it, as for a `GET`. A `HEAD` of an artifact is never sent as a `GET`: answered from a
  kept artifact, else forwarded as `HEAD`, as before. *Revised on 2026-11-26 by [Q-BAS-479](#q-bas-479--a-get-a-bastion-sends-for-a-head-says-so-in-a-header-of-the-request) (package
  W34-E19, [interface version 9](#the-interface-version-9-a-head-is-no-download-and-a-replica-says-whose-cache-it-reports)):* the `GET` of a `HEAD` and the conditional `GET` of a
  `HEAD` carry `Quader-Bastion-For-Head: true`, and the main installation answers them as the `GET`s they are, marking included, but
  records no download for them, as for the `HEAD` they stand for (R-BAS-059); *until then it counted that `GET` as the document's download
  where it counts the `GET` of that document ([H-2375](../security/bastion.md#h-2375--the-get-of-a-head-is-a-download-at-the-main-installation), closed)*.
  A `HEAD` the Bastion answers is never reported as one (R-BAS-059). Code: [headfill.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/headfill.go)
  (`fillForHead`, `admitFill`, `headAsGet`), `rq.asGet` and `sentMethod` in [forward.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/forward.go).
- **Errors.** An answer that carries the marking is the main installation's own, whatever its status, and is passed on
  (`pass`). A connect or TLS error, a timeout, and an unmarked `5xx` (an ingress or proxy in front of the main installation)
  answer `502 bad_gateway` or `504 gateway_timeout` from the Bastion (R-BAS-029) and keep no answer.

Acceptance criteria:

- A cold `npm ci` of 20 tarballs with `$FULL` sends 20 tarball requests carrying `Authorization: Bearer $FULL` and
  `Quader-Bastion-Authorization` to the main installation, and the main installation's audit shows `$FULL` as actor.
- A tarball whose bytes the in-process main installation corrupts after the status line is aborted at the client, and a second
  request fetches again.
- *Added on 2026-11-26 (Q-BAS-475), as built:* unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, under 0.1 s together, documents of a few bytes):
  `TestR_BAS_021_AHeadMissOfADocumentIsFilledAsAGetAndAnsweredFromIt` (a full reader's cold `HEAD` sends the `HEAD` and the `GET`, three
  `HEAD`s and a `GET` after it nothing, a `HEAD` after the period one conditional `GET`, a moved document replaces the entry),
  `TestR_BAS_023_AHeadOfADocumentKeepsTheCopyOfACallerWithoutFull`, `TestR_BAS_021_AHeadOfADocumentAboveTheMemoryBoundStaysAHead`,
  `TestR_BAS_021_AHeadMissOfAnArtifactIsForwardedAsHeadAndKeepsAnswersOnly`, `TestR_BAS_035_TheGetOfAHeadIsAMissAndARefusedOnePassesTheHeadOn`
  and `TestR_BAS_096_AHeadIsChargedAsARequestAndItsGetAsAnUpstreamRequest`. Integration (area `bastion`, about 0.15 s of
  `TestR_BAS_021_R_BAS_094_AnAnonymousPullAndAnAnonymousDocumentSpareTheMainInstallation`): Docker's sequence (the `HEAD` of a tag no client
  fetched by `GET`, the manifest by digest, the blobs) from one address costs the main installation the `HEAD` and the `GET` of the tag, the
  same pull from another address nothing, counted at the main installation's side.

### R-BAS-022 · Artifacts
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040

A cached artifact is served to a caller only after the main installation said that this caller may read it, with an answer kept
for the bound (owner, Q-BAS-7):

- **Entry.** Per cache key: the content address (SHA-256), size, the response headers to replay, the addressed repository, and
  `validatedAt`, the time the main installation last answered `200` or `304` for it. The bytes are stored once per content
  address (R-BAS-030). *Amended on 2026-11-22, built on 2026-11-23 (R-BAS-084):* the entry also records `Package`, the `Quader-Bastion-Package` of the
  `200` that filled it, replaced by every later `200` or `304` for the key and cleared by a marking without one.
- **Shape first.** When the entry exists and the caller has no usable read-shape answer for its repository, the Bastion asks
  the check of R-BAS-011 for it, one request per credential and repository, collapsed; the shape then decides below. A caller
  whose credential the main installation called `invalid` gets the `401` of R-BAS-029.
- **Serve from the cache without a request** when the entry is fresh and the caller is allowed:
  - fresh: `now < validatedAt + bastion.cache.artifact_revalidate_after` and no `content` or `grants` entry for its repository was received
    after `validatedAt − 15 s` ([Q-BAS-31](#q-bas-31--cached-artifacts-are-revalidated-after-a-period)); the `content` entry also ends
    an entry's service while the main installation is unreachable and its periods are extended
    ([Q-BAS-122](#q-bas-122--a-content-entry-ends-the-service-of-a-cached-entry-also-while-the-main-installation-is-unreachable));
  - allowed: a usable read-shape answer `full` for the repository, or a usable URL answer `allowed` for the cache key.
- *Amended on 2026-11-22, built on 2026-11-23 (R-BAS-085):* **allowed** also holds with a usable package answer `full` on the entry's
  package. A caller without a usable shape answer gets one check for the repository and, when the entry names a package, for that
  package (collapsed per credential, repository and package). A caller whose usable shape answer is `partial` and who holds no package
  answer for the entry's package gets the conditional request below, not a check; its marking supplies the package answer.
- **Check** otherwise: a conditional `GET` with the caller's own credential and `If-None-Match: "<sha256>"` through the real
  route ([Q-BAS-27](#q-bas-27--a-cached-artifact-is-checked-through-the-real-route)). `304`: the bytes are served from the cache,
  and `validatedAt` and the caller's URL answer are renewed. `200`: the new bytes replace the entry and are served. A refusal:
  the main installation's answer is replayed, a `403` is kept as the caller's URL answer (not one that says `Cache-Control: no-store`, Q-CUR-44 of
  [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md)) and a `404` is not (Q-BAS-124), and the entry stays for other callers; only a
  `404` marked `absent` removes it. The main installation answers the conditional from PostgreSQL without reading its object
  store (R-STOR-012), so a check costs no artifact transfer.
- **Refuse without a request** when the caller's shape answer is `none`: the Bastion answers the stored status (R-BAS-029).
- `Range` and `If-Range` with the content address, `If-None-Match`, `If-Modified-Since` (evaluated only without `If-None-Match`,
  against the entry's `Last-Modified`, RFC 9110 section 13.1.3; R-BAS-056) and `HEAD` from the caller are answered from the entry
  (RFC 9110), after the same permission rule. A range is verified by reading the object to its end ([Q-BAS-82](#q-bas-82--a-range-is-verified-by-reading-the-object-to-its-end-a-callers-range-or-conditional-on-a-miss-is-answered-from-the-verified-spool)).
  The check of a `HEAD` of an artifact is a conditional `HEAD`, and a `HEAD` miss of an artifact stays a `HEAD`: a `GET` would be a
  download at the main installation. A kept document, by contrast, is checked for a `HEAD` by the conditional `GET` of R-BAS-023, and a
  `HEAD` miss of a document fills its entry by a `GET` (R-BAS-021, [Q-BAS-476](#q-bas-476--a-head-miss-learns-from-its-marking-that-it-addresses-a-document-and-then-sends-the-get)).
- **Content address.** A strong `ETag` names the SHA-256 when it is `"<64 hex>"` (R-STOR-012) or `"sha256:<64 hex>"` (the
  registry's spelling, R-OCI-008, Q-OCI-62); the Bastion's conditional request sends the entry's `ETag` as the main installation
  gave it (R-BAS-053). *Superseded in place on 2026-11-22: only the first spelling was read, so every OCI artifact would have been
  passed through.*

Acceptance criteria:

- Warm cache, `$FULL` with a usable `full` answer: `npm ci` of 20 tarballs sends no request to the main installation.
- Warm cache, `$PART` for `@acme/sdk` tarballs through `npm-all`: 1 conditional request per tarball, each answered `304`, no tarball
  bytes from the main installation; for a tarball outside `@acme/*` the main installation's `404` is replayed, and asked for again by each
  request. (`$PART` has no grant on `npm-remote`, so its package shape through `npm-all` stays `partial`; through `npm-local` it is `full`
  on `@acme/sdk`, R-BAS-085.)
- `$NONE` with a `none` answer on `npm-all`: the tarball request answers `404` without a request.
- After `artifact_revalidate_after`, the next request for a cached tarball by `$FULL` sends one conditional request.

### R-BAS-023 · Documents: shared for confirmed full readers, per caller otherwise
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-040

*Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-326](#q-bas-326--an-anonymous-ceiling-per-bastion-and-the-one-for-one-paths-removed) (R-BAS-094):* a document the main installation marks
`private` for the anonymous subject is the same for every anonymous caller, so it is kept once per replica in memory and reused for
`metadata_revalidate_after` without a conditional request, under the feed's `content` entries like a shared document; it is never written
to the cache backend. *Built on 2026-11-26 (package E14a):* `fromAnonymousCopy` in [readflow.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/readflow.go)
serves the anonymous caller's copy, judged by the period and the feed's entries as a cache entry is (`freshFor`, `entries.go`); a copy
without a validator is kept as well ([Q-BAS-437](#q-bas-437--the-anonymous-callers-copy-is-kept-also-without-a-validator-and-judged-as-a-cache-entry-is)).
A caller with a token still sends a conditional request on every use.

The main installation marks a document that is the same for every caller who reads the whole repository; the Bastion shares it
for the metadata period with each caller for whom the main installation confirmed a full read (owner,
[Q-BAS-18](#q-bas-18--metadata-shared-for-confirmed-full-readers-filtered-documents-per-caller)):

- **Shared document** (`Quader-Bastion-Class: shared`): kept in the cache backend under its cache key, with its validator, the
  replay headers, the repository, `validatedAt`, within `bastion.cache.documents_max_bytes` so that documents never evict
  artifacts. Served without a request to a caller with a usable `full` answer for the repository while
  `now < validatedAt + bastion.cache.metadata_revalidate_after` and no `content` entry for the repository was received after
  `validatedAt − 15 s`; a caller without a shape answer gets one first, as in R-BAS-022. Otherwise a conditional `GET` with the
  caller's credential and the stored validator: `304` with
  `shared` renews it and serves it; `200` with `shared` replaces it; `200` with `private` is served to this caller only and kept
  as its private copy; a refusal is replayed. A `304` marked `private` to the Bastion's own condition (the caller is a partial
  reader whose document is the same bytes) is answered with the entry's bytes as the caller's `200`, and the entry is not renewed
  ([Q-BAS-107](#q-bas-107--a-304-for-a-private-document-is-answered-with-the-shared-entrys-bytes)).
  *Amended on 2026-11-22, built on 2026-11-23 (R-BAS-085, [Q-BAS-244](#q-bas-244--documents-are-shared-per-package)):* a shared document
  is also served without a request to a caller with a usable package answer `full` on the entry's package, under the same freshness rule;
  the main installation marks such a caller's document `shared` (R-BAS-082). Which caller gets a check and which a conditional request is
  R-BAS-022's amended rule.
- **Private document** (`private`, a document filtered for the caller): never shared. It goes to the main installation per
  caller with a conditional request on every use: the Bastion keeps the caller's last copy in memory only, under (credential
  key, cache key), at most `bastion.cache.private_documents_max_bytes` per replica, and sends its validator; `304` serves the
  copy. A private copy is never written to the cache backend or to Valkey.
- **Search** and every other `pass` answer (`Volatile` routes, `-/whoami`) go to the main installation per caller on every
  request and are never kept ([Q-BAS-41](#q-bas-41--search-results-go-to-the-main-installation-per-caller)).
- **`HEAD`** (*added on 2026-11-26 by [Q-BAS-475](#q-bas-475--a-head-of-a-document-is-answered-from-what-the-bastion-keeps),
  built the same day*): a `HEAD` of a document is answered from the shared entry, the caller's copy or the anonymous caller's copy under the
  rules above, with the headers a `GET` answer carries and no body. A `HEAD` without any of them fills one by the `GET` of R-BAS-021, and
  the conditional request of a `HEAD` is the conditional `GET` above.
- Metadata of a new version reaches a `full` caller within `metadata_revalidate_after` (H-384).

```yaml
bastion:
  cache:
    metadata_revalidate_after: 1m       # default (proposed)
    artifact_revalidate_after: 10m      # default (proposed)
    documents_max_bytes: 2GiB           # default (proposed); a share of max_bytes
    private_documents_max_bytes: 256MiB # default (proposed), per replica, memory
```

Acceptance criteria:

- Warm cache, `dotnet restore` with a second `full` token that has not been seen: one check answers `full` for `nuget-all`, and
  no document request reaches the main installation within `metadata_revalidate_after`.
- `$PART` never receives the shared npm document of `npm-all` (it lists packages outside `@acme/*`): every `npm view` with
  `$PART` sends a conditional request and receives its filtered copy; the shared entry stays untouched.
- `npm search acme` with `$FULL` twice sends two search requests to the main installation.

### R-BAS-024 · Negative cache
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Names the main installation does not have are answered at the Bastion, because an anonymous request costs an attacker nothing
(owner, Q-BAS-12):

- A `404` marked `absent` is kept per cache key, with its body and headers, for `bastion.cache.negative_period`, in memory and,
  with Valkey, signed in Valkey; at most `bastion.cache.negative_max_entries` per replica.
- It is replayed only to callers with a usable `full` answer for the repository
  ([Q-BAS-42](#q-bas-42--negative-entries-are-served-only-to-full-readers)); every other caller goes to the main installation,
  so the speed of an answer never tells a `partial` caller whether a hidden name exists. A caller with a `none` answer receives
  its refusal anyway.
- A publish of the name at the main installation appears at the Bastion after `negative_period` at the latest (H-384).

```yaml
bastion:
  cache:
    negative_period: 1m                 # default (proposed)
    negative_max_entries: 100000        # default (proposed), per replica
```

Acceptance criteria:

- `npm-all` and its members `public` in both parts, so the anonymous subject is a `full` reader of `npm-all`: 10,000 anonymous requests from 100 addresses for 100 random
  missing names within a minute cause at most one request per name and replica (plus one check per replica) to the main
  installation, and one per name with Valkey.
- `$PART` asking for a missing name twice sends two requests to the main installation, and asking for a name that is cached but
  hidden from it twice sends two as well (`TestR_BAS_024_ANarrowedReaderCannotTellACachedHiddenNameFromAMissingOne`).

### R-BAS-025 · Concurrency budget towards the main installation and collapsed misses
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093, R-BAS-094, R-BAS-097; the owner's [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation), [Q-BAS-326](#q-bas-326--an-anonymous-ceiling-per-bastion-and-the-one-for-one-paths-removed) and [Q-BAS-331](#q-bas-331--the-maximum-throughput-is-enforced-at-the-bastion-on-every-byte-it-reads)):*
`max_concurrent`, `anonymous_share` and `queue_timeout` are the registration's `limits.slots`, resized on a new configuration without a
restart; a request on behalf of an anonymous caller is bounded by the anonymous ceiling as well; a fill is paced by the registration's
throughput, so at the cap it holds its slot longer, and a miss that waits `queueTimeout` answers `503 busy`; the write probe and the sentence
on its slot go (R-BAS-095). *Built by E9a (2026-11-26):* the slots are the configuration's and resized in place
(`SlotBudget.Resize`), and a request of the anonymous class takes from the anonymous ceiling after its slot, giving the slot back when the
ceiling refuses it ([Q-BAS-445](#q-bas-445--the-anonymous-ceiling-is-taken-in-the-slot-budget-after-the-slot)). The defaults are 64, 0.25
and **5 s** (R-BAS-096, [Q-BAS-448](#q-bas-448--the-defaults-of-the-anonymous-ceiling-and-of-the-slots)). *Built by E10 (2026-11-26):* a
forward that got its slot is admitted by the throughput, which refuses a miss at the cap at once with `503 busy` and the wait until its first
bytes ([Q-BAS-457](#q-bas-457--a-miss-at-the-cap-is-refused-at-once-when-its-first-bytes-would-come-after-its-queue-time)), and its body
is read at the cap's pace while it holds the slot (R-BAS-097). Since E8 a new registration's slots are
these (`bastionmain.DefaultLimits`).

- **Budget** ([Q-BAS-35](#q-bas-35--the-concurrency-budget-is-per-replica-with-a-share-for-anonymous-misses)). Every request to
  the main installation except the handshake and the feed takes a slot: forwards, conditional requests, checks, probes,
  download batches. A replica holds at most `ceil(bastion.main.max_concurrent ÷ bastion.replicas)` slots, of which requests on
  behalf of anonymous callers may hold at most `bastion.main.anonymous_share`, rounded down and at least one slot while the share is above 0
  ([Q-BAS-75](#q-bas-75--the-anonymous-cap-of-the-budget-is-the-share-rounded-down-at-least-one-slot)). A request that gets no slot within
  `bastion.main.queue_timeout` answers `503 busy` with `Retry-After: 1`. Misses can therefore never put more than the
  budget onto the main installation, whatever arrives. A slot is held until the response body ends, and no client's speed
  decides how long that is ([Q-BAS-123](#q-bas-123--the-fill-reads-the-main-installation-at-its-own-speed-and-no-client-holds-a-slot-or-a-waiter)):
  an artifact fill reads its body at the main installation's speed; the body of a pass-through is cut when the client takes a chunk
  slower than 10 s or, after a grace period of 30 s, averages less than 64 KiB per second. A write probe takes the class of the
  caller (a caller that presented a credential takes an authenticated slot, so `anonymous_share: 0` does not refuse its write
  with `503`).
- **Collapsing.** Concurrent misses for one cache key share one fetch per replica (single-flight), and with Valkey one fetch
  across replicas with the bucket backend, under a fetch lock of R-ARCH-033's form (`quader-bastion:<prefix>:flight:<sha256 of
  the cache key>`, 30 s, extended by the holder). A waiter is served from the result only when its own answer allows it
  (R-BAS-022, R-BAS-023); otherwise it makes its own conditional request. Collapsing never shares a decision. The flight ends
  when the fill is committed, not when the leader's client has taken the bytes, and a waiter that has waited 30 s answers `503
  busy` with `Retry-After: 1` and makes no request of its own. A waiter of an artifact fill does not wait: it follows the spool
  on its own permission, and across replicas it waits while the holder extends the lock, up to `bastion.cache.fill_wait_max`
  (R-BAS-054, [Q-BAS-172](#q-bas-172--a-ranged-miss-streams-from-the-spool-and-a-caller-of-a-running-fill-follows-it-on-its-own-permission);
  *superseded in place on 2026-11-22 for artifact fills*; a document fill is followed on a `full` shape only,
  [Q-BAS-200](#q-bas-200--a-caller-follows-a-running-document-fill-only-on-a-full-shape)). A result that depends on the caller's rights (a private
  document, a refusal) keeps collapsing off for that caller only ([Q-BAS-125](#q-bas-125--a-result-that-depends-on-the-callers-rights-switches-collapsing-off-for-that-caller-only)).
- `bastion.replicas` is rendered by the chart: `replicaCount`, or `autoscaling.maxReplicas` with autoscaling, so the sum over
  replicas never exceeds the configured budget ([Q-BAS-34](#q-bas-34--without-valkey-budgets-divide-by-the-charts-replica-count)).

```json
"slots": {"maxConcurrent": 64, "anonymousShare": 0.25, "queueTimeoutMillis": 5000}
```

*(default, the configuration's member `limits.slots` of R-BAS-093; `bastion.replicas`, the divisor, stays in the chart: `replicaCount`, or
`autoscaling.maxReplicas`)*

Acceptance criteria:

- With `maxConcurrent: 8`, two replicas and a main installation that delays every answer by 2 s, 500 concurrent cold requests
  never show more than 8 in-flight requests at the main installation, and anonymous ones never more than 2.
- 50 concurrent cold requests for one tarball cause one request to the main installation per replica, and one with Valkey and
  the bucket backend.
- Three connections that take a cold tarball one socket buffer at a time hold no slot: an unrelated anonymous request is
  served at once, and a second caller of the same cold key is served from the committed entry
  (`TestR_BAS_025_ClientsThatReadSlowlyDoNotHoldTheBudgetSlots`, `TestR_BAS_025_AWaiterOfACollapsedFetchIsNotHeldByTheLeadersClient`).

### R-BAS-026 · Applying the revocation feed
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The Bastion follows the revocation feed every few seconds, so a revoked token or a narrowed right is dropped within seconds
(owner, Q-BAS-8). *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7, R-BAS-112):* the link hands every entry it applied, and after a reset one entry of the
kind `grants`, to the public catalogue of the web interface, which reads the public set and the change list at once and again after the
builder's debounce; an entry of the kind `catalogue` changes no answer.

- Every replica polls `feed` every `bastion.feed.poll_interval` and applies each new entry by its ID: it records the entry with
  its receipt time, which makes every matching answer unusable (R-BAS-020 rule 3), and deletes the matching answers from memory
  and, best effort, from Valkey. `settings` triggers a handshake. A page is recorded as a whole and then the answers it matches are deleted in one pass
  ([Q-BAS-126](#q-bas-126--the-link-applies-a-page-as-a-unit-ends-the-start-read-at-the-end-of-the-feed-and-bounds-each-call)). Entries are kept for
  `answers.period + grace_period + 15 s`. The ID of an applied entry is kept for as long as the feed may send the entry again,
  so that an entry the feed sends again is not applied again: the lookback of R-BAS-015 is measured behind the cursor, which
  stands still while no entry is committed, so a quiet feed sends the same entries on every read. An ID goes when a read from a
  cursor later than its entry no longer returns it (on any page: the limit cuts only the entries after the cursor); the window only moves forward with the cursor, which therefore never moves
  backwards ([Q-BAS-152](#q-bas-152--the-id-of-an-applied-entry-is-kept-until-a-read-behind-which-it-lies-no-longer-returns-it)).
- **Start.** A starting replica reads the feed from `t:<now − answers.period − answers.grace_period − 15 s>` before it uses any
  answer from Valkey; that time is the start of its feed history (rule 4). Until the first read succeeds it uses no shared answer. A read that returns no entry moves a synthetic cursor forward to
  the time of the request, so the next read is cheap and the main installation's lookback covers late commits
  ([Q-BAS-76](#q-bas-76--the-synthetic-feed-cursor-moves-to-the-send-time-of-an-empty-read)). The history starts, and the
  unreachable state of a start ends, when the start read returns a page that says `more: false`; a first page that says
  more is not that read.
- **Reset.** On `reset: true` the replica drops every answer it holds and ignores every answer in Valkey obtained before the
  reset (rule 4 with the reset time as the history start).
- **Bound.** While the main installation is reachable, a narrowing committed at the main installation is in force at every
  Bastion replica within `poll_interval` plus one feed round trip (3 s with the defaults). While it is not, the grace period of
  R-BAS-027 applies (H-383).
- `quader_bastion_feed_lag_seconds` is the age of the last successful poll; `quader_bastion_feed_entries_applied_total{kind}` and
  `quader_bastion_feed_resets_total` count.

```yaml
bastion:
  feed:
    poll_interval: 2s                   # default (proposed); 1s to 10s
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A loop of `npm view` with `$FULL` through each of two replicas: after the token is revoked at the main installation, both
  replicas refuse it within 5 s, with and without Valkey, over 100 trials.
- Removing `acme-full` from the group that holds its grant refuses its next tarball request within 5 s although the tarball is
  cached and its `full` answer was minutes old.
- A replica started after the revocation does not accept the revoked token's answer stored in Valkey.
- The 5 s of a page of 1,000 entries against 200,000 answers is a target of the reference environment: `make test-performance` enforces it with `QUADER_PERF_GATE=1`; per change the test bounds the page by 100 times one matching pass over the same answers ([Q-BAS-140](#q-bas-140--where-the-5-s-of-a-burst-page-is-enforced)).

### R-BAS-027 · The main installation unreachable: grace period, then nothing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Answers the Bastion already holds stay valid for a configurable grace period beyond their normal period (owner,
[Q-BAS-9](#q-bas-9--the-main-installation-unreachable-grace-period-503-for-unseen-tokens-then-nothing)). *Revised on 2026-11-26 by the
owner's W-35 B.2b (R-BAS-111, built by W-35's P7):* the web interface has no grace period: its public catalogue is served whatever the
age of its last confirmation, which the pages show; the package answers below keep theirs.

- **Unreachable** ([Q-BAS-44](#q-bas-44--unreachable-means-a-failed-handshake-or-a-stale-feed)) is a state of each replica: it
  begins when the handshake fails (connect or TLS error, timeout, `5xx`, `401 bastion_token_invalid`, `400
  bastion_interface_mismatch`, a base URL mismatch) or when no feed poll has succeeded for `bastion.main.unreachable_after`, and
  ends when a handshake and a feed poll succeed again. Forward errors alone do not begin it (a `401 bastion_token_invalid` to a forward is a forward error, Q-BAS-121), and neither does one failed feed
  poll. A disable is no unreachable state: the disabled Bastion keeps its handshake and its feed and stops by its configuration
  (R-BAS-133). Every call of the link ends after `unreachable_after`, so a connection that swallows the request is a failed call at that time
  and not at `response_header_timeout`. A replica starts unreachable, since its start; the first poll that succeeds after a failed one is followed by a
  handshake; a `401 bastion_token_invalid` or a mismatch in the answer to any request begins the state at once
  ([Q-BAS-79](#q-bas-79--the-link-is-one-state-machine-per-replica-run-by-the-server)).
- While unreachable, the replica sends nothing to the main installation except handshake and feed probes every
  `poll_interval`, and:
  - a caller whose answers allow a cached entry (R-BAS-022, R-BAS-023, with rule 1 extended by `grace_period`) gets cached
    artifacts and shared documents, also past their revalidation periods (possibly stale metadata), and its own private copies; an
    entry that a `content` entry of the feed (which the link still reads while it can) names, received after `validatedAt − 15 s`,
    is not served: the grace period extends an answer, never past a withdrawal (Q-BAS-122);
  - a token the Bastion has not seen, and a miss, get `503 unavailable` with `Retry-After: 30`;
  - after the grace period of every answer has passed, at the latest `answers.period + grace_period` after unreachability began,
    the replica serves nothing: every read answers `503`.
- Download events are buffered (R-BAS-039). `quader_bastion_main_reachable` is 0 and
  `quader_bastion_main_unreachable_since_timestamp_seconds` holds the start.

```yaml
bastion:
  main:
    unreachable_after: 10s              # default (proposed); at least 3 × feed.poll_interval
```

Acceptance criteria:

- NetworkPolicy cuts the Bastion off from the main installation: within 10 s `quader_bastion_main_reachable` is 0; `$FULL`, seen
  2 minutes before, completes a warm `npm ci` and `dotnet restore`; a token never seen gets `503`; a cold package gets `503`;
  20 minutes after the cut (`period` 5m + `grace_period` 15m) every request answers `503`.
- After the policy is removed, the replica returns to `reachable` within `poll_interval` plus one handshake, and buffered
  download events arrive at the main installation.

### R-BAS-028 · Interface version mismatch at the Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- A `400 bastion_interface_mismatch`, or an answer whose `Quader-Bastion-Interface` differs from the Bastion's, makes the replica
  unreachable (R-BAS-027) and sets `quader_bastion_interface_mismatch 1`, `quader_bastion_interface_version{side="bastion"}` and
  `{side="main"}` to the two versions; the log names both and the release of the main installation if the handshake gave it.
- The PrometheusRule of the Bastion's chart fires `QuaderBastionInterfaceMismatch` (R-BAS-041). The mismatch clears when a
  handshake with equal versions succeeds, after either side was upgraded.

Acceptance criteria:

- The e2e suite upgrades the main installation to a build with `InterfaceVersion + 1`: the alert fires in the cluster's
  Prometheus within 2 minutes, the Bastion serves warm content for the grace period, and after the Bastion is upgraded the alert
  resolves and cold requests succeed.

### R-BAS-029 · Responses of the Bastion's own
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 ([Q-BAS-321](#q-bas-321--the-bastions-own-codes-are-named-by-their-status-its-texts-name-no-party-and-its-problem-type-is-aboutblank), R-BAS-095, R-BAS-099):* the codes `bastion_not_served`,
`main_unreachable`, `main_failed`, `main_timeout` and `bastion_busy` became `not_found`, `unavailable`, `bad_gateway`, `gateway_timeout`
and `busy`; `403 read_only` joins the table for a write; the texts are Q-BAS-321's and name no party; every answer of the
Bastion's own takes the error shape the format declares (`errorShape`), and where that is `problem`, problem details whose `type` is
`about:blank`; the package families answer a write `403`, and `405` stays for a path that serves `GET` and `HEAD` only. *Built by E16:*
the texts of Q-BAS-321 and the type `about:blank` with the status phrase as the title, on every problem of the client listener, the
chain's own refusals included (`errs.WithBastionAnswer`); the RateLimit policy names `requests`, `misses`, `failed-auth` and `blocking`
(R-BAS-099 rows 2 to 4). *Built by E7 (interface version 8):* the codes of the table below. *Built by E15:* every answer of the
table in the shape the format table's `errorShape` declares, through one renderer ([Q-BAS-450](#q-bas-450--every-answer-of-the-bastions-own-goes-through-one-renderer-by-the-declared-shape-and-each-shape-carries-the-code)),
with `403 read_only` for a write; before the first handshake the shapes of the format table stored with the configuration (R-BAS-093), and problem details only for a replica that has none (H-2359, closed). Where the
text below says problem details, it is the shape `problem`. *Completed by W-35's P8 on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-114):* the table of what a
forward relays below, each of its rows built.

The Bastion produces only these answers itself; every other body comes from the main installation
([Q-BAS-39](#q-bas-39--the-bastions-own-refusals-are-problem-details)). They are problem details (RFC 9457,
`application/problem+json`, R-ARCH-023's members) with the challenge of R-AUTH-002 for the path family on a `401`, and
`Cache-Control: no-store`:

| Status | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | `invalid_token`, `credentials_required` | a malformed or refused credential (R-BAS-019), a kept `invalid` answer, no anonymous reads at the main installation |
| `404`, `403`, `401` | the code of the kept refusal | a read-shape answer `none` (R-BAS-022) |
| `404` | `not_found` | a path outside the mirrored families (R-BAS-018) |
| `405`, `413`, `421` | `method_not_allowed`, `payload_too_large`, `misdirected_request` | R-BAS-014, R-BAS-018; `405` also for every method but `GET` and `HEAD` at an address of the web interface (R-BAS-116) |
| `503` | `not_ready` | an address of the web interface while the replica holds no catalogue to show, with `Retry-After: 30` (R-BAS-117) |
| `429` | `rate_limited`, `auth_timeout`, `address_blocked` | R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037, with `Retry-After` and the `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` fields of R-API-016 |
| `502`, `503`, `504` | `bad_gateway`, `unavailable`, `busy`, `gateway_timeout` | R-BAS-021, R-BAS-025, R-BAS-027 |
| `503` | `unavailable` with `Retry-After: 300`, capped by the format | every request while the replica applies a disable of its registration, and a forward or a check the main installation answered `503 bastion_disabled` (R-BAS-133); a page of the web interface is the page "Not available" (R-BAS-123) |

- Package clients act on the status and the challenge; the body is Quader's, not the format's. The difference is functional
  and shows only in the client's message.
- **Below `/v2/`** every answer of the Bastion's own carries `Docker-Distribution-API-Version: registry/2.0` and the distribution's
  error body `{"errors":[{"code":…,"message":…,"detail":{"code":"<the code above>"}}]}` instead of problem details, as every error
  below `/v2/` has at the main installation (R-OCI-003): `401` is `UNAUTHORIZED` with the registry's challenge, `404` is
  `NAME_UNKNOWN`, `405` and `421` are `UNSUPPORTED`, `413` is `SIZE_INVALID`, `429` is `TOOMANYREQUESTS`, `502`, `503` and `504` are
  `UNAVAILABLE` ([Q-BAS-169](#q-bas-169--the-bastions-own-answers-below-v2-are-in-the-distributions-error-shape)).
- **A format's refusal status.** For a format whose facts name another status for a rate limit (`rateLimitedStatus` of the
  handshake, R-BAS-057; the ClamAV definitions: `503`), the Bastion's own `429` answers of that format's family are given that
  status with the same `Retry-After` and problem body (R-BAS-056).
- **The wait of a `429`** (R-BAS-091). The wait of a refusal of R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037 is rounded up once, to whole seconds below two
  minutes and to whole minutes from there, as the main installation's refusals are ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md)
  Q-LIM-291). The `detail` (the `message` below `/v2/`) names that wait in words ("Too many requests from this address. Try again in 15
  minutes."); `Retry-After` and the `RateLimit` field's `t` carry it, but at most the longest wait the format of the request tells its
  clients (`retryAfterMaxSeconds` of the handshake's format table, R-BAS-057): NuGet and Ansible Galaxy 30 s, every other format the
  whole wait. Every other `Retry-After` of the Bastion's own (`unavailable` 30 s, `busy` 1 s) is held to the same cap.

**What a forward relays** (W-35's P8, built on 2026-11-26, [R-BAS-114](#r-bas-114--a-forwards-problems-name-nothing-of-the-main-installation)).
Every other body comes from the main installation, which renders the problems of a recognized forward for a caller of a Bastion
(`errs.ProblemFor`, [Q-BAS-385](#q-bas-385--a-forwards-text-is-chosen-at-rendering-from-what-the-error-carries)). The texts and codes a
format's handler or the core writes on the routes a Bastion forwards (`GET`, `HEAD` and the declared read routes with a body), read in the
code on 2026-11-26 per format (npm, NuGet, OCI and Helm, Debian, Ansible Galaxy, the raw files of `/files/`, the ClamAV definitions); the
rows that named something of the main installation and what a forward reads since, each with its unit test:

| # | Where (formats) | Code (status) | What the installation's own callers read | What a caller of a Bastion reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A remote's delivery rules ([refusal.go](../../internal/remotecuration/rules/refusal.go); npm, NuGet, OCI and Helm, Ansible Galaxy, `/files/` of a remote) | `not_allowed_in_repository` (403) | "left-pad 1.3.0 is not allowed in web/npm-remote: … Ask for it at https://…/ui/projects/web/repositories/npm-remote/upstream?name=left-pad.": the remote that holds the rules, through a virtual repository a member the caller did not address, and a page of the web interface | "left-pad 1.3.0 is not allowed in this repository: this repository delivers only what is allowed." (`TestR_BAS_114_ADeliveryRefusalThroughABastionNamesNoMemberAndNoPage`) |
