| 2 | The vulnerability block ([enforce.go](../../internal/vuln/enforce/enforce.go); every format whose downloads it judges) | `vulnerability_blocked`, `vulnerability_data_missing` (403) | the sentence and "Details: <`server.base_url`>/ui/vulnerabilities/findings/<id>"; the members `advisory` and `findingId` | the sentence without the link; `advisory` stays, `findingId` is left out (`TestR_BAS_114_ABlockThroughABastionNamesNoPageAndNoFindingOfTheInstallation`) |
| 3 | The signature gate ([gate.go](../../internal/signatures/gate/gate.go)) | `signature_not_verified` (403) | the sentence and "Details: <`server.base_url`>/ui/projects/…/files/…" | the sentence without the link; `reason` and `sha256` stay (`TestR_BAS_114_ASignatureRefusalThroughABastionNamesNoPageOfTheInstallation`) |
| 4 | The malware gate ([gate.go](../../internal/malware/gate/gate.go)) | `malware_found` (403; 404 on the ClamAV definitions) | the finding and "An instance auditor can release it on the page Malware under Security audit." | the finding alone (`TestR_BAS_114_AMalwareRefusalThroughABastionNamesNoPageOfTheInstallation`) |
| 5 | A virtual repository whose member of the project upstream is not switched on ([placeholder.go](../../internal/repository/placeholder.go); the engine's walk of npm, Debian and Ansible Galaxy, and the walks of their own of NuGet and OCI through `formats.VirtualPlan.Unknown`) | `not_found` and each format's own not-found code (404) | "upstream/npmjs is a member of this virtual repository, but an administrator of Quader has not switched it on." | "The resource does not exist.", or the format's own not-found sentence (`TestR_BAS_114_APlaceholderThroughABastionIsTheOneNotFound`, `TestR_BAS_114_AFormatsOwnWalkThroughABastionReadsItsOwnNotFound`) |
| 6 | npm's audit through a virtual repository ([handlers_audit.go](../../internal/formats/npm/handlers_audit.go)) | `npm_too_large` (413) | "The audit body exceeds what web/npm-remote accepts: …", the member that forwards | "… what this repository accepts: …" (`TestR_BAS_114_AnAuditBodyTooLargeThroughABastionNamesNoMember`) |
| 7 | Every status of 500 or more that is no rate limit, in every format: "The files service is not available on this replica." (`/files/`), "The authorization state of this replica could not be confirmed; retry." (`authz_stale`), "The stored archives cannot be read on this replica." (Ansible Galaxy), Debian's `deb_upstream_signature_invalid` with field errors that name a key's fingerprint, npm's `npm_audit_unavailable` (501) naming the repository, a database's or an object store's failure | the code of each (500 to 504) | the text as written, and its field errors | the neutral text of the status, without field errors ([Q-BAS-386](#q-bas-386--every-5xx-of-a-forward-reads-the-neutral-text-of-its-status-unless-its-error-vouches-for-its-own)): 501 "This operation is not served at this address.", 502, 503 and 504 the texts of the Bastion's own (Q-BAS-321), 500 and any other "The server failed to process the request."; a failure of the remote engine keeps "The package could not be fetched right now." (R-BAS-099 row 15). `malware_check_pending` and `signature_check_pending` (503) name only the artifact the caller asked for and stay, and so does the ClamAV definitions' 503 of a rate limit (`TestR_BAS_114_AForwardReadsATextOfTheInstallationOnlyWhereTheErrorVouchesForIt`, `TestR_BAS_114_ALimitRefusalOfTheDefinitionsThroughABastionKeepsItsWait`) |

Read and left as they are, since they name only what the caller addressed or sent: the decision point's `403` ("The action read is not
permitted on <the coordinate the caller sent>") and its one `404`; every format's not-found and invalid-request sentences, which name the
package, version or path asked for; `malware_not_checked` (the path, the addressed repository and the verdict's code); the refusals of
the download limits (R-BAS-099 row 7: the figure, the limit and the wait, and for an upstream limit the ceiling's class of callers); the
token service's `invalid_request` "This token service serves <host>", whose host is the response base URL's, the Bastion's; Debian's
`deb_members_unreadable`; the extension `repositoryClass` of a `405`, which only a write reaches and a Bastion refuses before. A registry
token a forward relays is R-BAS-115's. Not a text and left open: an Ansible Galaxy role served through a virtual repository carries the
member's key in its ID (H-2322). Headers other than those R-BAS-099 row 5 allows never reach a caller, so NuGet's `X-NuGet-Warning`, which
repeats the text of rows 1 to 4, is dropped as well.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each row has a table test case; `npm` and `dotnet restore` report the status of each, and a `401` makes both send their
  configured credentials (R-AUTH-002).
- A blocked address, a refused request and a failed-authentication timeout of 15 minutes answer on a NuGet and an Ansible Galaxy path
  `Retry-After: 30` and `t=30`, on an npm and an OCI path `900`, and name "15 minutes" in the detail on all four
  (`TestR_BAS_058_TheBastionsOwnRefusalsKeepTheFormatsLongestWait`, unit, milliseconds).

## The cache

### R-BAS-030 · Cache backends
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The cache holds a small part of the artifacts, never the main installation's object store, which the Bastion cannot read
(owner, [Q-BAS-10](#q-bas-10--the-cache-an-own-bucket-or-a-local-volume-never-the-main-installations-object-store)). *Lifted in part
by the owner on 2026-11-22 (decision 12 (b)): a fill may read one blob of the main installation's store by a link handed for it
(R-BAS-070); the cache itself is unchanged.* *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7, R-BAS-110):* the public catalogue of the web interface
is a tree of its own beside the layout below, `catalogue/documents/<h0h1>/<h2h3>/<64 hex>` and `catalogue/state.json` (with a cache key
`bc-<id>/g/…` and `bc-<id>/c/catalogue`). The chart chooses the backend (`bastion.cache.backend`):

- **`bucket`**: an S3 bucket of the Bastion's own, shared by every replica (credentials from `secrets.cacheBucket` or workload
  identity; a bucket of the guided-traffic stackit-s3-provisioner, or SeaweedFS in the local profile). Layout below `prefix`:
  `sha256/<h0h1>/<h2h3>/<64 hex>` (the bytes of artifacts, INV-4's form), `documents/<h0h1>/<h2h3>/<64 hex>` (the bytes of shared
  documents, [Q-BAS-87](#q-bas-87--the-bytes-of-documents-have-a-tree-of-their-own)), `entries/<k0k1>/<sha256 of the cache key>.json` (signed entries),
  `access/<64 hex>` (empty access markers, R-BAS-031), `audit-spool/<replica>/<unix ms>.jsonl` (R-BAS-039). Only `PutObject`,
  `GetObject`, `HeadObject`, `ListObjectsV2` and `DeleteObject` are used; no versioning, no conditional write.
- **`volume`**: a local volume per replica, the same layout below `bastion.cache.volume.dir`; generic ephemeral
  (`ReadWriteOnce`, deleted with the pod, the default) or persistent per pod (a StatefulSet with a claim template). No volume is
  shared (INV-13). Without routing by path (R-BAS-033) each replica fills its own copy.
- With `secrets.cacheKey` both backends keep R-BAS-061's layout below the tree of the key's identifier instead, every object encrypted or
  sealed, and the volume backend spools its fills on the pod's temporary volume.
- A fill is spooled to the pod's temporary volume (`tmp`, bucket backend) or to a temporary directory of the cache volume, and
  is written or renamed to its content address only after verification (R-BAS-021). The fills in progress of a replica hold
  together at most `bastion.cache.spool_max_bytes`; a write that would pass it makes that fill unkept (the answer is passed
  through, `quader_bastion_cache_errors_total{op="spool"}`) and gives its bytes back at once. The chart sizes the `tmp` volume from
  the spool and refuses a volume the spool does not fit
  ([Q-BAS-131](#q-bas-131--the-bytes-of-the-fills-in-progress-are-bounded-and-the-chart-sizes-the-volumes-from-the-bound),
  [H-450](#h-450--a-fill-that-does-not-fit-the-spool-is-passed-through-unkept-and-a-request-answered-from-the-spool-fails)).
- The bucket's client fails fast: three attempts and at most 2 s of backoff, not the object store's five attempts and 20 s, so a
  failing bucket is a miss within seconds ([Q-BAS-89](#q-bas-89--the-bucket-backend-reaches-s3-through-a-plain-adapter-and-fails-fast)).
- The backend is gated at the first readiness only (R-STOR-035's pattern); a failing backend afterwards turns hits into misses
  that are passed through, counted in `quader_bastion_cache_errors_total{op}`, never into failed requests.

```yaml
bastion:
  cache:
    backend: volume                     # default (proposed): volume | bucket
    max_bytes: 20GiB                    # default (proposed)
    max_object_bytes: 2GiB              # default (proposed); larger answers are passed through
    spool_max_bytes: 2GiB               # default (proposed); the fills in progress of a replica together; at least max_object_bytes
    volume:
      dir: /var/cache/quader-bastion     # chart-managed
    bucket:
      endpoint: ""                      # example: https://object.storage.eu01.onstackit.cloud
      region: ""                        # example: eu01
      bucket: ""                        # required with backend bucket; example: quader-bastion-partners
      prefix: quader-bastion             # default (proposed)
      force_path_style: false           # default (proposed)
      credentials:
        source: static                  # default (proposed): static | webIdentity | default
        role_arn: ""                    # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With `backend: bucket` and two replicas, a tarball fetched through replica A is served by replica B from the bucket without a
  request to the main installation (with a usable answer on B).
- With `backend: volume`, killing a pod with an ephemeral volume loses its cache and nothing else; a persistent volume keeps it
  across a rollout.
- The bucket's access log of the e2e run shows only the five operations above.

### R-BAS-031 · Size, eviction by last access and sweeps
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-333](#q-bas-333--what-was-served-twice-is-protected-in-the-cache)
([R-BAS-098](#r-bas-098--the-cache-protects-what-was-served-twice), built 2026-11-26):* a fill writes no access marker, so an entry
with one was served twice and is protected; the sweep evicts unprotected entries first, then protected ones, with at most 80 % of an area
protected. *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7, R-BAS-110):* the public catalogue's documents have a reserved share of their own,
`bastion.gui.max_bytes` (4 GiB): artifacts are limited to `max_bytes − documents_max_bytes − gui.max_bytes`, which must hold one object of
`max_object_bytes` (the role refuses to start and the chart to render otherwise, naming the four keys); no sweep of the areas lists or
evicts a document of the catalogue.

- **Size.** Bytes plus documents stay below `bastion.cache.max_bytes`; documents below `documents_max_bytes`, which is their reserved
  share: artifacts are limited to `max_bytes − documents_max_bytes` ([Q-BAS-88](#q-bas-88--documents-have-a-reserved-share-and-entries-are-removed-when-read)), and that room
  holds at least one object of `max_object_bytes`: a configuration whose artifacts' room is smaller does not start, and the chart refuses to
  render it, each with a message that names the three keys and what to change (a cache of 2 GiB with the default 2 GiB of documents would refuse every fill for lack of room,
  measured 2026-11-26). A sweep runs every
  `bastion.cache.sweep_interval`, and at once when an area passes 95 % of its limit between two of them; above 95 % of a limit it deletes
  what was served once in order of last access, then what was served twice (R-BAS-098), until 85 % remain
  ([Q-BAS-43](#q-bas-43--the-bucket-backend-evicts-by-listing-access-markers)). No commit takes an
  area past its limit between the sweeps: [R-BAS-089](#r-bas-089--the-cache-stays-below-its-size-between-sweeps).
- **Last access.** An entry served from the cache writes its access marker (an empty object or file named by its content address)
  at most once per `bastion.cache.access_resolution` per replica; a fill writes none, its object's own time is its access. The sweep
  orders by the markers' modification times,
  read with two listings, and deletes the bytes, the entries that point at them and the markers. An entry whose bytes are gone is
  a miss and is removed when it is read; the sweep itself does not read entries (Q-BAS-88, H-452).
- **Who sweeps.** With the volume backend every replica sweeps its own volume. With the bucket backend and Valkey one replica
  sweeps, under a lease in Valkey (`quader-bastion:<prefix>:sweep`, 2 × `sweep_interval`); without Valkey every replica sweeps at
  a randomized interval around `sweep_interval`, which is safe because a sweep only deletes, and may evict more than needed.
- `quader_bastion_cache_bytes{area="artifacts|documents"}`, `quader_bastion_cache_capacity_bytes`,
  `quader_bastion_cache_evictions_total{reason="size|stale|missing"}`.

```yaml
bastion:
  cache:
    sweep_interval: 5m                  # default (proposed)
    access_resolution: 1h               # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- A configuration whose `max_bytes` less `documents_max_bytes` is below `max_object_bytes` (`max_bytes: 2GiB` with the defaults) stops the
  role at start naming the three keys; room of exactly one largest object starts
  (`TestR_BAS_031_ACacheWithoutRoomForOneLargestObjectIsRefused`, unit); the chart refuses the same values
  (`TestR_BAS_030_TheSpoolFitsTheTemporaryVolume`, chart).
- With `max_bytes: 100MiB`, 300 MiB of tarballs in the bucket (written past the room R-BAS-089 admits, as a lowered `max_bytes` or
  replicas between their listings leave it) and the first 20 MiB read again: the next sweep leaves those 20 MiB cached and the total below
  100 MiB.
- Two replicas sweeping the same bucket without Valkey never delete an entry that was accessed within `access_resolution`
  while the total is below 85 %.

### R-BAS-089 · The cache stays below its size between sweeps
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The planner's finding of W-34 (2026-11-26), reproduced in a unit test on the code before the change: the sweep of R-BAS-031 ran only on its
timer, every `sweep_interval` (5 minutes by default), and nothing looked at the size when a fill was committed. Between two sweeps the cache
grew past `max_bytes` as fast as fills arrived: 32 fills of 64 KiB into an artifact area of 896 KiB held 960 KiB after the fifteenth commit
and 2 MiB after the last. On the volume backend the volume then fills; fills fail to write, and an `emptyDir` over its `sizeLimit` gets the
pod evicted with its cache. The owner's case of 2026-11-26 is an attacker who loads a Bastion with many distinct artifacts until its
cache overflows; the planner derived that at 80 MB/s of fills the room left after a sweep is gone in a minute or two. Built on 2026-11-26 in
`internal/bastion/cache` ([room.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/room.go), [sweep.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sweep.go)) with the
decisions [Q-BAS-301](#q-bas-301--a-commit-is-admitted-against-a-running-estimate-of-its-area-and-a-fill-without-room-is-passed-through-unkept)
to [Q-BAS-305](#q-bas-305--the-spool-of-fills-does-not-count-in-the-areas)
([ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted)).

- **A running estimate per area.** Each replica keeps an estimate of the bytes of each area, artifacts and documents, in the bytes the store
  holds (with a cache key the objects of the stored format of R-BAS-061, record and tags included, as a listing counts them). Every listing
  of the areas sets it (a sweep lists before and after it evicts, and a replica lists once at start); every commit of the replica adds to it.
  Between listings it never decreases, so it errs high, never low, for what the replica writes itself (Q-BAS-301).
- **A commit is admitted when it keeps its area at or below its limit** (`max_bytes − documents_max_bytes` for artifacts,
  `documents_max_bytes` for documents, [Q-BAS-88](#q-bas-88--documents-have-a-reserved-share-and-entries-are-removed-when-read)), or when the
  store holds its content address already, which costs no room. A fill without room is not kept: its callers are answered from its spool
  as after a refused write of the backend (R-BAS-030), the next request for it is a miss, `quader_bastion_cache_no_room_total{area}` counts it
  and a sweep is started. Nothing of it reaches the area, so a cache volume holds at most `max_bytes`, the spool of the fills in progress
  ([Q-BAS-305](#q-bas-305--the-spool-of-fills-does-not-count-in-the-areas)) and the entries and markers
  ([H-452](#h-452--the-entries-of-evicted-bytes-stay-until-they-are-read-and-are-not-counted-in-the-cache-size)); the chart already refuses a
  `cacheVolume.size` below `max_bytes` plus the spool (Q-BAS-131).
- **A sweep at once.** The commit that takes an area over 95 % of its limit (R-BAS-031's high mark), a fill whose announced length would,
  a commit without room, and a listing at start that finds an area above the mark each ask for a sweep, which evicts down to 85 % as
  R-BAS-031 says, under the sweep lease where one is used. A replica runs its sweeps one at a time: a request while one runs or waits is one
  more sweep after it, never one per commit, and a sweep the size asked for starts at least a second after the last one ended
  ([Q-BAS-303](#q-bas-303--at-once-is-one-sweep-at-a-time-asked-for-by-any-number-of-commits-at-most-one-a-second);
  [Q-BAS-304](#q-bas-304--the-marks-are-r-bas-031s-a-sweep-at-95--a-refusal-only-at-the-limit)).
  `quader_bastion_cache_sweeps_total{trigger}` counts the sweeps a replica ran: `interval` (the timer) and `size`.
- **The first commit.** The first commit of a replica waits for the listing at start, or makes it, so that a cache that holds bytes from
  before the start is not taken for an empty one. A listing that fails leaves the estimate unset and the commit admitted: a backend that
  cannot list is failing, and its writes are counted errors (R-BAS-030); the next commit lists again.
- **The volume backend** belongs to one replica, whose estimate holds every write to its area: the area stays at or below its limit at every
  moment.
- **Replicas sharing a bucket.** A replica learns what the other replicas wrote and evicted only from its own listings. Between them it counts
  each of its commits `bastion.replicas` times, as if every replica filled as much as it does
  ([Q-BAS-302](#q-bas-302--a-replica-on-a-shared-bucket-counts-each-of-its-commits-once-per-replica)). With Valkey only the holder of the
  sweep lease sweeps; another replica lists, deleting nothing, at a sweep's turn when it committed since its last listing. The bound is then
  an estimate, not a guarantee: [H-2270](#h-2270--a-replica-learns-another-replicas-writes-to-a-shared-bucket-only-at-its-own-listings).

What this does not change: the order of eviction (R-BAS-031, and since E11 R-BAS-098's protection of what was served twice) and what a fill
costs the transfer network. A churn of distinct artifacts is kept within the cache's size by this requirement; that it no longer evicts what
was served twice is R-BAS-098's, and what it costs the network is still
[H-2272](#h-2272--a-churn-of-distinct-artifacts-still-evicts-the-working-set-and-crosses-the-transfer-network).

Acceptance criteria (unit, `internal/bastion/cache` on a temporary volume with `max_bytes` 1 MiB and objects of 64 KiB; unit,
`internal/bastion/engine`; integration, `test/integration/bastioncache` on the stack's bucket):

- 32 fills of 64 KiB into an artifact area of 896 KiB with no sweep between: 14 kept, 18 refused with `ErrNoRoom` and counted, the area never
  above 896 KiB after any commit, one sweep asked for, no spool file left. Before the change the area held 960 KiB after the fifteenth.
- A fill without room answers its caller whole from its spool; the next request for it is a miss.
- A fill announced above the high mark and the commit that passes it each ask for a sweep; five commits without room leave one request.
- Bytes written behind the replica are found by its first commit's listing, bytes evicted behind it by its next listing; an address held
  already is admitted in a full area; documents and artifacts have their own room; with a cache key the stored bytes are counted.
- With the bucket backend and two replicas a replica keeps half the fills, lists without the lease only after it committed, and two replicas
  on the stack's bucket never hold more than the area.
- The sweeper lists at start, sweeps an area above its mark at once, and sweeps again when a commit asks, without its timer.

Built: `TestR_BAS_089_*` in [room_test.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/room_test.go) (eight tests, 0.35 s together with the race detector
off), `TestR_BAS_089_AFillWithoutRoomIsServedAndNotKept` in [engine/room_test.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/room_test.go) (0.01 s) and
`TestR_BAS_089_TwoReplicasSharingABucketKeepItBelowItsLimit` in [bastioncache](../../test/integration/bastioncache/room_test.go)
(objects of 4 KiB, 0.14 s measured). The tests of R-BAS-031 and R-BAS-061 that need a cache over its limit write it through the backend, past the
room. What each leg gains: the unit job about 0.4 s, the integration shard that holds `bastioncache` about 0.2 s, no end-to-end leg anything;
nothing grows with the number of formats.

### R-BAS-032 · Integrity of cached content
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- Artifact bytes are stored under their SHA-256 and verified while they are served, with R-STOR-013's verifying reader and its
  hold-back: a mismatch aborts the transfer, deletes the object and its entries, and counts
  `quader_bastion_cache_corrupt_total`.
- Entries (and documents' digests in them), negative entries and answers in Valkey are signed with HMAC-SHA-256 under the key of
  `secrets.signingKey`, over every field and the cache key; a record that fails its signature is ignored and deleted. A holder
  of write access to the bucket or Valkey without the key can delete records but cannot make the Bastion serve other bytes or
  accept a forged answer (H-387).
- The key is required with the bucket backend or Valkey; it is rotated by replacing the Secret, which makes every signed record
  unverifiable and costs one refill (performance only). With the volume backend and no Valkey the key may be absent: the entries are
  then stored without a signature, the bytes are verified all the same ([Q-BAS-98](#q-bas-98--the-cache-takes-no-signer-where-the-configuration-allows-no-key-and-keeps-plain-entries), H-460).

Acceptance criteria:

- Replacing a cached tarball's object in the bucket with other bytes makes the next download abort before its last 64 KiB, and
  the following one fetch from the main installation.
- An entry rewritten in the bucket to point at another content address, and an answer written into Valkey by hand, are ignored.

### R-BAS-061 · The cache encrypted in the stored format
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision 13 (a) of 2026-11-22: the Bastion's own cache is encrypted in the same format as the main installation's encrypted
connections once its chart gives it a key; off by default ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-076, R-STOR-077;
[Q-BAS-210](#q-bas-210--the-cache-key-is-one-file-in-the-bastions-chart-and-the-formats-keys-derive-from-it),
[Q-BAS-211](#q-bas-211--with-a-cache-key-every-object-of-the-cache-store-is-encrypted-or-sealed-and-named-without-a-digest)). Stage 2
of the owner's topic; built on 2026-11-22 in `internal/bastion/cache` over the format's package `internal/blob/blobcrypt`, which seals every
byte, with the builder's decisions
[Q-BAS-212](#q-bas-212--the-record-of-a-cached-object-lies-in-front-of-its-body-in-the-same-object) to
[Q-BAS-215](#q-bas-215--the-sweep-of-other-layouts-deletes-them-in-a-replicas-first-hour-and-while-it-still-finds-some). It does not change
what the Bastion may read: never the main installation's object store (Q-BAS-10) but by the handover of decision 12 (b)
(R-BAS-070), whose fills it keeps in this format like every fill.

- **The key.** `secrets.cacheKey` of the Bastion's chart (`existingSecret`, `key`, default empty) is mounted at
  `/var/run/secrets/quader/cache-key/`, beside the chart's other Secrets, and named by `bastion.cache.encryption_key_file` (managed by the
  chart): 32 random bytes, raw or base64, the key ring's file rules ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-021). Without it the cache is as
  R-BAS-030 says. From the file's key `K` derive, with `FMT` = `quader-blob-v1`: the storage key `HKDF(K, "", FMT ‖ " bastion storage")`, the
  key's identifier `bc-` followed by the hex of the first 8 bytes of `HKDF(K, "", FMT ‖ " bastion key id")` and the name key
  `HKDF(K, "", FMT ‖ " bastion names")`. The key is read at start: a file that cannot be read or holds no key of the form stops the start, with
  a message that names the path and the rule and no byte of the file. The file's bytes and `K` are cleared once the keys are derived; the
  storage key and the name key live in the replica's memory for its life. A new file is a rollout.
- **What is encrypted.** With a key, every object the Bastion writes into its cache store, bucket or volume, lies below
  `<prefix>/<key identifier>/`, and every one but the empty access markers is an object of the format of R-STOR-076 with its record
  (R-STOR-077) under a data key of its own. The record lies in front of the body, `FMT ‖ u8(len(id)) ‖ id ‖ W ‖ C` (182 bytes), because
  neither backend keeps object metadata ([Q-BAS-212](#q-bas-212--the-record-of-a-cached-object-lies-in-front-of-its-body-in-the-same-object)):
  - artifact bytes and documents under the names `a/<m0m1>/<m2m3>/<m>` and `d/<m0m1>/<m2m3>/<m>` with
    `m = HMAC-SHA-256(name key, FMT ‖ " name" ‖ area ‖ digest)` (`area` one byte, `a` or `d`);
  - entries, signed as R-BAS-032 says, as objects whose plaintext is the object's name, a line feed and the signed entry, under
    `e/<m0m1>/<m>` with `m` the keyed name of area `e` over the SHA-256 of the cache key
    ([Q-BAS-213](#q-bas-213--entries-and-the-spools-files-are-objects-of-the-format-bound-to-their-names));
  - access markers, empty, under `x/<m>` with the `m` of their object; every file of the audit spool (R-BAS-039), bound to its name like an
    entry, under `s/<replica>/<unix ms>`; and the probe of the first readiness check (R-BAS-043), bound likewise under `p/<32 hex>` and
    deleted at once.
- **Reads.** An artifact is read as [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-082 says, its content address and the size its stored size gives as the
  copy's digest and size, so that steps 1 to 6 of R-STOR-077 run before the first byte; then R-BAS-032's verification against its content
  address and hold-back. A ranged read of a cached artifact reads the record, then only the segments of its window, each authenticated
  (which narrows [H-451](#h-451--a-ranged-read-of-a-cached-artifact-is-not-verified): still not checked against the digest, but no byte that
  was not written by the Bastion). A refusal of the record, a segment or the digest, for any reason and `unknown_key` included (the tree of
  an identifier holds only what its key wrote), deletes the object and the entry that found it, as a corrupt object today; an entry or a
  file of the spool that is refused, or bound to another name, is deleted, the entry as one that fails its signature.
- **The spool of fills.** With a key the volume backend spools its fills on the pod's temporary volume, as the bucket backend does, and
  writes only the sealed object to the cache volume; the chart sizes `tmp` for it
  ([Q-BAS-214](#q-bas-214--with-a-key-the-volume-backend-spools-its-fills-on-the-pods-temporary-volume)).
- **A new key, a lost key.** A key change gives a new identifier and so an empty tree: every read is a miss until refilled (performance only).
  The sweep of R-BAS-031 deletes the trees of other identifiers and, with a key, the plain layout of a cache that ran without one; a cache
  without a key deletes every tree. It does so in each sweep of a replica's first hour after its start and in every later sweep that follows
  one that still found something, at most 10,000 objects per sweep
  ([Q-BAS-215](#q-bas-215--the-sweep-of-other-layouts-deletes-them-in-a-replicas-first-hour-and-while-it-still-finds-some)). A lost key
  costs the cache, nothing else. What a key change leaves open is [H-1325](#h-1325--a-change-of-the-cache-key-loses-the-download-events-spooled-under-the-old-layout)
  and [H-1326](#h-1326--after-a-key-change-the-old-tree-stays-readable-to-a-holder-of-the-old-key-until-the-sweep-has-deleted-it); what the
  key does not protect, [H-1327](#h-1327--a-taken-over-bastion-pod-holds-the-cache-key).
- **What stays in the clear, and why**
  ([H-1318](../security/stored-content-visibility.md#h-1318--the-bastions-cache-shows-sizes-counts-and-times-and-stays-plain-without-a-key)):
  the number and sizes of objects (which give away the plaintext sizes), their times, and the modification times of the access markers, which
  the eviction reads by listing (R-BAS-031); the key's identifier; the replica's name and the time in the name of each file of the audit
  spool; the answers in Valkey, which are signed (R-BAS-032) and short-lived and lie in Valkey, not in the cache store; and the spool of fills
  in progress on the pod's temporary volume, as the main installation's spool ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-004).

Acceptance criteria (unit, `internal/bastion/cache`, a temporary volume; chart render tests):

- With a key, after a tarball's fill no object below the cache's prefix contains a 16-byte run of the tarball and no name contains its SHA-256
  or the hash of its cache key; a second cache over the same directory serves it; a flipped bit makes the read abort and the entry go.
- With another key the first read is a miss and the next sweep removes the old tree; without a key the layout is R-BAS-030's.
- The chart mounts `secrets.cacheKey` into the Bastion's pods and sets `bastion.cache.encryption_key_file` only when `existingSecret` is set.

Built: `TestR_BAS_061_*` in [sealed_test.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sealed_test.go) (every family of the store, a changed byte, an
object of another name, family or key, a restart, another key, the key file and its known answers, ranges, the sweep, the race detector),
`TestR_BAS_061_ACacheWithAKeyOnTheBucket` in [test/integration/bastioncache](../../test/integration/bastioncache/sealed_test.go) and
`TestR_BAS_061_TheCacheKeyIsMountedAndNamedOnlyWithItsSecret` in [test/chart](../../test/chart/bastion_cachekey_test.go).

### R-BAS-033 · Routing by path for local volumes
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- With `backend: volume` and `cacheVolume.routeByPath: true`, the chart makes HAProxy Ingress choose the replica by a
  consistent hash of the request path (URI hashing of the path alone, so an HTTP/1.1 and an HTTP/2 request for one path reach
  the same replica, [Q-BAS-154](#q-bas-154--routing-by-path-hashes-the-path-alone-so-http1-and-http2-clients-meet)), so each artifact lives on one replica and the volumes together hold more
  than one could (owner, Q-BAS-11). The annotation names are R-BAS-045's; the controller has no key for consistent hashing, so
  the chart renders it as a `config-backend` snippet, which a controller that forbids snippets drops without failing (H-434).
- Routing changes nothing in correctness: a request on another replica is a miss. A replica added or drained moves about
  `1 ÷ n` of the paths.
- The chart refuses `routeByPath` with the bucket backend and without `ingress.enabled`.

Acceptance criteria:

- With three replicas and routing on, 300 distinct tarballs requested twice cause 300 requests to the main installation, not
  up to 900, and each tarball is on exactly one volume.

## Shared state

### R-BAS-034 · Optional Valkey
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Valkey is optional (owner, [Q-BAS-11](#q-bas-11--valkey-is-optional-and-without-it-budgets-are-divided-by-the-replicas)). With
it, the replicas share:

| State | Keys (prefix `quader-bastion:<valkey.key_prefix>:`) | Without Valkey |
|---|---|---|
| Block list (R-BAS-037) | `block:<address>`, TTL = remaining duration | per replica |
| Rate-limit and failed-authentication counters (R-BAS-035, R-BAS-036) | R-ARCH-034's sliding windows, limiters `bastion.<name>` | per replica, at the configured value ÷ `bastion.replicas` |
| Fetch coordination (R-BAS-025), sweep lease (R-BAS-031), the public catalogue's sync lease (R-BAS-109) | `flight:<…>`, `sweep`, `catalogue` | per replica |
| The main installation's answers (R-BAS-020; the kinds credential, shape, URL and package of R-BAS-084), negative entries (R-BAS-024) | `ans:<kind>:<sha256 of the key>`, TTL = remaining validity, signed (R-BAS-032) | per replica |

- This refines INV-3 for the Bastion: its Valkey holds positive authorization results of the main installation, by the
  owner's decision, and only in a form it cannot forge ([Q-BAS-32](#q-bas-32--answers-validate-themselves-against-the-feed-and-are-signed-in-valkey));
  the self-validation of R-BAS-020 holds whatever Valkey returns. Losing Valkey costs performance, never correctness: every
  answer is asked again per replica, blocks and counters work per replica at the divided values, and collapsing is per replica.
- Connection, Sentinel discovery, TLS and degradation follow R-ARCH-031 with the Bastion's own `valkey` section;
  `valkey.mode: none`, the default, means no Valkey. Valkey being unavailable never makes a replica unready;
  `quader_valkey_available` is 0 and `QuaderBastionValkeyUnavailable` fires (R-BAS-041). The shared metrics are
  `quader_valkey_available` and `quader_ratelimit_fallback{limiter}` (1 for a limiter that answers from its share).
- **The keys as formed** ([Q-BAS-91](#q-bas-91--the-bastions-keys-are-formed-by-the-cluster-package-without-a-keyspace-and-reuse-the-fetch-lock)):
  `quader-bastion:<valkey.key_prefix>:<mechanism>:v1:<parts>`: `block:v1:<address>`, `block:level:v1:<address>`,
  `timeout:v1:<address>`, `ans:v1:<kind>:<sha256>`, `lock:fetch:v1:<sha256>`, `sweep:v1`, `catalogue:v1`, and the counters `rl:v1:…` of R-ARCH-034.
  The table above names the families; the version segment, the encoding of an address and the reuse of the fetch lock are decided
  in Q-BAS-91.
- **Signed answers** ([Q-BAS-93](#q-bas-93--the-store-signs-and-verifies-the-answer-records)): the store signs a record on `Put` and verifies it on `Get`; a
  record that fails is not returned, is deleted (only if it still holds the failed value) and counts as `bad_signature`.
- **Memory in front of Valkey** ([Q-BAS-153](#q-bas-153--a-stale-answer-in-a-replicas-memory-does-not-hide-the-one-valkey-holds)): a
  replica looks an answer up in its memory first; a copy there that fails a rule of R-BAS-020 is dropped and the record in Valkey is
  read, so an answer another replica obtained since is used, also for the failed-authentication timeout of R-BAS-036.

Acceptance criteria:

- With Valkey, a token checked on replica A is served on replica B without a second check; stopping Valkey makes B check once
  itself, and no request fails.
- With Valkey stopped, the anonymous limit of R-BAS-035 admits at most the configured rate in total across two replicas
  (± one burst per replica).

## Abuse protection

### R-BAS-035 · Per-address rate limits
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093, R-BAS-096; the owner's [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation)):* the figures are the
registration's `limits.flood`, not chart values, applied without a restart; a third class `gui` holds the web interface's pages per address
([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-307); `exempt_cidrs` is the configuration's `exemptNetworks`; the subject's budgets
of R-BAS-096 apply on top. *Built by E9a (2026-11-26):* the guard reads its figures from the configuration a request read at its start
(`settings.Holder.For`), and the class `gui` is `guard.Page`, which no route asks before W-35's pages exist.

Blocking runs in two stages (owner, [Q-BAS-16](#q-bas-16--blocking-in-two-stages)); this is the Bastion's own stage, with
Quader's knowledge of credentials and misses:

- **Requests** per client address, in three classes: requests with a credential (`limits.flood.authenticated`), requests
  without (`limits.flood.anonymous`, stricter), and pages of the web interface (`limits.flood.gui`). Limiters of R-ARCH-034, scope
  `cluster` with Valkey; refusals answer `429 rate_limited`. A figure that changes while the replicas run replaces the limiter under its
  name ([Q-BAS-449](#q-bas-449--a-limiter-whose-figures-change-is-replaced-under-its-name)).
- **Misses** per client address: requests that need the main installation (forwards, checks, conditional requests, probes),
  `missesPerMinute` of the two classes of callers; a page is never a miss. A refused miss answers `429 rate_limited`; hits of the same
  address keep being served.
- Addresses in `limits.flood.exemptNetworks` are not limited.
- The request limits are the token bucket (without Valkey) or the sliding window (with Valkey) of R-ARCH-034; the miss limits
  are counts of the sliding minute in both forms
  ([Q-BAS-92](#q-bas-92--the-counters-are-sliding-windows-and-the-timeout-starts-at-the-last-allowed-failure)). A limit admits up
  to its rate: a refused request or miss does not consume the budget of its address, so a client slightly over its limit is
  admitted at the limit and not starved, and the refusals it collects stay far below the threshold that blocks
  ([Q-BAS-127](#q-bas-127--a-refused-request-or-miss-does-not-consume-the-limit-it-was-refused-by)). The sliding estimate is
  approximate around a window boundary ([H-474](#h-474--the-sliding-estimate-of-a-limit-admits-more-than-the-limit-in-a-minute-that-spans-a-boundary)).

```json
"flood": {
  "anonymous": {"requestsPerSecond": 50, "burst": 1000, "missesPerMinute": 1000},
  "authenticated": {"requestsPerSecond": 200, "burst": 4000, "missesPerMinute": 4000},
  "gui": {"requestsPerSecond": 20, "burst": 100}
}
```

*(default: the Internet preset's figures, usage-and-limits.md R-LIM-046, and the built-in configuration's; per address)*

The defaults are set from a measurement of real clients so that one normal command of every client passes them (R-BAS-092).

Acceptance criteria, held at small figures so that a test counts in milliseconds (anonymous 10 a second with a burst of 40,
with a credential 50 and 200, misses 300 and 30 a minute, the defaults before R-BAS-092); the rules are the same at any figures:

- 1,000 anonymous requests from one address within 10 s are admitted at most 140 times (burst 40 plus 10 per second); a second
  address is not slowed down.
- An address that requests 100 random missing names per minute anonymously sends at most 30 requests to the main installation
  per minute, while its hits are served.
- An address that asks for 330 misses a minute with a credential (limit 300) is admitted about 300 a minute from the second
  minute on, answers `rate_limited` for the rest, and is not blocked; the same holds for an anonymous client at 11 requests a
  second against 10, with and without Valkey.

### R-BAS-036 · Failed-authentication timeout
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093):* the three figures are the registration's `limits.flood.failedAuth`. *Built by E9a
(2026-11-26).*

- More than `maxFailures` failed authentications from one address within `windowSeconds` put the address into a timeout of
  `timeoutSeconds` (`limits.flood.failedAuth`). A failure is a credential the Bastion refuses itself (R-BAS-019)
  or one the main installation answered `invalid`.
- During the timeout, a request with a credential for which the Bastion has no usable answer answers `429 auth_timeout` with
  `Retry-After` and is not sent to the main installation; a credential with a usable answer keeps working, so colleagues behind
  one address are not cut off ([Q-BAS-36](#q-bas-36--a-failed-authentication-timeout-refuses-unverified-credentials-only));
  anonymous requests stay anonymous requests.
- The counter is a count-only limiter of R-ARCH-034 (`bastion.failed_auth`). Its window is 1 s to 12 h, the range of the
  limiters of R-ARCH-034
  ([Q-BAS-128](#q-bas-128--the-local-forms-evict-in-constant-time-the-block-decision-locks-per-address-and-the-window-range-is-the-limiters)); the
  wire refuses no longer one, so the Bastion counts a longer window as 12 h, and the main installation's API (E8) is where a longer one is
  to be refused. The Bastion's limit is stricter than the main
  installation's R-AUTH-038, which still applies to the real client behind it (R-BAS-017).
- The failure that brings the count of the window to `max_failures` starts the timeout, so the next credential without a usable
  answer is the first one refused (Q-BAS-92); the acceptance below is that reading.

```json
"failedAuth": {"maxFailures": 20, "windowSeconds": 600, "timeoutSeconds": 900}
```

*(default: the Internet preset's and the built-in configuration's)*

Acceptance criteria:

- 21 random well-formed tokens from one address: the 21st and every later unknown token within 15 minutes answer `429
  auth_timeout` without a request to the main installation; `$FULL`, used from that address before, keeps working.

### R-BAS-037 · Blocking of flooding addresses and the shared block list
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093):* the figures and the exempt networks are the registration's
`limits.flood.blocking` and `exemptNetworks`; in Audit at the Bastion the blocks still hold
([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-309). *Built by E9a (2026-11-26).*

- An address that collects more than `threshold` refusals of R-BAS-035 and R-BAS-036 within `windowSeconds` is blocked for
  `durationSeconds` (`limits.flood.blocking`); each further block within 24 h doubles the duration, up to `maxDurationSeconds` ([Q-BAS-37](#q-bas-37--one-refusal-threshold-blocks-an-address-with-doubling-durations)).
- Blocking is the answer to a flood and not to a client slightly over its limit: only a request or miss beyond the limit is a
  refusal and a refusal consumes nothing (Q-BAS-127), so a client at 110 % of its limit collects a tenth of its requests as
  refusals, and the default threshold of 3,000 refusals a minute is reached only by an address that sends, after its burst, at
  least twice the anonymous rate (6,000 a minute against 3,000 admitted) or 1.25 times the rate with a credential (15,000 against
  12,000); one that floods at the ingress's 1,000 a second is blocked within about four seconds
  ([Q-BAS-314](#q-bas-314--the-block-threshold-is-the-anonymous-classs-minute-3000-refusals)).
- A blocked address answers `429 address_blocked` with `Retry-After` at step 2 of R-BAS-018, before any further work, and its
  requests are not logged one by one (a counter and one log line per block).
- With Valkey the block list is shared: a block set by one replica holds on every replica at its next request. Without Valkey
  each replica blocks by its own count (H-389).
- `quader_bastion_blocks_total{reason}`, `quader_bastion_blocked_addresses`, and the log line `bastion address blocked` with the
  address, the reason, the duration and the count: the number of blocks of the address within 24 h, this one included
  (Q-BAS-92). The reason of the metric is `refusals`; the log line names the kind of refusal that crossed the threshold.

```json
"blocking": {"threshold": 3000, "windowSeconds": 60, "durationSeconds": 900, "maxDurationSeconds": 86400},
"exemptNetworks": []
```

*(default: the Internet preset's and the built-in configuration's; an exempt network is a canonical prefix, example
`"198.51.100.0/24"`)*

Acceptance criteria:

- At the defaults, in the e2e cluster: an address sending 6,000 anonymous requests at up to 900 a second is blocked on every
  replica (with Valkey) within the minute and answers `429 address_blocked` (`TestBastion_R_BAS_049_FloodingAddress`); at the
  defaults, in a unit test: an address sending 1,000 anonymous requests a second is blocked within ten seconds
  (`TestR_BAS_092_TheDefaultsHoldOneNormalCommandOfEveryClient`).
- At the small figures of R-BAS-035's criteria (threshold 300): a block lasts 15 minutes and a second flood after it yields 30
  minutes; an address that sends 3,000 anonymous misses in 30 seconds is blocked, whereas an address that sends 330 misses a
  minute with a credential is not (Q-BAS-127).

### R-BAS-038 · The coarse per-address limit at HAProxy Ingress
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093):* the Bastion's own figures leave the chart, so the chart's refusal of an
edge figure at or below the authenticated figure (the second bullet, `_validate.tpl`) goes; the Bastion reports its edge figure with every
handshake, and the card warns where a configured per-address figure lies above it ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-240);
`limit-whitelist` is rendered from the new `edgeLimit.exemptCIDRs` instead of `config.bastion.blocking.exempt_cidrs`. *Built by E9a
(2026-11-26):* the second bullet below is gone; the chart renders the edge figure into the configuration file as `bastion.edge_limit`
(`enabled`, `requests_per_second`, `connections`), and every handshake reports it in `Quader-Bastion-Edge-Limit`, `off` with
`edgeLimit.enabled: false` ([Q-BAS-447](#q-bas-447--the-edge-figure-is-a-chart-managed-section-of-the-configuration-file-and-every-handshake-reports-it)).

- The chart can put a coarser per-address limit in front, at the Bastion's HAProxy Ingress: `edgeLimit.enabled` (default on)
  renders HAProxy Ingress's per-address request-rate and connection limits for `edgeLimit.requestsPerSecond` and
  `edgeLimit.connections` on the Bastion's Ingress (owner, Q-BAS-16). It can be switched off.
- It is meant to be wider than the Bastion's own, so that the Bastion's stage, which knows credentials and misses, decides first and the
  ingress only cuts what would overload the Bastion itself; the card of the main installation warns where a flood figure of the
  registration lies above it (R-UI-240, built by E12 on 2026-11-26), since the chart no longer knows those figures.
- What the controller does with the values (verified for v0.16.3, [Q-BAS-56](#q-bas-56--haproxy-ingress-annotations-as-verified-against-the-controller-of-the-local-profile)):
  it tracks the connection's source address in a stick table and answers `429` while the address has more than
  `edgeLimit.connections` concurrent tracked streams or more than `edgeLimit.requestsPerSecond` new ones in the last second,
  except for the addresses of `limit-whitelist`. There is no burst: a client whose rate is above the per-second value is
  refused while it stays above. The address is the TCP peer's, so behind a load balancer that does not pass the client
  address on, all callers share one budget (H-432).
- **What it counts is HTTP requests, not connections** (read on 2026-11-26 for R-BAS-092,
  [Q-BAS-315](#q-bas-315--the-edge-defaults-hold-the-fastest-normal-command-1000-requests-a-second-and-256-in-flight)): the template of
  v0.16.3 tracks the address with `http-request track-sc1 src` in the backend of an HTTP Ingress, and HAProxy 2.8 (the image's base,
  `haproxy:2.8.31-alpine`) starts the counters of a tracked entry for every stream it tracks (`stream_start_counters` in
  `include/haproxy/stream.h`: `conn_cur` and `conn_rate` count one per tracking), and every request of a kept-alive connection is a
  stream of its own. So `edgeLimit.requestsPerSecond` is HTTP requests of the address in the last second, kept-alive or not, and
  `edgeLimit.connections` its requests in flight at once. HAProxy's own documentation still says "connections" for these counters;
  the code counts what is tracked. Read, not measured on a running controller (the e2e flood of R-BAS-049 refuses at the edge
  either way). One `npm ci` of 475 packages over 15 kept-alive connections is 475 counted requests in 2.5 s (about 190 a second):
  the former default of 100 refused it at the ingress.
- The defaults, 1,000 requests a second and 256 in flight, hold the fastest normal command of the measurement and two of them
  from one address (R-BAS-092).
- Volumetric attacks on bandwidth are the network provider's, not the Bastion's (H-382).

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm template` renders `edgeLimit` into the Ingress's annotations, `edgeLimit.exemptCIDRs` into `limit-whitelist` and the figure
  into `bastion.edge_limit` of the configuration file, and refuses a value under `config.bastion.edge_limit`
  (`TestR_BAS_038_TheEdgeLimitIsRenderedAndReported`).
- In the e2e cluster, 20,000 requests from one address within 10 s are partly refused by the ingress (`429` without a request
  log line at the Bastion) and the Bastion's replicas stay below their in-flight limit.

### R-BAS-092 · The built-in figures hold one normal command of every client
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision 18 for the main installation ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-59: request figures that normal use
never meets, set from a measurement of real clients), applied to the Bastion's own figures of R-BAS-035, R-BAS-037 and R-BAS-038. Found by
the planner of the owner's task W-34: one anonymous `docker pull` of an image of 40 layers is 48 requests within 0.28 s, and docker does not
retry a `429`; the burst of 40 refused it at the Bastion, and its 48 misses on a cold Bastion met the 30 misses a minute
(`TestR_BAS_092_TheDefaultsHoldOneNormalCommandOfEveryClient` on the former figures: 18 of 48 requests refused; `npm ci` of 475 packages
with a credential 175 of 475). The Bastion faces the internet and bears its traffic alone, so it keeps refusing and blocking an address that
floods ([Q-BAS-312](#q-bas-312--the-bastions-request-figures-are-the-main-installations-profiles-anonymous-and-standard) to
[Q-BAS-315](#q-bas-315--the-edge-defaults-hold-the-fastest-normal-command-1000-requests-a-second-and-256-in-flight)).

What one normal command needs (Q-LIM-59's measurement on the kind cluster, and the clients' documented concurrency):

| Command | Requests | In | At once |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docker pull`, an image of 40 layers | 48 (39 in its busiest second) | 0.28 s | 3 downloads (`max-concurrent-downloads`) |
| `podman pull`, an image of 40 layers | 44 | 0.48 s | [not verified] |
| `npm ci`, a lockfile of 475 packages | 475 | 2.5 s | up to 15 connections |
| `dotnet restore`, N packages over F feeds | about F + N × (F + 1) | seconds | unbounded on Linux (`maxHttpRequestsPerSource` is `Int32.MaxValue` there, 16 on macOS, by NuGet's documentation) |
| `apt-get update` and `install` of N packages | 10 to 15, then N | seconds | up to 10 pipelined on a connection |
| `ansible-galaxy collection install` of C collections | about 4 C | tens of seconds | one after the other |

On a cold Bastion every one of these requests is a miss as well.

| Figure | Before | Now | Why | One address, a minute, now (before) | A thousand addresses, a minute |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limits.anonymous` | 10/s, burst 40 | 50/s, burst 1,000 | the main installation's profile Anonymous: two installs of 475 packages, or ten pulls of 40 layers, at once | 4,000 in the first minute, 3,000 in each further (640, 600) | 3,000,000 (600,000) at the Bastion's own stage; hits are served from the cache, everything else is bounded by the replicas' `server.max_in_flight` (1,024 each) and the network (H-382) |
| `limits.authenticated` | 50/s, burst 200 | 200/s, burst 4,000 | the main installation's profile Standard: an install of up to 4,000 packages at once | 16,000 in the first minute, 12,000 in each further (3,200, 3,000) | as above; a credential the Bastion holds no answer for costs a check, an invalid one the failed-authentication timeout (R-BAS-036, unchanged) |
| `limits.misses.anonymous_per_minute` | 30 | 1,000 | on a cold Bastion every request is a miss: a minute holds what the anonymous burst holds at once | 1,000 requests to the main installation (30) | 1,000,000 by count (30,000), but the main installation is reached through the 16 anonymous slots of a Bastion of two replicas (R-BAS-025, unchanged): the 17th waits 2 s and is answered `503 busy`, and each forward is charged to its caller's own budget at the main installation (R-BAS-017) |
| `limits.misses.authenticated_per_minute` | 300 | 4,000 | as above, the burst with a credential | 4,000 (300) | bounded by the 64 slots of the budget (`bastion.main.max_concurrent`), as above |
| `blocking.threshold` | 300 | 3,000 | the anonymous class's minute: an address is blocked only once it was refused as many requests in a minute as the class admits in one | blocked when it sends, after its burst, 6,000 anonymous (900) or 15,000 with a credential (3,300) requests a minute; within about 4 s at 1,000 a second | each address on its own, as before; a flood spread thin enough stays below every per-address figure (H-382, H-455) |
| `edgeLimit.requestsPerSecond` | 100 | 1,000 | HAProxy Ingress counts HTTP requests also on a kept-alive connection (R-BAS-038): an `npm ci` is about 190 a second, two at once from one address about 380 | at most 60,000 reach the Bastion's own stage (6,000) | per address only, as before |
| `edgeLimit.connections` | 50 | 256 | requests in flight of one address: `npm ci`'s 15 and docker's 3 fit either; a `dotnet restore` on Linux has no bound of its own (H-2276) | 256 at once (50), a quarter of one replica's `server.max_in_flight` | per address only, as before |

- The failed-authentication timeout (20 failures in 10 minutes, then 15 minutes) and the block's durations (15 minutes, doubling to
  24 hours) are unchanged: a normal command does not fail its sign-in, and a flood is blocked as long as before.
- Without Valkey each replica holds the rate and the burst divided by `bastion.replicas` (R-ARCH-034); with two replicas an anonymous burst
  is 500 per replica, which still holds two installs of 475 packages spread over both replicas.
- What the figures leave refused: many clients with credentials behind one address beyond the burst of 4,000, twenty CI jobs of one
  address at once for example (H-2277); an exempt network of the configuration (`limits.flood.exemptNetworks`) exempts such an address.
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 by E9a (R-BAS-093):* the figures of the second table are no chart values any more but the configuration's
  `limits.flood` (the names `limits.anonymous` and so on stand for its members `anonymous`, `authenticated`, `missesPerMinute` and
  `blocking.threshold`); they are the Internet preset's and the built-in configuration's (`settings.Builtin`), and the 2 s wait of the
  third row is 5 s by default since R-BAS-096 sizes the slots for one restore (Q-BAS-448).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/guard`, milliseconds, no data): at the built-in figures, read from the built-in configuration, every
  command of the first table passes a cold Bastion from one address without a refusal of a request or a miss, two installs of 475 packages
  at once and ten pulls in a row anonymously included, and an address that sends 1,000 anonymous requests a second is blocked within ten
  seconds (`TestR_BAS_092_TheDefaultsHoldOneNormalCommandOfEveryClient`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/settings`) and the chart test (`test/chart`): the defaults of the built-in configuration and of the chart's
  edge values are the ones of the second table, and the chart renders `limit-rps: "1000"` and `limit-connections: "256"`.

## Audit, observability, lifecycle

### R-BAS-039 · Reporting downloads served from the cache
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-041

- While the handshake says `recordDownloads: true`, every artifact the Bastion serves from its cache (a hit, or a check answered
  `304`) appends an event of R-BAS-016 to a bounded in-memory buffer (`bastion.audit.buffer_events`); the buffer is sent every
  `bastion.audit.flush_interval` or at `batch_size` events. With R-BAS-059 the rule becomes: every cached answer whose fill the main
  installation counted as a download, a document included (the manifest of an OCI tag, Q-OCI-222), is reported when it is served
  from the cache, a hit, a check answered `304` or a caller that followed a fill
  ([Q-BAS-177](#q-bas-177--a-bastion-reports-a-hit-as-a-download-when-the-main-installation-counted-its-fill-as-one)); an artifact the main
  installation did not count is not reported.
- While the main installation is unreachable the buffer keeps growing up to its bound; an event that finds it full is dropped,
  counted in `quader_bastion_audit_events_dropped_total`, and reported in the next batch's `dropped`
  ([Q-BAS-45](#q-bas-45--downloads-are-buffered-in-memory-and-spooled-at-shutdown)).
- At shutdown the replica sends its buffer within the drain; what it cannot send it writes to the cache backend's
  `audit-spool/`, at most `bastion.audit.spool_max_events`, and any replica sends spooled files once the main installation is
  reachable, deleting each after a `2xx`. With a volume backend the spool survives only with a persistent volume (H-391).
- A drain writes one spool file, one batch of at most `batch_size` events per line, the unreported `dropped` count on the first
  line; `spool_max_events` bounds one drain's file. A batch the main installation refuses as a whole (`400`, `413`, `422`) is
  dropped and counted, every other failure is retried; a spool file of which some lines were delivered is replaced by one with
  the rest ([Q-BAS-78](#q-bas-78--a-refused-batch-is-dropped-everything-else-is-retried-and-a-spool-file-is-one-drain)).

```yaml
bastion:
  audit:
    buffer_events: 100000               # default (proposed), per replica
    batch_size: 500                     # default (proposed)
    flush_interval: 1s                  # default (proposed)
    spool_max_events: 1000000           # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With the main installation cut off for 2 minutes during a warm `npm ci` loop, every download appears in the main
  installation's audit after the cut ends, with its original time; with `buffer_events: 100` the excess is reported as one
  `bastion.downloads.dropped` event whose count equals the Bastion's counter.
- A drain of a replica during a main installation outage leaves its events in `audit-spool/`, and another replica delivers
  them.

### R-BAS-040 · Metrics
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The Bastion exports R-OPS-007's conventions on its ops listener, with the request metrics of R-OPS-008, and these (no label
carries an address, a token, a path or a repository's name):

| Metric | Type | Labels |
|---|---|---|
| `quader_bastion_requests_total` | counter | `class` (`artifact`, `shared`, `private`, `absent`, `pass`, `refused`), `result` (`hit`, `checked`, `miss`, `refused`, `error`) |
| `quader_bastion_bytes_served_total` | counter | `source` (`cache`, `main`) |
| `quader_bastion_main_requests_total` | counter | `kind` (`forward`, `conditional`, `check`, `feed`, `handshake`, `downloads`, `catalogue`), `outcome` |
| `quader_bastion_main_request_duration_seconds` | histogram | `kind` |
| `quader_bastion_main_in_flight`, `quader_bastion_main_budget` | gauge | `class` (`authenticated`, `anonymous`) |
| `quader_bastion_main_budget_exhausted_total` | counter | `class` |
| `quader_bastion_main_reachable`, `quader_bastion_main_unreachable_since_timestamp_seconds`, `quader_bastion_base_url_mismatch` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_interface_mismatch` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_interface_version` | gauge | `side` (`bastion`, `main`) |
| `quader_bastion_grace_period_seconds`, `quader_bastion_answer_period_seconds` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_answers` | gauge | `kind` (`credential`, `shape`, `url`, `package`) |
| `quader_bastion_answers_total` | counter | `kind`, `result` (`hit`, `miss`, `expired`, `dropped`, `bad_signature`) |
| `quader_bastion_feed_lag_seconds` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_feed_entries_applied_total` | counter | `kind` |
| `quader_bastion_feed_resets_total` | counter | — |
| `quader_bastion_token_remaining_seconds`, `quader_bastion_token_warn_before_seconds`, `quader_bastion_main_token_refused` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_token_reloads_total` | counter | `outcome` (`loaded`, `refused`) |
| `quader_bastion_cache_bytes` | gauge | `area` (`artifacts`, `documents`) |
| `quader_bastion_cache_capacity_bytes` | gauge | `area` |
| `quader_bastion_cache_evictions_total` | counter | `reason` |
| `quader_bastion_cache_corrupt_total`, `quader_bastion_cache_errors_total` | counter | `op` for errors |
| `quader_bastion_cache_sweeps_total` | counter | `trigger` (`interval`, `size`) |
| `quader_bastion_cache_no_room_total` | counter | `area` (`artifacts`, `documents`) |
| `quader_bastion_cache_protected_bytes` | gauge | `area` (`artifacts`, `documents`) |
| `quader_bastion_refused_total` | counter | `reason` (`blocked`, `rate_limited`, `miss_limited`, `auth_timeout`, `invalid_token`, `busy`, `unreachable`, `not_served`, `read_only`, `foreign_location`, `anonymous_ceiling`, `throughput`, `budget`, `disabled`) |
| `quader_bastion_blocks_total` | counter | `reason` (`refusals`, `failed_auth`, `refused_requests`) |
| `quader_bastion_blocked_addresses` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_audit_events_total` | counter | `outcome` (`sent`, `spooled`, `dropped`) |
| `quader_bastion_audit_buffer_events` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_audit_events_dropped_total` | counter | — |
| `quader_bastion_handovers_total` | counter | `outcome` (`read`, `fallback`, `continued`, `refused`) |
| `quader_bastion_fill_bytes_total` | counter | `source` (`main`, `store`), `class` (`authenticated`, `anonymous`) |
| `quader_bastion_handover_enabled`, `quader_bastion_handover_cooldown` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_configuration_revision` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_configuration_source` | gauge | `source` (`main`, `stored`, `builtin`) |
| `quader_bastion_disabled` | gauge | `mode` (`soft`, `hard`) |
| `quader_bastion_throughput_limit_bytes_per_second` | gauge | `bucket` (`total`, `anonymous`) |
| `quader_bastion_throughput_wait_seconds_total` | counter | `class` (`anonymous`, `signed_in`, `catalogue`) |
| `quader_bastion_throughput_refused_total` | counter | `class`, `reason` (`busy`, `hour`) |
| `quader_bastion_limits_mode` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_budget_events_total` | counter | `figure` (the eleven of R-LIM-004), `mode` (`limited`, `would_limit`) |
| `quader_bastion_gui_enabled` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_catalogue_confirmed_timestamp_seconds`, `quader_bastion_catalogue_stale_after_seconds` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_catalogue_bytes`, `quader_bastion_catalogue_max_bytes`, `quader_bastion_catalogue_documents` | gauge | — |
| `quader_bastion_catalogue_sync_total` | counter | `outcome` (`confirmed`, `failed`, `followed`) |

- The last four rows are the public catalogue's of the web interface (W-35's P7, built on 2026-11-26): `quader_bastion_gui_enabled` is 1
  while the switch gui is on for the replica (R-BAS-102); `…_confirmed_timestamp_seconds` the Unix time of the replica's last confirmed
  state, 0 while it holds none, and `…_stale_after_seconds` `bastion.gui.stale_after` (R-BAS-111); `…_catalogue_bytes` what the catalogue's
  tree holds in the cache backend as stored, `…_max_bytes` its share `bastion.gui.max_bytes`, `…_documents` the documents the replica
  serves (R-BAS-110); `…_sync_total` a round by its outcome, `followed` for a replica of a shared bucket that took the state the syncing
  one wrote (R-BAS-109). The catalogue's reads of the main installation are `kind="catalogue"` of `quader_bastion_main_requests_total`, its
  wait for the throughput `class="catalogue"` of `quader_bastion_throughput_wait_seconds_total`, and a stored document that fails its
  verification counts in `quader_bastion_cache_corrupt_total`. The feed's `catalogue` is a value of `kind` of
  `quader_bastion_feed_entries_applied_total`.
- `quader_bastion_refused_total` counts requests the Bastion refused itself. `reason="read_only"` counts a write refused with `403
  read_only` (R-BAS-014), whether the probe answered it or the kept answer replayed it, and a body above
  `bastion.main.max_forwarded_body`; a `404` that the main installation answers to a probe (a path with no route) is its own answer,
  relayed, and raises no counter either fresh or replayed ([Q-BAS-147](#q-bas-147--only-a-403-read_only-counts-as-a-read_only-refusal-fresh-or-replayed)).
  `reason="foreign_location"` counts an answer of the main installation the Bastion did not pass on because its `Location` named another
  scheme, host or port than the Bastion's, answered `502` instead (R-BAS-099 row 6,
  [Q-BAS-427](#q-bas-427--a-location-on-another-host-is-answered-502-at-the-bastion-whatever-the-status)); it stays at 0 while the main
  installation renders a forward's URLs on the Bastion's base URL. `reason="anonymous_ceiling"` counts a request refused `503 busy` above the
  anonymous ceiling (R-BAS-094, since E9a). `reason="throughput"` counts a miss the throughput did not admit, `503 busy` at the cap or `429`
  with its class's hour used up (R-BAS-097, since E10). `reason="budget"` counts a request a budget of the Bastion's place refused in
  Enforce with a code of R-LIM-020 (R-BAS-096, since E9b).
- `quader_bastion_limits_mode` is 1 while the budgets of the Bastion's place refuse (Enforce) and 0 in Audit (R-LIM-044);
  `quader_bastion_budget_events_total` counts each decision of a budget by its figure, `limited` for a refusal in Enforce and `would_limit`
  for what Audit would have refused (R-BAS-096, since E9b). `quader_bastion_blocks_total` counts by the reasons of the status's closed list
  (R-BAS-096): `refusals` (R-BAS-037), `failed_auth` (the timeout of R-BAS-036, counted since E9b) and `refused_requests` (a subject over its
  `refusedPerHour`, R-LIM-025 at the Bastion).
- `quader_bastion_throughput_limit_bytes_per_second` is the configured figure of the whole Bastion per bucket, 0 while unlimited;
  `quader_bastion_throughput_wait_seconds_total` the seconds this replica's reads waited for the cap, a rate near 1 per transfer saying that
  the cap, not the main installation, sets the pace; `quader_bastion_throughput_refused_total` the misses refused by the cap (`busy`) or by a
  class's hourly volume (`hour`) (R-BAS-097, since E10).
- `quader_bastion_configuration_revision` is the revision of the configuration the replica applies and `quader_bastion_configuration_source`
  is 1 for where it came from: `main` after a handshake, `stored` for the one a replica found in its cache backend at start, `builtin`
  without one (R-BAS-093, Q-BAS-327, since E9a).
- `quader_bastion_disabled` is 1 for the way of the disable the replica applies and 0 for the other, both 0 while it works;
  `quader_bastion_refused_total{reason="disabled"}` counts the requests answered while disabled (R-BAS-133, since W-41's A2).
- The cache hit rate is `quader_bastion_requests_total{result="hit"}` over all; bytes served from the cache are
  `quader_bastion_bytes_served_total{source="cache"}`; requests to the main installation are
  `quader_bastion_main_requests_total` (the observability item of phase 5b).
- `quader_valkey_available` and `quader_ratelimit_fallback{limiter}` are the shared ones.
- `class` of `quader_bastion_fill_bytes_total` is R-BAS-090's (2026-11-26): the budget class of the caller whose request started the fill
  ([Q-BAS-307](#q-bas-307--the-class-of-a-fills-bytes-is-the-class-of-the-request-that-started-it)).
- `quader_bastion_cache_sweeps_total` and `quader_bastion_cache_no_room_total` are R-BAS-089's (2026-11-26): the sweeps a replica ran, by
  `interval` (its timer) or `size` (an area passed its high mark between two timed sweeps, or a fill found no room), and the fills it passed
  through unkept for want of room. A rate of `size` sweeps near one a second, or a rising `no_room`, says that fills arrive faster than the
  sweep frees room: the cache churns.
- `quader_bastion_cache_protected_bytes` is R-BAS-098's (built 2026-11-26): the bytes of an area that were served twice and that the last
  sweep of the replica protected, at most 80 % of the area's limit. A sweep of the timer sets it for both areas, a sweep the size started
  for the area it swept ([Q-BAS-463](#q-bas-463--the-protected-bytes-are-counted-by-the-sweep-and-shown-by-the-replica-that-swept)). A
  replica of a shared bucket that did not hold the sweep lease shows 0, so the release's figure is the largest of its replicas'. Near 80 %
  of `quader_bastion_cache_capacity_bytes` it says that more was served twice than the protected share holds: the oldest of it is evicted
  like what was served once.
- `quader_bastion_answers` is per replica: the answers of a kind the replica holds in its memory, not the lookups. An answer leaves it
  when a use finds it past its period (R-BAS-020) or when period and grace have passed without a use (the janitor, R-BAS-026), so a
  replica that served no lookup for that long reads 0 while `quader_bastion_answers_total{result="hit"}` keeps its count; the other
  replica of a release reads 0 for a credential it never served unless the shared store gave it the answer
  (`TestR_BAS_020_TheCounterAndTheGaugeOfTheAnswersFollowTheLookups`).
- The value `package` of `kind` of `quader_bastion_answers` and `quader_bastion_answers_total` (R-BAS-084, built on 2026-11-23,
  `metrics.AnswerPackage`) is the one addition of the read shapes per package; no label carries a package's name.
- The last four rows are the handover per blob's (R-BAS-075, built on 2026-11-23): one outcome per handover by the path it took
  ([Q-BAS-290](#q-bas-290--a-handover-counts-one-outcome-by-the-path-it-took)), the bytes written into fills by their source, the
  handshake's member and the cooldown. `quader_bastion_bytes_served_total` keeps its two sources: the caller of a fill whose source is
  the direct read is counted `main`, as every fill's caller is; where the bytes came from is `quader_bastion_fill_bytes_total`.

Acceptance criteria:

- The e2e suite reads every metric of the table from both replicas, and `quader_bastion_requests_total{result="hit"}` rises by 20
  on a warm `npm ci` of 20 tarballs.

### R-BAS-090 · The bytes between a Bastion and the main installation are counted
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's task W-34 of 2026-11-26 asks that the main installation be protected from being flooded through a Bastion and that the
throughput between the two can be bounded; before a figure can bound it, the bytes have to be visible. Until this requirement the main
installation counted the requests of a Bastion per registration (`quader_bastion_forwarded_requests_total{bastion, class}`, R-BAS-008) and no
byte, and the Bastion counted the bytes of its fills by their source without the caller's class. Built on 2026-11-26 with the decisions
[Q-BAS-306](#q-bas-306--the-main-installation-counts-the-body-bytes-the-marking-stage-writes-by-registration-and-the-callers-class) and
[Q-BAS-307](#q-bas-307--the-class-of-a-fills-bytes-is-the-class-of-the-request-that-started-it) ([ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted)).

- **At the main installation**, `quader_bastion_forwarded_bytes_total{bastion, class}`: the bytes of the response bodies the main installation
  wrote to the recognized forwarded requests of a registration (R-BAS-013), counted where the marking is written, by the class of the caller:
  `anonymous` for the anonymous caller (an anonymous registry token included, R-BAS-052) and `authenticated` for a request that carried a
  credential, accepted or not. Every answer of a forward counts: artifacts, documents, refusals, the empty body of a handover (R-BAS-073) and
  the answers of write probes. The interface's own routes (handshake, check, feed, downloads) do not; they are
  `quader_bastion_interface_requests_total`'s. Headers, TLS and chunk framing are not in the count. `bastion` is the registration's name,
  bounded by `bastions.max_registrations`; `class` has the values of the Bastion's budget (R-BAS-025).
- **At the Bastion**, `quader_bastion_fill_bytes_total{source, class}`: the bytes written into its fills, by where they came from (`main`, the
  main installation; `store`, the object store through a handover, R-BAS-074) and by the budget class of the caller whose request started the
  fill (`authenticated`, `anonymous`). The bytes a Bastion read through a handover are thereby apart from those it read from the main
  installation. A body the Bastion does not keep (a pass-through, R-BAS-021) and a document kept from memory are read from the main
  installation without a fill; they are in `quader_bastion_bytes_served_total{source="main"}`, without a class
  ([H-2274](#h-2274--the-main-installation-counts-no-handover-and-the-bastion-counts-only-its-fills-by-class)).
- The figures are counted, not bounded: no figure of the main installation or of the Bastion limits the bytes per registration
  ([H-2273](#h-2273--the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted-and-not-bounded)).

Acceptance criteria (unit, `internal/api/bastionmark` and `internal/bastion/engine`):

- A forward of an artifact of 1,000 bytes with a token, one with a refused credential and one of 300 bytes without a credential: the main
  installation counts the 1,000 bytes and the refusal's body `authenticated` and the 300 `anonymous` for the registration; an interface route
  and an ordinary request count nothing.
- A fill started by a caller with a credential and one started anonymously count their bytes under their classes and the source `main`; the
  handover's tests count the source `store` apart.

Built: `TestR_BAS_090_TheBytesOfRecognizedForwardsAreCountedByRegistrationAndClass` in
[mark_test.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark_test.go) and `TestR_BAS_090_FillBytesCarryTheClassOfTheCallerThatStartedTheFill` in
[engine/room_test.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/room_test.go), each under 0.05 s; the handover's tests read the source over both classes.
What each leg gains: the unit job under 0.1 s; nothing else, and nothing per format.

### R-BAS-041 · PrometheusRule
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The chart's PrometheusRule (`metrics.prometheusRule.enabled`) holds these alerts; names are stable, each can be disabled with
`metrics.prometheusRule.disabledAlerts`, thresholds come from gauges, not from chart values (R-HA-045's rule):

| Alert | Expression (sketch) | For | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QuaderBastionInterfaceMismatch` | `max(quader_bastion_interface_mismatch) == 1` | 1m | critical |
| `QuaderBastionMainUnreachable` | `max(quader_bastion_main_reachable) == 0` (every replica) | 2m | critical |
| `QuaderBastionMainUnreachableSingleReplica` | `min(quader_bastion_main_reachable) == 0 and max(quader_bastion_main_reachable) == 1` | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionGraceExhausted` | `time() - min(quader_bastion_main_unreachable_since_timestamp_seconds > 0) > max(quader_bastion_answer_period_seconds + quader_bastion_grace_period_seconds)` | 0m | critical |
| `QuaderBastionBaseURLMismatch` | `max(quader_bastion_base_url_mismatch) == 1` | 1m | critical |
| `QuaderBastionTokenExpiresSoon` | `min(quader_bastion_token_remaining_seconds) < max(quader_bastion_token_warn_before_seconds)` | 1h | warning |
| `QuaderBastionTokenRefused` | `max(quader_bastion_main_token_refused) == 1` | 1m | critical |
| `QuaderBastionFeedStale` | `max(quader_bastion_feed_lag_seconds) > 30` | 2m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionMainBudgetSaturated` | `sum(rate(quader_bastion_main_budget_exhausted_total[5m])) > 0` | 10m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionAuditEventsDropped` | `increase(quader_bastion_audit_events_dropped_total[15m]) > 0` | 0m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionCacheCorrupt` | `increase(quader_bastion_cache_corrupt_total[1h]) > 0` | 0m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionHandoverFailing` | `sum(increase(quader_bastion_handovers_total{outcome=~"fallback\|continued\|refused"}[15m])) > 0 and sum(increase(quader_bastion_handovers_total{outcome="read"}[15m])) == 0` (R-BAS-075) | 15m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionCatalogueStale` | per replica: `time() - quader_bastion_catalogue_confirmed_timestamp_seconds > quader_bastion_catalogue_stale_after_seconds`, while it holds a state and `quader_bastion_gui_enabled == 1` (R-BAS-111) | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionCatalogueMissing` | per replica: `quader_bastion_catalogue_confirmed_timestamp_seconds == 0` while `quader_bastion_gui_enabled == 1` (R-BAS-111) | 15m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionCatalogueOverBound` | `max(quader_bastion_catalogue_bytes) > max(quader_bastion_catalogue_max_bytes)` (R-BAS-110) | 15m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionValkeyUnavailable` | `max(quader_valkey_available) == 0` (rendered only with Valkey configured) | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderBastionReplicasNotReady` | `min(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment=~"<fullname>"}) < 2` (or the StatefulSet's) | 5m | warning |

Expressions are sketches. Two things differ from them in the chart ([Q-BAS-57](#q-bas-57--the-rule-tests-run-with-a-pinned-promtool-and-the-rules-are-scoped-to-the-release)):
`QuaderBastionMainUnreachable` uses `max(…) == 0`, because `min(…) == 0` is true as soon as one replica is cut off and would fire
next to the single-replica alert instead of only when every replica is; and every selector is scoped to the release
(`namespace` and `service="<fullname>-ops"`, the labels the chart's ServiceMonitor puts on the series), because one Prometheus
scrapes several Bastions and an aggregate over all of them would blend their states. The two alerts of the catalogue's age are per
replica, matched `on(namespace, service, pod)`, because a replica's confirmation is its own and each page says its own age (W-35's B.2b);
the bound is the release's, since the replicas of a bucket report the one shared tree (built on 2026-11-26, W-35's P7).

Acceptance criteria:

- `promtool check rules` and `promtool test rules` pass, with one test per alert that fires on its failure input and stays
  silent on a healthy one. *As built for the catalogue's three alerts* ([rules_test.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader-bastion/tests/rules_test.yaml),
  part of `TestR_BAS_041_PromtoolRules`): the stale replica fires and the fresh one beside it does not, nothing fires with the web interface
  off, a replica without a state fires after 15 minutes, a catalogue above its share fires.
- The e2e suite sees `QuaderBastionInterfaceMismatch` and `QuaderBastionMainUnreachable` fire in the cluster's Prometheus
  (R-BAS-049).

### R-BAS-042 · Logs, traces and redaction
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- The request log of R-OPS-010 at the Bastion carries the client address, the class and result of R-BAS-040, the token hint
  (never the token), the main installation's `X-Request-Id` when one was involved, and the refusal reason. Blocked addresses are
  summarized (R-BAS-037).
- The Bastion starts a span per request and propagates W3C trace context to the main installation, so a forwarded request is one
