  trace (R-OPS-018). The Bastion itself never accepts incoming trace context from callers (`tracing.incoming_context: none` is
  fixed for the role); the main installation accepts the Bastion's context when the Bastion's addresses are among its
  `tracing.trusted_peers`.
- `Authorization`, `Quader-Bastion-Authorization`, the token file and the signing key are redacted everywhere (R-OPS-013).

Acceptance criteria:

- A request through the Bastion and its forward share one trace ID in both request logs; no log line of the e2e run contains a
  token secret (scanner pattern of R-AUTH-022 over the collected logs).

### R-BAS-043 · Startup, readiness and drains
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **Startup**: configuration validation (R-BAS-001), the token file (R-BAS-006), TLS material, the cache backend's first check,
  the listeners; then the handshake and the feed history (R-BAS-026), which do not gate readiness.
- **Who runs what.** The server runs the link (handshake, feed, reachability), the token reloader, the download buffer and the cache
  sweeper for the life of the process and drains them in the order below; the engine reads their state, starts none of them and runs
  only its own janitor ([Q-BAS-79](#q-bas-79--the-link-is-one-state-machine-per-replica-run-by-the-server),
  [Q-BAS-100](#q-bas-100--one-implementation-of-the-link-the-budget-the-sweep-and-the-cache-use-and-the-role-builds-real-components-only),
  [Q-BAS-101](#q-bas-101--the-server-runs-the-cache-sweeper-and-the-drain-stops-it-before-the-engine)).
- **Readiness** does not depend on the main installation
  ([Q-BAS-44](#q-bas-44--unreachable-means-a-failed-handshake-or-a-stale-feed)): a replica that cannot reach it still serves what
  the grace period allows. It fails while draining, while the listeners are not bound, and before the cache backend's first
  check passed.
- **Drain** follows R-ARCH-024: readiness flips, the drain delay passes, in-flight requests finish within the termination grace
  period, the sweeper and the buffer's flush loop stop, the engine drains, the audit buffer is sent or spooled (R-BAS-039), the link
  and the token reloader stop, the Valkey leases are released. A transfer cut at the deadline is
  resumed by the client with `Range` and `If-Range` on another replica (R-BAS-022).
- At least two replicas spread across nodes behind a PodDisruptionBudget that evicts one pod at a time (INV-12's rule for a
  long-running role); the chart enforces it with `highAvailability.enforce` (R-BAS-045).

Acceptance criteria:

- `kubectl drain` of the node of one Bastion replica during a 10-minute `npm ci` and `dotnet restore` loop on the e2e cluster
  causes zero failed client runs.
- A Bastion started while the main installation is down becomes ready, answers `503 unavailable`, and serves after the main
  installation comes back without a restart.

### R-BAS-044 · TLS on every connection of the Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Every connection the Bastion makes or accepts can run with TLS, and its material is reloaded without a restart (INV-20,
R-ARCH-035):

- its client listener (`server.tls`, the pair of `tls.existingSecret` or the cert-manager Certificate of the chart) and its ops
  listener;
- the connection to the main installation (`https` required: an `http` `bastion.main.url` or `bastion.main.packages_url`
  stops startup; the trust is the system roots plus `trustedCA`);
- **after the main installation's cut into roles** (phase 6a; the key `bastion.main.packages_url` is built, the chart of the
  main installation renders the roles with WP6a.3; [ha-and-helm.md](ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-002, Q-HA-74): the forwards and
  the probes of the client (`mainclient.HTTPClient.Do`) go to `packages_url`, the interface operations (handshake,
  check, feed, downloads, and since interface version 8 the catalogue's) to `url`; the same trust (system roots plus `trustedCA`) applies to both; the interface of R-BAS-008 (`/api/v1/bastion/…`) is served by the
  main installation's role `api` and the forwarded package and raw-file requests by `packages`. A `bastion.main.url` that
  names the main installation's edge reaches both, because the edge splits by path. A Bastion that calls the main
  installation's Services directly sets `bastion.main.url` to the Service of `api` and `bastion.main.packages_url` to the
  Service of `packages`; the forwards then go to `packages_url`, everything else to `url`. `packages_url` empty (the
  default) means `url` for both;
- Valkey and Sentinel (R-ARCH-031), and the cache bucket (`https` endpoint, `trustedCA`);
- the chart's Ingress (`ingress.tls`), Service, probes and ServiceMonitor (R-HA-063's wiring).

Acceptance criteria:

- Rotating the listener certificate, the CA bundle and the Valkey client certificate on a running Bastion is picked up without a
  restart; `http://quader.example.com` as `bastion.main.url` stops startup.

## Chart

### R-BAS-045 · Chart `quader-bastion`: resources and naming
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

A second Helm chart for this instance type (owner, [Q-BAS-5](#q-bas-5--a-second-helm-chart-quader-bastion)), in
`deploy/helm/quader-bastion`, released with the chart `quader` by the Release Docker & Helm workflow, with its own SemVer and
`appVersion` = Quader version (R-ARCH-025). It renders, for the release name `<fullname>`:

| Resource | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Deployment, or StatefulSet with `cacheVolume.type: persistent` | `<fullname>` | `quader serve --role bastion`; container ports `https` 8443 and `ops` 8081 |
| ConfigMap | `<fullname>-config` | `/etc/quader/quader.yaml` from `config`, with the chart-managed keys |
| Service | `<fullname>` (`https`, no session affinity), `<fullname>-ops` | — |
| Ingress | `<fullname>` | host of `config.server.base_url`; `ingress.tls`; the annotations of `edgeLimit`, `cacheVolume.routeByPath` and `ingress.backendTLS` |
| Certificate (cert-manager), optional | `<fullname>-tls` | with `tls.certManager.enabled` |
| NetworkPolicy | `<fullname>` | R-BAS-047: ingress rules only |
| PodDisruptionBudget, HorizontalPodAutoscaler | `<fullname>` | — |
| ServiceAccount | `<fullname>` | `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; no Role, no RoleBinding |
| ServiceMonitor, PrometheusRule | `<fullname>` | R-BAS-041 |

- It renders no Secret: the Bastion token, the signing key, the cache key, the bucket and Valkey credentials come from existing Secrets
  (`secrets.*`, created by GitOps, the internal-secrets-operator or the stackit-s3-provisioner).
- **Validation** (fail at `helm template`): `config.server.base_url` and `config.bastion.main.url` set and `https`;
  `secrets.mainToken.existingSecret` set; `secrets.signingKey.existingSecret` set with the bucket backend or Valkey;
  `config.bastion.cache.bucket.bucket` with the bucket backend; `routeByPath` only with the volume backend and `ingress.enabled`;
  `edgeLimit` wider than the Bastion's limits (R-BAS-038); `config.server.trusted_proxies` while `ingress.enabled`, because behind
  the Ingress every request arrives from the controller's pods
  ([Q-BAS-130](#q-bas-130--behind-the-ingress-the-chart-requires-the-trusted-proxies)); the spool of fills
  (`config.bastion.cache.spool_max_bytes`) at least `max_object_bytes`, and a `tmp.sizeLimit` (bucket backend, and volume backend with
  `secrets.cacheKey`, [Q-BAS-214](#q-bas-214--with-a-key-the-volume-backend-spools-its-fills-on-the-pods-temporary-volume)) or
  `cacheVolume.size` (volume backend) that holds it ([Q-BAS-131](#q-bas-131--the-bytes-of-the-fills-in-progress-are-bounded-and-the-chart-sizes-the-volumes-from-the-bound));
  with `highAvailability.enforce` at least two replicas, a PDB and
  host spreading; a value under `config` that is chart-managed or not in the role's schema; a certificate source for the
  listener while `tls.enabled` (`tls.existingSecret`, or `tls.certManager.issuerRef.name`); an ingress peer for the https
  port, because an empty peer list would mean "anywhere"; exactly one key in `trustedCA.keys`; an entry of
  `ingress.annotations` that the chart renders itself; a name in `metrics.prometheusRule.disabledAlerts` that is no alert
  ([Q-BAS-55](#q-bas-55--what-a-render-needs-and-what-the-values-file-left-open)).
- **HAProxy Ingress annotations** *(verified against HAProxy Ingress v0.16.3, the controller of the local profile,
  [Q-BAS-56](#q-bas-56--haproxy-ingress-annotations-as-verified-against-the-controller-of-the-local-profile))*, all with the
  controller's default prefix `haproxy-ingress.github.io/`:
  - `edgeLimit`: `limit-rps`, `limit-connections` and `limit-whitelist` (from `config.bastion.blocking.exempt_cidrs`,
    comma-separated, omitted while the list is empty);
  - `cacheVolume.routeByPath`: `balance-algorithm: uri path-only` (the path alone, Q-BAS-154), `assign-backend-server-id: "true"` (stable server IDs, so a pod added or
    replaced moves about `1 ÷ n` of the paths) and `config-backend: hash-type consistent`, because the controller has no key of
    its own for consistent hashing;
  - `tls.enabled`: `secure-backends: "true"`, `secure-sni: <fullname>.<namespace>.svc` and, while `ingress.backendTLS.verify`,
    `secure-verify-ca-secret` (`ingress.backendTLS.caSecret`, empty = the listener's Secret, which must carry `ca.crt`).

  A user value of `ingress.annotations` for one of these keys is refused. A controller other than HAProxy Ingress ignores them,
  and the chart's NOTES say so (H-434).

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm template` with only the required values (`config.server.base_url`, `config.server.trusted_proxies`,
  `config.bastion.main.url`, `secrets.mainToken.existingSecret` and a certificate source `tls.certManager.issuerRef.name`,
  [Q-BAS-55](#q-bas-55--what-a-render-needs-and-what-the-values-file-left-open)) renders a
  Deployment with two replicas, a PDB, the Ingress with the edge-limit annotations, a NetworkPolicy, and no Secret, no Role and no
  PersistentVolumeClaim.
- The chart test pins the annotation names to the controller version of the local profile: a change of
  `DEV_HAPROXY_INGRESS_IMAGE` fails it until the names are verified against the new version. The e2e suite (R-BAS-049) runs
  against that controller: the edge limit refuses a flood, routing by path pins a path to one pod.

### R-BAS-046 · Values reference
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-093):* `config.bastion.main.max_concurrent`, `anonymous_share` and `queue_timeout`,
`config.bastion.limits`, `config.bastion.failed_auth` and `config.bastion.blocking` leave the block below for the registration;
`edgeLimit.exemptCIDRs` (default `[]`) joins the edge's values; the chart renders the edge figure into the configuration file as the
chart-managed `bastion.edge_limit`. *Built by E9a (2026-11-26):* the block below. *Revised on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7, R-BAS-109 to
R-BAS-111):* `config.bastion.gui` joins the block (`poll_interval` 10 s, `max_bytes` 4 GiB, `stale_after` 1 h), `cache.max_bytes` less
`documents_max_bytes` less `gui.max_bytes` must hold one `max_object_bytes`, and the chart renders the chart-managed
`bastion.cache.volume.persistent` from `cacheVolume.type`.

Every value of `quader-bastion` with its default. The block below is the chart's `values.yaml`: every value is its default, and
a value is commented only where its name does not say its meaning, unit, range or consequence, with an `example:` where the
default is empty (owner, 2026-11-04: no content-free comments). Keys under `config`
are the Bastion's configuration file (R-BAS-001); the chart-managed keys (`server.tls`, `bastion.main.token_file`,
`bastion.main.ca_file`, `bastion.signing_key_file`, `bastion.cache.encryption_key_file`, `bastion.cache.volume.dir` and `persistent`, `bastion.cache.bucket.ca_file`,
`bastion.cache.bucket.credentials.access_key_id_file` and `secret_access_key_file`, `bastion.replicas`, `bastion.edge_limit`, the Valkey secret files
`valkey.username_file`, `valkey.password_file`, `valkey.sentinel.username_file`, `valkey.sentinel.password_file` and `valkey.tls.ca_file`) are rendered by the chart and refused when set; the binary
marks them in its schema (`x-quader-chart-managed`), and so are `server.ops_tls` and `tracing.ca_file`. The schema the chart
validates `config` against is `internal/config/bastion.schema.json`. The role has no `incoming_context` key under `tracing`
(R-BAS-042).

<details>
<summary>deploy/helm/quader-bastion/values.yaml</summary>

```yaml
# ── Global ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
global:
  imageRegistry: ""                     # empty = image.registry
  imagePullSecrets: []                  # example: [{name: registry-pull}]

nameOverride: ""
fullnameOverride: ""
commonLabels: {}
commonAnnotations: {}

image:
  registry: docker.io                   # Docker Hub, as the chart quader
  repository: guidedtraffic/quader       # the one Quader image
  tag: ""                               # empty = chart appVersion
  digest: ""                            # example: sha256:<64 hex>; wins over tag
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

highAvailability:
  enforce: true                         # ≥ 2 replicas, a PDB, DoNotSchedule host spreading

# ── Bastion pods: quader serve --role bastion ─────────────────────────────────
replicaCount: 2                         # ignored when autoscaling.enabled; rendered into bastion.replicas
minReadySeconds: 10
revisionHistoryLimit: 5
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120      # long transfers finish or are cut
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 1Gi                         # answers and private copies live in memory
    ephemeral-storage: 1Gi
  limits:
    memory: 2Gi                         # no CPU limit by default
autoscaling:
  enabled: false
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6                        # rendered into bastion.replicas
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
  targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 0  # 0 = no memory metric
  metrics: []
  behavior: {}                          # Kubernetes defaults
podDisruptionBudget:
  enabled: true
  maxUnavailable: 1
  minAvailable: null                    # mutually exclusive with maxUnavailable
  unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
topologySpread:
  enabled: true
  nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor
  zone:
    maxSkew: 1
    whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
  host:
    maxSkew: 1
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule    # required with highAvailability.enforce
topologySpreadConstraints: []           # non-empty replaces the generated constraints
affinity: {}
nodeSelector: {}
tolerations: []
priorityClassName: ""
podAnnotations: {}
podLabels: {}

# ── Cache volume ─────────────────────────────────────
cacheVolume:
  type: ephemeral                       # ephemeral | persistent | emptyDir; used with config.bastion.cache.backend volume
  storageClassName: ""                  # cluster default
  size: 25Gi                            # above config.bastion.cache.max_bytes
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]          # ReadWriteOnce | ReadWriteOncePod
  routeByPath: false                    # URI hashing at HAProxy Ingress

# ── Bastion configuration (rendered to /etc/quader/quader.yaml) ───────────────
config:
  server:
    listen: ":8443"
    ops_listen: ":8081"
    base_url: ""                        # required; example: https://packages.example.com
    trusted_proxies: []                 # REQUIRED while ingress.enabled: the CIDRs of the ingress controller's pods, example: ["10.244.0.0/16"]
    forwarded_header: x-forwarded-for   # x-forwarded-for | forwarded
    max_in_flight: 1024                 # per replica
  bastion:
    main:
      url: ""                           # required; example: https://quader.example.com (the main endpoint)
      packages_url: ""                  # empty = url; example: https://quader-packages.quader.svc:8080 (the main installation's packages Service)
      connect_timeout: 5s
      response_header_timeout: 30s
      max_forwarded_body: 8MiB          # bodies of read routes such as npm's bulk audit
      handshake_interval: 1m
      unreachable_after: 10s            # at least 3 × feed.poll_interval
      token_reload_interval: 10s
    answers:
      period: 5m                        # 30s to 1h
      grace_period: 15m                 # default (proposed; the owner's proposal); 0 to 24h
      max_entries: 200000               # per replica
    feed:
      poll_interval: 2s                 # 1s to 10s
    cache:
      backend: volume                   # volume | bucket
      max_bytes: 20GiB
      max_object_bytes: 2GiB
      spool_max_bytes: 2GiB             # the fills in progress of a replica hold at most this in temporary storage; at least max_object_bytes
      documents_max_bytes: 2GiB
      private_documents_max_bytes: 256MiB  # per replica, memory
      metadata_revalidate_after: 1m
      artifact_revalidate_after: 10m
      negative_period: 1m
      negative_max_entries: 100000      # per replica
      sweep_interval: 5m
      access_resolution: 1h
      fill_wait_max: 10m                # 30s to 1h; how long a replica waits for another replica's fill (R-BAS-054)
      bucket:
        endpoint: ""                    # AWS resolution; example: https://object.storage.eu01.onstackit.cloud
        region: ""                      # example: eu01
        bucket: ""                      # required with backend bucket; example: quader-bastion-partners
        prefix: quader-bastion
        force_path_style: false
        credentials:
          source: static                # static (secrets.cacheBucket) | webIdentity | default
          role_arn: ""                  # example: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-bastion
    audit:
      buffer_events: 100000             # per replica
      batch_size: 500
      flush_interval: 1s
      spool_max_events: 1000000
    token:
      warn_before: 720h                 # 30 days (the owner's proposal)
    gui:                                # the public catalogue of the web interface; on and off at the main installation (R-BAS-109 to R-BAS-111)
      poll_interval: 10s                # 1s to 10m; a feed entry reads at once
      max_bytes: 4GiB                   # a share of cache.max_bytes, reserved whether or not the web interface is on (compressed documents)
      stale_after: 1h                   # the pages say they are old after this, and QuaderBastionCatalogueStale fires; they are served on
  valkey:                               # optional; the keys of the chart quader, plus mode none
    mode: none                          # none | sentinel | standalone (development only)
    sentinel:
      addresses: []                     # required with mode sentinel; example: [quader-bastion-valkey-sentinel:26379]
      primary_name: ""                  # required with mode sentinel; example: quader-bastion
      tls: true
      refresh_interval: 5s
    address: ""                         # standalone mode only
    database: 0
    key_prefix: ""                      # empty = the host of config.server.base_url
    tls:
      mode: verify-full                 # verify-full | verify-ca | disable
      server_name: ""                   # host name of each address
    connect_timeout: 2s
    command_timeout: 500ms
  log:
    level: info                         # operations-and-observability.md
  tracing:                              # operations-and-observability.md
    enabled: false
    endpoint: ""                        # example: https://otel-collector.observability:4318
    sample_ratio: 0.1
  runtime:
    memory_limit_ratio: 0.85
  ui:                                   # bastion.md R-BAS-100
    # This Bastion's own imprint and privacy notice, for its web interface: Markdown, at most 64 KiB per page and language, rendered
    # at start under the README sanitizer. The Bastion's administrator answers for what they say; they name the operator of this
    # Bastion and are never taken from the main installation. A change is a rollout.
    legal:
      imprint:
        en: ""                          # example: "Example Operations GmbH\\\nMusterstraße 1\\\n12345 Berlin"
        de: ""
      privacy:
        en: ""
        de: ""

# ── Existing Secrets (the chart never creates one) ──────────────────────────
secrets:
  # The Bastion's token: issued on the main installation's Bastions page, or declared in its values (bastions.declared, R-BAS-127),
  # where the main installation's migration Job reads the same value from a Secret of its namespace, so that the registration survives a
  # fresh database. Make a value with `quader admin bastion token generate`.
  mainToken:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required; example: quader-bastion-token (the qdr_bst_ token)
    key: token
  signingKey:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required with the bucket backend or Valkey; example: quader-bastion-signing (32 random bytes)
    key: key
  cacheKey:
    existingSecret: ""                  # empty = the cache stays plain; example: quader-bastion-cache-key (32 random bytes); a new key empties the cache
    key: key
  cacheBucket:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required with credentials.source static; example: quader-bastion-s3 (stackit-s3-provisioner)
    accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id
    secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key
  valkey:
    existingSecret: ""                  # no authentication; example: quader-bastion-valkey
    usernameKey: username
    passwordKey: password
  valkeySentinel:
    existingSecret: ""                  # no authentication at the Sentinels; example: quader-bastion-valkey-sentinel
    usernameKey: username               # empty = the default user
    passwordKey: password
  valkeyCA:
    existingSecret: ""                  # system roots plus trustedCA
    key: ca.crt

trustedCA:
  existingSecret: ""                    # example: corp-ca-bundle; trust for the main installation, its object store, Valkey and the bucket
  existingConfigMap: ""                 # example: corp-ca-bundle (trust-manager target)
  keys: [ca-bundle.crt]                 # exactly one key: the bundle is one file (bastion.main.ca_file)

# ── TLS of the Bastion's own listener ───────────────────────────
tls:
  enabled: true                         # false only with the explicit plaintext switch of INV-20
  existingSecret: ""                    # empty = the cert-manager Certificate below
  certManager:
    enabled: true
    issuerRef:
      kind: ClusterIssuer
      name: ""                          # required with certManager.enabled; example: internal-ca
    duration: 2160h
    renewBefore: 720h

# ── Pod identity and security ──────────────────────────────────────────────
serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: ""                              # <fullname>
  annotations: {}                       # the IRSA role annotation of the cache bucket goes here
  # eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-bastion
  automountServiceAccountToken: false   # the Bastion never calls the Kubernetes API

podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 65532
  runAsGroup: 65532
  fsGroup: 65532
  fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  privileged: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  runAsNonRoot: true
  capabilities:
    drop: [ALL]
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

tmp:
  sizeLimit: ""                         # empty = 1Gi with the volume backend; where fills are spooled here (the bucket backend, or the volume backend with secrets.cacheKey) config.bastion.cache.spool_max_bytes plus 256Mi; example: 3Gi

# ── Probes ──────────────────────────────────────────
probes:
  startup:
    enabled: true
    path: /healthz
    periodSeconds: 2
    timeoutSeconds: 2
    failureThreshold: 60
  liveness:
    enabled: true
    path: /healthz
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 3
    failureThreshold: 6
  readiness:
    enabled: true
    path: /readyz
    periodSeconds: 5
    timeoutSeconds: 3
    failureThreshold: 1
    successThreshold: 1

# ── Exposure ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 8443
  opsPort: 8081
  annotations: {}
  labels: {}
  ipFamilyPolicy: ""                    # example: PreferDualStack
  ipFamilies: []

ingress:
  enabled: true                         # the Bastion is reached through its own Ingress
  className: haproxy                    # HAProxy Ingress, the owner's edge
  annotations: {}                       # appended to the generated ones
  labels: {}
  hosts: []                             # empty = host of config.server.base_url
  tls: []                               # example: [{secretName: quader-bastion-public-tls, hosts: [packages.example.com]}]
  backendTLS:                           # TLS from the Ingress to the pods while tls.enabled; HAProxy Ingress keys
    verify: true                        # the controller verifies the pods' certificate against caSecret
    caSecret: ""                        # empty = the listener's Secret (tls.existingSecret or <fullname>-tls), which must carry ca.crt

edgeLimit:                              # stage 1 of the blocking; HAProxy Ingress counts HTTP requests, also on a kept-alive connection; rendered into bastion.edge_limit and reported to the main installation
  enabled: true
  requestsPerSecond: 1000               # per address, in the last second, no burst; keep it above the signed-in flood figure of the Bastion's registration, which the card warns about
  connections: 256                      # per address: requests in flight at once
  exemptCIDRs: []                       # addresses the ingress does not limit (limit-whitelist); example: ["198.51.100.0/24"]

# ── Network policy: ingress rules only, each rule with its port ─────────────
# No egress value exists: the chart renders no egress rule; the Bastion pods' egress is the cluster's own policy.
networkPolicy:
  enabled: true
  ingress:
    https:
      from:                             # the ingress controller's namespace
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: haproxy-ingress
    ops:
      from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
    probeCIDRs: []

# ── Monitoring ──────────────────────────────────────
metrics:
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: false
    namespace: ""                       # release namespace
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s
    labels: {}                          # example: {release: kube-prometheus-stack}
    relabelings: []                     # appended after the fixed role relabeling (role="bastion")
    metricRelabelings: []
  prometheusRule:
    enabled: false
    labels: {}
    disabledAlerts: []                  # example: [QuaderBastionCacheCorrupt]
    extraRules: []

# ── Extension points ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
extraEnv: []
extraEnvFrom: []
extraVolumes: []
extraVolumeMounts: []
initContainers: []
sidecars: []
extraObjects: []
```

</details>

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm show values deploy/helm/quader-bastion` equals this block, except for formatting; a CI test compares the key sets.
- The `config` subtree is validated against the schema the binary emits for the role `bastion` (R-HA-029's mechanism), so a
  key the binary does not know fails `helm install`.

### R-BAS-047 · Network policy
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's rule ([ADR-154](../decisions.md#adr-154--network-policies-are-ingress-rules-between-the-charts-pods-each-with-its-port),
2026-11-04, for this chart since 2026-11-05): the chart writes only ingress rules, only for the pods it deploys, and every rule
names its specific port. With `networkPolicy.enabled: true` (default) it renders one NetworkPolicy `<fullname>` that selects the
Bastion pods, with `policyTypes: [Ingress]`:

- the `https` port only from `networkPolicy.ingress.https.from`, the ingress controller's namespace: the Bastion is reached
  through its Ingress, never directly. An empty list is refused at render time, because Kubernetes reads it as "from anywhere";
- the ops port only from `networkPolicy.ingress.ops.from` (the monitoring namespace) and `networkPolicy.ingress.probeCIDRs`;
  with neither, the rule is left out and no pod reaches the port.
- **Egress.** None. The chart renders no egress rule and has no `networkPolicy.egress` values. Until 2026-11-05 it rendered an
  egress policy, on by default; the owner removed it under ADR-154 and rejected keeping it as an exception of this chart or as
  an opt-in. Containing the outbound connections of a taken-over Bastion pod is the cluster operator's own policy; the gap is
  [H-522](../security/bastion.md#h-522--the-chart-restricts-no-egress-of-the-bastion-pods). An operator who restricts egress lets
  the Bastion pods reach DNS; the main installation's addresses (`bastion.main.url`, and `bastion.main.packages_url` where set)
  on their ports; Valkey and its Sentinels while `valkey.mode` is not `none`; the cache bucket with the bucket backend, and its
  credential endpoint with `credentials.source` `webIdentity` or `default`; the span collector while tracing is enabled; and, while its
  registration's handover is on, the public address of every connection of the main installation a handover may name (R-BAS-078). The
  Bastion contacts no upstream registry, no OIDC issuer and no PostgreSQL (R-BAS-001).

Acceptance criteria:

- In every value set of `deploy/helm/quader-bastion/ci`, the chart renders the policy with `policyTypes: [Ingress]`, no `egress`
  key, exactly one port per rule and no empty peer list; a value under `networkPolicy.egress` fails the render
  (`TestR_BAS_047_NetworkPolicy`).
- On the CNI of the kind profile, a pod of a namespace the https rule does not admit is refused at a Bastion pod's https and
  ops ports; a pod of the admitted namespace (the ingress controller's) completes a TLS handshake at the https port and is
  refused at the ops port; the Bastion serves through its Ingress meanwhile (`TestBastion_R_BAS_049_NetworkPolicy`).

## Tests

### R-BAS-048 · Integration suite against an in-process main installation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Go tests in `internal/bastion` and `test/integration/bastion` start an in-process main installation (the `web` role against
the integration stack's PostgreSQL, Valkey with Sentinel and S3) and one or two in-process Bastion replicas, each with and
without Valkey and with both cache backends (the volume backend on a temporary directory, the bucket backend on the stack's
S3). Test names carry the requirement IDs (`TestR_BAS_0nn_…`). The suite holds every Go-side acceptance criterion of this page,
at least:

- cold and warm cache for npm and NuGet, with `$FULL`, `$PART`, `$NONE` and anonymous callers;
- revocation by every feed kind, with the 5 s bound; an answer obtained before a revocation and stored after it;
- the main installation unreachable (a fault-injecting transport): grace, `503` for unseen tokens, nothing after;
- interface mismatch; base URL mismatch; a revoked Bastion token;
- write probes, the read route with a body, the marking contract over the route table;
- the negative cache, the budget, collapsing, the limits, the failed-authentication timeout, blocking with and without Valkey;
- corrupt cache content, forged entries and answers, a feed reset.

**As built** ([Q-BAS-105](#q-bas-105--the-integration-suites-main-installation-is-the-web-role-behind-a-tls-front-another-interface-version-is-simulated-on-the-wire)):
`test/integration/bastion` starts, per test, the web role of the stack (PostgreSQL, Valkey with Sentinel, S3) with `npm-local`, `npm-remote`
(over the counting test upstream), `npm-all` and the NuGet counterparts in one project, the fixture principals, a registration `partners` with its token,
`server.trusted_proxies` and `server.additional_base_urls`, behind a TLS front that records every request of the Bastion and can cut the link,
delay, hold or alter the interface version of a request or an answer; and one or two Bastion replicas from a configuration file, with the volume
backend or the stack's S3, with and without Valkey. The tests are named `TestR_BAS_0nn_…`; the table of
[developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-integration-suite-r-bas-048) lists them.

Acceptance criteria:

- `make test-integration` runs the suite, and the coverage generator records every requirement of this page whose criteria
  are integration tests from its passing test names.

### R-BAS-049 · End-to-end suite on kind with npm and NuGet
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The e2e driver ([developer/e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md)) installs the chart `quader` and, in a second namespace, the chart
`quader-bastion` with two replicas behind HAProxy Ingress, once with the volume backend and once with a SeaweedFS bucket and
Valkey. The clients are npm, pnpm, Yarn 4 and `dotnet restore`, run from a pod outside the Bastion's namespace through the
Bastion's Ingress:

| Scenario | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Cold cache | `npm ci` and `dotnet restore` succeed with `$FULL`; every tarball and package reaches the main installation once |
| Warm cache | a second run with an empty client cache within `metadata_revalidate_after` sends no request for a tarball, a `.nupkg` or a document to the main installation; after it, only conditional requests that transfer no artifact |
| Main installation unreachable | NetworkPolicy cut: warm runs succeed for the grace period, a cold package and an unseen token get `503`, everything `503` after `period + grace_period`; `QuaderBastionMainUnreachable` fires ([Q-BAS-112](#q-bas-112--the-alert-rows-assert-the-gauges-the-rules-read-held-for-the-rules-for-the-profile-has-no-prometheus)) |
| Token revoked at the main installation | a client loop is refused within 5 s on both replicas |
| Interface mismatch | an upgrade of the main installation to `InterfaceVersion + 1` fires `QuaderBastionInterfaceMismatch`; the Bastion's upgrade clears it ([Q-BAS-111](#q-bas-111--the-interface-mismatch-is-exercised-with-a-release-binary-built-under-a-go-overlay), Q-BAS-112) |
| Flooding address | an address sending 2,000 requests a minute is blocked on both replicas; another address is unaffected |
| Failed-authentication timeout | 21 random tokens put the address into the timeout; a known token from it keeps working |
| Anonymous miss flood | anonymous requests for 10,000 random names within a minute send at most the anonymous miss budget and the anonymous share of `max_concurrent` to the main installation |
| Read-only | `npm publish` and `dotnet nuget push` are refused in the client's shape, pointing at the main installation |
| Drain | `kubectl drain` of one Bastion replica's node during a 10-minute client loop: zero failed runs |
| Replica lost | a Bastion replica force-deleted (`--grace-period=0 --force`) under a client loop, with the volume backend and with the bucket backend: zero failed commands with the clients' own retries, the replacement becomes ready, warm content keeps being served (bucket: no artifact fetched again; volume: at most once per replica) ([Q-BAS-141](#q-bas-141--zero-failed-commands-means-after-the-clients-own-retries-the-bastion-does-not-retry-a-forward), [Q-BAS-143](#q-bas-143--what-warm-content-keeps-being-served-means-after-a-replica-is-lost)) |
| Main installation failing over | under a client loop through the bucket Bastion: a PostgreSQL switchover, a Valkey failover and a force-deleted `packages` pod of the main installation: zero failed commands with the clients' own retries, including the commands for packages the Bastion has not seen (misses), and the replicas are never all unreachable for the alert's two minutes (R-HA-052, [Q-BAS-141](#q-bas-141--zero-failed-commands-means-after-the-clients-own-retries-the-bastion-does-not-retry-a-forward), [Q-BAS-142](#q-bas-142--the-failure-suite-runs-one-load-with-a-miss-loop-and-one-fault-after-the-other)) |
| Rolling upgrade of either side | `kubectl rollout restart` and a `helm upgrade` with a changed pod annotation of the main installation's `packages` and `api` Deployments, and of the Bastion's Deployment (both backends), each under a client loop: zero failed commands, `quader_bastion_interface_mismatch` never 1 (R-BAS-028), the replicas are never all unreachable for two minutes ([Q-BAS-144](#q-bas-144--the-links-state-under-maintenance-is-judged-by-the-alerts-condition)) |
| Hidden content | a package hidden by a permission at the main installation is hidden at the Bastion, cached or not, and a narrowed permission hides cached content within the revocation bound ([Q-BAS-114](#q-bas-114--hidden-content-in-the-suite-is-a-package-permission-the-exposure-rules-of-an-endpoint-are-not-the-bastions)) |

- The drain, the failure scenarios (replica lost, main installation failing over, rolling upgrade of either side), the flood and the anonymous flood are long tests: they run nightly, on dispatch and locally, not in the release
  path, and a red long leg is a finding, not a blocker (the owner's rule of 2026-11-01). The other scenarios run with every
  change to the Bastion.

Acceptance criteria:

- The e2e job `bastion` runs the short scenarios on every push that changes `internal/bastion`, `internal/bastionmain`,
  `deploy/helm/quader-bastion`, this page or the suite's own files, and is green without running anything for any other change (the
  release's `needs` holds it); the nightly job runs all of them, the long ones in the set `bastion-long`.
- The suite is deployed and measured as [developer/e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#the-bastion-tests) says, with the decisions
  [Q-BAS-110](#q-bas-110--the-e2e-bastions-are-two-releases-of-the-chart-in-one-namespace-the-bucket-one-with-a-valkey-of-its-own) to
  [Q-BAS-114](#q-bas-114--hidden-content-in-the-suite-is-a-package-permission-the-exposure-rules-of-an-endpoint-are-not-the-bastions) where the profile cannot do
  what a row says. The second flood of the flooding-address row, which yields 30 minutes (R-BAS-037), needs the first block to expire (15 minutes) and is the
  integration tier's.
- The end-to-end run found four defects, each fixed with a test: the Bastion chart had no Sentinel credential (R-BAS-046, `secrets.valkeySentinel`); a replica did not find
  the document its peer kept (R-BAS-018, R-BAS-023: the Vary names are learned per replica); a write probe through a main installation that refuses anonymous requests
  got `401` instead of `403 read_only` (R-BAS-014, fixed on main by Q-BAS-118); and a partial reader got a `304` it had not asked for (R-BAS-023, Q-BAS-107).

## Every format

The owner's decision of 2026-11-22, after he read that a Bastion serves neither container images nor Debian: "Wieso liefert der
Bastion kein Debian oder Images, das ist doch total wichtig. Er soll alles liefern wie die Hauptinstanz." Read as: a Bastion serves the
read paths of every format a main installation serves (pull, install, `apt update` and the downloads behind them), for every format
there is and every format to come. Not meant, because other decisions of his stand: a web interface at the Bastion (Q-BAS-14), writes
through it (R-BAS-014, Q-BAS-2), and access of the Bastion to the main installation's object store (Q-BAS-10, which a working paper of
his own puts to him separately). Both exclusions this section ends were deferrals of the development agent
([formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md#q-oci-23--no-exposure-rules-and-no-bastion-for-the-format-in-this-phase) Q-OCI-23,
[formats/debian.md](formats/debian.md#q-deb-26--no-exposure-rules-no-bastion-and-no-vulnerability-matching-for-the-format-in-this-phase) Q-DEB-26,
and [formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md#q-ans-25--no-exposure-rules-no-bastion-and-no-vulnerability-matching-for-the-format-in-this-phase)
Q-ANS-25 by the same reasoning), each argued from the exposure rules of an endpoint, which a Bastion on the default endpoint does not
meet (Q-BAS-4, Q-BAS-114).

Status: specified on 2026-11-22 by the planner in the owner's absence. Built on 2026-11-22: the two contracts and kit check 19
(package A of [developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#work-packages-and-what-they-own)): `catalog.Facts.Bastion` and the core's
two header lists, check 19 over every format (R-BAS-058), and the interface at version 4 with the handshake's format table and
bound repository, `Quader-Bastion-Counted` and the registry token's form and anonymous reading (the wire of R-BAS-052, R-BAS-057 and
R-BAS-059). Built the same day, the main installation's side (package B): the backstop admits `/v2/`, the token service and the catalog
tell the marking their kind, a write below `/v2/` is refused with the image prefix (R-BAS-051's main side); a registry token's shape is
capped at `partial` at the marking and the check, the check presents a registry token below `/v2/`, an `insufficient_scope` `401` keeps
its subject (R-BAS-052's main side); the six withdrawals are `content` entries of the feed (R-BAS-055's feed); the handshake carries the
format table and the bound repository (R-BAS-057's main side); the marking says `Quader-Bastion-Counted` (R-BAS-059's main side).
Built the same day, the Bastion's side (package C): the registry root as a family of the Bastion with its core routes and the
distribution's error shape, registry tokens, the content address `"sha256:<hex>"`, the replay of the core's representation headers and
the format's declared ones, `If-Modified-Since` from an entry, the format's rate-limit status, the format table and the bound repository
on the link, ranged misses that stream and callers that follow a running fill, the wait for another replica's fill up to
`bastion.cache.fill_wait_max`, shared documents above the memory bound spooled by their content address, and the report of every serve
of an entry the main installation counted (R-BAS-050 to R-BAS-054, R-BAS-056, R-BAS-057, R-BAS-059's reporting). Built the same day, the
client case on kind and the manual (package D, R-BAS-060): `TestOCI_R_BAS_051_ThroughABastion` in the set `oci` pulls an image through a Bastion
release of the leg with Docker, Podman and a pod's kubelet, and the manual says that a Bastion serves every format
([Q-BAS-204](#q-bas-204--the-set-oci-runs-in-a-profile-of-its-own-that-carries-the-main-installations-side-of-its-bastion) to
[Q-BAS-207](#q-bas-207--the-case-runs-on-a-push-that-changes-ocis-own-paths-and-in-the-nightly)). The
main side's tests carried the decisions' IDs while the Bastion's side was not built (a test named by a requirement would have counted it
as implemented before then); with both sides built they carry the requirements' IDs, as every Go test does. Two
points the table below left unverified were established by the builder with a test: the shape resolver cannot see a registry token's
grant (`authz.Subject` has no member for it, `TestR_BAS_080_TheDecisionPointDoesNotSeeTheGrant`), and the token service of a forward checks
`service` against the Bastion's host (`TestR_BAS_051_ABastionsHostReachesTheTokenServicesServiceCheck`). The decisions are
[Q-BAS-165](#q-bas-165--the-registry-root-is-a-path-family-of-the-bastion-at-its-own-host-root) to
[Q-BAS-180](#q-bas-180--the-tests-of-the-feature-each-behaviour-once-at-the-cheapest-tier-and-one-client-case-in-the-formats-own-set)
and the builders' [Q-BAS-181](#q-bas-181--the-cores-representation-and-per-request-headers-are-two-lists-of-the-catalog-and-the-content-headers-of-r-arch-007-are-representation-headers)
to [Q-BAS-190](#q-bas-190--the-checks-paths-count-as-served-on-every-replica)
