### R-BAS-050 · Every format's read paths at the Bastion's host
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

- A Bastion serves the read paths of every format of the main installation, exactly as the main installation's default endpoint
  serves them: `/api/<format>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…` of every format with routes below its prefix (npm, NuGet, Debian, Ansible
  Galaxy, the ClamAV definitions, and every format to come), `/files/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…`, and the registry root `/v2/…` at the
  host root of the Bastion's `server.base_url` (R-BAS-051). On a host the main installation binds to one repository, the Bastion whose
  base URL is that host serves the bound-host prefixes of the bound repository's format (R-BAS-057).
- **What stays.** The Bastion is read-only (R-BAS-014), has no web interface (R-BAS-003), keeps its own cache and reaches the main
  installation's object store only by a link handed for one blob (R-BAS-030, R-BAS-070), and its code holds no knowledge of a format: what is particular to a format reaches it as the
  main installation's marking of a response (R-BAS-013) or as the format's facts in the handshake (R-BAS-057). The registry root is a path
  family of INV-6, like `/files/`, and the Bastion knows families, not formats.
- **A format to come** is served by every Bastion without a decision of its own when it keeps the duties of R-BAS-058, which kit check 19
  holds; a format that needs a path family INV-6 does not have, or a host root that R-BAS-057 does not cover, needs one
  ([Q-BAS-179](#q-bas-179--a-format-to-come-is-served-by-a-bastion-through-its-route-kinds-and-its-declared-facts-without-a-decision-of-its-own)).
- **Credentials of a format.** The Bastion reads what the main installation reads on the protocol family: Bearer, Basic with the token as
  the password, and the scheme Token of the Galaxy clients, which the main installation decides on per route
  ([Q-BAS-203](#q-bas-203--the-galaxy-clients-scheme-token-is-a-credential-of-the-protocol-family-keyed-apart)).
- The client setup for a Bastion (R-BAS-007) renders every format's snippets on the Bastion's base URL, the image prefix
  `<bastion host>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>` of OCI included; it does so today, before the Bastion serves `/v2/`.

Acceptance criteria:

- For every format of `internal/formats/all` with routes, a route example of each read route, addressed through the Bastion, reaches the
  read flow and is forwarded with the caller's credential; for the registry-root format at `/v2/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…`
  (`TestR_BAS_050_EveryFormatsReadRoutesReachTheReadFlow`, unit, against the engine's double of the main installation,
  [Q-BAS-201](#q-bas-201--the-engines-tests-of-every-format-run-over-the-engines-double-of-the-client)).
- The test table of R-BAS-003 holds `/v2/…` among the served families, and `/api/v1/…`, `/ui/…`, `/auth/…`, `/-/…` and `/.well-known/…`
  outside a bound host among the refused ones.

### R-BAS-051 · The registry root at a Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

The distribution API of the format `oci` (formats/oci.md R-OCI-001, R-OCI-003) is served at the Bastion's own host root, so an image
reference reads `packages.example.com/web/docker/library/nginx:1.29` *(example)* and one `docker login packages.example.com` covers every
repository ([Q-BAS-165](#q-bas-165--the-registry-root-is-a-path-family-of-the-bastion-at-its-own-host-root)).

- **Classification** (R-BAS-018 step 3). `/v2/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/<rest>` is read with the rules of `qname.ParseRegistryAddress`
  (a project or key with `%` is no name; INV-5's grammar) and the rules of Q-BAS-121 (an encoded or dot segment of the family, the project
  or the key is not classified); the addressed repository is `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`. The format is the one whose entry of the handshake's
  table says `registryRoot` (R-BAS-057); a table that names none serves nothing below `/v2/`. The core routes are `/v2` and `/v2/` (the version
  check), `/v2/_token` (the token service) and `/v2/_catalog`. Every other path below `/v2/` answers the Bastion's own `404` with
  `NAME_UNKNOWN` in the distribution's shape, without a request.
- **The version check.** Without a credential the Bastion answers it itself, `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
  realm="<base>/v2/_token",service="<host>"` of its own base URL, because the main installation answers every version check without a
  credential so (Q-OCI-20), whatever is `public`; with a credential it is forwarded and `pass`.
- **The token service** ([Q-BAS-166](#q-bas-166--the-token-service-at-a-bastion-is-the-main-installations-reached-by-a-forward)). `GET`
  and `POST /v2/_token` are forwarded with the caller's credential to the main installation's token service, which issues the registry
  token (R-OCI-004, R-OCI-005); the answer is `pass`, never kept and never collapsed, and its body is never logged. The token service
  checks `service` against the host of the response base URL, which for a recognized Bastion request is the Bastion's host (R-BAS-017).
  The Bastion reads the one credential the token service reads, for its own syntax check, slot class and limits, and keeps or logs
  nothing of it: the Basic password of a `GET`, the form's `password` of a `POST`. A `POST` is a read route that takes a body: since interface
  version 8 the format table names it (`readWithBody` of the entry with `registryRoot`, R-BAS-095) and the Bastion forwards it at once;
  up to version 7 its probe was answered `204` with `Quader-Bastion-Route: read-with-body` (R-BAS-014). The request carries the form (at most 16 KiB,
  within `bastion.main.max_forwarded_body`). A `POST` whose form holds a `password` takes an authenticated slot and the authenticated
  limits; a malformed token in it is refused `401` without a forward and counted (R-BAS-036). The anonymous `GET` of a token
  follows R-BAS-019: refused `401` by the Bastion itself while `anonymousReads` is false. The Bastion's own challenge below `/v2/` names no
  scope ([Q-BAS-196](#q-bas-196--the-bastions-own-registry-challenge-names-no-scope)).
- **The catalog** is forwarded per request and `pass` (R-OCI-017 decides its names per caller).
- **The main installation's side.** A forward below `/v2/` goes to `bastion.main.packages_url` like every forward, since the role
  `packages` serves the registry root, its token service included (R-HA-041, R-OCI-003). The backstop of Q-BAS-115 admits `/v2/…` as a
  family a Bastion forwards, judged on the routing segments as today; the token service and the catalog tell the marking stage their kind before they authenticate or read a body: the
  token service `Volatile` with the action `read` (a read route that takes a body for `POST`), the catalog `Volatile` with `read`. The
  repository routes below `/v2/` are marked by the dispatcher as every format route is. The refusal of a write names the main
  installation's image prefix of the repository (`quader.example.com/web/docker-local`) for the format that declares the registry root,
  and the protocol base path for every other format. *Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-094, R-BAS-095, R-BAS-099):* an anonymous `GET` or
  `POST /v2/_token` is answered by the Bastion itself ([Q-BAS-335](#q-bas-335--the-bastion-answers-an-anonymous-token-request-itself)); a
  `POST` with a credential is a read route with a body of the format table's `readWithBody` and is forwarded without a probe; a write
  below `/v2/` is the Bastion's own `403 read_only` in the distribution's shape and names no image prefix. *Built by E16:* the refusal
  names no image prefix and no protocol base path, for every format (R-BAS-099 row 1); `bastionmark.Options.RegistryRoot` and `MainURL`
  are gone. *Built by E14a:* an anonymous `GET` or `POST` of the token service is answered by the Bastion (`answerAnonymousToken` in
  [registry.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/registry.go)); an anonymous `HEAD` is the token service's `405` there
  ([Q-BAS-436](#q-bas-436--an-anonymous-token-request-is-one-without-a-credential-and-the-bastion-reads-neither-its-scope-nor-its-service)). *Today, until E15
  lands:* a token request with a credential is forwarded, and a `POST` with one is probed first. *Built on 2026-11-22 (package B):* `forwardablePath` admits `/v2` and `/v2/…`
  ([recognize.go](../../internal/bastionmain/recognize.go)); the token service and the catalog call the marking's observer through
  `tellRoute` ([bastion.go](../../internal/api/registry/bastion.go)) only for the methods they answer, so a probe of any other method gets the
  route's own `405` ([Q-BAS-189](#q-bas-189--the-core-routes-below-v2-tell-the-marking-their-kind-only-for-the-methods-they-answer)); the
  version check answers `GET` and `HEAD` only and decides nothing, so it tells nothing; a token answer names the caller the token service
  accepted, which the chain's stage never sees ([Q-BAS-187](#q-bas-187--a-token-answer-names-the-caller-the-token-service-accepted)).
- **Answers of the Bastion's own** below `/v2/` carry `Docker-Distribution-API-Version: registry/2.0` and the distribution's error body
  (R-BAS-029, Q-BAS-169).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, against the engine's double, Q-BAS-201): `GET /v2/` without a credential answers `401` with the Bearer challenge on the
  Bastion's host and the API version header, and `maintest` records no request; with a token it is forwarded; `GET /v2/_token?…` with
  Basic credentials is forwarded with the header, its `200` body reaches the client and is not in the cache, the shared store or the
  request log; `GET /v2/web/docker` and `/v2/%77eb/docker/app/manifests/1` answer `404` `NAME_UNKNOWN` without a request
  (`TestR_BAS_051_TheRegistryRootIsAPathFamilyOfTheBastion`).
- Unit (`internal/bastionmain`): `forwardablePath` admits `/v2/web/docker/app/manifests/1`, `/v2/_token` and `/v2/` and still refuses
  `/api/%76%31/tokens`; the probe of `POST /v2/_token` answers `403` (since interface version 8, a probe of a read route is refused) and the probe of `POST /v2/web/docker-local/app/blobs/uploads/`
  answers `403` `DENIED` in the distribution's shape whose message is the read-only sentence of R-BAS-099 row 1
  (`TestR_BAS_051_TheMainInstallationForwardsTheRegistryRoot`). *As built, in three packages, since the domain package of the backstop
  imports neither the token service nor a format's error shape:* the backstop in `internal/bastionmain` (`TestR_BAS_051_TheMainInstallationForwardsTheRegistryRoot`), the refusal of
  three writes below `/v2/` through the dispatcher's registry handler and OCI's error shape in `internal/api/bastionmark`
  (`TestR_BAS_051_AWriteBelowTheRegistryRootNamesNoAddress`), and the token service's and the catalog's probes, the token answer's
  subject and the service check of a forward in `internal/api/registry` (`TestR_BAS_051_TheTokenServiceAndTheCatalogTellTheMarkingTheirKind`,
  `TestR_BAS_051_ABastionsHostReachesTheTokenServicesServiceCheck`).
- Integration (area `bastion`, R-BAS-060): the sequence of a `docker login` and a `docker pull` replayed by Go's client through an
  in-process Bastion (ping, challenge, `GET` token with Basic, manifest by tag, manifest by digest, two blobs) and containerd's (`HEAD` of the
  tag, `POST` token with the form, index by digest, manifest by digest, blobs) both succeed cold and warm
  (`TestR_BAS_051_R_BAS_053_ADockerAndAContainerdPullThroughABastion`; containerd's replay reads a single-platform manifest by digest, no
  index).

### R-BAS-052 · Registry tokens at the Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-025

- **A credential of its own.** Below `/v2/` the Bastion accepts a registry token (`qdr_rgt_`, R-OCI-005) as `Authorization: Bearer`, as at
  the main installation (R-AUTH-001); on any other family it is an unknown prefix (`401`, counted). It has no checksum and the Bastion
  holds no key ring, so its syntax is checked by form only: the prefix, base64url, one `.`, base64url, at most 4 KiB; a token outside the
  form answers `401 invalid_token` with the registry's challenge and `error="invalid_token"` without a request and counts as a failed
  authentication (R-BAS-036). Its answers are keyed by the SHA-256 of the string like every token's (R-BAS-019)
  ([Q-BAS-167](#q-bas-167--a-registry-token-is-checked-by-the-main-installation-and-its-read-shape-is-at-most-partial)). The form is
  `iface.RegistryTokenWellFormed`, both parts decoded as the token service decodes them
  ([Q-BAS-185](#q-bas-185--a-registry-tokens-form-is-checked-as-the-token-service-decodes-it-and-the-anonymous-principal-is-its-claim-a)).
- **Checked by the main installation.** A forward carries it unchanged; the check of R-BAS-011 hands a credential with the prefix
  `qdr_rgt_` to the authentication stage on a path below `/v2/` (`/v2/bastion-check`, served by no route), every other credential on
  `/api/bastion-check` as today, so the stage verifies the MAC, the expiry, the endpoint and the token behind it (R-OCI-005).
- **Its read shape on the repository is at most `partial`**, at the marking (R-BAS-013) and at the check: a grant names image names and
  never a whole repository, and the decision point does not see the grant, which the enforcement point in front of `/v2/` checks
  (Q-OCI-56). A `full` answer on the repository would let a token granted one image read every cached image of the repository from the
  Bastion. So a registry token is never served a negative entry. A Quader token presented directly below `/v2/` (Basic or Bearer,
  R-OCI-004) is a token like any other and may be `full`. The Bastion records at most `partial` on the repository for a registry token
  whatever the main installation marks
  ([Q-BAS-198](#q-bas-198--the-bastion-caps-a-registry-tokens-shape-and-reads-insufficient_scope-itself)).
- **Its read shape on a package of its grant may be `full`** (*amended on 2026-11-22, built on 2026-11-23:* R-BAS-080 to R-BAS-085,
  [Q-BAS-167](#q-bas-167--a-registry-token-is-checked-by-the-main-installation-and-its-read-shape-is-at-most-partial) option (b)). The
  main installation limits the package shape of a credential with a registry grant to the pairs (repository, image) its grant allows to
  pull (`Grant.Allows`), at the marking and at the check. The Bastion records a package answer `full` for a registry token only when the
  token's grant, read from its claims without verifying them (the claim `g`, entries `{r, n, a}` with pull as bit 1, payload version 1,
  `iface.RegistryTokenGrant`), names that repository and package with pull; otherwise it records `partial`, whatever the main
  installation marks ([Q-BAS-246](#q-bas-246--the-bastions-own-guard-for-registry-tokens)). Trusting the unverified grant can only lower
  what is read. A token granted one image is then served that image's cached tag documents, manifests, blobs, tags list and cosign tags
  without a request once one check has given it the package answer (R-BAS-085), and every other image's after a request to the main
  installation; what a pull still costs is
  [H-1242](#h-1242--every-pull-with-a-registry-token-costs-the-main-installation-its-token-request-and-one-check).
- **An anonymous registry token is the anonymous caller** ([Q-BAS-168](#q-bas-168--an-anonymous-registry-token-is-the-anonymous-caller-at-the-bastion)).
  The Bastion decodes the payload of R-OCI-005 (`1:<key id>:<claims>`) without verifying it, and a token whose claims name the anonymous
  principal is dropped from the request: its answers are those of `anonymous` (R-BAS-019), shared by every anonymous caller, and it is
  forwarded without `Authorization`, which the main installation serves as an anonymous request where artifacts are `public` (R-OCI-004
  step 1). Trusting the unverified bit can only lower what is read, because a client can always send no credential. A payload that does
  not decode is a registry token like any other. The reading is `iface.RegistryTokenAnonymous`: the member `a` true in the claims of
  payload version 1 (Q-BAS-185).
- *Revised on 2026-11-26 ([Q-BAS-339](#q-bas-339--a-registry-token-reads-only-its-anonymity-its-expiry-and-its-grant)):* the three readers (`RegistryTokenAnonymous`, `RegistryTokenExpiry`,
  `RegistryTokenGrant`) read payload versions 1 and 2, and the main installation issues version 2, whose only readable claims are `a`, `exp`
  and `g`; an anonymous caller of a Bastion receives the Bastion's own token (R-BAS-094). *Built by E14a:* the
  anonymous caller's token is the Bastion's. *Today, until E7 and E17 land:* the readers read version 1, and the main installation's
  tokens carry every claim readable.
- **Its expiry is its own.** The subject the marking and the check report for a registry token carries the registry token's expiry
  (`auth.Credential.ExpiresAt` already is that), so no answer outlives it (R-BAS-020 rule 2). A request with a registry token past its
  expiry is answered `401` with the registry's challenge and `error="invalid_token"` by the Bastion, and is not counted as a failed
  authentication: an expired registry token is the end of its life, which a client answers with a new token request. The expiry is the
  member `exp` of the token's claims, read without verifying them (`iface.RegistryTokenExpiry`), so every replica knows it, also one that
  never saw the token; trusting it can only refuse
  ([Q-BAS-252](#q-bas-252--option-b-of-q-bas-202-is-bundled), which replaced the expiry remembered per replica of
  [Q-BAS-202](#q-bas-202--a-registry-tokens-expiry-is-the-one-the-main-installation-reported-remembered-per-replica) on 2026-11-23).
- **`insufficient_scope` is no statement about the credential.** A `401` whose challenge carries `error="insufficient_scope"` is marked
  with the subject the authentication stage accepted, not `invalid`; the Bastion replays it, keeps no answer for it and counts no failed
  authentication, also when a main installation marks it `invalid` (Q-BAS-198). Every other `401` stays `invalid` (Q-BAS-71, H-442).
- *Built on 2026-11-22, the main installation's side (package B):* the cap is `bastionmain.CapRegistryShape`, applied by the marking to
  every caller whose credential carries a grant (an anonymous registry token included) and by the check
  ([shape.go](../../internal/bastionmain/shape.go), [mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go),
  [bastion_check_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_check_api.go)); the challenge is read at the status line (`insufficientScope`). The
  check's stage counts its two paths as served on every replica, so a replica of the role `api`, which answers the interface but serves
  no package family, verifies a registry token too ([Q-BAS-190](#q-bas-190--the-checks-paths-count-as-served-on-every-replica)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`): a well-formed registry token is forwarded below `/v2/` and refused `401` without a request on
  `/api/npm/…`; `qdr_rgt_` followed by `!!` or 5 KiB answers `401` without a request and counts once; an anonymous registry token (claims
  built by the test with `registrytoken`'s encoder and a key the Bastion does not have) is forwarded without `Authorization` and its
  answers are `anonymous`'s; a token past the expiry its claims name answers `401` and counts nothing, on the replica that saw it and on one
  that never did; an `insufficient_scope` `401` counts nothing and keeps no `invalid` answer (`TestR_BAS_052_RegistryTokensAtTheBastion`).
- Unit (`internal/api/bastionmark`, `internal/api/v1`): the marking of a request with a registry token whose principal reads the whole
  repository says `partial`, and the check's answer for it too; the check of a registry token answers `token` with the registry token's
  expiry, and of a Quader token as before; an `insufficient_scope` `401` is marked with the token's subject
  (`TestR_BAS_052_ARegistryTokensShapeIsAtMostPartial`, `TestR_BAS_052_TheCheckPresentsARegistryTokenBelowTheRegistryRoot`). *As built:* `TestR_BAS_052_ARegistryTokensShapeIsAtMostPartial`,
  `TestR_BAS_080_TheDecisionPointDoesNotSeeTheGrant`, `TestR_BAS_052_InsufficientScopeIsNoStatementAboutTheCredential`
  (`internal/api/bastionmark`), `TestR_BAS_052_TheCheckPresentsARegistryTokenBelowTheRegistryRoot` (`internal/api/v1`, through the real
  authentication stage with a registry token issued by the real signer, and one of another key, which is `invalid`), and
  `TestR_BAS_052_TheCheckDecidesItsPathsAsAReplicaThatServesThePackageFamilies` (`internal/app`).

### R-BAS-053 · Container images in the Bastion's cache
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

What a Bastion keeps of the registry follows from the kinds of the format's routes (formats/oci.md R-OCI-007, R-OCI-009 to R-OCI-017;
[routes.go](../../internal/formats/oci/routes.go)), with no rule of its own for the format:

| Route | Kind | At the Bastion |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest by tag (`GET`, `HEAD …/manifests/<tag>`) | `Metadata` | a document: shared for a `full` reader, the caller's private copy otherwise; revalidated after `metadata_revalidate_after`, so a moved tag reaches the Bastion within the period ([H-384](#h-384--a-version-newly-published-appears-at-the-bastion-only-after-the-metadata-period)). A `HEAD` of the tag fills the document by a `GET` and is answered from it (R-BAS-021, Q-BAS-475; true since 2026-11-26, before which only a `GET` kept it) |
| Manifest by digest, blob (`GET`, `HEAD`) | `Download` | an artifact, kept under its content address, immutable |
| Tags list | `Metadata` | a document, with its `Link` for the next page |
| Referrers | `Volatile` | `pass`: forwarded per request, never kept, so a signature or an attestation pushed at the main installation is listed through a Bastion at once |
| Catalog, token service, version check | core | R-BAS-051 |

- **Signatures and attestations** are manifests and blobs like any other (signatures.md R-SIG-023, R-SIG-024): the referrers list is
  `pass`, a signature's or an attestation's manifest by digest and its blobs are artifacts, and a cosign tag `sha256-<hex>.sig` or
  `.att` is a tag's document; Quader's own receipt attestation (R-SIG-054) is a referrer the main installation lists. `cosign verify`
  and `notation verify` through a Bastion read what they read at the main installation.

- **Content address.** The registry's `ETag` `"sha256:<hex>"` is a content address (R-BAS-022); the conditional request of the Bastion
  sends it back as given, which the format compares in both spellings (`storedValidators` in
  [handlers_manifest.go](../../internal/formats/oci/handlers_manifest.go)).
- **Headers.** A cached answer replays the format's declared headers besides the representation headers: `Docker-Content-Digest`,
  `Docker-Distribution-API-Version`, `OCI-Filters-Applied` and `Link` (R-BAS-057,
  [Q-BAS-171](#q-bas-171--a-cached-answer-replays-the-headers-its-format-declares-held-by-the-kit)), so a `HEAD` of a tag answered from
  the cache tells containerd the digest it resolves, and a tags list served from the cache still pages.
- **`HEAD`, `Range`, `If-None-Match`** are answered from the entry (R-BAS-022); a layer download that a drain cut is resumed with
  `Range` on another replica.
- **The gates of the main installation.** The signature gate (signatures.md R-SIG-063, R-SIG-064), the image block of the vulnerability
  scanning (vulnerability-scanning.md R-VULN-033 to R-VULN-037) and the malware gate (malware-scanning.md R-MAL-018) judge a request at
  the main installation: a fill, a conditional request, a check. Their `403 DENIED` is kept as the caller's URL answer, their `503` with
  `Retry-After` (a signature or a scan pending) is passed and kept nowhere. An entry the Bastion holds is revalidated when a `content`
  entry of its repository arrives (the gates' events in R-BAS-015's table: R-VULN-013, R-MAL-021, R-MAL-026, R-SIG-070, R-SIG-075) and
  otherwise within `artifact_revalidate_after` ([H-385](#h-385--a-withdrawal-the-feed-does-not-carry-reaches-the-bastion-within-the-artifact-revalidation-period),
  [H-1102](#h-1102--the-bastion-serves-what-it-cached-for-up-to-ten-minutes-after-the-switch-is-turned-on)). The signature gate judges
  manifests and not blobs at the main installation (R-OCI-009), and so a blob a caller may read stays servable from the Bastion after
  its manifest is refused, as it is at the main installation.
- **A scan token** (R-OCI-037) is never accepted by a Bastion: it is valid on the scan listener only (R-EP-010), and the Bastion's
  forward reaches the default endpoint.
- **Writes.** `docker push` through a Bastion: its `HEAD` requests for blobs are reads; the `POST` that starts an upload is refused by
  the Bastion itself `403` `DENIED` with the read-only sentence, which names no image prefix (R-BAS-095, R-BAS-099 row 1).

Acceptance criteria:

- Integration (area `bastion`): with an image of one config and one layer of 1 KiB each pushed to `web/docker-local` through the main
  installation, a pull through the Bastion with a user's registry token fills the manifest by digest and both blobs, a second pull with a
  new registry token sends one check besides the token step, no conditional request and no artifact bytes (R-BAS-085; until 2026-11-23
  one conditional request per artifact), a `HEAD` of the tag answered from the cache for a
  direct Quader token carries `Docker-Content-Digest`, and a tags list of 3 tags with `n=2` served from the cache carries its `Link`
  (`TestR_BAS_051_R_BAS_053_ADockerAndAContainerdPullThroughABastion`, with R-BAS-051's replays; a second registry token is a second's
  wait away, because a token names the second it was issued in and the same token's URL answers serve without a request).
- Integration: an image whose manifest is deleted at the main installation answers `404` through the Bastion within the feed's bound after
  it was served warm (`TestR_BAS_053_AWithdrawnImageIsRefusedWithinTheFeedsBound`). *As built:* the block of the vulnerability scanning
  reaches a Bastion through the same `content` entry kind (R-BAS-015's table); its own case needs the scanning's findings, which the
  stack of this suite does not hold, and is not built.

### R-BAS-054 · Large artifacts
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Images bring layers of gigabytes. The fill of R-BAS-021 stays: spooled at the main installation's speed, verified against its content
address, committed, the last 64 KiB of every transfer withheld until then. Three things change
([Q-BAS-172](#q-bas-172--a-ranged-miss-streams-from-the-spool-and-a-caller-of-a-running-fill-follows-it-on-its-own-permission)):

- **A ranged miss streams.** A caller's `Range` on a miss is served from the spool as it grows past the range's start, with the range's
  last 64 KiB withheld until the fill is verified and committed (a range is verified by reading the object to its end, Q-BAS-82),
  instead of after the whole fill (`waitFill` before). A range of at most 64 KiB is therefore served whole after the commit
  ([Q-BAS-197](#q-bas-197--a-range-shorter-than-the-withheld-tail-is-served-after-the-commit)). The caller's `If-None-Match`,
  `If-Modified-Since` and `If-Range` are decided at once from the answer's validator, date and length.
- **A second caller follows the running fill.** A caller of a cache key whose artifact fill runs on its replica gets its own permission
  first (a usable `full` answer, or a conditional request naming the fill's content address answered `304`; a refusal is replayed) and
  is then served from the spool like the leader's client, instead of waiting 30 s and being answered `503 busy`. A registry-token
  caller of a layer that fifty pods ask for at once therefore costs one transfer and fifty conditional requests. *Amended on 2026-11-22,
  built on 2026-11-23 (R-BAS-085):* a usable `full` answer also means a package answer `full` on the fill's package, which the leader's
  marking supplies, so fifty pods whose registry tokens each hold such an answer follow the fill without a request; a token that has none
  yet still pays its one request (a check or a conditional request, R-BAS-022).
- **Across replicas** (the bucket backend with Valkey), a caller whose replica finds another replica's fetch lock waits while the holder
  keeps extending the lock, up to `bastion.cache.fill_wait_max`, sending nothing, then decides again, which is a hit once the other fill
  committed, or fetches itself ([H-1245](#h-1245--a-caller-on-another-replica-waits-for-a-running-fill-without-a-byte-up-to-fill_wait_max)).
- A fill holds its budget slot until the main installation's body ends ([H-1244](#h-1244--cold-fills-of-large-blobs-hold-budget-slots-and-spool-for-the-length-of-their-transfer));
  a fill read by a handover holds it for the handover's answer only (R-BAS-074). *Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-097):* a fill is paced
  by the registration's throughput, so at the cap it holds its slot and its spool longer. *Built by E10 (2026-11-26);* the time a fill
  waits for the cap is no stall.
  The defaults of `max_object_bytes` and `spool_max_bytes` (2 GiB each) stay; a layer above them is passed through on every request, and
  the manual's sizing of the cache names images.

```yaml
bastion:
  cache:
    fill_wait_max: 10m                  # default (proposed); 30s to 1h; how long a replica waits for another replica's fill
```

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, a blob of 256 KiB with the engine's double of the main installation sending it in 16 KiB steps, each
  released by the test): a caller's `bytes=0-131071` receives its first byte before the fill ends and its last 64 KiB after the commit
  (Q-BAS-197); a second caller of the running fill, a partial reader, receives the whole blob from the spool with one conditional request
  and no second transfer, and its serve is reported; with a fill that fails its digest both transfers are cut
  (`TestR_BAS_054_LargeArtifacts`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, a blob of 16 KiB whose first transfer breaks off after 4 KiB and whose close the test holds): only a
  caller of a running fill follows it. A fill that fails ends its flight before its callers are cut, so a caller that comes after the
  failure, while the fill still closes its source, is a miss of its own and receives the whole blob with a second transfer
  (`TestR_BAS_054_ACallerAfterAFailedFillIsAMissOfItsOwn`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, two engines on one shared state and one cache): a replica that meets another's lock waits while it is
  held, sending nothing, and serves the committed entry afterwards; past `fill_wait_max` it fetches itself
  (`TestR_BAS_054_AReplicaWaitsForAnotherReplicasFill`).

### R-BAS-055 · Debian through a Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

- **Signed indexes pass unchanged.** The Bastion rewrites no body (R-BAS-017), so `InRelease`, `Release`, `Release.gpg` and the indexes
  reach the client as the main installation signed them (a local or virtual repository's own key, R-DEB-016) or as the upstream signed
  them (a remote, R-DEB-019), and the client verifies them with the key of its source line (R-DEB-029).
- **What is kept** follows the route kinds of formats/debian.md R-DEB-003: the release documents and the indexes are `Metadata`, and
  `signing-key.asc` is `Computed` (documents); by-hash files and pool files are `Download` (artifacts). An index path names no package
  (Q-DEB-20), so only a reader without package patterns is `full` on a Debian repository and is served the shared documents; a reader
  narrowed to package names reads its package files, as at the main installation.
- **Consistency of an `apt update`** ([Q-BAS-174](#q-bas-174--debian-the-release-documents-are-documents-of-the-metadata-period-and-by-hash-keeps-an-apt-update-consistent)).
  A release document is kept for the metadata period like every document. Every `Release` Quader writes says `Acquire-By-Hash: yes`
  (R-DEB-011), and so do the releases of the Debian and Ubuntu archives, so APT fetches every index by the SHA-256 the `InRelease` it
  read names; those files are immutable artifacts, and the main installation keeps them for `deb.by_hash_keep` and at least three
  generations (R-DEB-012), longer than the period. An `apt update` that meets an `InRelease` up to a period old therefore reads exactly
  the indexes it names. The plain path of an index (an upstream without by-hash, a flat repository) can disagree with that `InRelease`
  for up to the period ([H-1243](#h-1243--a-plain-index-path-of-a-debian-remote-without-by-hash-can-disagree-with-the-inrelease-a-bastion-serves)).
- **Unreachable.** While the main installation is unreachable an `InRelease` is served for the grace period, and a by-hash file it names
  that the Bastion has not cached answers `503`; APT keeps its previous list for that index.
- **Conditionals.** APT's `If-Modified-Since` on a release document is answered from the entry (R-BAS-022, R-BAS-056).
- **The feed.** `deb.package.deleted`, `deb.coordinates.removed`, `deb.signing_key.promoted` and `deb.signing_key.retired` are `content`
  entries (R-BAS-015, Q-BAS-175): a withheld package, a package taken out of a suite, a new primary key and a withdrawn key end the
  service of what the Bastion holds of the repository and of the virtual repositories over it at once. *Built on 2026-11-22 (package B),
  with `oci.manifest.deleted` and `ansible.version.deleted`: each is mapped from the event's repository like `package.deleted`
  (`mappers` in [feed.go](../../internal/bastionmain/feed.go)); every one of the six names its repository by its qualified name (read in the
  producers of `internal/formatdata`).*
- **A compromised Bastion** can serve an older genuine `InRelease` of a repository whose release carries no `Valid-Until`
  ([H-1246](#h-1246--a-compromised-bastion-can-serve-an-older-genuine-document-of-a-repository)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Integration (area `bastion`): a local repository `web/apt` with one package of 1 KiB, its index built (R-DEB-014's wait), through the
  Bastion with a token without package patterns: `InRelease`, the by-hash `Packages.gz` it names and the pool file are served cold and
  warm, the `InRelease` verifies with `signing-key.asc` read through the Bastion; after a second upload and build, a `GET` of the
  first generation's by-hash file still answers `200`; after `DELETE` of the package file a `content` entry ends the service of the
  cached pool file within the feed's bound (`TestR_BAS_055_DebianThroughABastion`).
- Unit (`internal/bastionmain`): the four `deb.*` events, `oci.manifest.deleted` and `ansible.version.deleted` map to `content` for the
  repository and its virtual repositories; `ansible.tombstone.cleared` maps to none with its reason; every journaled event stays
  classified (`TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`).

### R-BAS-056 · The ClamAV definitions through a Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **Served like every repository.** The endpoint `/api/clamav/upstream/clamav/…` (formats/clamav.md R-CLAMAV-004) is served through a
  Bastion to the anonymous caller while the repository is `public` and **ClamAV definition updates** is on, and to a token whose subject
  may read it; while the switch is off the main installation answers `404` and so does the Bastion. A ClamAV installation outside the
  company names the Bastion's address in `PrivateMirror`.
- **No client certificate through a Bastion** ([Q-BAS-176](#q-bas-176--the-clamav-definitions-through-a-bastion-anonymous-and-tokens-no-client-certificate)).
  The certificate subject exists only on an endpoint whose TLS ends at Quader and verifies the chain (R-CLAMAV-010); a Bastion's forward
  reaches the default endpoint, which admits no certificates, and Quader never reads a certificate from a header (Q-CLAMAV-8). The
  certificate admission stays a further endpoint of the main installation ([H-1247](#h-1247--the-certificate-admission-of-the-clamav-definitions-does-not-reach-a-bastion)).
- **Containers above 64 MiB are kept.** The routes are `Metadata` (Q-CLAMAV-2), so a container is a document; a container above the
  memory bound of documents is spooled by its content address (R-BAS-021, Q-BAS-173) instead of passed through to every `freshclam`.
- **`freshclam`'s check is answered from the cache.** `Range: bytes=0-511` with `If-Modified-Since` is `304` when the entry's
  `Last-Modified` is not after the date sent, and `206` with the 512 bytes otherwise (R-BAS-022).
- **Never `429`.** The format's facts name `503` for a rate limit (R-BAS-057), so the Bastion's own refusals of its limits, its block
  list and its failed-authentication timeout on the format's family are `503` with `Retry-After` (R-BAS-029); a `403` a client of the
  format receives through a Bastion is only ever the main installation's own answer, which renders none (R-CLAMAV-005).

Acceptance criteria:

- Integration (area `bastion`, containers of a few hundred bytes as in R-CLAMAV-009): `freshclam`'s requests replayed by Go's client
  through the Bastion: `daily.cvd` with `Range: bytes=0-511` cold (`206`), the whole file (`200`), the check again with the `Last-Modified`
  it was given (`304` from the Bastion, no request to the main installation within the metadata period; the endpoint's `Last-Modified` is
  the time of the commit, not the build time); an address over the Bastion's request limit
  is answered `503` with `Retry-After` on `/api/clamav/…` and `429` on `/api/npm/…` (`TestR_BAS_056_TheClamAVDefinitionsThroughABastion`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`): the Bastion's own refusals of its limits and its block list on `/api/clamav/…` are `503` with
  `Retry-After` and on `/api/npm/…` `429`; `Range: bytes=0-511` with `If-Modified-Since` is answered `304` from the entry when it is not
  newer and `206` with the 512 bytes otherwise, without a request (`TestR_BAS_056_TheFormatsRateLimitStatusAndIfModifiedSince`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`): the memory bound of documents is a parameter the test sets to 64 KiB, so no test holds 64 MiB; a
  shared document of 100 KiB with a content-address `ETag` is spooled, verified and served from the cache, and one without such an
  `ETag` is passed through (`TestR_BAS_021_AShareableDocumentAboveTheMemoryBoundIsSpooled`).

### R-BAS-057 · Format facts at the Bastion: the handshake's format table and bound hosts
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

- **The format table** ([Q-BAS-170](#q-bas-170--a-formats-facts-reach-the-bastion-in-the-handshake)). The handshake (R-BAS-010) gains
  `formats`, one entry per registered format with routes, and `boundRepository`:

```json
{
  "formats": [
    {"id": "npm", "registryRoot": false, "replayHeaders": ["Npm-Notice"], "rateLimitedStatus": 429, "retryAfterMaxSeconds": 0, "boundPrefixes": []},
    {"id": "nuget", "registryRoot": false, "replayHeaders": [], "rateLimitedStatus": 429, "retryAfterMaxSeconds": 30, "boundPrefixes": []},
    {"id": "oci", "registryRoot": true,
     "replayHeaders": ["Docker-Content-Digest", "Docker-Distribution-Api-Version", "Oci-Filters-Applied", "Link"],
     "rateLimitedStatus": 429, "retryAfterMaxSeconds": 0, "boundPrefixes": ["/v2/"]},
    {"id": "clamav", "registryRoot": false, "replayHeaders": [], "rateLimitedStatus": 503, "retryAfterMaxSeconds": 0, "boundPrefixes": []}
  ],
  "boundRepository": "web/docker-hub"
}
```

*(example members, beside those of R-BAS-010)*

- `replayHeaders`, `rateLimitedStatus` and `retryAfterMaxSeconds` are `catalog.Facts.Bastion` of the format (R-BAS-058;
  `rateLimitedStatus` is `Bastion.RateLimited()`, 429 where nothing is declared; `retryAfterMaxSeconds` is `Bastion.RetryAfterMax` in
  seconds, 0 where the format tells its clients the true wait, R-BAS-091); `registryRoot` is `catalog.Facts.RegistryRoot`; `boundPrefixes` are the
  literal bound-host patterns of the format (endpoints.md R-EP-006), `catalog.Facts.BoundPrefixes()`, derived from the registry root
  ([Q-BAS-183](#q-bas-183--the-bound-host-prefixes-are-derived-from-the-registry-root-not-declared)). The interface's types are
  `iface.HandshakeFormats` and `iface.HandshakeFormat` ([wire.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/wire.go)). The
  Bastion keeps the table until the next handshake; a format the table does not name gets the defaults (no replay headers, `429`,
  the true wait).
  A table that fails the interface's rules (`HandshakeFormats.Validate`) fails the handshake
  ([Q-BAS-199](#q-bas-199--a-format-table-the-bastion-cannot-rely-on-fails-the-handshake)).
  The Bastion knows the format of a request from its family: the format segment of `/api/<format>/`, the format whose entry says
  `registryRoot` for `/v2/`, none for `/files/`.
- **Bound hosts** ([Q-BAS-178](#q-bas-178--a-host-the-main-installation-binds-is-served-by-a-bastion-whose-base-url-is-that-host)).
  `boundRepository` is the qualified name the default endpoint's `host_roots` binds the Bastion's host to (R-EP-006), absent when it
  binds none. A Bastion with a bound repository classifies a path that matches a bound-host prefix of that repository's format as that
  repository (`/v2/library/alpine/manifests/3` is `web/docker-hub`, image `library/alpine`); every path below `/v2/` but the core routes
  is that repository, as the main installation's dispatcher reads it (R-OCI-029,
  [Q-BAS-195](#q-bas-195--on-a-bound-host-every-path-below-v2-but-the-core-routes-is-the-bound-repository-as-the-main-installation-reads-it)), so a Docker Engine with
  `registry-mirrors: ["https://mirror-bastion.example.com"]` *(example)* pulls through it (R-OCI-029). A Docker Engine mirror through
  Bastions is one release of the chart per bound host. A binding changed at the main installation reaches the Bastion at its next
  handshake ([H-1248](#h-1248--a-binding-changed-at-the-main-installation-reaches-a-bastion-at-its-next-handshake)). The main installation reads the
  binding of the Bastion's host from the response base URL its re-derivation of a recognized Bastion request resolved to (the Bastion's
  address in its registration's `egress`, Q-BAS-430): the default endpoint without a host set binds by the request's own host, which for a
  forward is the main installation's (`bastionForwarded` in [wire_bastion.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion.go); found by
  `TestR_BAS_057_ABoundHostThroughABastion` and fixed with the Bastion's side).
- The members raise the interface to version 4 (R-BAS-009); `retryAfterMaxSeconds` raises it to version 7 (R-BAS-091).
- *Built on 2026-11-26 by E7 (interface version 8):* every entry carries `errorShape` and `readWithBody` (R-BAS-095), from
  `catalog.Facts.Bastion.ErrorShape` and `ReadWithBody` of the format; `BastionFormatTable` writes a declared pattern below
  `/api/<format>/{project}/{repo}` (and below `/v2/{project}/{repo}` for the format of the registry root) and adds the token service's
  `POST /v2/_token` to the entry of the registry root ([Q-BAS-353](#q-bas-353--a-format-declares-its-read-routes-with-a-body-below-the-repository-and-kit-check-19-holds-the-list-to-its-routes)). The Bastion reads `readWithBody` (`HandshakeFormat.ReadsWithBody`) to
  forward a read route with a body at once; it renders no shape yet (E15).
- *Built on 2026-11-22, the main installation's side (package B):* the table is `v1.BastionFormatTable(formats.List())`, built once by the
  composition root, one entry per format with routes in the order of the format IDs (generic, which has none, has no entry); the lists
  are empty, never null, and a replica without the table answers `"formats": []`
  ([bastion_handshake_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_handshake_api.go)). `boundRepository` is the binding as the match of `/v2/`
  reads it for the host of the handshake request, which for a Bastion is its own (R-BAS-017): a binding to a repository that does not
  exist or is not of the format that declares the registry root is no binding there and is not named
  ([Q-BAS-188](#q-bas-188--the-bound-repository-is-named-as-the-match-of-v2-reads-the-binding)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/api/v1`, `internal/bastion/link`): the handshake lists every format with routes of `internal/formats/all` with its
  facts, OCI's four headers and ClamAV's `503`; with `host_roots: {packages.example.com: web/docker-hub}` it names
  `boundRepository`; the link keeps the table and the engine reads it (`TestR_BAS_057_TheHandshakeCarriesTheFormatTable`). *As built on
  the main installation's side:* `TestR_BAS_057_TheHandshakeCarriesTheFormatTable`
  (`internal/api/v1`: the table over `internal/formats/all`, the answer validated against the OpenAPI document, an unbound and a bound
  host).
- Integration (area `bastion`): a Bastion whose host is bound to an OCI repository serves `GET /v2/library/alpine/manifests/3` from that
  repository, and `/v2/web/docker-local/library/alpine/manifests/3` on the same host names the image `web/docker-local/library/alpine` of
  the bound repository, as at the main installation (R-OCI-029, Q-BAS-195; `TestR_BAS_057_ABoundHostThroughABastion`). *As built:* the
  bound repository is a local one; the classification at the Bastion does not depend on the class, and the stub upstream would add the
  remote engine's time to a case about the binding.
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`): with `boundRepository` the paths below `/v2/` are classified as the bound repository and its shape
  answer is kept for it (`TestR_BAS_057_ABoundHostIsClassifiedAsItsRepository`).

### R-BAS-058 · What a format owes a Bastion, and kit check 19
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The contract a format keeps so that every Bastion serves it without a decision of its own
([Q-BAS-179](#q-bas-179--a-format-to-come-is-served-by-a-bastion-through-its-route-kinds-and-its-declared-facts-without-a-decision-of-its-own);
[developer/formats.md](../developer/formats.md#what-a-bastion-needs-of-a-format)):

| Duty | Why the Bastion needs it | Held by |
|---|---|---|
| A `Download` route serves immutable bytes for a path, with `Content-Length` and a strong `ETag` that is a content address (`"<hex>"` or `"sha256:<hex>"`) equal to the SHA-256 of the body | the Bastion keeps an artifact under its content address and verifies it; without one it passes the bytes through on every request | kit check 19 |
| A `Metadata` or `Computed` document is the same for every reader of the whole repository, or the route is `Volatile` | a shared document is served to every `full` reader | kit check 12 (built) |
| A document route answers a conditional request with its own validator `304` | the Bastion revalidates documents with conditional requests; a route that ignores them costs a whole transfer per revalidation | kit check 19 |
| Every response header of a content route is a representation header of the core, a header of the core's own (a request ID, a rate-limit field), or one of `catalog.Facts.Bastion.ReplayHeaders` | a cached answer replays the representation headers and the declared ones, and drops every other | kit check 19 |
| A header a client of the format needs on any answer the Bastion passes on (a refusal, a `Volatile` answer) is a representation header of the core, one of the fixed list of R-BAS-099 row 5, or one of `catalog.Facts.Bastion.ReplayHeaders` (npm declares `Npm-Notice`, the notice of an audit that left names out; NuGet `X-Nuget-Warning`, the text of a refused download `dotnet` prints, formats/nuget.md Q-SIG-241) | a forwarded answer passes an allowlist: the representation headers, the declared ones and the fixed list (R-BAS-099 row 5, [Q-BAS-425](#q-bas-425--the-headers-of-a-forwarded-answer-pass-an-allowlist-and-a-formats-need-is-a-replay-header)) | the format's author; kit check 19 holds the content routes and the refusals of a download's checks (the malware gate, the vulnerability block) that `WriteError` renders for a forward |
| `WriteError` renders its error through `errs.ProblemFor` with the request, so that the answer to a recognized forward of a Bastion names no member repository of a remote's failure, carries no request ID of the main installation and, in problem details, has the type `about:blank` | a forward's answer reaches a caller of the Bastion, who learns nothing of the main installation (R-BAS-099 rows 3, 7 and 15, [Q-BAS-428](#q-bas-428--a-forward-is-marked-on-the-requests-context-and-every-writer-of-an-error-renders-through-one-function)) | kit check 19 (through `WriteError`) |
| A rate limit of the format answers the status `catalog.Facts.Bastion.RateLimitedStatus` (429 unless declared) | the Bastion's own rate-limit refusals of the format's family take that status | kit check 19 (through `WriteError`) |
| A rate limit of the format tells the client the wait capped by `catalog.Facts.Bastion.RetryAfterMax` (the whole wait unless declared): a wait of a second as one second, a wait of a day as the cap or as a day | the Bastion's own refusals of the format's family tell the declared wait (R-BAS-091); a cap `WriteError` applies and the facts do not declare would reach the format's clients from a Bastion uncapped | kit check 19 (through `WriteError`) |
| A write has a writing kind or an action other than `read`; a read route that takes a body is `Volatile` with `read` | the main installation's backstop (R-BAS-095); until E15 the probe of R-BAS-014 | built (R-BAS-014) |
| *Built on 2026-11-26 by E7 (Q-BAS-353):* a route with a writing method whose kind is a read is listed in `catalog.Facts.Bastion.ReadWithBody`, and no entry lists a route the format does not have; the format declares `catalog.Facts.Bastion.ErrorShape`. *Built on 2026-11-26 by E15 (Q-BAS-453):* `WriteError` renders the backstop's refusal of a write in the declared shape (`problem`, `npm`, `text`, `distribution`, `galaxy`) as `errs.ReadShape` reads it | the Bastion's own refusal of a write and every answer of its own in the format's shape, and the backstop's alike (R-BAS-095, [Q-BAS-337](#q-bas-337--a-bastions-own-refusals-take-one-of-five-error-shapes-a-format-declares)) | kit check 19 |
| `absent` comes from the core's lookups | the negative cache (R-BAS-024) | built (Q-BAS-70) |
| Every rights decision of a content route is made through the host before its status line; a response that draws on packages other than the one it was decided for also decides a package-less read; a reader of only the response's package receives the same status, body and validators as a reader of the whole repository | a document marked `shared` for a reader of one package is served to every reader of that package in full (R-BAS-081, R-BAS-082) | kit check 21 (R-BAS-086) |

- **The contract's addition** (an ADR, [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table)):
  `catalog.Facts.Bastion` of the type `catalog.BastionFacts` with `ReplayHeaders []string` (canonical header names, none of the core's
  representation or per-request headers, none with the prefix `Quader-`) and `RateLimitedStatus int` (0 is 429; 429 or 503). OCI declares
  the four headers of R-BAS-053, the ClamAV definitions and Ansible Galaxy `503` (Galaxy since E15,
  [Q-BAS-451](#q-bas-451--ansible-galaxy-answers-a-rate-limit-503-because-ansible-galaxy-does-not-survive-the-retry-of-a-429)). A second addition
  ([ADR-299](../decisions.md#adr-299--the-longest-wait-a-formats-client-is-told-is-a-fact-of-the-format)): `RetryAfterMax time.Duration`
  (0 or whole seconds) with `BastionFacts.CapRetryAfter`, the longest wait the format's clients are told (R-BAS-091). NuGet and Ansible
  Galaxy declare 30 s, the `maxRetryAfter` of their `WriteError`; npm, OCI, Debian and the ClamAV definitions declare none. npm declares
  the replay header `Npm-Notice` (2026-11-26, R-BAS-099 row 5), NuGet `X-Nuget-Warning` (the day's findings of 2026-11-26, batch B:
  `dotnet` prints it for a refused download, Q-SIG-241, and its text is the forward's since W-35's P8, R-BAS-114).
- **Kit check 19** (`checks_bastion.go` of the conformance kit): over every content case, the duties above marked "kit check 19"; a
  `testformat` defect each (`DownloadWithoutContentAddress`, `UndeclaredReplayHeader`, `DocumentIgnoresConditional`,
  `RateLimitedStatusDiffers`, `CapsRetryAfterUndeclared`, `DeclaresRetryAfterCap`, `IgnoresTheForward`, `DeclaresAnotherErrorShape`,
  `UndeclaredRefusalHeader`: a header of the refusal of a download's checks a Bastion would not pass on, `downloadRefusals`). A route whose answers cannot meet a duty by design is listed in the fixture with its reason, as for the
  other checks. Runs in every format's `TestR_ARCH_010_Conformance`, without PostgreSQL.
- **As built** ([Q-BAS-181](#q-bas-181--the-cores-representation-and-per-request-headers-are-two-lists-of-the-catalog-and-the-content-headers-of-r-arch-007-are-representation-headers)
  to [Q-BAS-184](#q-bas-184--kit-check-19-judges-what-a-bastion-keeps-and-a-route-is-exempt-from-two-duties-only-with-a-reason)): the core's
  representation headers are `catalog.RepresentationHeaders()` (`Content-Type`, `Content-Encoding`, `Content-Language`,
  `Content-Disposition`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `Cache-Control`, `Expires`, `Vary`, `Repr-Digest` and the content headers of R-ARCH-007,
  `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`), its per-request headers `catalog.PerRequestHeaders()`
  (`Content-Length`, `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Date`, `Age`, `X-Request-Id`, `X-Quader-Replica`, `Cache-Status`, `Retry-After`,
  `Quader-Resolved-From`). The header duty judges the `200`, `206` and `304` of `Download`, `Metadata` and `Computed` routes, the answers a
  Bastion keeps. `Fixture.NoBastion` exempts a route from the content-address and the conditional duty with a reason, never from the header
  duty; npm's root, dist-tags, keys and attestations and OCI's tags list are listed there with [H-1249](#h-1249--five-documents-of-npm-and-oci-carry-no-validator-so-a-bastion-fetches-them-whole-once-per-metadata-period).
  Register refuses a declaration that breaks the rules above (`catalog.BastionFacts`); `catalog.Facts.BoundPrefixes()` is `/v2/` for the
  registry root ([Q-BAS-183](#q-bas-183--the-bound-host-prefixes-are-derived-from-the-registry-root-not-declared)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/formats/formattest/testformat`): each defect fails check 19 and no other check (`TestR_BAS_058_KitCheck19`); npm,
  NuGet, OCI, Debian, Ansible Galaxy, the ClamAV definitions and generic pass it (each format's `TestR_ARCH_010_Conformance`; generic,
  which has no routes, skips it with its reason).

### R-BAS-091 · The longest wait a format's client is told, and the interface version 7
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

A client of a format is told the same longest wait by a Bastion's own refusals as by the main installation
([Q-BAS-310](#q-bas-310--the-longest-wait-a-formats-client-is-told-is-a-fact-of-the-format-zero-tells-the-true-wait)). Found by the
planner of the owner's task W-34: the main installation told NuGet's and Ansible Galaxy's clients at most 30 s, while a Bastion's own
refusals (R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037) told them the whole wait, a block's 15 minutes to 24 hours included; a NuGet client waits any
`Retry-After` against the one `--timeout` of its command (formats/nuget.md R-NUGET-002, R-NUGET-032).

- **A fact of the format.** `catalog.Facts.Bastion.RetryAfterMax` (R-BAS-058) is the longest wait the format's clients are told, in
  `Retry-After` and in the RateLimit field's `t`: 0 tells the true wait, otherwise whole seconds. It is the cap the format's `WriteError`
  applies at the main installation, one constant per format, and kit check 19 holds the declaration to `WriteError` for every format:
  a rate limit of a second is told a second, a rate limit of a day the cap or a day. The handshake's format table carries it as
  `retryAfterMaxSeconds` (R-BAS-057).
- **What each format declares, and why:**

| Format | Longest wait | From |
|---|---|---|
| npm | the whole wait | `WriteError` cuts nothing; npm waits what `Retry-After` says ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-59) and has no budget of the whole command the wait would spend |
| NuGet | 30 s | `maxRetryAfter` of its `WriteError` (formats/nuget.md R-NUGET-002): the clients wait any `Retry-After` against the one `--timeout` of the command |
| OCI | the whole wait | formats/oci.md R-OCI-008: `Retry-After` is never cut, a client told 60 s for a wait of six hours retries into the same refusal; docker exits at a `429` whatever it says, podman waits it |
| Debian | the whole wait | `WriteError` cuts nothing; APT prints the status line (the manual's table of the clients); whether APT waits a `Retry-After` is not verified |
| Ansible Galaxy | 30 s | `maxRetryAfter` of its `WriteError` (formats/ansible.md R-ANS-007): the client counts the wait against its own timeout |
| generic (`/files/`) | the whole wait | no routes and no entry in the table, so a Bastion takes the table's default; the main installation's problem details cut nothing; `curl --retry` waits what it says |
| ClamAV definitions | the whole wait | a rate limit is `503` (R-CLAMAV-005), which `freshclam` counts as a failed attempt without reading `Retry-After`, so the value reaches no schedule |

- **At the Bastion.** The engine caps the `Retry-After` of every answer of its own by the entry of the request's format
  (`HandshakeFormat.CapRetryAfter`), and the `t` of the RateLimit field of a refusal of its guard; the detail names the true wait (R-BAS-029).
  A format the table does not name gets the true wait.
- **The interface version 7.** `retryAfterMaxSeconds` is a member of `iface.HandshakeFormat`, required and never negative
  (`HandshakeFormats.Validate`); `iface.InterfaceVersion` is 7, `testdata/interface.txt` and the OpenAPI document's
  `BastionHandshakeFormat` and `x-quader-bastion-interface: 7` say so. Main installation and Bastions are upgraded together (R-BAS-009).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, milliseconds): a block, a request limit and a failed-authentication timeout of 15 minutes answer
  `Retry-After: 30` and `t=30` on NuGet's and Galaxy's paths, `900` on npm's and OCI's, and "15 minutes" in every detail
  (`TestR_BAS_058_TheBastionsOwnRefusalsKeepTheFormatsLongestWait`); the wait is rounded once (`TestR_BAS_029_ARefusalNamesOneWait`).
- Kit (every format, milliseconds): check 19 holds `WriteError` to the declaration; the `testformat` defects `CapsRetryAfterUndeclared`
  and `DeclaresRetryAfterCap` fail it (`TestR_BAS_058_KitCheck19`'s table in `testformat`).
- Unit (`internal/api/v1`, `internal/bastion/iface`, `internal/formats/catalog`): the handshake's table carries 30 for NuGet and Ansible
  Galaxy and 0 for every other format, equal to the table of `maintest` (`TestR_BAS_057_TheHandshakeCarriesTheFormatTable`); a negative
  value fails `Validate`; Register refuses a negative cap or one of a part of a second.
- Cost: no integration or e2e case; the kit's duty is two calls of `WriteError` per format, under a millisecond each, about 25 ms with 25
  formats.

### R-BAS-059 · Downloads, usage and audit for every format
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: RMT-041

The existing rules hold for every format: a hit at the Bastion is not counted at the main installation (usage-and-limits.md R-LIM-001,
"Later"), and a download the Bastion serves from its cache is reported to the main installation's audit (R-BAS-016, Q-BAS-13).

- **What a download is, is the main installation's.** The marking gains `Quader-Bastion-Counted: download` (`iface.Marking.Counted`) on a
  response whose serving counted a download at the main installation (the item store's download recording notes it, as its lookups note `absent`, Q-BAS-70);
  the Bastion records it on the entry and reports every serve of that entry from its cache, a hit or a check answered `304`
  ([Q-BAS-177](#q-bas-177--a-bastion-reports-a-hit-as-a-download-when-the-main-installation-counted-its-fill-as-one)).
  *Built on 2026-11-22, the main installation's side (package B), where the code disagreed with the sentence above:* the download
  recording (`items.Store.Served`) runs after the body, the marking goes out with the status line, so a note there would never reach a
  header. The note is made at the status line of an answer the core counts once its body is complete - a `GET` answered `200`, or `206`
  from byte 0 - by the writer of the three serves that count (`bastionmain.CountingWriter`): the item store's serve (every format's stored
  artifacts and documents, local, remote hit and virtual), the remote engine's artifact answer (its streamed miss) and `/files/`
  ([Q-BAS-186](#q-bas-186--a-counted-download-is-noted-at-the-status-line-of-the-serve-that-counts-it)). The fourth place the main
  installation counts, `ItemStore.RecordDownload` of a document a format answers itself (a remote OCI tag's manifest, Q-OCI-222), notes
  the count too, and the format records it before its status line (it counted after the body before; the bytes are in memory and a `200`
  follows, so it counts the same requests). Every call of `items.Store.Served` is therefore preceded by the note on a Bastion request,
  which is how the marking follows the main installation's own rule of a download for every format. The marking sets `Counted` on a `200`
  only. Marked although not counted: a streamed miss the remote engine passes through during an outage of the object store
  ([H-1290](#h-1290--a-miss-passed-through-during-an-outage-of-the-object-store-is-marked-as-counted)).
- **An image.** By the main installation's rule (formats/oci.md Q-OCI-222), a pull of a tag is the download of its manifest by the tag or
  by its digest, a `HEAD` is none, and a blob is a download of its item. Through a Bastion: `docker pull` of a warm single-platform image
  `GET`s the tag (a document, counted at its fill, so reported) and the blobs (artifacts, reported); containerd `HEAD`s the tag (not
  reported) and `GET`s the manifests by digest and the blobs (reported). *Since 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-021, Q-BAS-475):* the `HEAD` of a tag
  the Bastion does not hold is followed by the `GET` that keeps it; *since W34-E19 (interface version 9, [Q-BAS-479](#q-bas-479--a-get-a-bastion-sends-for-a-head-says-so-in-a-header-of-the-request),
  [Q-BAS-481](#q-bas-481--the-get-of-a-head-records-nothing-a-head-does-not-and-is-charged-at-the-main-installation-as-the-head))* that `GET` says so and the main installation records no download for it: no
  download statistics, no repository activity, no `artifact.downloaded` and no download figure of the limits, as for the `HEAD` it stands
  for; it is still marked `Counted`, so a later `GET` the Bastion serves from what it kept is reported as the tag's download. *Until
  W34-E19 the main installation counted that `GET` as the tag's download for the caller that sent the `HEAD`, once per fill (H-2375,
  closed).* The `HEAD`s the Bastion answers from it are reported as nothing. The audit trail of a Bastion pull is therefore what the main
  installation's own audit trail would hold for the same requests: Docker's sequence (`HEAD` of the tag, `GET` of the manifest by its
  digest, the blobs) records the manifest by digest and the blobs, one image as their unit (R-OPS-054).
- **Usage and limits.** What a Bastion forwards is charged at the main installation to the caller's subject (R-LIM-003), the token
  requests by the token service's own rule and the conditional requests of a registry token as requests of the token's subject; what the
  Bastion serves from its cache is charged nowhere. *Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-096, [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md)
  R-LIM-045):* what the Bastion serves from its cache is charged at the Bastion's place to the caller's subject and reported to the main
  installation's usage store; a forward stays charged at the main installation as well (two budgets, Q-LIM-306). *Built by E8:* the main
  installation stores a reported usage row at the Bastion's place. *Built by E9b (2026-11-26):* the Bastion charges what it serves at its
  place and reports it with every flush (R-BAS-096). Since the read shapes per package are built (2026-11-23), a warm pull with a registry
  token is charged its token request and one check instead of a conditional request per manifest and blob (R-BAS-085, Q-BAS-253).
- **Audit.** `artifact.downloaded` with `details.origin: bastion`, the request path as `path` (`/v2/web/docker/library/nginx/blobs/sha256:…`)
  and the qualified repository, as for every format (R-BAS-016). The interface version is 4 (R-BAS-057).

Acceptance criteria:

- Integration (area `bastion`): a warm pull by tag through the Bastion reports the tag's document and the two blobs and nothing for a
  `HEAD` of the tag; a warm `npm ci` still reports its tarballs and no packument (`TestR_BAS_059_AHitIsReportedWhenTheMainInstallationCountedItsFill`).
- Unit, the main installation's side:
  `TestR_BAS_059_ACountedDownloadIsNotedAtItsStatusLine` (`internal/bastionmain`: which status lines note, before the stage below reads
  the note), `TestR_BAS_059_ARemoteTagIsCountedBeforeItsStatusLine` (`internal/formats/oci`: a remote tag's download exists when its status
  line goes out) and `TestR_BAS_059_ADownloadTheCoreCountedIsMarkedCounted` (`internal/api/bastionmark`: a download and a document marked, a
  `304`, a `404` and an ordinary caller not).
- *Added on 2026-11-26 (W34-E19, [Q-BAS-479](#q-bas-479--a-get-a-bastion-sends-for-a-head-says-so-in-a-header-of-the-request) to [Q-BAS-482](#q-bas-482--the-main-installation-honours-the-statement-of-a-head-on-a-documents-route-only)), as built:*
  integration (area `bastion`, about 3.5 s, an image of two blobs of 1 KiB): Docker's sequence through a Bastion records at the main
  installation the manifest by digest and the two blobs, one image as their unit, and nothing for the `GET` that filled the tag's `HEAD`,
  which carried the statement; a `GET` of the tag afterwards costs the main installation nothing and is reported by the Bastion
  (`TestR_BAS_059_DockersHeadOfATagIsNoDownloadAtTheMainInstallation`). Unit, the Bastion's side (milliseconds, documents of a few
  bytes): `TestR_BAS_059_OnlyTheGetOfAHeadSaysItIsForAHead` (`internal/bastion/engine`: the fill's `GET` and the `HEAD`'s conditional
  `GET` carry it, the `HEAD`, a caller's `GET` and its conditional `GET` do not), `TestR_BAS_059_TheStatementOfAHeadIsTheEnginesAlone`
  (`internal/bastion/mainclient`: a caller's own header never reaches the main installation). Unit, the main installation's side
  (milliseconds, no data): `TestR_BAS_059_OnlyARecognizedGetSaysItIsForAHead` and
  `TestR_BAS_059_TheStatementOfAHeadHoldsOnADocumentsRouteOnly` (`internal/bastionmain`), `TestR_BAS_059_TheGetOfAHeadRecordsNoDownload`
  (`internal/items`), `TestR_BAS_059_TheGetOfAHeadIsChargedAsTheHead` (`internal/limits`).

### R-BAS-060 · Tests of the feature and what they cost
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

By the owner's rule "Tests stay runnable" of 2026-11-20 (the repository's working rules): each behaviour once, at the cheapest tier
([Q-BAS-180](#q-bas-180--the-tests-of-the-feature-each-behaviour-once-at-the-cheapest-tier-and-one-client-case-in-the-formats-own-set)).
The run times are estimates of the planner (marked [J]); the builder records the measured ones on
[developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md).

| Tier | Test | Data | Run time [J] |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit, `internal/bastion/engine` | R-BAS-050 to R-BAS-054, R-BAS-056 and R-BAS-059 on the fake main installation `maintest`: families, the registry root's core routes, registry tokens, the distribution's error shape, the content address, replay headers, `If-Modified-Since`, the format's rate-limit status, large artifacts | bytes; one blob of 256 KiB | under 3 s together |
| unit, `internal/bastionmain`, `internal/api/bastionmark`, `internal/api/v1` | the backstop, the token route's kind, the shape cap, `insufficient_scope`, the check below `/v2/`, the feed mappings, the handshake's table, the counted marking | none | under 1 s |
| kit, every format | check 19 (R-BAS-058) | the fixture's content cases | about 20 ms per format |
| integration, area `bastion` | one replay per format with Bastion behaviour of its own: OCI (R-BAS-051, R-BAS-053, a blocked image, R-BAS-059), Debian (R-BAS-055), the ClamAV definitions (R-BAS-056); once, format-independent: the bound host (R-BAS-057) | an image of two blobs of 1 KiB; a package of 1 KiB; containers of a few hundred bytes | about 4 s, 3 s, 1 s and 2 s: about 10 s |
| e2e, set `oci` (on a push that changes the format's code or the Bastion, and nightly; *superseded in place on 2026-11-22 by [Q-BAS-207](#q-bas-207--the-case-runs-on-a-push-that-changes-ocis-own-paths-and-in-the-nightly): on a push that changes OCI's own paths, and nightly; a change of the Bastion alone does not start it*) | one case `TestOCI_R_BAS_051_ThroughABastion`: `docker login`, a cold and a warm `docker pull`, a `podman pull`, and a Kubernetes pod whose image comes through the Bastion, of a `FROM scratch` image of two layers of a few KiB, through one Bastion release (volume backend, one replica, no Valkey) installed in the leg | a few KiB | about 40 s and about 60 s for the Bastion's release [J]; *measured on 2026-11-22: 16.7 s and 16.4 s in all, the release ready after about 5.5 s ([developer/e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#the-bastion-case-of-the-set-oci))* |
| measurement, once before landing (not a test) | `docker`, `podman`, `crictl pull` through a Bastion; `apt-get update` and `apt-get install` in Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04; `ansible-galaxy collection install`; `freshclam` 1.5.5: each against a local Bastion, the numbers written on developer/bastion.md | real clients | minutes, once |

- **What each leg gains** [J]: the unit job about 4 s; the integration shard that holds the area `bastion` about 10 s (139 s now,

## The handover per blob

The owner's decision 12 (b) of 2026-11-22 in his working paper on the stored content. His wish was "Ein Bastion kann auch einen
Read-Only Account auf ein s3 Bucket bekommen und damit die Hauptinstanz weiter entlasten"; he chose instead: a Bastion gets no account
of the store, and when it needs a blob it does not hold, the main installation may hand it, for that one blob, a short-lived signed link
of the object store and, where the blob lies on an encrypted connection, the data key of that blob, so that the Bastion reads the bytes
from the object store itself and the main installation's bandwidth is spared. It lifts his decision
[Q-BAS-10](#q-bas-10--the-cache-an-own-bucket-or-a-local-volume-never-the-main-installations-object-store) for a link and a data key per
released blob and for nothing else. Since a Bastion serves images ([Every format](#every-format)), its first fills are layers of
gigabytes; the handover takes them off the main installation.

Status: specified on 2026-11-22 by the planner; the wire is built (package 1, 2026-11-23: interface version 6, R-BAS-073's types and
checks, [Q-BAS-280](#q-bas-280--the-wire-checks-storedsize-against-ssize-itself) and
[Q-BAS-281](#q-bas-281--the-wires-checks-are-narrower-than-the-list-of-r-bas-073)); the main installation's side for plain copies is
built (package 2, 2026-11-23: the registration's switch, the serve point's decision of R-STOR-095 steps 1 to 7, 9 and 11, the marking,
[Q-BAS-285](#q-bas-285--only-the-journaled-switch-off-is-listed-as-yielding-no-feed-entry)); the Bastion's side is built (package 3,
2026-11-23: the offer, the direct read of a plain and of an encrypted copy, its failures, the metrics, the alert,
[Q-BAS-290](#q-bas-290--a-handover-counts-one-outcome-by-the-path-it-took) to
[Q-BAS-293](#q-bas-293--a-value-the-bastion-refuses-starts-the-cooldown)); the surface is built (package 5, 2026-11-23: the card's switch
**Direct reads from the object store** with its reasons, the manual's section,
[Q-BAS-295](#q-bas-295--the-card-names-the-connections-a-bastion-cannot-read-and-only-those) and
[Q-BAS-296](#q-bas-296--until-the-data-keys-are-handed-the-cards-sentence-names-no-key-and-an-encrypted-connection-has-its-line)). A plain copy is
handed over once an administrator has switched a registration's handover on; the integration case that joins the two sides is built
(2026-11-23, `TestR_BAS_070_ALargeFileIsReadFromTheObjectStore`): the two sides meet as each expected the other, and the look at the hosts'
check against what the main installation signs found that a refused value did not start the cooldown, which the Bastion's side now does
(Q-BAS-293). The data keys are built (package 4, 2026-11-23: a copy on an encrypted connection is handed over with its own data key where no
plain copy can serve, after its trace `bastion.data_key.handed`, [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095's as-built note; the joined case on an
encrypted connection, `TestR_BAS_070_AnEncryptedFileIsReadFromTheObjectStoreWithItsDataKey`). It builds on specifications whose code is on `main`: the serve point and
the domain package of the signed links ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-070 to R-STOR-074, package 2 of
[developer/download-links.md](../developer/download-links.md)), the copies a read would try now (`blob.Store.Servable`, R-STOR-062, stage
1's package A), and for an encrypted connection the storage keys and `blob.Store.CopyDataKey` (R-STOR-083, packages 2 and 3 of
[developer/stored-content-encryption.md](../developer/stored-content-encryption.md)). The format's reader that opens an object with its
data key is built (`internal/blob/blobcrypt`). The main installation's side is [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095 and R-STOR-096; the
security perspective is [security/bastion-handover.md](../security/bastion-handover.md) (H-1340 to H-1345); the build plan is
[developer/bastion-handover.md](../developer/bastion-handover.md); the decisions are
[Q-BAS-230](#q-bas-230--the-handover-is-an-answer-to-the-forward-of-a-miss) to
[Q-BAS-239](#q-bas-239--the-tests-once-at-the-cheapest-tier-one-integration-case-no-end-to-end-case) and storage.md's Q-STOR-340 to
Q-STOR-347; the record is
[ADR-250](../decisions.md#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward).

```text
 caller ── GET of a file it may read ──► Bastion: a miss
 Bastion ── the forward with the caller's credential and
            Quader-Bastion-Handover: accept; max-size=<bytes> ─────────► main installation (default endpoint)
                       decides as the caller's own request (R-BAS-013), the gates, the limits' Admit;
                       picks a copy, a plain one first; signs a link for GET; for an encrypted copy opens
                       its record (one HeadObject) and records bastion.data_key.handed; counts the download
 Bastion ◄── 200, Content-Length: 0, the file's own headers, Quader-Bastion-Class: handover,
             Quader-Bastion-Handover: <link, its expiry, digest, sizes[, data key]>   (the budget slot is free again)
 Bastion ── GET <link>, no credential, no header of the interface ──► object store (the connection's public address)
 Bastion ◄── the stored object: the bytes, or segments it opens with the data key
 Bastion: verifies (the digest; on an encrypted copy every segment, the final segment and the digest), spools,
          commits, serves the caller and every caller that follows the fill (R-BAS-054);
          a failure: the bytes through the main installation (R-BAS-075)
```
