### R-BAS-070 · The handover per blob: a link and a data key per released blob
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **What leaves the main installation, per handover:** one link signed for `GET` of one object on one connection, for the life of the
  installation's links ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-014's `linkLifeSeconds`, R-STOR-072); the blob's SHA-256, its size and its stored
  size; the connection's identifier; and, only where the copy lies on an encrypted connection, that copy's data key. The answer that
  carries them carries the file's own headers, as every forwarded answer does (R-BAS-073).
- **What never leaves:** an account or a credential of the object store (the connection's credential signs the link at the main
  installation and stays there, R-STOR-072); a storage key, a name key, a wrap or a record; anything of the key ring; a data key of any
  other blob or of another copy (each encrypted copy has a data key of its own, R-STOR-087).
- **A released blob** is one the main installation would stream to the same request: the caller may read it there and then (the forward
  is decided as the caller's own request, R-BAS-013), its content is sound, the format's serve-time check passed, and every gate that
  applies passed on a decided state ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095).
- **For what:** a fill of the Bastion's cache (R-BAS-021, R-BAS-054). The Bastion reads the object whole, verifies it, keeps it and serves
  it. Never a document, a range, a `HEAD`, a conditional answer, an answer of the registry's token service, or a file larger than the
  Bastion would keep (R-BAS-072).
- **Q-BAS-10 lifted for this and for nothing else.** The Bastion's cache stays its own (R-BAS-030); it holds no credential of the main
  installation's store, lists nothing, writes nothing, and reads no object it was not handed a link for. R-BAS-001's rule that a Bastion
  pod makes no request to the main installation's bucket holds while no registration's handover is on (R-BAS-071), as in the end-to-end
  suite.
- **Off by default**, switched per registration at the main installation (R-BAS-071).

Acceptance criteria:

- Integration (area `bastion`): with the handover on for the registration and the links' `minSize` 0, a cold `GET` through the Bastion
  of a file of 64 KiB below `/files/` of a generic repository returns the file; the main installation's request log holds one line for it
  with `delivery` `handover` and `response_bytes` 0; the Bastion's `quader_bastion_fill_bytes_total{source="store"}` rose by 65,536; a
  second `GET` is a hit; with the handover off, the same cold `GET` is a forward whose line has no `delivery`
  (`TestR_BAS_070_ALargeFileIsReadFromTheObjectStore`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the main installation's half of the criterion (package 2):* with no Bastion that offers yet, the integration
case of the area `bastion` sends the forward itself, as the Bastion will, to the stack's main installation: a recognized `GET` of a file
of 64 KiB below `/files/` with `Quader-Bastion-Handover: accept; max-size=1048576` is streamed while the registration's switch is off, and
once it is on answered with the file's `200` without its bytes, the class `handover` and a value whose link a client without a credential
reads the file from at the stack's object store; the request log's line has `delivery` `handover` and `response_bytes` 0
(`TestR_STOR_095_AForwardThatOfferedIsHandedOverFromTheStacksStore`, removed on 2026-11-23 with the case below, which shows all of it).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the case that joins the two sides:* `TestR_BAS_070_ALargeFileIsReadFromTheObjectStore` in
[handover_test.go](../../test/integration/bastion/handover_test.go) runs the suite's main installation, with the switch on for its
registration through the API, the links' `minSize` 0 and the default connection's public address on a relay to the stack's store (on
`localhost`, which is not the host of the Bastion's `bastion.main.url`), and the Bastion role, which trusts the stack's CA in one bundle of
`bastion.main.ca_file`. It shows the criterion and what only the join shows: the caller gets the file's bytes and the representation
headers the main installation serves; the main installation answered the class `handover` with `Content-Length: 0` and no body, wrote
`delivery` `handover` and `response_bytes` 0, and counted the handover in its metric; the Bastion counts `read` and 65,536 bytes from the
store and names the outcome in its request log; the download is counted once at the main installation, and the hit that follows asks it
nothing and is reported once by the Bastion; an npm tarball of a partial reader is handed over and kept with the package its handover answer
named (R-BAS-082); a read cut after its first segment is continued with the Bastion's own `Range` and `If-Range`, which the real serve point
answers `206` with the same `ETag`, counting no second download; a link the store refuses falls back to the bytes through the main
installation, which counts the download again (H-1342 as specified); an ordinary request that sends the offer gets the file and no marking;
with the switch off the main installation streams an offered forward within its snapshot, the handshake tells the Bastion, and its read comes
as bytes from the main installation; no log line of either side holds a usable link. The look at the hosts' check against what the main
installation signs (the stack's endpoint without a public address is the front's host) found that a refused value fell back at every miss
without the cooldown ([Q-BAS-293](#q-bas-293--a-value-the-bastion-refuses-starts-the-cooldown)). The two halves the sides were built with were removed
with it, since it shows everything they showed ([the build plan](../developer/bastion-handover.md#tests-and-what-they-cost)).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the same case on an encrypted connection (package 4):*
`TestR_BAS_070_AnEncryptedFileIsReadFromTheObjectStoreWithItsDataKey` beside it runs the suite's main installation with its one connection
encrypted (keyed names; the storage key drawn at its first start under the stack's key ring), the switch on, the links' `minSize` 0 and the
relay as the public address, and the Bastion role with the bundle. A cold read of a file of 65 KiB (one segment and 1 KiB, so the read
crosses a segment's boundary) returns its plaintext; the main installation answered the class `handover` with no body and a value with
`encrypted: true`, `storedSize` `S(size)` and the `dataKey`, counted `kind="link_and_key"`, wrote `delivery` `handover` and
`bastion.data_key.handed` with its members (the caller, the caller's address, the registration as the resource, the item, and in `details`
the registration, the Bastion replica, the digest, the connection, the storage key's identifier and the link's expiry) and without the key or
the link; the store sent exactly the stored size through its public address; the Bastion counted `read` and holds no key afterwards
(`handover.Client.KeysHeld`). A second file of the same size, whose object the relay answers with the first one's stored bytes, under another
data key, falls back before the first byte to the bytes through the main installation, without the cooldown, and its trace stands: the trail
names a key whose read fell back (H-1342). No log line of either side holds the handed key in hexadecimal, base64 or base64url, or a usable
link.

### R-BAS-071 · The switch: per registration at the main installation, off by default
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation) (R-BAS-093):* the switch is `switches.handover` of the
registration's configuration, set on the card beside `gui` and `docs`; a change of it writes `bastion.configuration.changed` beside
`bastion.handover.enabled` or `.disabled` (the journal and its replay of a switch-off stay), and the feed's `settings` entry brings it to every
Bastion within about 3 s; the handshake carries it in `configuration.switches`, no longer at its top level. *Built by E7 and E8
(2026-11-26):* as written; the registration's API names it `switches.handover`
([Q-BAS-444](#q-bas-444--the-api-shows-a-registrations-switches-and-limits-as-members-of-their-own-and-its-patch-is-decided-per-member)).

- **Where** ([Q-BAS-232](#q-bas-232--the-switch-is-per-registration-at-the-main-installation-and-the-bastions-chart-has-none)): a member of
  the registration, `handover`, kept at the main installation (`bastion.handover boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`), read by every replica
  from a snapshot of the registrations that a change area refreshes within the bound of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-018
  (2 s), so a forward costs no query for it. Neither chart has a value for it (R-BAS-078).
- **API** (the operations of R-BAS-004): `GET /api/v1/bastions` and `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` show `handover`;
  `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/{name}` takes `{"handover": true}` or `false` with `endpoints:write`; `POST /api/v1/bastions` does not take it, so
  a new registration has the handover off.
- **Audit and journal:** `bastion.handover.enabled` (transactional, not journaled) and `bastion.handover.disabled` (transactional, journaled
  with the entry `{principalId, name}`); the journal's replay sets the member off, so a restore to a point before a switch-off keeps the
  handover off (Q-BAS-145's pattern; R-HA-054's table gains the row with the code, since its test holds the table to the registry). The
  feed carries no entry for either: the main installation decides each forward from its snapshot, and a Bastion learns the member at its
  next handshake; both are listed in `noFeedEntry` with that reason (R-BAS-015).
- **The handshake** (R-BAS-010) gains `"handover": <the member>`. The Bastion offers to take a handover only while it is true (R-BAS-072)
  and exports it as `quader_bastion_handover_enabled` (R-BAS-075).
- **The screen** (R-BAS-007, Q-BAS-95): the card of a registration shows a switch **Direct reads from the object store**, off as the value in
  the field, with one sentence: "Large files go from the object store to this Bastion by a link per file, and for an encrypted store with
  that file's key; the main installation decides and counts every download as before." While it is on, the card lists each connection with
  whether it can serve a handover and its reason where not ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-096), and links to the storage settings'
  section **Download links**, whose details hold the minimum size, the links' life and the public addresses (R-STOR-014, R-UI-200). The
  switch is never part of creating a registration. *Amended on 2026-11-23 by package 5:* the card names only the connections a Bastion
  cannot read, each with its reasons, and links to the storage settings only where one of them is a plain connection; nothing of the
  connections while every one can serve a handover
  ([Q-BAS-295](#q-bas-295--the-card-names-the-connections-a-bastion-cannot-read-and-only-those)). Until the data keys are handed
  (package 4) the sentence names no key, and an encrypted connection has its line
  ([Q-BAS-296](#q-bas-296--until-the-data-keys-are-handed-the-cards-sentence-names-no-key-and-an-encrypted-connection-has-its-line)).
  *Amended again on 2026-11-23, when package 4 landed
  ([Q-BAS-300](#q-bas-300--with-the-data-keys-handed-the-cards-sentence-names-the-key-and-an-encrypted-connection-is-judged-as-a-plain-one)):*
  the sentence is the one above, with the key, and an encrypted connection is judged by its `handoverUsable` and `handoverReasons` like a
  plain one.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/api/v1`, `internal/bastionmain`): `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/partners {"handover": true}` by a caller with
  `endpoints:write` answers `200` and records `bastion.handover.enabled`, by one with `endpoints:read` `403`; `{"handover": false}` records
  `bastion.handover.disabled` with its journal entry, and the replay of that entry sets the member off; `POST /api/v1/bastions` with
  `handover` answers `400`; the handshake of `partners` says `"handover": true` after the change; `bastion.handover.disabled` is in
  `noFeedEntry` (`TestR_BAS_071_TheSwitchIsPerRegistration`, `TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`).
- Vitest: the card shows the switch off for a new registration and, once on, a connection's reason `not_https`.

*As built on 2026-11-23, the main installation's side (package 2 of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-handover.md)):* the column
`bastion.handover` (migration `00110_bastion_handover`, which also makes a change of it a new revision of the registration, the ETag)
and the member `handover` of `GET`, `PATCH` and of the answers of `POST` ([registrations.go](../../internal/bastionmain/registrations.go),
[bastion_registrations_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_registrations_api.go)); `POST` refuses the member as every unknown one
(`400`), and a `null` of `handover` or `enabled` in a `PATCH` reads as absent: before, a `null` of `enabled` decoded as `false` and
disabled the registration. `PATCH` records `bastion.handover.enabled` or `bastion.handover.disabled` with the journal entry
`{principalId, name}` and announces the change area `bastion_handover`; the journal's replay (domain `bastion`,
[handover.go](../../internal/bastionmain/handover.go)) switches the member off, `already in effect` when it is off, `subject unknown` for
an ID that names no registration. Only `bastion.handover.disabled` is in `noFeedEntry`
([Q-BAS-285](#q-bas-285--only-the-journaled-switch-off-is-listed-as-yielding-no-feed-entry)). Every replica that serves downloads keeps
the snapshot `bastionmain.RegistrationSnapshot` (the registrations whose member is on, by principal ID; read at start, on every change of
the area and once a minute; a failed read keeps the last one, off before the first), which the serve point and the handshake read; a
registration turned on after the first read asks the connections' link checks again (R-STOR-096). The handshake's `handover` is the
snapshot's value for the calling registration. The criterion is split by what it needs: the operations' answers before the service, the
handshake, the snapshot and the registry and replay handler are unit tests (`TestR_BAS_071_TheOperationsOfTheSwitchAndTheHandshake` in
`internal/api/v1`, `TestR_BAS_071_TheSnapshotOfTheSwitches` and `TestR_BAS_071_TheSwitchOffIsJournaledAndReplayed` in
`internal/bastionmain`); what the service writes, records and journals and the replay against PostgreSQL are the integration area
`bastionreg`'s (`TestR_BAS_071_TheSwitchIsPerRegistration`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the screen (package 5):* every card holds `<quader-bastion-handover>`
([bastion-handover.ts](../../web/src/app/features/bastions/bastion-handover.ts)) between its actions and **Last contact**: for a holder
of `endpoints:write` the heading **Direct reads from the object store** and the switch (`quader-switch`, named "Direct reads from the
object store for <name>"), for who may only read the settings pages' sentence "**Direct reads from the object store** are on." or "are

and the sentence "Large files go from the object store to this

did not answer a test link as expected (<detail>)") and for an encrypted connection "the connection is encrypted"; where a plain connection

[H-1480](#h-1480--the-bastions-screen-shows-what-the-main-installation-can-sign-not-what-a-bastion-can-read). The Vitest

### R-BAS-072 · The Bastion offers to take a handover on a miss
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- The Bastion adds `Quader-Bastion-Handover: accept; max-size=<n>` to every `GET` it forwards (R-BAS-021) and to its own conditional `GET`
  (R-BAS-022: a `200` to it may be a handover), while all of these hold: the last handshake said `handover: true` (R-BAS-071); the replica
  is not cooling down (R-BAS-075); and the request is no probe (R-BAS-014), no conditional request of a caller that follows a running fill
  (R-BAS-054), no continuation and no forward that replaces a failed handover (R-BAS-075).
- `n` is the smaller of `bastion.cache.max_object_bytes` and the bytes the spool can take at that moment (`spool_max_bytes` less the fills
  in progress, R-BAS-030), so that the main installation hands over only what the Bastion would keep
  ([Q-BAS-233](#q-bas-233--only-artifacts-the-bastion-keeps-are-handed-over)). A larger artifact is streamed by the main installation and
  passed through as today (R-BAS-021); the manual's sizing says to raise both values for images with large layers (R-BAS-078).
- The offer says nothing about the caller. The main installation ignores it on every answer it does not apply to ([storage.md](storage.md)
  R-STOR-095), so the Bastion needs no knowledge of a route's kind to send it.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`): a cold `GET` sends the offer with `max-size` the smaller of the two values; a `HEAD`, a probe, the
  conditional request of a follower, a continuation, a forward that replaces a failed handover, a request while the handshake says
  `handover: false` and one while the replica cools down send none (`TestR_BAS_072_TheBastionOffersToTakeAHandover`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's side (package 3 of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-handover.md)):* `offerFor` in
[engine/handover.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/handover.go) decides the offer of every forward the read flow sends (`send` in
[forward.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/forward.go)); the size is `min(max_object_bytes, Cache.SpoolRoom())`, the spool's room being
`spool_max_bytes` less what the fills in progress hold. `mainclient.Forward.Offer` carries it, set after the copy of the caller's headers, which
drops a caller's own `Quader-Bastion-Handover`. No offer also on a core route of the registry root and on a key marked after a digest that failed
(R-BAS-075; [Q-BAS-292](#q-bas-292--the-forward-that-replaces-a-handover-counts-no-second-miss-and-a-core-route-carries-no-offer)). The
handshake's member reaches the engine as `link.State.Handover` and `quader_bastion_handover_enabled`. The test covers the continuation and the
replacing forward in `TestR_BAS_075_ADirectReadThatFails`.

### R-BAS-073 · The handover answer and the interface version 6
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The answer** to a forward the main installation hands over ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095;
  [Q-BAS-231](#q-bas-231--the-handover-rides-in-a-marking-header-of-the-items-own-200-with-an-empty-body)): status `200`; the headers the
  file's own `200` would carry, the format's included (an image's `Docker-Content-Digest` and its `ETag` `"sha256:<hex>"`);
  `Content-Length: 0` and no body; the marking of R-BAS-013 with `Quader-Bastion-Class: handover`, `Quader-Bastion-Repository`,
  `Quader-Bastion-Read`, `Quader-Bastion-Subject`, `Quader-Bastion-Counted: download` and, where the request named exactly one package,
  `Quader-Bastion-Package` and `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read` (R-BAS-082); and `Quader-Bastion-Handover: <value>`, the JSON
  below in base64url without padding ([RFC 4648](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648) §5), at most 8 KiB:

```json
{
  "link": "https://objects.example.com/quader-blobs/quader/sha256/9f/86/9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=…&X-Amz-Date=20261122T100000Z&X-Amz-Expires=60&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=…",
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-22T10:01:00Z",
  "connection": "default",
  "sha256": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
  "size": 5242880,
  "storedSize": 5242880,
  "encrypted": false
}
```

*(example: a plain copy)*. For a copy on an encrypted connection `"encrypted": true`, `"storedSize": 5245188` (`S(L)` of
[storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-076) and `"dataKey": "<43 characters: the 32 bytes of the data key in base64url>"`, and the link names the
object by its keyed name where the connection has keyed names (R-STOR-086).

- **What the Bastion checks before it reads** (a failure is a bad answer, which ends in the forward of R-BAS-075): `link` is an absolute
  `https` URL whose host is none of R-BAS-074's; `expiresAt` lies in the future; `connection` is an identifier of R-STOR-050; `sha256` is 64
  hexadecimal digits and equals the content address of the answer's `ETag` (R-BAS-022); `size` is at most the `max-size` it offered;
  `storedSize` equals `size` on a plain copy and `S(size)` on an encrypted one; `dataKey` is present exactly when `encrypted` is true and holds
  32 bytes. *Amended on 2026-11-23 ([Q-BAS-281](#q-bas-281--the-wires-checks-are-narrower-than-the-list-of-r-bas-073)):* the link also
  carries no user information and no fragment, and its host is compared by name, case-insensitively and whatever its port; the digest's
  digits are lower case; the sizes are not negative; the value and the data key are strict base64url without padding, and the value one JSON
  object without an unknown member or trailing data; the offer has one spelling, `accept; max-size=<n>` with `n` from 1 to 2⁶³−1 without a
  sign or a leading zero, and the main installation treats any other value, or more than one, as no offer.
- **The interface's additions** (R-BAS-009), which raise `iface.InterfaceVersion` to 6, the version after the read shapes per package
  (R-BAS-087, [Q-BAS-251](#q-bas-251--the-version-numbering-against-the-handover); *amended on 2026-11-22: it said 5*): the request header `Quader-Bastion-Handover` with the
  value `accept; max-size=<n>`, the class `handover`, the response header `Quader-Bastion-Handover` with the value above, and the handshake's
  member `handover` (R-BAS-071). The types are `iface.HandoverOffer` and `iface.Handover`, each with its encoding and its checks. Main
  installation and Bastions are upgraded together, as for every version (R-BAS-009).
- **Only a recognized forward that offered gets one.** The marking stage adds the class and the header to a recognized forward (R-BAS-008)
  whose request carried the offer, and to nothing else; a request without a valid Bastion token that sends the header is an ordinary request
  and gets the file, as R-BAS-008 says of every `Quader-Bastion-*` header. The Bastion's client removes every `Quader-Bastion-*` header from
  an answer before the engine sees it (R-BAS-021), so the value never reaches a caller, and the engine has no path that writes a `handover`
  answer's status or headers to a caller (R-BAS-074).
- **Redaction.** `Quader-Bastion-Handover` is redacted like `Authorization` in every log, span and support bundle of both sides
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-013's rule for header names gains it); neither side's request log
  keeps a header (R-OPS-010).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/iface`): a plain and an encrypted value round-trip; a value with an `http` link, a data key of 31 bytes, a data key
  on a plain copy, a digest that is not 64 hexadecimal digits, a `storedSize` that is not `S(size)` on an encrypted copy, or more than 8 KiB is
  refused; `handover` is a valid class; the interface's file holds version 6 and the four additions
  (`TestR_BAS_073_TheHandoverValue`, `TestR_BAS_009_TheInterfaceChangesOnlyWithItsVersion`).
- Unit (`internal/api/bastionmark`): the class and the header are added only to a recognized forward that offered; an ordinary request that
  sends `Quader-Bastion-Handover: accept; max-size=1048576` gets the file and no `Quader-Bastion-` header
  (`TestR_BAS_073_OnlyARecognizedForwardThatOfferedGetsAHandover`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the wire (package 1 of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-handover.md)):* `iface.InterfaceVersion` is 6, and
[interface.txt](../../internal/bastion/iface/testdata/interface.txt) records `HeaderHandover`, `ClassHandover` (a valid class),
`Handshake.Handover` (`"handover"`, always present, the registration's member since package 2) and the types of
[handover.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/handover.go): `HandoverOffer` with `String`, `Set`, `ParseHandoverOffer` and `HandoverOfferFrom`;
`Handover` with `EncodeHandover`, `DecodeHandover`, `Set`, `HandoverFrom` and `Check(HandoverCheck)`; `HandoverKey` for the data key;
`MaxHandoverBytes` (8 KiB) and `ETagContentAddress`. `DecodeHandover` holds every check that needs nothing but the value, `S(size)` included
([Q-BAS-280](#q-bas-280--the-wire-checks-storedsize-against-ssize-itself)); `Check` holds the rest (the expiry against the Bastion's clock, a
zero clock refusing, the offer, the `ETag`, the hosts); `EncodeHandover` refuses whatever `DecodeHandover` refuses, so the main installation
cannot send a value the Bastion refuses on its form. The data key is a `HandoverKey` whose bytes sit behind a pointer: `String`, `GoString`,
`Format` (every verb), `LogValue` and `MarshalJSON` write `[REDACTED]`, and `Handover`'s own `String`, `Format`, `LogValue` and `MarshalJSON`
leave out the link and the key; the wire form exists only in `EncodeHandover` and `DecodeHandover`, and no error text holds the link, the key
or a byte of a malformed value (a JSON syntax error is reported by its offset) (`TestR_BAS_073_TheHandoverValue`,
`TestR_BAS_073_TheChecksBeforeTheRead`, `TestR_BAS_072_TheOffer`, `TestR_BAS_076_AHandedKeyIsRenderedNowhere`; the copies of `S` and of the
connection pattern are held to `blobcrypt.StoredSize` and `config.ValidConnectionID` by `TestR_BAS_073_TheStoredSizeIsTheFormats` and
`TestR_BAS_073_TheConnectionIsAnIdentifierOfTheConfiguration`). The redaction of R-OPS-013 names the header whole
(`quader_bastion_handover`, so the request log's `bastion_handover` outcome stays readable) and scrubs the value after the header's name and,
bare, by its start, the base64url of `{"link":"` (`TestR_BAS_073_TheHandoverHeaderIsRedactedLikeAuthorization`). `maintest` speaks version 6:
`SetHandover` is the registration's switch and the handshake's member, `HandOver` answers a forward with a handover only while the switch is on,
the forward offered and the blob is within the offer, and `Forwarded.Offer` reads what a forward offered. The Bastion's client offers nothing
yet and refuses an answer of the class `handover`, or one that carries the header, as a bad answer, so a defect of the main installation never
reaches the engine as an empty `200` (`TestR_BAS_073_TheClientAndTheFakeSpeakVersion6`, which also shows that a caller's own
`Quader-Bastion-Handover` never reaches the main installation). With package 1 alone nobody offered and nobody handed over: the marking
stage and `TestR_BAS_073_OnlyARecognizedForwardThatOfferedGetsAHandover` came with package 2 and the engine's offer and read with package 3,
both below.

*As built on 2026-11-23, the main installation's side (package 2):* the recognition stage reads the offer of a forwarded `GET` into the
`Recognition` (`Offer`, `Offered`; a refused value or two values is no offer) and takes `Quader-Bastion-Handover` out of every request,
recognized or not, so no stage behind it, and no handler, sees the header
([recognize.go](../../internal/bastionmain/recognize.go)). The serve point, which decides on the `Recognition` alone, notes the encoded
value in the marking stage's record of the request (`bastionmain.NoteHandover`, refused on a request that is no recognized forward that
offered or that the stage does not mark, so that the serve point then streams) right before it writes the file's `200` with
`Content-Length: 0`; the marking stage, which strips every `Quader-Bastion-*` header a handler set, writes the class `handover` and the
value for a `200` of a forward that offered, with the rest of the marking as for every answer (`Quader-Bastion-Counted: download`, the
package and its shape of R-BAS-082), and counts `quader_bastion_forwarded_requests_total{class="handover"}`
([mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go)). A value on another status is no handover. Tests:
`TestR_BAS_073_OnlyARecognizedForwardThatOfferedGetsAHandover` (`internal/api/bastionmark`), `TestR_BAS_072_TheRecognitionReadsTheOffer`
and `TestR_BAS_073_NoteHandoverOnlyOnAMarkedForwardThatOffered` (`internal/bastionmain`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's side (package 3):* the client's blanket refusal is replaced by "only when the forward offered"
(`takeHandover` in [mainclient/client.go](../../internal/bastion/mainclient/client.go)): an answer of the class `handover` to a forward that
offered arrives as `Response.Handover`, read before the marking is stripped, or as `Response.HandoverErr` when its value is missing, refused, or
on another status than `200`, which the engine replaces by the forward without the offer; the same answer to a forward that did not offer, and a
value on an answer of another class, stay bad answers (`TestR_BAS_073_TheClientTakesAHandoverOnlyWhenTheForwardOffered`,
`TestR_BAS_073_TheClientAndTheFakeSpeakVersion6`). The engine calls `Handover.Check` with its clock, the offer it sent, the answer's `ETag` and
the hosts of `server.base_url`, `bastion.main.url` and `bastion.main.packages_url` before it opens anything. The marking stage is package 2's.

*As built on 2026-11-23, the value of an encrypted copy (package 4):* the main installation writes `"encrypted": true`, `storedSize` as
`blobcrypt.StoredSize(size)` and `dataKey` as the copy's own data key, which `iface.EncodeHandover` carries in base64url; the key enters the
value as an `iface.HandoverKey` copied from the format's key (destroyed at once) and is destroyed right after the encoding
([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095's as-built note, Q-STOR-472). Nothing of the wire changed.

### R-BAS-074 · The direct read and its verification
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

*Revised on 2026-11-26 (R-BAS-097):* a direct read is paced by the registration's throughput like a fill from the
main installation, so the cap covers both sources. *Built by E10 (2026-11-26):* the engine reads the direct read through the throughput's
pacer (`throughput.Pacer.Reader`) in the class of the caller whose miss offered the handover; it was admitted as that miss and is never
refused, only slowed; a continuation from the main installation is paced without an admission (`mainclient.Throughput.Running`).

- **The fill's source.** A `handover` answer starts the fill of R-BAS-021 with the object store as its source instead of the answer's body.
  The answer's body is empty, so its budget slot is free at once, and the direct read holds no slot of the budget towards the main
  installation (R-BAS-025), which narrows [H-1244](#h-1244--cold-fills-of-large-blobs-hold-budget-slots-and-spool-for-the-length-of-their-transfer)
  for what is handed over. Everything else of the fill stays: the spool and its bound (R-BAS-030), the stall bound of 60 s, the withheld
  tail towards every caller (R-BAS-021), the callers that follow the fill on their own permission and the ranged misses served from the
  spool (R-BAS-054), the fetch lock across replicas (R-BAS-025), and the commit's check of the SHA-256 against the content address of the
  `ETag` (R-BAS-032).
- **The link client** (`internal/bastion/handover`), a client of its own and never the client of the main installation: TLS verified against
  the system roots and the trust of `bastion.main.ca_file` (the chart's `trustedCA`), read again without a restart
  ([Q-BAS-237](#q-bas-237--the-store-is-trusted-with-the-charts-trust-bundle)); the timeouts `bastion.main.connect_timeout` and
  `bastion.main.response_header_timeout`; no redirect followed (a redirect is a failure before the first byte); no cookie; no `Authorization`,
  no credential of a caller, no header of the interface and no forwarded header; `User-Agent: quader-bastion/<release>`. It refuses a link
  that is not `https` or whose host is the host of `server.base_url`, `bastion.main.url` or `bastion.main.packages_url`, so that nothing meant
  for Quader leaves on the path that carries no Bastion token and no link leads back into Quader. The address policy of the upstream clients
  does not apply, as for the connection to the main installation ([H-446](#h-446--the-connection-to-the-main-installation-is-not-under-the-egress-address-policy)):
  the host comes from the main installation.
- **One `GET` of the whole object**, from byte 0. Before the first byte the status is `200` and `Content-Length` equals `storedSize`.
- **A plain copy:** the bytes go into the spool as they arrive; the commit compares their SHA-256 with `sha256` and with the `ETag`'s content
  address, and no caller receives the last 64 KiB before it (R-BAS-021).
- **An encrypted copy** ([Q-BAS-234](#q-bas-234--the-bastion-opens-the-object-with-the-handed-data-key-alone)): the Bastion builds the data key
  from `dataKey`, `sha256` and `size` and reads through the format's reader with the digest checked (`blobcrypt.NewReader`,
  [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-082): a segment's plaintext reaches the spool only after its tag, the last data segment's only after the
  final segment's length and digest and the plaintext's SHA-256 have matched; then the commit checks as for every fill. The Bastion reads no
  record: it holds no storage key, and the main installation opened the record before it handed the key (steps 1 to 6 of R-STOR-077, in
  `CopyDataKey`); a body that is not the object under that key fails at its first segment.
- **What is kept** is an artifact entry as for an `artifact` answer (R-BAS-022): the content address, the size, the replay headers taken from
  the handover answer (R-BAS-057's rules), the repository, `validatedAt` the time the forward left, `Counted` from the marking, and
  `Package` from the marking's `Quader-Bastion-Package` (R-BAS-084). With a cache key it is encrypted under the Bastion's own key (R-BAS-061).
- **Callers that follow the fill** do so on their own permission (R-BAS-054), a package answer `full` on the fill's package included
  (R-BAS-085).
- **Reported downloads.** The main installation counted the download when it handed over ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095). The leader's
  caller is that download; the callers that follow the fill and every later hit are reported by the Bastion, as today (R-BAS-059).
- **Never passed to a caller.** The engine consumes a `handover` answer; a value it cannot use ends in the forward of R-BAS-075, never in a
  status or a header for the caller.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/handover`, `internal/bastion/engine`, the engine's double of the client and a TLS test store): a plain object of
  192 KiB and an encrypted one (written with the format's writer under a data key the double hands over) are read, committed and served,
  each caller's last 64 KiB after the commit; a second caller of the running fill follows it; the double's budget slot is free before the
  read ends; the link client sends no `Authorization` and no `Quader-` header, follows no redirect, and refuses an `http` link and a link on
  the Bastion's own host (`TestR_BAS_074_TheDirectReadAndItsVerification`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's side (package 3):* the link client is `handover.Client` in
[handover/client.go](../../internal/bastion/handover/client.go), a client of the outbound factory of its own (purpose `bastion_handover`) with
the system roots and `bastion.main.ca_file` re-read, the two timeouts, no redirect followed (a `3xx` is a failure before the first byte), no
cookie jar, no tracer, no upstream log and no outbound metrics (the client of the main installation registers those once per process); its
request is built from the link alone, with `User-Agent: quader-bastion/<release>`, and it refuses a link that is not `https`, carries user
information or names a refused host on any port, again after the engine's check. `Open` returns once the status is `200`, `Content-Length` is
`storedSize`, and the first 64 KiB of plaintext are verified: on an encrypted copy the first segment authenticated, and a blob of one segment,
plain or encrypted, read and checked whole ([Q-BAS-291](#q-bas-291--a-blob-of-one-segment-is-verified-whole-before-its-first-byte)). The
plain reader hashes as it reads and ends in `handover.ErrDigest` instead of the end when the digest differs; the encrypted reader is
`blobcrypt.NewReader` with the digest checked, over a data key built with `blobcrypt.KeyFromBytes` from the handed one (whose copy and
`HandoverKey` are destroyed at once) after `blobcrypt.StoredSize(size)` was compared with `storedSize`. The engine's `onHandover` closes the
handover answer's body before anything else, prepares the fill (`newFillRun`, shared with a fill from the main installation, so the entry carries
the marking's package, counting and repository), checks the spool's room, opens the read with the fill's detached context and hands it to
`runFill`, which the waiters of the flight follow as any fill. The cache keeps the plaintext through `cache.Fill`, sealed under its own key where it
has one. Tests: `TestR_BAS_074_TheLinkClientSendsNothingOfQuaders`, `TestR_BAS_074_TheLinkClientsRefusals`,
`TestR_BAS_074_ThePlainAndTheEncryptedRead`, `TestR_BAS_074_TheTrustIsReadAgain` (`internal/bastion/handover`, against the TLS store of
`maintest.Store`); `TestR_BAS_074_TheDirectReadAndItsVerification` (`internal/bastion/engine`, plain and encrypted blobs of 192 KiB, a follower, the
handover answer's body closed while the read runs, the entry's package, a cache with a key); at the integration tier the case that joins the two
sides, `TestR_BAS_070_ALargeFileIsReadFromTheObjectStore` (R-BAS-070's as-built note), which replaced the Bastion's half against `maintest`
(`TestR_BAS_074_ABastionReadsAHandedFileFromTheObjectStore`, removed on 2026-11-23).

### R-BAS-075 · A direct read that fails
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

Every failure of the direct read ends in the bytes through the main installation or in the refusal of a fill that exists today
([Q-BAS-235](#q-bas-235--a-failure-before-the-first-byte-is-a-forward-after-it-a-continuation-by-a-range)):

- **Before the first byte** (a link the store refuses or that has expired, a connect, name or TLS error, a timeout, a status other than
  `200`, another length, a redirect, a value R-BAS-073 refuses, a spool that cannot take the size, and on an encrypted copy a first segment
  that does not open): the Bastion sends the forward again without the offer and goes on as for a miss today; the caller sees a delay. The main
  installation counts and charges that second answer too ([security/bastion-handover.md](../security/bastion-handover.md) H-1342).
- **After the first byte** (a cut, the stall bound, on an encrypted copy a later segment that does not open): the fill continues from the main
  installation with a forward of the Bastion's own `Range: bytes=<n>-` and `If-Range: <the ETag>`, without the offer, where `n` is the length
  in the spool (on an encrypted copy a multiple of 65,536, since a segment's plaintext reaches the spool only after its tag); a `206` with
  `Content-Range: bytes <n>-<size − 1>/<size>` and the same `ETag` continues the spool, anything else fails the fill as a fill fails today
  (the callers cut before their last 64 KiB, nothing kept). The main installation counts no download for a `206` that starts after byte 0
  (Q-BAS-186), charges its bytes, and on an encrypted copy its ranged read re-reads the failed segment, so a damaged copy is marked and fallen
  over there (R-STOR-082). The commit's SHA-256 decides as for every fill.
- **A digest that differs at the end** (a plain copy changed in the bucket, the bytes of another object): the fill fails as every fill does,
  and the cache key is marked for `bastion.cache.artifact_revalidate_after`; its next fills send no offer, so the main installation's
  verifying read (R-STOR-013) meets the copy and marks it.
- **The cooldown** ([Q-BAS-236](#q-bas-236--a-replica-that-cannot-read-the-store-offers-no-handover-for-a-minute)). After a failure before the
  first byte whose cause is the network or the store (connect, name, TLS, timeout, a `403` or `5xx` of the store, another length), the
  replica sends no offer for 60 s, so a Bastion whose network does not reach the store costs one more forward per replica and minute, not
  one per miss. *Amended on 2026-11-23 ([Q-BAS-293](#q-bas-293--a-value-the-bastion-refuses-starts-the-cooldown)):* a value the Bastion
  refuses before the read starts the cooldown as well.
- **Metrics** (the builder adds them to R-BAS-040's table with the code, which a test holds to it): `quader_bastion_handovers_total{outcome}`
  with `read` (read from the store and committed), `fallback` (failed before the first byte), `continued` (finished through the main
  installation), `refused` (the bytes failed verification); `quader_bastion_fill_bytes_total{source}` with `main` and `store`; the gauges
  `quader_bastion_handover_enabled` (the handshake's member) and `quader_bastion_handover_cooldown` (1 while the replica sends no offer).
  The request log of the Bastion names the outcome in `bastion_handover`, never the link.
- **The alert** `QuaderBastionHandoverFailing` (warning, `for: 15m`): fallbacks, continuations or refusals within 15 minutes and no `read`,
  that is the Bastion's network does not reach the store or the store's answers fail (the builder adds the row to R-BAS-041's table and the
  name to the chart test's list).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, the engine's double and a TLS test store): a link the store refuses with `403` ends in a forward without
  the offer whose bytes the caller receives, counts `fallback` and starts the cooldown (the engine's field set to 1 s in the test); a cut after
  128 KiB of a plain object, and a flipped third segment of an encrypted one, continue with `Range: bytes=131072-` and `If-Range`, and the
  caller receives the whole blob; a plain object replaced by other bytes of the same length cuts every caller before its last 64 KiB, keeps
  nothing, and the next miss of the key sends no offer (`TestR_BAS_075_ADirectReadThatFails`).
- Chart: `QuaderBastionHandoverFailing` fires on a series of fallbacks without a read and stays silent on reads (`promtool test rules`,
  `TestR_BAS_041_PromtoolRules`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's side (package 3):* `fallback` in [engine/handover.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/handover.go) sends
the forward without the offer for every failure before the first verified bytes (a value the engine or the interface refuses, a fill the cache
cannot start, a spool without room, and every `handover.Error` of `Open`); the cooldown starts for a `handover.Error` whose cause is the
network or the store (`Cooldown()`: connect, name, TLS, a timeout, a body that broke off before its first byte, `403`, `5xx`, another length)
and, since the joined integration case of 2026-11-23, for a value the interface or the checks of `checkHandover` refuse
([Q-BAS-293](#q-bas-293--a-value-the-bastion-refuses-starts-the-cooldown)), and is the engine's field `handoverCooldown`. After the first byte `fillRun.run` asks `turnToMain`: the plain digest and the encrypted plaintext's
digest (`handover.ErrDigest`) fail the fill and mark the key; any other break (a cut, the stall bound, which ends only the direct read, a later
segment or the final segment that does not open) closes the read and continues the spool from the main installation with `Range` and `If-Range`
(`mainclient.Forward.RangeFrom`, `IfRange`), and `continues` accepts only a `206` of the rest with the fill's `ETag`. A commit whose SHA-256
fails after a direct read marks the key too. The four outcomes count once per handover by the path it took, and the request log's
`bastion_handover` names it, or `reading` for a caller that left while the read ran
([Q-BAS-290](#q-bas-290--a-handover-counts-one-outcome-by-the-path-it-took)). The replacing forward counts no second miss
([Q-BAS-292](#q-bas-292--the-forward-that-replaces-a-handover-counts-no-second-miss-and-a-core-route-carries-no-offer)). The alert's expression
is `(sum(increase(…{outcome=~"fallback|continued|refused"}[15m])) > 0) and (sum(increase(…{outcome="read"}[15m])) == 0)`, scoped to the
release. Besides the criteria above, `TestR_BAS_075_ADirectReadThatFails` shows that an expired link, a blob above the offer, a digest that is
not the `ETag`'s and a link on a host of the Bastion or of the main installation fall back without a read and start the cooldown, so that the
next miss offers nothing (Q-BAS-293), and that a continuation answered `200`, or `206` with another `ETag`, fails the fill.

### R-BAS-076 · The data key at the Bastion: held for one read, written nowhere
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- The data key lives in the memory of the replica that reads, from the start of the direct read to its end, whatever the end; then it is
  destroyed (`blobcrypt.Key.Destroy`). The handover's value lives in the request's memory until the read starts.
- It is written to no object of the cache store, no file of the spool, no Valkey key, no log record, no metric, no span and no line of the
  audit spool; its `String` and `LogValue` render nothing of it (the format's package). The link appears in no log either.
- A data key is never needed again: a revalidation is a conditional request (R-BAS-022), a refill is a new forward. What the Bastion keeps of a
  handed blob is what it keeps of every fill: the plaintext in its cache, encrypted under its own cache key where its chart gives one
  (R-BAS-061).
- Go's AES implementation keeps an expanded key schedule that no code can erase, so the memory of a Bastion pod holds the data keys of its
  current direct reads, as the memory of the main installation's pods holds theirs
  ([security/stored-content-keys.md](../security/stored-content-keys.md) H-1309). What a taken-over Bastion gains is
  [security/bastion-handover.md](../security/bastion-handover.md) H-1340.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, `internal/bastion/handover`): after a read that ends whole, one that fails before its first byte and one
  that fails after it, the data key is destroyed (a hook of the test counts it), and no object of the cache, no file of the spool, no
  record of the captured log and no metric of the test's registry holds the key's bytes in hexadecimal or base64url
  (`TestR_BAS_076_TheDataKeyIsWrittenNowhere`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's side (package 3):* the handed `HandoverKey` is destroyed when `handover.Client.Open` returns, whatever
happens, and by `onHandover` on every path that does not reach `Open`; the format's key lives in the read and is destroyed by `Read.Close`, which
the fill calls at the end of the read, at a break before the continuation and at every failure (`Open` destroys it itself when it fails). A
caller who leaves does not end the read: the fill outlives its caller (Q-BAS-123), so its key lives until the fill ends. `Client.KeysHeld` and
the option `OnKeyDestroyed` let the tests count. Tests: `TestR_BAS_076_TheKeyIsDestroyedAtEveryEnd` (`internal/bastion/handover`: a whole read,
a failure before and after the first byte, a cancelled read, no key in an error text) and `TestR_BAS_076_TheDataKeyIsWrittenNowhere`
(`internal/bastion/engine`: the same ends and a caller that leaves, then no file of the cache and its spool, no log record and no metric holds a
key in hexadecimal, base64url or base64).

### R-BAS-077 · A blob withdrawn while its link lives
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- The main installation decides when the forward arrives. A decision taken after it (the blob deleted, a malware find or a withdrawn release,
  a narrowed signature gate, a vulnerability block, a lowered visibility, a revoked grant or token) does not stop a direct read that has begun,
  as it does not stop a forwarded fill today ([Q-BAS-238](#q-bas-238--a-blob-withdrawn-during-a-fill-is-treated-as-in-a-forwarded-fill)): the
  fill completes, its caller and the callers that followed it receive the blob, and the entry is committed with a `validatedAt` from before
  the change. The feed's entry (R-BAS-015: `content`, `grants`, `token`, `principal`) then refuses the entry to every later caller (R-BAS-020,
  R-BAS-022, Q-BAS-122), whose request asks the main installation and gets its refusal.
- A read that starts after the object is gone (a deletion the collection completed, [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-024) gets the store's
  `404`, a failure before the first byte: the forward that replaces it gets the main installation's refusal (R-BAS-075).
- The link is used once, at once. A link taken out of a Bastion serves its object to whoever holds it for the rest of its life
  ([H-12](storage.md#h-12--presigned-download-urls-are-bearer-capabilities)), which is the installation's `linkLifeSeconds` (60 s unless the
  administrator sets 10 s to an hour). A data key outlives the withdrawal of its blob wherever the blob's ciphertext stays
  ([security/bastion-handover.md](../security/bastion-handover.md) H-1340).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`): a `content` entry for the repository that arrives while a direct read runs leaves the fill's callers
  served and the entry committed, and the next caller's request for the key is a conditional request whose refusal is replayed
  (`TestR_BAS_077_AWithdrawalDuringADirectRead`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's side (package 3):* nothing of its own: a fill whose source is the direct read is the same `fillRun`, its
entry's `validatedAt` the time the forward left, and `withdrawn` judges it as every entry (`TestR_BAS_077_AWithdrawalDuringADirectRead`).

### R-BAS-078 · The operator's side: the charts, the admin area, the manual and the egress
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **No value in either chart** (Q-BAS-232). The switch is the registration's member at the main installation (R-BAS-071), and the links'
  details are the installation's ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-014). The Bastion's chart holds what the link client needs already: its trust
  bundle (`trustedCA`) and the timeouts of `config.bastion.main`. Its change, made with the build: the alert of R-BAS-075 in the
  PrometheusRule with its promtool test, and the comment of `trustedCA.existingSecret` (today "trust for the main installation, Valkey and the
  bucket"), which gains the main installation's object store, in the chart's `values.yaml` and in R-BAS-046's block together, which the values
  test compares.
- **The admin area:** the card's switch and the connections' reasons (R-BAS-071); the links' details on the storage settings page
  (R-STOR-014, [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-200), whose test link the administrator opens from a machine of the Bastion's network to
  see whether it reaches a connection's public address, an encrypted connection's included ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-074, R-STOR-096).
- **The egress.** The chart renders no egress rule (R-BAS-047, [H-522](../security/bastion.md#h-522--the-chart-restricts-no-egress-of-the-bastion-pods)).
  An operator who restricts the Bastion pods' egress admits, while the handover is on, the public address of every connection a handover may
  name (R-STOR-074: its public address, or its endpoint without one), on its port.
- **The manual** (`docs/manual/admin/bastion.md`, a section "Direct reads from the object store"): when to switch it on (images and other
  large files read through the Bastion); what must hold first (each connection's public address reachable from the Bastion's network, `https`,
  with a certificate the Bastion trusts through the system roots or `trustedCA`; the test link opened from that network); what leaves the main
  installation (a link per file, and for an encrypted connection that file's data key); what to do when a Bastion is taken over (switch the
  handover off, revoke its token, and for encrypted content whose bucket or backup target its holder may read, a new connection that the
  reconciliation fills with new data keys, [security/stored-content-keys.md](../security/stored-content-keys.md) H-1311); and the sizing
  (`max_object_bytes` and `spool_max_bytes` at least the largest layer). It lands with the build, as the repository's documentation rule says.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart render tests: the PrometheusRule holds `QuaderBastionHandoverFailing` scoped to the release; no value of either chart is added
  (`TestR_BAS_041_PrometheusRuleAlerts`, `TestR_BAS_046_ValuesReferenceIsTheSpecBlock`).

*As built on 2026-11-23, the Bastion's chart (package 3):* the alert in [_rules.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader-bastion/templates/_rules.tpl)
with its two promtool cases in [rules_test.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader-bastion/tests/rules_test.yaml) and its name in the list of
`disabledAlerts`, and the comment of `trustedCA.existingSecret` (`trust for the main installation, its object store, Valkey and the bucket`). No
value was added.

*As built on 2026-11-23, the admin area and the manual (package 5):* the card's switch and the connections' reasons are R-BAS-071's
as-built note; the storage settings page offers every connection's public address and its test link, an encrypted connection's too, with
what such a connection serves today ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-200,
[Q-UI-958](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-958--an-encrypted-connection-has-its-address-and-its-test-link-for-a-bastion-and-says-what-it-serves-today)).
The manual's section [Direct reads from the object store](../manual/admin/bastion.md#direct-reads-from-the-object-store) says what the
handover is, when to switch it on (the measurement of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-handover.md#tests-and-what-they-cost)), what
it needs (a public address on a host name that is not the main installation's, `trustedCA`, the Bastion's network), what an administrator
takes on and what to do when a Bastion is taken over, the sizing, how to see that it works and why it does not, and that a file of an
encrypted connection is handed with its own data key.

### R-BAS-079 · Tests of the handover and what they cost
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

By the owner's rule "Tests stay runnable" of 2026-11-20: each behaviour once, at the cheapest tier
([Q-BAS-239](#q-bas-239--the-tests-once-at-the-cheapest-tier-one-integration-case-no-end-to-end-case)). Nothing of it depends on a format:
the main installation hands over a stored file of any format through one serve point, and the Bastion reads artifacts without knowing a
format. The run times are the planner's estimates; the builder records the measured ones on
[developer/bastion-handover.md](../developer/bastion-handover.md).

| Tier | Test | Data | Run time (estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit, `internal/bastion/iface` | the value, the offer, the class, the interface's file (R-BAS-073) | none | under 0.1 s |
| unit, `internal/downloadlinks`, `internal/api/edge`, `internal/formathost`, `internal/api/rawfiles` | the conditions of R-STOR-095 one by one, the choice of the copy, what is counted and charged, the link check's two results (R-STOR-095, R-STOR-096) | the in-memory store, objects of 1 KiB | about 1 s |
| unit, `internal/api/bastionmark`, `internal/bastionmain`, `internal/api/v1` | the marking only on an offer, the switch, its events and replay, the handshake's member (R-BAS-071, R-BAS-073) | none | about 0.5 s |
| unit, `internal/downloadlinks` with an encrypted connection, `internal/archtest` | the data key from `CopyDataKey`, the trace before the answer, a failed insert streams, the callers of `CopyDataKey` (R-STOR-096) | objects of 1 KiB | about 0.4 s |
| unit, `internal/bastion/handover`, `internal/bastion/engine` | the read, its verification, its failures, the continuation, the mark, the cooldown, the key written nowhere, a withdrawal during a read (R-BAS-072, R-BAS-074 to R-BAS-077) | objects up to 256 KiB, made in memory | about 1.5 s |
| chart | the alert's promtool case and its name in the list (R-BAS-075, R-BAS-078) | none | about 0.2 s |
| Vitest | the card's switch and reasons (R-BAS-071) | fixtures | about 0.5 s |
| integration, area `bastion` | one case (R-BAS-070) against the stack's object store: a cold fill by a handover, a hit, a fallback with an unreachable public address; once encrypted connections exist, the same with an encrypted connection | one file of 64 KiB | about 3 s, and about 2 s more |
| measurement, once before landing (not a test) | `docker pull` of an image with a layer of about 300 MiB through a Bastion with the handover on, against the local stack: bytes the main installation sent against bytes the store sent | real clients | minutes, once |

- **What each leg gains** (estimates): the unit job about 3.7 s; the web unit job about 0.5 s; the chart test about 0.2 s; the integration
  shard that holds the area `bastion` about 5 s; every end-to-end leg and the nightly nothing.
- **With 25 formats:** the same. No test is per format, no leg loads a client image for it.

Acceptance criteria:

- The tests named in R-BAS-070 to R-BAS-078 and in [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095 and R-STOR-096 pass in their tiers.

*As built on 2026-11-23 (package 4):* the data key's unit tests run 0.65 s under the race detector with atomic coverage, of which 0.31 s are
new in the conditions' table (each condition once more on an encrypted connection); the integration case with an encrypted connection runs
3.0 s in the area `bastion`, two files of 65 KiB; the measured numbers and what each leg gains are on
[the build plan](../developer/bastion-handover.md#tests-and-what-they-cost).

## Read shapes per package

The development agent's decision of 2026-11-22 on [Q-BAS-167](#q-bas-167--a-registry-token-is-checked-by-the-main-installation-and-its-read-shape-is-at-most-partial),
option (b), after the owner's word that its favourite is built and not what was built first. A registry token, and every reader narrowed by
package, reads the whole repository rarely and one package of it often. Today the Bastion knows only the caller's shape on the repository,
so such a caller is served every cached artifact after a conditional request: a warm pull of an image of ten layers costs the main
installation twelve requests against the miss limit of the client's address
([H-1242](#h-1242--every-pull-with-a-registry-token-costs-the-main-installation-its-token-request-and-one-check)). This section gives the
Bastion a fourth kind of answer, the caller's shape on one package of a repository, and the entries the package they belong to.

- **The main installation's core already knows a response's package.** Every format decides the reads of its package through the host
  (`Host.Authorize` with `Target.Package`), and the core notes that package for a recognized Bastion request as it notes `absent` and
  `counted` today (R-BAS-081). No format code is involved.
- **The marking** gains two headers: the response's package and the caller's shape on it, `full` or `partial` (R-BAS-082). **The check**
  can be asked about (repository, package) pairs (R-BAS-083). For a registry token the main installation limits the package shape to the
  token's grant, and the Bastion compares it with the grant it reads without verifying it (R-BAS-052, Q-BAS-246).
- **The Bastion** keeps package answers keyed by (credential, repository, package) and records the package on each cache entry. An entry of
  package P is served without a request to a caller with a usable `full` answer on P (R-BAS-084, R-BAS-085). Such an answer follows the same
  four validity rules and the same feed as a `full` answer on the repository, so nothing is served longer than today's rules allow a full
  reader.
- **The format contract** gains kit check 21: what a reader of only the response's package receives equals what a reader of the whole
  repository receives (R-BAS-086). **The interface** takes the next version, 5 (R-BAS-087).

Status: specified on 2026-11-22; the wire (package 1 of the build plan: R-BAS-087 and the types of R-BAS-082 and R-BAS-083), the decision
point and the format contract (package 2: R-BAS-080, R-BAS-086) and the main installation's side (package 3: R-BAS-081 to R-BAS-083) built on
2026-11-22, the Bastion's side (package 4: R-BAS-084, R-BAS-085) built on 2026-11-23: all four built. The planner's design was read against
`main` on 2026-11-22; the build plan is
[developer/bastion-package-shapes.md](../developer/bastion-package-shapes.md); the decisions are
[Q-BAS-240](#q-bas-240--what-full-on-a-package-means) to [Q-BAS-254](#q-bas-254--the-tests), Q-BAS-255, Q-BAS-260, Q-BAS-261,
[Q-BAS-265](#q-bas-265--the-read-scope-a-format-meets-has-mayread-rows-only) and, from the build of package 4,
[Q-BAS-270](#q-bas-270--a-package-answer-that-ended-with-its-shape-answer-is-renewed-by-the-check) and
[Q-BAS-271](#q-bas-271--the-end-to-end-warm-assertion-counts-what-a-warm-pull-asks-about-artifacts); the gaps are
[H-1380](#h-1380--changes-the-feed-does-not-carry-reach-registry-token-and-package-narrowed-readers-within-the-revalidation-periods-no-longer-at-their-next-read)
to [H-1384](#h-1384--the-first-read-of-a-cached-entry-by-a-credential-without-a-shape-answer-costs-two-requests-an-uncached-one-costs-one),
H-1390, [H-1395](#h-1395--an-official-image-of-a-docker-hub-remote-without-a-namespace-prefix-names-two-packages-and-carries-none),
[H-1420](#h-1420--while-the-main-installation-admits-anonymous-reads-a-clients-first-head-of-a-tag-without-a-credential-is-forwarded-on-every-pull)
and the new text of H-1242 (H-1295 closed); the record is
[ADR-254](../decisions.md#adr-254--read-shapes-per-package-at-a-bastion-a-registry-token-is-full-on-the-images-of-its-grant).

**Measured on 2026-11-23** (R-BAS-088, [developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-real-clients-through-a-bastion); a kind cluster,
an image of one manifest, a config and ten layers, private, a registry token per pull, every entry cached and fresh). Requests to the main
installation per warm pull, before and after package 4: Docker 29.9.3 **16 → 4** (the probe and the token, its `HEAD` of the tag without a
credential, which the Bastion forwards while anonymous reads are on, H-1420, and the `HEAD` of the tag, which has no entry because Docker
never `GET`s it); Podman 5.8.9 **13 → 2** and **14 → 2** (the token and the tag's forward, then the token and one check); crictl with
containerd 2.3.4 **19 → 6** and **18 → 5** (two probes, two tokens and a check per token). No conditional request remains in a warm pull.

*The planner's derivation of 2026-11-22, kept for comparison:* derived from reading the read flow and from the measurement of 2026-11-22 on
smaller images. The image has a single platform, a config and ten layers, its content is not `public`, and the Bastion answers the anonymous
version check or `HEAD` itself (no request). "Warm" means every entry is cached and within its revalidation period. Requests to the main
installation per pull:

| Client (token step) | Before, cold | Before, warm | After, cold | After, warm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Podman (`GET /v2/_token`: 1) | 13: token, tag, config, 10 layers; all transferred | 13: token, tag (forwarded and transferred, `private`), 11 conditional requests answered `304`; 14 when a full reader's `shared` tag entry exists (one check more) | 13; the tag is now kept `shared` | **2**: token and one check |
| Docker 29 (probe and `POST`: 2) | 14 | 14 (15) | 14 | **3** |
| containerd and the kubelet (probe and `POST`: 2; `HEAD` of the tag, manifest by digest) | 15 | 15 (16) | 15 | **3** |

- The 11 to 12 conditional requests per pull and the forward of the tag's document disappear. The token request (with its probe for a
  `POST`) stays, and so does the first read of each new registry token: the check.
- Revalidation is amortized: one conditional request per tag per `metadata_revalidate_after` (1 minute) and one per artifact per
  `artifact_revalidate_after` (10 minutes), paid by whichever caller arrives first.
- A rollout behind one address (300 misses a minute): about 20 to 23 pulls a minute before, about 100 (Docker, the kubelet) or 150 (Podman)
  after.
- npm, a reader narrowed to `@acme/*` in every member, running `npm ci` of 20 `@acme` tarballs: 21 requests per run before (1 check and 20
  conditional requests); after, 20 for the first run in a period (1 check, then 19 conditional requests that each supply a package answer)
  and none for every later run with the same token within the period.
