### R-BAS-080 · Read shapes per package at the decision point
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The package shape** of subject S on the addressed repository R and package P, where P is the name as the format's coordinates carry it
  (`authz.Coordinate.Package`), is computed by `authz.Engine.PackageReachOn(ctx, idx, sub, repo, pkgs)` beside `ReachOn`
  ([Q-BAS-240](#q-bas-240--what-full-on-a-package-means)):
  - A `full` shape on R is `full` on every package. A `none` shape on R is `partial` on every package on the wire, never `none`
    ([Q-BAS-243](#q-bas-243--package-shapes-have-two-values-and-absent-stays-per-repository)).
  - **R local or remote:** `full` when all five hold: (1) the endpoint exposes everything (`exposesEverything`); (2) no path pattern can
    tell two paths of R apart for S (`readsByPath(R)` is false); (3) on the artifact state, with `content:metadata-read` left out, the read
    of P is allowed, decided as `ReadScope.MayRead(R, P, "")` decides it; (4) the wiki of P is readable (`MayReadWiki(R, P, "")`); (5) for
    a remote repository, S has the populate right for P. Otherwise `partial`. Conditions 2 and 3 together cover every version: a version is
    decided on the package's path and on its file's path (Q-AUTHZ-255), and without a path pattern both decisions come from the package
    patterns alone.
  - **R virtual:** `full` when the gate read of R is allowed for metadata and for artifacts, and every member, recursively (depth 16, as
    `reachVirtual`), is `full` on P with R as the addressed repository. Otherwise `partial`.
  - **A credential with a registry grant:** `full` only where the grant allows pull on (R, P) (`Grant.Allows`); applied by the marking
    and the check (R-BAS-082, R-BAS-083), since `authz.Subject` holds no grant.
- **Whom it serves:** every caller whose shape on the repository is `partial`: registry tokens; personal, service-account and CI tokens
  narrowed by package patterns in a grant or in a token scope; CI contributions narrowed by package. A reader with a `full` shape on the
  repository needs no computation. The anonymous caller gains nothing in practice, because visibility levels are per repository.
- **The limit of the rule.** A reader narrowed in one member and without rights in another member of a virtual repository stays `partial`
  on that repository's packages: `$PART` through `npm-all` has no grant on `npm-remote` and is `partial` there, and through `npm-local` it is
  `full` on `@acme/sdk`. Any path pattern of a grant on R makes every package of R `partial` for that subject.

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_080_PackageShapeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint` (`internal/authz`), over every subject, endpoint, repository, package, version and
  path of the reach fixture (15 subjects, 3 endpoints, 15 repository keys, 4 packages): a `full` package shape never meets a refused read
  (metadata, artifact or wiki) of any version or path of that package, and a `full` repository shape implies `full` on every package.
- `TestR_BAS_080_PackageShapes`: a grant `packages.include: ["@acme/*"]` on a local repository is `full` on `@acme/sdk` and `partial` on
  `x`, and `partial` on both with a path pattern; a token scope listing `@acme/*` gives `full`; an endpoint with exposure rules gives
  `partial`; a remote repository without the populate right gives `partial`, and `full` with it; a virtual repository with an unreadable
  member gives `partial`; no wiki read gives `partial`; `content:metadata-read` alone gives `partial`.

*As built on 2026-11-22* ([reach_package.go](../../internal/authz/reach_package.go), [Q-BAS-260](#q-bas-260--the-fill-of-a-package-is-decided-without-a-path)):
`authz.PackageReacher` with `Engine.PackageReachOn(ctx, idx, sub, repo, pkgs) (map[string]Reach, error)`, `ReachFull` or `ReachPartial` for
each name, an empty name partial. It derives the subject's state once, asks the repository's reach first (`full` and `none` decide every
package), and then the five conditions per package: `exposesEverything`; `readsByPath` on the state without `content:metadata-read`, since
that capability never reads an artifact and would hide a grant's path pattern; the read scope's own `MayRead(R, P, "")` on that state and
`MayReadWiki(R, P, "")` on the full one; for a remote repository `populate` on P without a path, so that a fill narrowed by path patterns is
refused. A virtual repository asks its gate for a metadata and an artifact read and every member as `reachVirtual` does. The fixture of the
reach (`reachFixture` in [reach_test.go](../../internal/authz/reach_test.go)) has 26 subjects, 3 endpoints, 16 repository keys and 4 packages;
it gained the case of each condition: an exposure rule with a version range, a grant of a package document's path alone, an auditor with
member grants and a path-pattern grant, a fill narrowed by package, an external user and a scoped internal token reading one package of a
repository whose wiki is `internal`, a reader of a nested virtual repository's leaves without its gate. Each of the five conditions, the virtual
gate's artifact read, the members' rule and the nested gate was taken out once, and `TestR_BAS_080_PackageShapeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint`
failed each time. **The build found two holes in `ReachOn` (R-BAS-012), closed in the same change:** the wiki and the fill of a frozen mirror
were decided on a coordinate without a package and a path, which a grant or a token scope narrowed by package matches whatever its
patterns say (R-AUTHZ-005). An external user with a grant on `@a/*` of a repository whose artifacts are `public` and whose wiki is
`internal`, an internal user's token scoped to `@a/*` there, and a reader whose `deploy` on a frozen mirror is narrowed to `@acme/*` were
`full` on the repository while the wiki, or the fill, of another package was refused, so the marking would have let a Bastion share a
document with a README, or a remote's document, with them. `ReachOn` now asks the wiki's own read shape (`readShapeOf` with the part wiki) and,
for a frozen mirror, the action on every package and path (`actsEverywhere`); `TestR_BAS_012_ShapeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint` asks the wiki of
every package as well, and fails without either change.

### R-BAS-081 · The package of a response
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The core notes the package of every rights decision** of a recognized Bastion request into the request's `Absence` record
  (`bastionmain.NotePackage(ctx, pkg)`), with no format code ([Q-BAS-241](#q-bas-241--how-the-main-installation-learns-a-responses-package)):
  `Host.Authorize`, whether it allows or refuses; `Host.WikiReadable`; each path of `Host.PathsAllowed`, through the format's `Classify`;
  and each `MayRead` row of the read scope that `formathost/virtual.go` hands out (a format asks the wiki through `Host.WikiReadable`,
  [Q-BAS-265](#q-bas-265--the-read-scope-a-format-meets-has-mayread-rows-only)).
- **The response's package is P** exactly when at least one decision named P, every decision named P, and none named no package. The record
  is read at the status line, as `absent` and `counted` are.
- **What a format owes** is kit check 21 (R-BAS-086): every decision of a content route before its status line; a response that draws on
  packages other than the one it was decided for also decides a package-less read (`Host.Authorize` with a target that names no package, as
  npm's audit and signature handlers do), so that it carries no package; a reader of only the response's package receives the same status,
  body and validators as a reader of the whole repository.
- `/files/` decides through `files.Access`, not through the host, and names no package: only the repository shape applies there. For OCI the
  image name the handlers authorize is the enforcement point's `route.Target.Image`, and a test holds the two equal.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/formathost`, `internal/bastionmain`): `Authorize(P)` twice yields P; `Authorize(P)` and `MayRead(Q)` yield none;
  `Authorize(P)` and a package-less `Authorize` yield none; a refused `Authorize(Q)` after P yields none; `PathsAllowed` over paths of P
  yields P; `WikiReadable(P)` yields P.
- Unit (`internal/api/bastionmark`, every format registered), through the dispatcher's registry handler with tokens from the real signer:
  `GET /v2/web/docker-local/app/blobs/sha256:…` is marked `Quader-Bastion-Package: app`, equal to the enforcement point's image, also on a
  bound host; a `/files/` download, npm's root and npm's search carry no package.

*As built on 2026-11-22 (package P3 of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-package-shapes.md)):* `bastionmain.NotePackage` folds each
decision into the request's `Absence` record and `Absence.Package` applies the rule; a package-less decision or a second package clears the
record for good ([absence.go](../../internal/bastionmain/absence.go)). The production host notes in `Host.Authorize` (before the decision, so a
refusal names its package too), `Host.WikiReadable`, each path of `Host.PathsAllowed` (`notePaths`, which classifies only on a recognized
Bastion request, `bastionmain.NotesPackages`) and the read scope's `MayRead` (likewise only on such a request) ([host.go](../../internal/formathost/host.go),
[virtual.go](../../internal/formathost/virtual.go)). Two production decisions that check 21 does not reach are noted as well and can only clear
the package: the serve-time signature gate's write question on the served path (`mayWrite`; the kit's host has no signature gate), and the
path of OCI's second spelling of a Docker Hub official image on a remote without a namespace prefix (a remote handler,
[H-1390](#h-1390--kit-check-21-runs-over-the-local-class-only)), which takes the gain away from those images
([H-1395](#h-1395--an-official-image-of-a-docker-hub-remote-without-a-namespace-prefix-names-two-packages-and-carries-none)). The tests:
`TestR_BAS_081_TheResponsesPackageIsTheOnePackageEveryDecisionNamed` (`internal/bastionmain`),
`TestR_BAS_081_TheHostNotesThePackageOfEveryDecision` (`internal/formathost`, the six cases of the criterion and their opposites), and
`TestR_BAS_081_TheImageTheHandlersAuthorizeIsTheEnforcementPointsImage` (`internal/api/bastionmark`): through `registry.Register`, the real
authentication stage with a real signer, the dispatcher and the OCI format's own handlers over the production host, a blob read with a token
granted the image is marked with the image the enforcement point's match names, `full`, on an unbound host, for a nested name, on a host bound
to the repository and in the cache view of a remote repository; a token granted another image is refused `401 insufficient_scope` without a
package; npm's root and its `-/v1/search` carry none. `/files/` is not run: `internal/files` and `internal/api/rawfiles` never note, so a
`/files/` response carries no package by construction, and the marking's side of it is the case "no decision names none" of
`TestR_BAS_082_TheMarkingPerPackage`.

### R-BAS-082 · The marking per package
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Headers** ([Q-BAS-242](#q-bas-242--the-wire-of-the-marking)): `Quader-Bastion-Package` and `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read` as in
  R-BAS-013's table: the package percent-encoded (every byte outside `A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~ @ /` as `%XX` with upper-case hexadecimal digits;
  decoded 1 to 512 bytes, valid UTF-8, no control character), present on a `200` or `304` of a `Download`, `Metadata` or `Computed` route
  and on a handover's `200` (R-BAS-073) whose request named exactly one package (R-BAS-081), absent everywhere else, every refusal and
  every `404` included; `-Package-Read` is present exactly with it and is `full` when `Quader-Bastion-Read` is `full` or the package shape
  of R-BAS-080, with a registry token's grant applied, is `full`. Like every `Quader-Bastion-` header they are stripped for every other
  caller.
- **The class rule.** `shared` for a `200` or `304` of a `Metadata` or `Computed` route when `Quader-Bastion-Read: full` **or**
  `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read: full` ([Q-BAS-244](#q-bas-244--documents-are-shared-per-package)). `absent` stays tied to a `full` shape on
  the repository.
- **The types.** `iface.Marking` gains `Package string` (decoded) and `PackageRead Read` (only `full` or `partial`). `ParseMarking` refuses
  one header without the other, more than one value of either, any other value of `-Package-Read`, a value that does not decode strictly,
  and a decoded name outside the bounds.
- **Examples.** A registry token granted `library/nginx` reading a blob: `Quader-Bastion-Read: partial`, `Quader-Bastion-Package:
  library/nginx`, `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read: full`. npm sends `@acme/sdk` unencoded; Debian's `g++` becomes `g%2B%2B`.
- **Where it is computed.** The marking keeps the subject and the index of `Decided` and computes the package shape at the status line
  (`ShapeResolver.PackageShapes`, `bastionmain.CapRegistryPackage` for the grant).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/api/bastionmark`): a token granted read on `npm-local` with `@acme/*`, reading a tarball of `@acme/sdk` through
  `web/npm-local`: `Read: partial`, `Package: @acme/sdk`, `Package-Read: full`, and its package document `Class: shared`; through
  `web/npm-all`: `Package-Read: partial` and `private`; `$FULL`: `Read: full`, `Package-Read: full`; a `404` and a refusal carry no package;
  a registry token granted `app` reading `app`: `Package-Read: full`.
- Unit (`internal/bastion/iface`): `ParseMarking` refuses each of the five malformed cases above; `g++` round-trips as `g%2B%2B`.

*As built on 2026-11-22, the wire (package P1 of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-package-shapes.md)):* `iface.HeaderPackage`,
`iface.HeaderPackageRead`, `Marking.Package` and `Marking.PackageRead`; the bounds are `iface.ValidPackage` and `iface.MaxPackageBytes`
(512), the encoding is in [package.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/package.go). Decoding strictly means: every byte is one of the
verbatim set or starts `%XX` with two upper-case hexadecimal digits, and `%XX` never stands for a byte of the verbatim set, so a name has
exactly one spelling on the wire (`%41` for `A` is refused). `Marking.Set` writes both headers only for a name within the bounds and
writes `partial` unless `PackageRead` is `full`, so a defect at the writer claims less, never more. `ParseMarking` refuses the five cases
(`TestR_BAS_082_ParseMarkingRefusesAMalformedPackage`, `TestR_BAS_082_TheMarkingCarriesThePackage`). P1 wrote no header: the
main installation's marking (P3) and the Bastion's reading of them (P4) are built since.

*As built on 2026-11-22, the main installation's marking (package P3):* `Decided` keeps the request's context, the subject and the index
beside the repository shape; at the status line `marking` reads `Absence.Package` for a `200` or `304` of a `Download`, `Metadata` or
`Computed` route that is no probe, and `packageRead` gives `-Package-Read`: `full` for a `full` repository shape, `partial` for `none` or no
shape, and for a `partial` one `ShapeResolver.PackageShapes` (`authz.Engine.PackageReachOn`, in memory on the kept index, no database
statement); a registry token is then limited by `bastionmain.CapRegistryPackage` with `httpserver.RegistryGrant.PullsImage`, which also
refuses a grant pinned to one manifest (a scan token's reaches no image's tags). `classOf` makes a document `shared` on `Read: full` or
`Package-Read: full`. A name `iface.ValidPackage` refuses gives no package and no `shared` by it
([mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go)). `TestR_BAS_082_TheMarkingPerPackage` holds the criterion's cases with the rig's notes
(a narrowed reader's tarball and document, `304`, `HEAD`, a package read in part, a full reader without a question to the decision point, a
registry token on its image and on another, two packages, a package-less decision, a `404`, a `206`, a `Volatile` route, a probe, a refusal, a
repository read none of, a pinned grant, a shape that cannot be computed); `TestR_BAS_082_TheTwoHeadersReachNoOrdinaryCaller` holds the strip.
The criterion's `web/npm-local` and `web/npm-all` are the rig's `partial` shape with a `full` and a `partial` package shape; the decision
point's own answer for them is `TestR_BAS_080_PackageShapes`.

### R-BAS-083 · The check per package
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

`POST /api/v1/bastion/check` (R-BAS-011) gains one member in the request and one in the answer, both always present:

```json
{"credential": "qdr_rgt_…", "clientAddress": "203.0.113.7", "repositories": ["web/docker"],
 "packages": [{"repository": "web/docker", "package": "library/nginx"}]}
```

```json
{"subject": {"kind": "token", "tokenId": "0192…", "principalId": "0191…", "expiresAt": "2026-11-22T10:05:00Z"},
 "repositories": {"web/docker": {"read": "partial"}},
 "packages": [{"repository": "web/docker", "package": "library/nginx", "read": "full"}]}
```

*(example request and answer)*

- **Request rules.** The package is a decoded JSON string with the bounds of the header (R-BAS-082); its repository is named in
  `repositories`; no pair appears twice; at most `bastions.check.max_repositories` elements (16, the existing value, no new setting). A
  violation answers `422` with a field error at `/packages/<i>` for the first element that breaks a rule, as the check's other field errors
  do ([Q-BAS-255](#q-bas-255--a-checks-package-that-breaks-a-rule-answers-422-as-the-checks-other-field-errors)).
- **Answer rules.** One element per requested pair, in request order; an empty array for a subject that is not usable; a pair whose
  repository reads `none` reads `partial`. A credential with a registry grant is limited to its grant (R-BAS-080).
- **The types.** The OpenAPI schemas `BastionCheckRequest` and `BastionCheckAnswer` gain the members; `x-quader-bastion-interface` is the
  new version on all four operations (R-BAS-087); `iface.CheckRequest.Packages` and `iface.CheckAnswer.Packages`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/api/v1`), through the real authentication stage: a registry token granted `web/docker-local/app` asked about the packages
  `[app, other]` answers `full`, `partial`; a package whose repository is not named, more than 16 elements, or a name of 513 bytes answers
  `422` at `/packages/<i>`; an `invalid` subject answers `packages: []`; a repository that reads `none` gives its packages `partial`.

*As built on 2026-11-22, the wire (package P1):* `iface.CheckRequest.Packages` (`iface.CheckPackages` of `iface.CheckPackage`) and
`iface.CheckAnswer.Packages` (`iface.PackageReads` of `iface.PackageRead`); both are written `[]` when empty, whoever builds the body, so
the member is always present. The request rules are `iface.CheckRequest.PackagesProblem`, shared by the main installation's check and the
fake main installation of the Bastion's tests (`maintest`); its codes are `count`, `invalid_package`, `unknown_repository` and
`duplicate`. The OpenAPI schemas `BastionCheckPackage` and `BastionPackageRead`. The main installation validates the pairs and answers
`packages: []` to every check, so nothing changes for a caller until the main installation answers per pair (P3) and the Bastion asks
(P4) (`TestR_BAS_083_ACheckRequestsPackagesAreValidated`, `TestR_BAS_083_TheCheckCarriesPackages`,
`TestR_BAS_083_ThePackagesOfACheckAreValidated`). The criterion's answers per pair are P3's.

*As built on 2026-11-22, the answers per pair (package P3):* `checkPackages` in [bastion_check_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_check_api.go)
answers one element per pair in request order from the shapes the check computed for its repositories, before the registry cap: `full` for a
repository read in full, `partial` for one read none of or not known, and for a repository read in part the decision point's package shapes
(`ShapeResolver.PackageShapes`), asked once per such repository on the check's index; every pair of a registry token is then limited by
`bastionmain.CapRegistryPackage` with the grant the authentication stage carried (`httpserver.RegistryGrant.PullsImage`). A refusal of the
decision point to decide is the check's error, as for the shapes. `TestR_BAS_083_ARegistryTokenIsFullOnlyOnTheImagesOfItsGrant` (the real
authentication stage, a registry token of a real signer granted `web/docker-local/app`, the token behind it `full` on the repository: `[app,
other]` answers `full`, `partial`, the repository `partial`; the Quader token itself `full` on both) and
`TestR_BAS_083_TheCheckAnswersEachPairInRequestOrder` (a repository read none of is `partial` although the decision point would say `full` on
the package; only the repository read in part is asked). The integration area `bastioniface` asserts the pairs of `$PART`
(`TestR_BAS_011_ACheckAnswersTheSubjectAndTheShapes`).

### R-BAS-084 · Package answers at the Bastion
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

| | Rule |
|---|---|
| Kind | `answers.Package`, a fourth kind beside credential, shape and URL (R-BAS-020) |
| Key | `<credential key>\|<projectKey>/<repoKey>\|<package>`; in memory `package\|…`; in Valkey `quader-bastion:<prefix>:ans:v1:package:<sha256 of the key>`, signed, with a TTL of the period plus the grace period, as every answer |
| Recorded from | (a) the marking of any forward, conditional request or handover answer whose `Quader-Bastion-Repository` equals the request's repository; (b) the check's `packages`. Only while the caller's shape on the repository is not `full`, since a `full` answer on the repository covers every package. For a registry token `full` is recorded only when the token's unverified grant names (repository, package) with pull, otherwise `partial` ([Q-BAS-246](#q-bas-246--the-bastions-own-guard-for-registry-tokens)); this is checked when the answer is recorded, so no part of the grant is kept |
| Validity | the four rules of R-BAS-020, unchanged. Rule 2 ends a registry token's package answer with the token, at most 300 s after its issue, never extended, also not in the grace period. Rule 3: `token`, `principal` and `grants` entries match package answers; `content` entries do not, and make the cache entry stale instead (R-BAS-022, [Q-BAS-249](#q-bas-249--the-feed-is-unchanged)) |
| Renewal | by use ([Q-BAS-248](#q-bas-248--package-answers-renew-by-use)): no background refresh; once the answer has expired, the next read sends one conditional request, and its marking renews the answer. *As built:* when the shape answer ended with it, which is the usual case, that one request is the check of R-BAS-085 step 4, which renews both ([Q-BAS-270](#q-bas-270--a-package-answer-that-ended-with-its-shape-answer-is-renewed-by-the-check)) |
| Bound per caller | no count of its own ([Q-BAS-247](#q-bas-247--bounds-on-package-answers)): each package answer needs a marked response or a check, and each of those is a miss of the caller's address (300 a minute); a registry token can be `full` on at most its grant's 16 entries |
| Bound in total | `bastion.answers.max_entries` (200,000 per replica), shared by every kind, least recently used first; at the bound an answer of any kind is evicted and its caller pays one request at its next read. A warm pull leaves about 3 answers (credential, shape, package) instead of about 14 (credential, shape, 12 URL answers) |
| Cache entries | keys unchanged; `cache.Entry` gains `Package string` (omitted when empty, signed with the entry), set from the marking of the `200` that filled the entry, replaced by every later `200` or `304` for the key, cleared by a marking without a package. A replica of the previous release decodes an entry with `json.Unmarshal`, ignores the member and serves by the repository shape only |

- `storedCheck` rebuilds the package answer as well. No new configuration value on either side.

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_084_PackageAnswers` (`internal/bastion/engine`, `internal/bastion/answers`): an answer obtained before a `grants` entry is not
  used after it; a `token` entry naming the Quader token behind a registry token drops its package answers; the answer is unusable at the
  registry token's expiry; with the local shared store an answer recorded on replica A serves on B; a registry token whose unverified grant
  does not name (repository, package) is recorded `partial` although the marking says `full` (tokens from the real `registrytoken`
  encoder).

*As built on 2026-11-23 (package P4 of [the build plan](../developer/bastion-package-shapes.md)):* `answers.Package` (the kind `package`);
rule 3 (`FeedLog.matches`) and the engine's `entryMatcher` treat it as a shape answer: `token`, `principal` and `grants` entries match it,
`content` entries do not ([answers.go](../../internal/bastion/answers/answers.go), [answerstore.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/answerstore.go)).
The key is `packageKey` (`<credential key>|<projectKey>/<repoKey>|<package>`; a repository name holds no `|`, so it splits one way only),
in memory `package|…` and in Valkey `ans:v1:package:<sha256>` (`shared.AnswerPackage`); the record holds the answer's time, identity,
expiry, repository and read, and the package only as part of the hashed key, so it stays within Valkey's 1 KiB whatever the name. Answers
are recorded by `putPackage` ([packages.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/packages.go)): from `recordAnswers` for a marking whose repository
is the request's while the capped shape is `partial`, and from `recordCheck` for the one pair the Bastion asked (the element is found by
repository and package, never by position, so an element it did not ask for is not recorded). `capPackage` applies Q-BAS-246 to both. A
registry token's answer ends at the earlier of the expiry the main installation reported and the `exp` of its claims, so a report that names
a later expiry or none cannot extend it. A name `iface.ValidPackage` refuses is never recorded nor asked. `cache.Entry.Package` is written by
`entryPackage` (the marking's package when the marking is of the request's repository, none otherwise) in `storeDocument`, `spoolEntry` and
both `304` paths (`onArtifact`, `onShared`), so every renewal replaces it and a marking without a package clears it. `storedCheck` rebuilds
the package answer with its own time (`checkResult.packageAt`), so recording it again does not extend it. **Renewal:** no background
refresh asks a package; the next read after a package answer ended sends one request, the conditional request while the caller's shape
answer is still usable and otherwise the check of R-BAS-085 step 4, since both answers are obtained together and end together; either
renews it ([Q-BAS-270](#q-bas-270--a-package-answer-that-ended-with-its-shape-answer-is-renewed-by-the-check)). The tests:
`TestR_BAS_084_PackageAnswers` in `internal/bastion/engine` (the criterion's five cases, an answer from before a `grants` entry also for an
entry another caller revalidated since, the expiry with and without a reported one, a grant of another image, another repository, push
only) and in `internal/bastion/answers` (each feed kind against a package answer, the expiry in the grace period), and
`TestR_BAS_084_TheEntryCarriesThePackageOfItsLastMarking` (a `304` naming another package and one naming none).

### R-BAS-085 · Serving per package
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

**The read flow** for a request whose cache key has an entry E with package P, repository R and credential C
([Q-BAS-245](#q-bas-245--when-the-bastion-asks)):

1. C's shape on R is `none`: refused without a request (unchanged).
2. **Allowed** means: C's shape on R is `full`, or P is set and C's package answer on (R, P) is `full`, or C's URL answer allows this key.
3. Allowed, not withdrawn, and fresh (or the main installation unreachable): served from the cache.
4. C has **no usable shape answer on R**: one check with `repositories: [R]` and, when P is set, `packages: [{R, P}]`, collapsed per
   (credential, repository, package); then steps 2 and 3, otherwise the conditional request.
5. C has a **usable shape answer on R that is not `full`**, P is set, and C has no package answer on (R, P): the conditional request, not a
   check; its marking supplies the package answer. This step costs no extra round trip, so a narrowed caller cannot tell a cached package
   from an uncached one by timing.
6. Otherwise: the conditional request (unchanged).

- **Followers of a running fill** (R-BAS-054, Q-BAS-200): a usable `full` answer also means a package answer `full` on the fill's package,
  which the leader's marking supplies. Negative entries and private documents are unchanged.
- **What a `full` answer on image I of repository R covers:** the tag documents of I (`Metadata`, `shared`), its manifests by digest with an
  index's child manifests (`Download`), its blobs, its tags list, and its cosign tags `sha256-<hex>.sig` and `.att`: every entry whose last
  marking named I.
- **Blobs shared between images.** A blob request always names an image (`/v2/<p>/<r>/<name>/blobs/<digest>`), and the main installation
  answers it only when an item of that name holds the blob (R-OCI-010). The Bastion stores the bytes once per content address but keeps
  entries per cache key, each written only after a marked `200` or `304` for that key and carrying the package of that marking; no path serves
  bytes by digest alone, and the referrers list (`Volatile`) and the catalog are passed on and never kept. The evidence for a blob is the
  path, which names I, and the main installation's answer for that path. A token granted `library/nginx` asking for
  `/v2/web/docker/library/redis/blobs/sha256:X`, the same bytes as an nginx layer, meets another cache key whose entry is marked
  `library/redis`; its package answer on redis is `partial` (the main installation's limit and the Bastion's comparison with the grant); the
  Bastion sends a conditional request or, without an entry, a forward, and replays the main installation's `401 insufficient_scope`, which
  is not kept. Such a request costs what an uncached path costs today: one request.
- **Every gate at the main installation's download** ([Q-BAS-249](#q-bas-249--the-feed-is-unchanged)):

| Gate | On a forward or conditional request | When a `full` package answer serves from the cache | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credential valid (expiry, revocation, owner disabled; for a registry token the token behind it) | the authentication stage | a package answer carries the token ID (of the Quader token behind a registry token), the principal ID and the expiry; a `token` or `principal` entry drops it, rule 2 ends it at the expiry | 3 s (R-BAS-026); the expiry exactly; during an outage `period + grace`, never past the expiry (H-383) |
| The decision point: grants, roles, levels, token scope, CI, exposure, populate right | the coarse check and `Authorize` | the answer is computed on the same index; a `grants` entry follows a policy, role, member, lowered visibility, settings, exposure, a repository moved, disabled or deleted, or a claim change; a `principal` entry a group change or the external flag; either drops it | 3 s |
| The registry grant | the enforcement point | `full` only within the grant, limited at the main installation and compared at the Bastion; the grant does not change during the token's life | the token's life |
| Repository patterns, members, pin rules (R-REPO-005, R-REPO-061); global claims (R-REPO-025) | `Authorize` | `repository.narrowed` or `claims_changed` yields a `content` (or `grants`) entry; the entry is no longer fresh, so the next read is a conditional request the gates judge | 3 s |
| The format's serve-time checks (unpublish, a deleted manifest, Debian's withholding, Ansible Galaxy's deletion) | the serve | `content` entries (Q-BAS-175) | 3 s; withdrawals the feed does not carry: `artifact_revalidate_after` (H-385) |
| The malware gate (R-MAL-018) | the serve | a find or a withdrawn release yields `content`; the switch turned on is not in the feed (H-1102) | 3 s, or 10 min |
| The vulnerability block (R-VULN-033 to R-VULN-037) | the serve | a block set in triage yields `content`; an automatic block is not in the feed (H-385) | 3 s, or 10 min |
| The signature gate (R-SIG-063, R-SIG-064) | the serve (manifests) | withdrawn releases and narrowed trust yield `content`; a pending `503` is never kept | 3 s |
| Download limits (byte budgets, parallel transfers, a block) and request figures | `Admit` (never on a `304`); stage 7 | not applied to hits, as for full readers today (R-LIM-001); because package answers renew by use, the renewing conditional request of a blocked or limited subject is refused within one period | at most `answers.period` ([H-1381](#h-1381--the-main-installations-limits-and-blocks-do-not-reach-hits-from-per-package-answers)) |
| Download recording | `Served` | the Bastion's download events (R-BAS-039, R-BAS-059) | buffered |

A `full` package answer obeys exactly the validity rules of a `full` answer on the repository, and the entry the same freshness and
withdrawal rules (`fresh`, `withdrawn`, Q-BAS-122). What changes is who gets those bounds: registry tokens and narrowed readers, who until
now asked the main installation per artifact and met every gate at every pull
([H-1380](#h-1380--changes-the-feed-does-not-carry-reach-registry-token-and-package-narrowed-readers-within-the-revalidation-periods-no-longer-at-their-next-read)).

- **Downloads, limits and the audit trail** ([Q-BAS-253](#q-bas-253--limits-and-download-events-stay-unchanged)): download records keep
  their shape and number. A serve after a `304` is reported today (R-BAS-039) and a hit after the change is reported the same way, with the
  token ID (of the Quader token behind a registry token), the principal, the client address, the repository, the request path and the
  SHA-256; download events carry no package. The main installation no longer sees its request-log lines of the 11 to 12 conditional
  requests per pull nor charges them to the subject's request figures (`requestsPerSecond`, `requestsPerHour` are charged 3 requests instead
  of 14 per warm pull); the token request is still logged and charged; `cachedBytesPerHour`, `bytesPerDay` and `parallelTransfers` are
  unchanged, since a `304` carries no body and is answered before `Admit`, and hits are counted nowhere (R-LIM-001).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, over the engine's double `fakeMain`): an entry of P is served without a request to a credential holding a
  `full` answer on P, and not so to one holding `full` on Q; `TestR_BAS_085_AWarmPullWithANewRegistryTokenCostsOneCheck`: a tag document and
  11 blobs cost exactly 1 check and 0 conditional requests; `TestR_BAS_085_NoRoundTripTellsACachedPackageFromAnUncachedOne`: with a known
  `partial` shape on the repository, a cached and an uncached path of an unreadable package each cost exactly one request and no check is
  sent; after a `content` entry the next read of a caller `full` on the package is a conditional request; a follower of a running fill with
  `full` on the fill's package follows it without a request.
- Integration (area `bastion`): in `TestR_BAS_051_R_BAS_053_ADockerAndAContainerdPullThroughABastion` the second pull with a new registry
  token sends one request below `/v2/` (a check) besides the token step and no conditional request; a second replayed `npm ci` through
  `web/npm-local` within the period sends nothing; R-BAS-022's criterion for `$PART` through `npm-all` stays as a regression test.
- End-to-end (set `oci`): the warm assertion of `TestOCI_R_BAS_051_ThroughABastion` is tightened to at most one request below `/v2/` besides
  the token step. *Changed on 2026-11-23 by [Q-BAS-271](#q-bas-271--the-end-to-end-warm-assertion-counts-what-a-warm-pull-asks-about-artifacts):*
  a warm pull asks the main installation nothing about an artifact (a manifest by digest or a blob), and the cold pull starts once the
  Bastion received the set-up's feed entries more than the skew margin before; what the real clients send about the tag, the version check, the referrers and an anonymous
  challenge is the measurement's, not the assertion's.

*As built on 2026-11-23 (package P4):* `fromEntry` in [readflow.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/readflow.go) is steps 2 to 6: `allowed`
adds `packageAnswer` (the caller's usable answer on the entry's package, asked only for an entry of the request's repository and only while
the shape is not `full`); step 4 is `checkShape` with the entry's repository and package, which sends the pair (`checkPackages`) and
collapses per credential, repository and package (`check|<credential key>|<repository>|<package>`); a known shape that is not `full` never

`TestR_BAS_085_AWarmPullWithANewRegistryTokenCostsOneCheck` (a tag document and 11 blobs: exactly one check, which names the image, no

`TestR_BAS_085_AContentEntryMakesTheNextReadOfAPackageReaderAConditionalRequest`,

### R-BAS-086 · What a format owes: kit check 21
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Kit check 21** ([Q-BAS-250](#q-bas-250--the-format-contract)) runs over every `GET` and `HEAD` content case below `400` of a `Download`,
  `Metadata` or `Computed` route: it seeds `Fixture.OtherPackage` (a package other than the case's own, required for a format with package
  names; generic skips the check with its reason), serves the case as a reader of the repository, and derives P from the decisions the kit's
  host recorded. When P is set it serves the case again as a reader of only P. Status, body, `ETag`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Encoding`,
  `Vary` and `Cache-Control` must be equal, and no decision may be recorded after the status line.
- The kit's host records `MayRead`, `PathsAllowed` and `WikiReadable` besides `Authorize`, and the status line; the duties are the row of
  R-BAS-058's table and [developer/formats.md](../developer/formats.md#what-a-bastion-needs-of-a-format).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/formats/formattest/testformat`): the defects `ListsAnotherPackage` and `DecidesAfterItsStatusLine` each fail check 21 and no
  other check (`TestR_BAS_086_KitCheck21`); every format's `TestR_ARCH_010_Conformance` runs it, with `Fixture.OtherPackage` for npm, NuGet,
  OCI, Debian, Ansible Galaxy and the ClamAV definitions.

*As built on 2026-11-22* ([checks_package.go](../../internal/formats/formattest/checks_package.go), [Q-BAS-261](#q-bas-261--kit-check-21s-reader-of-one-package-has-no-path-pattern)):
`formattest.CheckPackageShape`. The kit's host records every decision of a request in order (`Host.Decisions()`: `Authorize` allowed or
refused, `WikiReadable`, each path of `PathsAllowed` in the package `Classify` gives it, each `MayRead` row of its read scope) and whether the
status line was out (`ServeRequest` hands the route a writer that tells it). The package is derived by R-BAS-081's rule. The reader of only P
is the host's `Allow` refusing every other package and every path in no package, with the read scope's `VersionsByPath` false
(`HostOptions.NoPathPatterns`), and is served on the same seeded host with its renditions forgotten. `Fixture.OtherPackage` is a `Name` and a
`Seed`; the check holds the seed to a package row of the name, refuses a case whose status changes with it stored or whose answer belongs to
it, and fails a format with package names that compares no case. A format with routes or package names cannot skip it; generic skips it with its reason. npm, NuGet, OCI, Debian,
Ansible Galaxy and the ClamAV definitions passed it as they were: no handler decided after its status line and none drew on another package
without a package-less decision, so no format was repaired. It runs over the local class only ([H-1390](#h-1390--kit-check-21-runs-over-the-local-class-only)).

### R-BAS-087 · The interface version
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- The two headers of R-BAS-082, their values and the check's members of R-BAS-083 raise `iface.InterfaceVersion` to the next version, 5,
  with the reading of the token's grant (`iface.RegistryTokenGrant`, beside `RegistryTokenAnonymous`) and, if its builder keeps it, of the
  token's expiry ([Q-BAS-252](#q-bas-252--option-b-of-q-bas-202-is-bundled)). The interface file and the four OpenAPI operations carry it.
  The handover (R-BAS-073), built since, takes the version after it, 6
  ([Q-BAS-251](#q-bas-251--the-version-numbering-against-the-handover)).
- **At a mismatch** nothing changes and nothing is owed (R-BAS-009, R-BAS-027, R-BAS-028): the main installation answers `400
  bastion_interface_mismatch`, a Bastion replica treats it as unreachable and raises `QuaderBastionInterfaceMismatch`; callers with live
  answers (credential, shape, package, URL) get warm content for up to `period + grace`, never past a token's expiry or a withdrawal the feed
  carried; every image pull fails with `503 unavailable` for the window, because the token request is a forward and a new registry token
  is a stranger, while npm and NuGet callers whose tokens were seen in the last period keep installing warm content. A rolling update of the
  main installation's replicas makes a Bastion replica switch to unreachable and back, as today. A Bastion rolled back to version 4 that
  shares a bucket with version 5 replicas ignores the member `package` of entries.
- **Order:** the main installation first, the Bastion releases at once after it; the window lasts as long as the Bastion's rollout.
- **Where this meets the handover** (R-BAS-070 to R-BAS-079): its answer's marking carries the two package headers (R-BAS-073), the entry kept
  from it records `Package` (R-BAS-074), a follower of a direct read may follow on a `full` package answer (R-BAS-054), a withdrawal during a
  direct read stops later package answers through the same feed entries (R-BAS-077), and warm reads send fewer conditional requests, so the
  main installation is offered fewer handovers (a `304` never carried one).

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_009_TheInterfaceChangesOnlyWithItsVersion` sees the two headers, their values and the check's members under version 5; the
  OpenAPI document says `x-quader-bastion-interface: 5` on the four operations; `iface.RegistryTokenGrant` reads the grant of a token from the
  real `registrytoken` encoder; a token whose claims do not decode yields no grant, so its package answers are recorded `partial`.

*As built on 2026-11-22 (package P1):* `iface.InterfaceVersion` is 5; [interface.txt](../../internal/bastion/iface/testdata/interface.txt)
records the headers, the check's members, `ValidPackage`, `MaxPackageBytes` and the two readers, and the four operations say
`x-quader-bastion-interface: 5`. `iface.RegistryTokenGrant` returns the entries of the claim `g` as `iface.RegistryGrant`, whose `Pulls`
compares repository and image byte for byte with the pull bit `iface.RegistryGrantPull` (1); it also yields no grant for claims that
name a system subject (the member `s` of a scan or blob token, which reaches one manifest or blob, never a whole image), which can only
lower what is read. The expiry reader of Q-BAS-252 is kept: `iface.RegistryTokenExpiry` reads the member `exp`. Each reader decodes only
the members it reads, so `RegistryTokenAnonymous` answers as before. Both are tested against tokens from the real encoder, entry by entry
against what the verifier decodes (`TestR_BAS_087_TheGrantIsReadAsTheTokenServiceWritesIt`,
`TestR_BAS_087_TheExpiryIsReadAsTheTokenServiceWritesIt`); `maintest` speaks version 5, marks packages through `Main.Mark` and holds the
check's pairs to the main installation's rules; the Bastion's client reads a package from a marking and sends a check's pairs
(`TestR_BAS_087_TheClientAndTheFakeSpeakTheVersionWithPackages` in `internal/bastion/mainclient`). Nothing reads the grant or the expiry
yet: the Bastion's recording of package answers and its use of the expiry are P4's. Nothing on `main` used version 5 before.

Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

By the owner's rule "Tests stay runnable" of 2026-11-20: each behaviour once, at the cheapest tier
([Q-BAS-254](#q-bas-254--the-tests)). Times marked [J] are the planner's estimates; the builder records the measured ones on
[developer/bastion-package-shapes.md](../developer/bastion-package-shapes.md).

| Tier | Test | Data | Run time |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit, `internal/bastion/iface` | the markings and their refusals, the check's bodies, the grant reader with the real encoder, the interface file (R-BAS-082, R-BAS-083, R-BAS-087) | none | under 0.1 s [J] |
| unit, `internal/authz` | the agreement test over the reach fixture and the named shapes (R-BAS-080) | none; about 50,000 decisions in memory | about 0.2 s [J] |
| kit, every format | check 21 (R-BAS-086) | the fixture's content cases and one second package | about 40 ms per format [J]; the defects about 0.1 s, joining the table that builds the fixture once |
| unit, `internal/api/bastionmark`, `internal/bastionmain`, `internal/formathost`, `internal/api/v1` | the notes, the marking, the grant limit, the image equal to the enforcement point's, the check per package (R-BAS-081 to R-BAS-083) | hundreds of bytes | about 0.4 s [J] |
| unit, `internal/bastion/engine`, `internal/bastion/answers` | R-BAS-084, R-BAS-085 over `fakeMain` | bytes | about 0.6 s [J]; measured 0.16 s for the eight engine tests, 0.00 s for the answers test (race detector, atomic coverage) |
| integration, area `bastion` | the changed assertions of the OCI and npm replays (R-BAS-085) | existing (two blobs of 1 KiB) | about −0.1 s (fewer requests) [J]; the area ran 159.9 s, within the noise of before |

The owner's words this section rests on. His task of about 10:40: "Die Download-Limits müssen sich durch den Administrator detailiert
konfigurieren lassen. Ich denke es ist auch Sinnvoll, eine angepasste Konfiguration pro Bastion zuzulassen. Intern könnten die Limits
deaktiviert sein und auf dem Bastion könnten sie deutlich eingeschränkt sein um Missbrauch der Registry über das offene Internet zu
vermeiden oder zumindest abzuschwächen. Auch finde ich gut, wenn man zusätzlich den maximalen Throughput zwischen Hauptinstanz und Bastion
konfigurieren könnte, so könnte man vermeisten, dass ein Anfreifer von außen den Bastion mit vielen unterschiedlichen Artefakten so
auslastet, dass der Cache überläuft und quasi jede Anfrage über die Hauptinstanz läuft und ggf. das Transfernetz sättigt." His framing of
10:55: "Der kerngedanke, des Bastions ist ja, dass er dem Internet ausgesetzt wird und dafür ggf. auf einer Edge-Node läuft. Traffic und
Angriffe auf dem Bastion, muss nur er aushalten und wir etablieren maßnahmen unsere interne Hauptinstanz über den Bastion vor überflutig
zu schützen. Der Bastion bietet nach außen nur eine lesende API an. Es ist so gebaut, dass es keine Schreib-API gibt die angegriffen
werden kann. … Nutzer können sich außschließlich über ein Token, PAT oder Zertifikat gegenüber dem Bastion identifizieren, OIDC oder
username/password ist ausgeschlossen und es exsistiert nicht mal eine API dafür. Je kleiner der Footprint, desto besser!" And his rule
of 11:51, written as a note to the refusal of a write and read as a rule for every answer: "Der Bastion verrät keine internen
Informationen über die Hauptinstanz. Es ist davon auszugehen, das es einen Grund gibt wieso ein User auf dem Bastion landet und nicht
direkt auf der Hauptinstanz."

### R-BAS-093 · A Bastion's configuration comes from its registration
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-024

The owner's choice (a) of [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation): a Bastion is configured
on its card at the main installation. It replaces "configuration only through the chart" (R-BAS-002, Q-BAS-15) for what an administrator
of the main installation decides; the chart keeps what the installation of the pods sizes.

- **What the registration holds**, beside its name, description, its disable (R-BAS-133, a member of the configuration the handshake
  sends) and tokens (R-BAS-004):

| Member | What it sets | Default of a new registration | Changed with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `switches.handover` | the handover per blob (R-BAS-071, moved here from the registration's top level) | off | `endpoints:write` |
| `switches.gui`, `switches.docs` | the web interface and its documentation (W-35's packages define what they switch) | off | `endpoints:write` |
| `limits.mode` | Audit or Enforce at this Bastion ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-044) | `enforce` | `limits:write` |
| `limits.preset` | `internet`, `partnerNetwork` or `internal` (R-LIM-046); `custom` once a kind rule or a flood figure differs from the preset's | `internet` | `limits:write` |
| the rules of the Bastion place | through `/api/v1/bastions/{name}/limits/assignments` ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-043) | the preset's kind rules | `limits:write` |
| `limits.flood` | per address: the request and miss figures of the classes `anonymous`, `authenticated` and `gui`, the failed-authentication timeout, the blocks, the exempt networks (R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037) | the preset's | `limits:write` |
| `limits.slots` | `maxConcurrent`, `anonymousShare`, `queueTimeout` (R-BAS-025) | 64, 0.25, 5 s (R-BAS-096) | `limits:write` |
| `limits.throughput` | R-BAS-097 | 200 MB/s, an anonymous share of 25 %, no hourly volume (Q-BAS-455) | `limits:write` |
| `limits.anonymousCeiling` | R-BAS-094 | 100 a second, burst 2,000, 36,000 an hour (R-BAS-094, from E4's measurement) | `limits:write` |
| `egress` | the addresses the Bastion connects from (R-BAS-017, R-UI-243) | empty | `endpoints:write` |

- **What stays in the chart**: the cache (backend, sizes, periods), the answers' periods, the timeouts, the replicas, TLS, Valkey, the
  edge limit `edgeLimit.*` with the new `edgeLimit.exemptCIDRs` (the addresses HAProxy Ingress does not limit, `limit-whitelist`), and
  what W-35 adds to it (the imprint and the privacy notice). `config.bastion.limits`, `config.bastion.failed_auth`, `config.bastion.blocking`
  and `config.bastion.main.max_concurrent`, `anonymous_share` and `queue_timeout` leave the chart and the role's schema; a file that still
  sets one stops startup with an error naming the key (R-BAS-001's rule). The chart's cross-check of `edgeLimit.requestsPerSecond`
  against the authenticated figure (`_validate.tpl`) goes: the figure is no chart value any more.
- **Delivery.** The handshake answer carries one member `configuration` (its wire below): `revision`, `switches` and `limits`. `revision`
  is the registration's revision (`principal.revision`, its `ETag`), which every change of a member above raises, and a change of a rule
  of the Bastion place or of a profile such a rule names raises as well
  ([Q-BAS-320](#q-bas-320--the-configuration-travels-as-one-member-with-each-rules-effective-figures-and-its-revision-is-the-registrations)).
  A change writes the transactional audit event `bastion.configuration.changed` (`details`: the registration, the parts changed, before
  and after), which the feed maps to a `settings` entry (R-BAS-015), so every replica handshakes again within one poll and one round trip
  (about 3 s with the defaults); without the feed the next regular handshake (`bastion.main.handshake_interval`) brings it. *Since the
  interface version 10 (R-BAS-128):* the member also carries `display`, the installation's default form of a time, which is no member of
  the registration and changes without its revision; its change (`system.time_format_changed`) is a `settings` entry too, and a replica
  applies a configuration that differs in any member.
- **Applying.** A replica swaps the whole configuration at once, never a part of it: the guard's figures, the slots, the throughput, the
  ceiling, the switches and the place's table change together. A configuration the Bastion's rules refuse fails the handshake, as a format
  table does (Q-BAS-199). The replica exports `quader_bastion_configuration_revision` (the revision it applies) and
  `quader_bastion_configuration_source{source="main|stored|builtin"}`.
- **While the main installation cannot be reached**
  ([Q-BAS-327](#q-bas-327--a-replica-without-its-configuration-serves-with-the-stored-one-else-with-a-built-in-one-that-fails-closed)):
  a running replica keeps applying its last configuration. Each replica that applied a configuration writes it as one object of its cache
  backend, `configuration/current.json`, signed with `bastion.signing_key_file` where the backend's entries are signed (R-BAS-032) and in
  R-BAS-061's stored format with a cache key; a replica that starts while the main installation is unreachable applies that object when
  its signature holds, and otherwise a built-in configuration that fails closed: every switch off, the Internet preset's flood figures,
  slots and ceiling, Enforce, the throughput of Q-BAS-455. It leaves the built-in or the stored configuration at its first handshake.
  The object holds the handshake's format table (R-BAS-057) beside the configuration, written again when either changes; a replica that
  applies the stored configuration holds that table until its first handshake, so its own answers take each format's error shape and a
  declared read route with a body is forwarded (R-BAS-095); a table the Bastion's rules refuse refuses the whole object. *Built on
  2026-11-26 (the day's findings, batch B):* `settings.Holder.Apply` takes the table, `LoadStored` returns it, `link.Link.UseStoredFormats`
  holds it, closing H-2359 of [security/bastion.md](../security/bastion.md#h-2359--before-its-first-handshake-a-bastion-answers-in-problem-details);
  tests `TestR_BAS_093_AReplicaStartedWithoutTheMainInstallationAppliesTheStoredConfiguration` (settings),
  `TestR_BAS_095_BeforeItsFirstHandshakeABastionAnswersInTheStoredShapes` (engine) and
  `TestR_BAS_093_ARestartDuringAnOutageAppliesTheStoredConfiguration` (server, two starts, npm's shape before the handshake).
- **The edge figure.** The Bastion reports its edge figure, which the chart renders into its configuration file as the chart-managed
  `bastion.edge_limit` (`requests_per_second`, `connections`, or off), with every handshake in the header `Quader-Bastion-Edge-Limit`, and
  the main installation records it with the contact (R-BAS-010). The card warns where a per-address request figure of the configuration lies
  above it (R-UI-240): the ingress would refuse what the Bastion admits.
- **Permissions** ([Q-BAS-325](#q-bas-325--the-limit-members-of-a-registration-need-limitswrite-the-others-endpointswrite)):
  `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/{name}` takes `limits` with `limits:write` and the other members with `endpoints:write`; `GET` shows `limits` to
  a holder of `endpoints:read` or `limits:read`. `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` admits either: `endpoints:read` reads every member,
  `limits:read` alone reads `id`, `name`, `limits` and `status` (the state the replicas reported, its blocks among it) and no other
  member, so the limits page and its tab **Blocks** (R-UI-241) work for a holder of `limits:read` without the tokens, contacts, networks,
  switches and description; a caller with neither gets `403`. The list `GET /api/v1/bastions` stays `endpoints:read`'s. `GET
  /api/v1/bastions/presets` (`limits:read`) lists the three presets of R-LIM-046 as `bastionmain.Presets` holds and the patch applies
  them, which the preset's dialog reads ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) Q-UI-1485); `presets` is therefore no registration name. *Built on
  2026-11-26 (the day's findings, batch B):* `GetBastion`, `toBastionLimits` and `ListBastionPresets` of
  [bastion_registrations_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_registrations_api.go), the reserved name in `bastionmain.ValidName`; tests
  `TestR_BAS_093_TheReadOfARegistrationNeedsEndpointsReadOrLimitsRead`, `TestR_BAS_093_ThePresetsAreReadWithLimitsRead` (unit, no
  database) and `TestR_BAS_004_CapabilitiesGateTheOperations` (area `bastionreg`, a token cut down to `limits:read`).
