### R-BAS-094 · What an anonymous request may cause at the main installation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's choice (c) of [Q-BAS-326](#q-bas-326--an-anonymous-ceiling-per-bastion-and-the-one-for-one-paths-removed): a ceiling for all
anonymous callers of a Bastion together, and the paths on which an anonymous request reached the main installation one for one removed.

- **The anonymous ceiling.** Per registration, `limits.anonymousCeiling`: requests to the main installation per second with a burst, and
  per hour, for all anonymous callers of that Bastion together. It counts every request a replica sends to the main installation on behalf
  of an anonymous caller: forwards, conditional requests, checks, and the background refresh of an anonymous answer or document (R-BAS-020,
  which today no guard counts). Above it the Bastion answers `503 busy` with `Retry-After` (capped by the format, R-BAS-091) in the format's
  error shape (R-BAS-095); hits are served; a refused request consumes nothing (Q-BAS-127's rule). It is one limiter key, in memory or,
  with Valkey, in Valkey (each replica holds its share without Valkey, R-ARCH-034).
- **Anonymous registry tokens come from the Bastion**
  ([Q-BAS-335](#q-bas-335--the-bastion-answers-an-anonymous-token-request-itself)). A `GET` or `POST /v2/_token` without a credential is
  answered by the Bastion while `anonymousReads` is true (R-BAS-019 otherwise): `200` with the body of the token service of R-OCI-005
  (`token`, `access_token`, `expires_in` 300, `issued_at`), the token in the registry token's form with the payload
  `1:bastion:{"a":true,"exp":<issued + 300 s>}` (version 1, which every reader of the interface reads, so the package needs no raise; no
  grant and no other claim), and a MAC of 32 random bytes that nobody verifies. Wherever such a token is presented, the Bastion drops it
  (Q-BAS-168), so the main installation is neither asked for it nor ever sees it.
- **Anonymous documents are kept like shared ones.** A document the main installation marks `private` for the anonymous subject is the
  same for every anonymous caller (the anonymous subject is one principal, R-BAS-019): it is kept once per replica, in memory, under the
  anonymous key and the cache key, and reused for `bastion.cache.metadata_revalidate_after` without a conditional request, under the
  feed's `content` entries like a shared document (R-BAS-023). It is never written to the cache backend.
- **Writes** are refused by the Bastion itself (R-BAS-095); no probe reaches the main installation.
- **The anonymous `/v2/_catalog`** is answered from W-35's public catalogue once that exists; until then it is forwarded under the ceiling.
- **Anonymous protocol searches** (npm, NuGet, Ansible Galaxy) stay forwarded per request and `pass`, under the ceiling: rendering them
  needs format knowledge, which the Bastion does not hold (R-BAS-001).

Every way a request at the Bastion reaches the main installation, after the packages of this section:

| # | Path | Today | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The forward of a `GET` or `HEAD` miss | the per-address miss figures of R-BAS-035 and the slots of R-BAS-025 | plus the subject's upstream budget at the Bastion (R-BAS-096), the anonymous ceiling and the throughput (R-BAS-097) |
| 2 | A `404` the main installation did not mark `absent` | one for one | under the ceiling |
| 3 | `pass` routes: search, npm's `-/whoami`, `/v2/_catalog`, `/v2/_token` | one for one | the anonymous token answered at the Bastion; the anonymous catalogue from W-35's catalogue; the rest under the ceiling |
| 4 | The check of a credential | once per answer period; anonymous answers are shared | unchanged |
| 5 | The background refresh of an answer | counted by no guard | counted against the ceiling |
| 6 | A conditional request for a private document | one per use | an anonymous document kept for the metadata period |
| 7 | The probe of a write | once per distinct method and path | none (R-BAS-095) |
| 8 | A read route that takes a body | a probe, then the forward | the forward only |
| 9 to 12 | The download batches, the handshake, the feed, the handover | as today | the batches carry usage and status as well (R-BAS-016) |

The planner derived for today (not measured): rows 1 to 8 are bounded by the 16 anonymous slots of a Bastion of two replicas alone, which
at 10 ms an answer is about 1,600 requests a second at the main installation from callers spread over many addresses.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (package E14a), rows 3 and 6 for the anonymous caller:* the anonymous token (`answerAnonymousToken` in
[registry.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/registry.go), Q-BAS-435, Q-BAS-436) and the anonymous documents (`fromAnonymousCopy` in
[readflow.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/readflow.go), Q-BAS-437), with no change of the interface. The Bastion's own token answers count as
`quader_bastion_requests_total{class="pass",result="hit"}` and a kept anonymous document as `{class="private",result="hit"}`; neither is in
`quader_bastion_main_requests_total`. What an anonymous request still causes at the main installation, path by path, as built after E14a
(measured: rows 1, 3 and 6 in the integration case below; derived from the code: the rest):

| # | Path | Per anonymous request after E14a |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The forward of a miss | one per miss; a cold anonymous pull of an image of two blobs sent four forwards and nothing else (measured) |
| 2 | A `404` not marked `absent` | one per request |
| 3 | `pass` routes | the token service none (measured); search, npm's `-/whoami` and `/v2/_catalog` one per request |
| 4 | The check | none per request: one per repository and answer period for all anonymous callers together |
| 5 | The background refresh | none per request; one per kept answer and period, counted by no guard |
| 6 | The conditional request of a private document | none per request: one per document, replica and metadata period (measured: ten reads, one request) |
| 7 | The probe of a write | one per distinct method and path and metadata period, until E15 |
| 8 | A read route with a body | a probe and a forward per request, until E15 (the anonymous `POST /v2/_token` none) |
| 9 to 12 | The batches, the handshake, the feed, the handover | none per request |

*Built on 2026-11-26 by E9a, the ceiling:* [guard.Ceiling](../../internal/bastion/guard/ceiling.go), taken in the slot budget
(`mainclient.SlotBudget`) by every request of the anonymous class once it has its slot, so it counts forwards, conditional requests, checks,
probes and the background refresh of an anonymous answer alike, and a request the slots refuse takes nothing from it
([Q-BAS-445](#q-bas-445--the-anonymous-ceiling-is-taken-in-the-slot-budget-after-the-slot)). The hour is read before the second's bucket
and counted only once the bucket admitted the request, so a refused request takes nothing; requests in flight together may pass the hour
by their number (H-2356). A refusal answers `503 busy` with the ceiling's wait as `Retry-After` (the bucket's, or a minute for the hour),
which the format caps (R-BAS-091), in the family's shape of today (E15 brings the five shapes), and counts
`quader_bastion_refused_total{reason="anonymous_ceiling"}`; a refused background refresh counts
`quader_bastion_main_requests_total{kind="check",outcome="busy"}`. Two limiters, `bastion.ceiling_requests` and `bastion.ceiling_hour`, under
one key for all anonymous callers; with Valkey shared by the replicas, without it each replica holds the figures divided by
`bastion.replicas` (Q-BAS-34): two replicas allow the figure together while the load is spread over both, one replica that takes the
whole load half of it, and with autoscaling (`bastion.replicas` is `autoscaling.maxReplicas`) a Bastion that runs fewer replicas than its
maximum allows that share of it (H-2356). *Not built* (W-35's catalogue, `/v2/_catalog`). Since E8 every registration's configuration
holds the ceiling, a new one the default below.

**The default** ([Q-BAS-448](#q-bas-448--the-defaults-of-the-anonymous-ceiling-and-of-the-slots)), for all anonymous callers of one
Bastion together: **100 requests a second with a burst of 2,000, and 36,000 an hour** (the measurement's proposal, developer/bastion.md
"The proposal for the figures"). It counts requests to the main installation, not requests at the Bastion: a hit costs nothing. What
it lets through, from the measured cold anonymous commands of 2026-11-26 (requests to the main installation per command measured, the
commands per hour derived; a podman pull has one request less since the Bastion answers the anonymous token, E14a):

| Command, cold, anonymous | Requests to the main installation | Commands an hour within 36,000 | At once within the burst of 2,000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm ci` of 475 packages | 475 | 75 | 4 |
| `dotnet restore` of 200 packages | 401 | 89 | 4 |
| `docker pull`, small / 40 layers / 1 GiB | 4 / 43 / 11 | 9,000 / 837 / 3,272 | 500 / 46 / 181 |
| `podman pull`, small / 40 layers / 1 GiB | 3 / 42 / 10 | 12,000 / 857 / 3,600 | 666 / 47 / 200 |
| `apt-get update` and `install` (the measurement's suite; a real suite and 106 packages, R-LIM-042) | 8 (118 derived) | 4,500 (305) | 250 (16) |
| `ansible-galaxy collection install` of 4 collections (12, R-LIM-042) | 17 (49 derived) | 2,117 (734) | 117 (40) |
| `curl` of one file | 1 | 36,000 | 2,000 |
| a warm `docker pull` (the tag's `HEAD`, Q-BAS-271; until 2026-11-26) | 1 | 36,000 | 2,000 |
| a warm `docker pull` since Q-BAS-475 (within the metadata period; one conditional `GET` of the tag per period after it) | 0 | not bound by the ceiling | not bound |

- The hour binds a sustained load: 36,000 an hour is 10 a second on average, the second's figure of 100 only shapes a burst. The main
  installation answered the measurement's restore at about 115 requests a second through 16 slots on a loaded workstation (derived from
  the measured 401 requests in 3.5 s), so
  the default keeps all anonymous internet callers of one Bastion below what one restore takes there, and a flood of distinct artifacts
  from any number of addresses at 100 misses a second at most, 10 on average over the hour (the attack of the measurement reached 12 to
  18 a second with files of 4 MiB, bounded only by the slots).
- **Where the two sides pull apart** (derived): a public image pulled warm sent its tag's `HEAD` to the main installation every time, so
  one Bastion served at most 36,000 anonymous `docker pull`s an hour (864,000 a day) before it answered `503 busy`. *Since 2026-11-26
  (R-BAS-021, [Q-BAS-475](#q-bas-475--a-head-of-a-document-is-answered-from-what-the-bastion-keeps)):* the tag's `HEAD` is answered from
  the kept document, so a warm pull costs the main installation nothing within `metadata_revalidate_after` and one conditional `GET` of the
  tag per period after it where the entry is kept; the ceiling no longer bounds warm pulls.
  The cold installs of a busy public mirror whose content changes are still 75 `npm ci` an hour. A large public audience of one Bastion beyond that needs a higher
  ceiling on the card, set by the administrator; the default picks the shield of the main installation, as the owner's rule says, and this
  is its price.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/guard`, `internal/bastion/engine`, under 1 s): at a ceiling of 10 a second with a burst of 20, the 21st anonymous
  miss within the burst answers `503 busy` with `Retry-After` in the format's shape while a hit and a signed-in miss are served; a refused
  miss consumes nothing; a background refresh of an anonymous answer takes from the ceiling. *As built* (0.05 s together, payloads of
  64 bytes): `TestR_BAS_094_AnAnonymousMissAboveTheCeilingIsBusyWhileHitsAndSignedInMissesAreServed` and
  `TestR_BAS_094_TheBackgroundRefreshOfAnAnonymousAnswerTakesFromTheCeiling` (`internal/bastion/engine`),
  `TestR_BAS_094_TheCeilingHoldsAllAnonymousCallersTogether` and `TestR_BAS_094_WithoutValkeyEachReplicaHoldsItsShareOfTheCeiling`
  (`internal/bastion/guard`, an injected clock), `TestR_BAS_094_ARefusalOfTheCeilingGivesTheSlotBack` (`internal/bastion/mainclient`).
- Integration (area `bastion`, about 2 s): the ceiling refuses above its figure while hits and a signed-in miss are served
  (`TestR_BAS_094_TheCeilingRefusesAboveItsFigureWhileHitsAreServed`, three npm tarballs and a document); (area `bastionshared`, 0.1 s)
  two replicas share one ceiling through Valkey (`TestR_BAS_094_WithValkeyTheReplicasShareOneCeiling`).
- Integration (area `bastion`, one case, about 3 s): an anonymous `docker pull` replay through the in-process Bastion makes no token request
  at the counting double of the main installation, and an anonymous npm document read ten times within the period sends one request.
  *As built:* `TestR_BAS_021_R_BAS_094_AnAnonymousPullAndAnAnonymousDocumentSpareTheMainInstallation` (the npm document of a local repository whose
  artifacts are public and whose wiki is not, so that it is filtered for the anonymous caller, Q-BAS-149); the engine's unit tests
  `TestR_BAS_094_TheBastionAnswersAnAnonymousTokenRequestItself` and `TestR_BAS_094_AnAnonymousDocumentIsKeptForTheMetadataPeriod`.

### R-BAS-095 · Writes are refused by the Bastion itself
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's choice (b) of [Q-BAS-336](#q-bas-336--the-bastion-refuses-a-write-itself), as his note changed it: the Bastion refuses a write
itself and names nothing of the main installation in the refusal (R-BAS-099). It replaces the probe of R-BAS-014.

- **The refusal.** A request on a package family (`/api/<format>/…`, `/files/…`, `/v2/…`, a bound-host prefix) whose method is not `GET`
  or `HEAD` answers `403 read_only` with the detail "This address is read-only: it serves downloads and accepts no uploads.", before the
  Bastion reads a byte of its body and without a request to the main installation. It names no host, no base URL, no image prefix and no
  "publish to". A write on a path that no route serves answers `403` as well, not `404`.
- **Read routes that take a body** are the format's declaration: the handshake's format table lists them per format as `readWithBody`
  (method and path pattern, below the wire). Today they are npm's `POST …/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk` and the registry root's
  `POST /v2/_token`. A request that matches an entry is forwarded as today, with its body (at most `bastion.main.max_forwarded_body`, a
  larger body `413 payload_too_large`) and the caller's credential, and its answer is `pass`; an anonymous `POST /v2/_token` is answered by
  the Bastion (R-BAS-094).
- **The shape** ([Q-BAS-337](#q-bas-337--a-bastions-own-refusals-take-one-of-five-error-shapes-a-format-declares)). The format table
  gains `errorShape`, one of five the Bastion renders, and the Bastion uses it for every answer of its own on the format's family (this
  refusal, the limits of R-BAS-096, the table of R-BAS-029), so a client receives a body it parses:

| `errorShape` | Formats | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `problem` | Debian, generic (`/files/`), the ClamAV definitions; the default for a format the table does not name | problem details (RFC 9457) |
| `npm` | npm | `{"error": "<detail>", "code": "<code>"}`, `application/json` (npm prints `error`) |
| `text` | NuGet | one line `read_only: <detail>`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8` |
| `distribution` | the registry root | `{"errors": [{"code": "DENIED", "message": "<detail>", "detail": {"code": "read_only"}}]}` (R-BAS-029's mapping of the other codes) |
| `galaxy` | Ansible Galaxy | `{"errors": [{"status": "403", "code": "read_only", "title": "Forbidden.", "detail": "<detail>"}]}`, `application/json`, the list a Galaxy's API answers |

What each format's clients print, measured on 2026-11-26 against a stub that answered the shapes (developer/bastion.md, "What each client
prints for a refusal"), and why each format declares its shape:

| Format | Shape | What the client prints | Why this shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| npm | `npm` | the status and the detail (`npm error 403 403 Forbidden - PUT … - <detail>`); retries a `503` after 10 s and 60 s of its own | npm reads the member `error` |
| NuGet | `text` | the status and reason phrase only, never a body; retries five times about 1 s apart | the body changes nothing dotnet shows; the line serves curl and logs, and is what `WriteError` writes |
| OCI (docker, podman) | `distribution` | podman and docker print the message (`denied: <detail>`); a refusal of a `HEAD` reaches docker without a body | the registries' own shape (R-OCI-008) |
| Ansible Galaxy | `galaxy` | with problem details `Message: <status phrase> Code: Unknown`; with the `galaxy` list `ERROR! Error when getting available collection versions for e4.app … (HTTP Code: 503, Message: <detail> Code: <code>)`, exit 1 (E15's run, below). A `429` on a document it caches (the version list) made ansible-galaxy 2.17.14 exit 250 ("Unexpected Exception … 'results'") whatever the body: it retries 429, 502 and 520 and reads the empty entry its first attempt left in its response cache; so the format answers a rate limit `503` ([Q-BAS-451](#q-bas-451--ansible-galaxy-answers-a-rate-limit-503-because-ansible-galaxy-does-not-survive-the-retry-of-a-429)), and a gateway failure `503` too (a `502` measured the same way, below) | none of the other four is a list ansible-galaxy reads |
| Debian | `problem` | APT prints the reason phrase only; `apt-get update` exits 0 when refused | the body changes nothing APT shows; problem details serve curl |
| ClamAV definitions | `problem` | freshclam acts on the status alone | as Debian |
| generic (`/files/`) | `problem` | curl prints the body as it is | the core's shape of `/files/` |

- **The main installation's backstop** stays: a forwarded write that reaches it anyway (a defect) is refused `403 read_only` in the format's
  error shape with the same neutral detail. Its admission of probes as the anonymous caller for routing (Q-BAS-118) goes, and so do the
  headers `Quader-Bastion-Probe` and `Quader-Bastion-Route`.
- **Kit check 19** gains two duties for every format (R-BAS-058): each route with a writing method whose kind is a read is listed in
  `readWithBody`, and the format's `WriteError` renders the declared `errorShape`.
- **What is given up:** the format's own refusal body beyond the five shapes; the `404` of a write to a path without a route; a read route
  with a body that a format forgets to declare, which is refused and so fails closed (H-2293).

*Built on 2026-11-26 by E7:* the members `errorShape` (five shapes, [Q-BAS-337](#q-bas-337--a-bastions-own-refusals-take-one-of-five-error-shapes-a-format-declares))
and `readWithBody` of the format table, declared by every format ([Q-BAS-353](#q-bas-353--a-format-declares-its-read-routes-with-a-body-below-the-repository-and-kit-check-19-holds-the-list-to-its-routes)); the code `read_only`; the headers
`Quader-Bastion-Probe` and `Quader-Bastion-Route` gone, the Bastion forwarding a declared read route with a body at once and the main
installation recognizing a probe by its form ([Q-BAS-351](#q-bas-351--until-e15-a-probe-is-recognized-by-its-form-and-a-read-route-with-a-body-is-the-format-tables)); kit check 19's duty that `readWithBody` equals the format's routes of a
writing method whose kind is a read, and that a format declares its `errorShape`. *Built by E16:* the backstop's neutral text. *Built by
E15 on 2026-11-26:* `write` in [write.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/write.go) refuses a write before its body or its credential is
read ([Q-BAS-452](#q-bas-452--a-write-is-refused-before-its-credential-is-read)) and asks the main installation nothing; every answer of
the Bastion's own renders through `writeShaped` in [shape.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/shape.go) by the declared shape
([Q-BAS-450](#q-bas-450--every-answer-of-the-bastions-own-goes-through-one-renderer-by-the-declared-shape-and-each-shape-carries-the-code));
`errs.ReadShape` ([shape.go](../../internal/errs/shape.go)) is what a client of each shape reads, and kit check 19 holds every format's
`WriteError` to it on the backstop's refusal ([Q-BAS-453](#q-bas-453--kit-check-19-reads-the-backstops-refusal-with-the-shapes-reader-and-check-16-takes-503-as-a-rate-limit),
the defect `DeclaresAnotherErrorShape`); the probe (`probe.go`, `mainclient.Forward.Probe`, the kind `probe` of
`quader_bastion_main_requests_total`), `bastionmain.IsProbe`, `Recognition.Probe`, the probe's admission in `BastionRouteAuth` and the
class `probe` of `quader_bastion_forwarded_requests_total` are gone. Ansible Galaxy answers a rate limit `503` (Q-BAS-451).

What ansible-galaxy 2.17.14 prints for the `galaxy` shape, run once on 2026-11-26 in the journeys' client image
`quader-e2e-ansibleclients-core217` against a stub that serves the API root and the collection document and answers the version list
`GET …/v3/collections/e4/app/versions/?limit=100` with the body `writeShaped` renders (`TestR_BAS_095_EachShapeRenders` holds the bytes),
`Retry-After` 30 and `Cache-Control: no-store` (the command and the stub are in
[developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-galaxy-shape-against-ansible-galaxy-217-measured-2026-11-26)):

| Status, code | Requests | What ansible-galaxy printed | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `429 rate_limited` | 3 (the API root, the collection document, the version list once) | `ERROR! Unexpected Exception, this is probably a bug: 'results'` | 250, after 1 s |
| `503 rate_limited` | 3 | `ERROR! Error when getting available collection versions for e4.app from cmd_arg (…) (HTTP Code: 503, Message: Too many requests from this address. Try again in 14 minutes. Code: rate_limited)` | 1, after 1 s |
| `503 busy` | 3 | `… (HTTP Code: 503, Message: Too many requests are waiting; try again in a moment. Code: busy)` | 1 |
| `429 rate_limited` on the collection document too | 8 (the collection document seven times over 53 s) | `ERROR! Error when getting the collection info for e4.app … (HTTP Code: 429, Message: … Code: rate_limited)` | 1 |
| `502 bad_gateway`, no `Retry-After` (run on 2026-11-26 after E15) | 3 | `ERROR! Unexpected Exception, this is probably a bug: 'results'` | 250, after about 1 s |
| `503 bad_gateway`, no `Retry-After` (the same run) | 3 | `ERROR! Error when getting available collection versions for e4.app from cmd_arg (…) (HTTP Code: 503, Message: This service could not answer; try again later. Code: bad_gateway)` | 1, at once |

The shape is read in every row; the `250` is the client's response cache, not the body (Q-BAS-451). So the `galaxy` shape answers a
gateway failure, the Bastion's `502 bad_gateway` and `504 gateway_timeout`, `503` with its code and detail (`galaxyStatus` of
[shape.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/shape.go)), and Ansible's `WriteError` answers an upstream's failure at the main installation the
same ([formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-007); a `504` is not retried by ansible-galaxy (`RETRY_HTTP_ERROR_CODES` is 429, 502
and 520 in 2.17.14 and 2.21.6) and answers `503` all the same, so that one status stands for every gateway failure. This closed H-2358
of [security/bastion.md](../security/bastion.md#h-2358--a-502-on-a-document-ansible-galaxy-caches-ends-the-client-with-exit-250).
*As built:* `TestR_BAS_095_TheGalaxyShapeAnswersAGatewayFailure503` (the five shapes, `502` and `504`, the `503`'s bytes the client
was run against; under 0.01 s) and `TestR_ANS_007_ErrorsHaveTheGalaxyShapeOfTheirRoute`'s rows of an upstream's failure and timeout.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, under 1 s): `PUT`, `POST`, `DELETE` and `PATCH` on npm, NuGet, OCI and `/files/` paths answer `403
  read_only` in the five shapes, the counting double of the main installation records nothing, and less than 64 KiB of a 1 MiB body is
  read; npm's bulk audit and `POST /v2/_token` with a credential are forwarded. *As built:*
  `TestR_BAS_095_AWriteIsRefusedAtTheBastionInTheFormatsShape` (also Ansible Galaxy and Debian, with, without and with an unreadable
  credential, reachable and unreachable; none of the body read; 0.03 s), `TestR_BAS_095_EachShapeRenders` (five shapes, five answers,
  `GET` and `HEAD`, read back with `errs.ReadShape`; under 0.01 s), `TestR_BAS_095_ARouteThatTakesABodyIsForwardedWithTheCallersCredential`;
  `POST /v2/_token` in `TestR_BAS_051_TheRegistryRootIsAPathFamilyOfTheBastion`, its anonymous form in
  `TestR_BAS_094_TheBastionAnswersAnAnonymousTokenRequestItself`.
- Kit (every format, about 20 ms each): the two duties; a `testformat` defect each. *As built:* the shape duty takes well under a
  millisecond per format; its defect is `DeclaresAnotherErrorShape` in `TestR_BAS_058_KitCheck19`, the read routes' are E7's.
- Integration (area `bastion`): `write_test` asserts the Bastion's refusal and no request at the main installation; the probe's cases go, so
  the area's time falls. *As built:* `TestR_BAS_095_WritesAreRefusedAtTheBastion`, one Bastion instead of two (anonymous access no longer
  matters to a write) and no loop of 1,000 writes.

### R-BAS-096 · Limits at a Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: BEYOND-030

The owner's choices (c) of [Q-LIM-305](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-305--a-bastion-protects-per-address-and-budgets-per-subject-on-everything-it-serves),
(a) of [Q-LIM-300](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-300--a-preset-per-bastion-rules-on-demand-two-profiles-of-the-bastion),
(a) of [Q-LIM-306](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-306--two-budgets-one-at-the-bastion-one-at-the-main-installation) and
(a) of [Q-LIM-301](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-301--audit-or-enforce-per-bastion). The model is the main installation's
([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md)), counted at a place of its own (R-LIM-043).

- **Flood protection stays per address**, an IPv6 address counted per `/64` (R-LIM-002's rule): the request and miss figures, the
  failed-authentication timeout and the blocks of R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-037, with their figures from the configuration (R-BAS-093). A third
  request class, `gui`, holds the web interface's pages per address
  ([Q-LIM-307](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-307--pages-of-the-web-interface-are-a-request-class-of-their-own-per-address)).
- **Download budgets apply per subject**, to everything the Bastion serves: hits, misses, the web interface's pages and the documentation.
  The eleven figures of R-LIM-004, read at a Bastion place:

| Figure | At a Bastion |
|---|---|
| `requestsPerSecond`, `requestsBurst`, `requestsPerHour` | every request of the subject at the Bastion, after step 4 of R-BAS-018 (the credential decided) |
| `cachedBytesPerSecond`, `cachedBytesPerHour` | bytes the Bastion serves from its own cache; the per-second figure paces a hit |
| `uncachedBytesPerSecond`, `uncachedBytesPerHour` | bytes the Bastion reads from the main installation (or by a handover from the object store) for a fill the caller leads; the per-second figure paces that fill |
| `upstreamRequestsPerHour` | the caller's misses: requests the Bastion sends to the main installation for it |
| `parallelTransfers` | the subject's transfers in progress at the Bastion (a lease, [Q-BAS-329](#q-bas-329--a-transfer-at-a-bastion-takes-a-lease-that-waits-at-most-10-s-and-the-waiting-leases-hold-at-most-a-quarter-of-a-replicas-request-slots)) |
| `bytesPerDay` | cached and uncached bytes |
| `refusedPerHour` | refusals of the subject at the Bastion, then a block (R-LIM-025) |

- **A download is a marking class.** An answer of the class `artifact`, and a file under `/files/`, is a transfer (R-LIM-007): it is
  checked before it starts against the hour and day figures, paced
  ([Q-BAS-330](#q-bas-330--a-hit-is-paced-by-the-callers-cached-bytes-per-second-never-below-64-kib-a-second)) and counted as a parallel
  transfer. A `shared` or `private` document, a page of the web interface and documentation are counted only, as R-LIM-007 says of a
  document.
- **Subjects** ([Q-BAS-328](#q-bas-328--the-subject-a-bastion-charges-is-the-one-the-main-installation-names)):

| Caller | Subject key | Where the key comes from |
|---|---|---|
| a user | `user:<id>` | the main installation's check answer and marking (`limits.key`) |
| a technical token | `technical_token:<id>` | as above |
| a CI project | `ci:<issuer>:<project>` | as above |
| a certificate | `certificate:<subject>`, decided by the place's kind rule for technical tokens (Q-LIM-96) | as above; whether a Bastion accepts a certificate at all is the owner's open paper (his f5 = a) |
| an anonymous caller, a page view, a crawler | `anonymous:<address prefix>` | the Bastion |

  The key is the main installation's `limits_subject` of R-LIM-030, never the token ID of the marking: a technical token's subject is
  `technical_token.id`, not the ID of the secret presented.
- **Two budgets.** What a caller takes through Bastion B counts against its budget at B's place, and those counters live at the Bastion
  (memory, or Valkey with cluster scope; without Valkey each replica holds its share). The main installation keeps charging each forward to
  the caller's own budget there, as today (R-BAS-017, R-LIM-003). The usage overview shows both and their sum (R-LIM-045).
- **The mode** is the registration's (R-LIM-044): in Audit the budgets count and refuse nothing; the flood protection, the ceiling, the
  slots and the throughput still hold
  ([Q-LIM-309](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-309--in-audit-a-bastion-still-holds-its-flood-protection-ceiling-slots-and-throughput)).
- **A refusal** carries R-LIM-020's code and members (`rate_limited`, `download_limit_reached`, `upstream_limit_reached`,
  `too_many_parallel_transfers`, `caller_blocked`), the policy names of R-LIM-020 in the RateLimit fields, a `Retry-After` capped by the format
  (R-BAS-091), in the format's error shape (R-BAS-095), and no member that names a place of the main installation (R-BAS-099).
- **Who resolves which rule** ([Q-LIM-302](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-302--the-main-installation-resolves-a-signed-in-callers-rule-the-bastion-the-address-and-kind-rules)):
  the main installation resolves a signed-in caller's rule at the Bastion place, because it knows the groups, and names the rule's ID in the
  check answer and the marking; the handshake carries the place's table, each rule's ID with its effective figures, the address rules and the
  kind rules; the Bastion resolves the address rules (the longest prefix wins) and the kind rules itself.

*Built on 2026-11-26 by E7, the wire's part:* `subject.limits` of the check answer and `Quader-Bastion-Limits` of the marking
(`iface.SubjectLimits`, read and written with the key percent-encoded; a marking that names limits for a subject other than a token, twice
or malformed is refused). *Built on 2026-11-26 by E8:* the check answer's `subject.limits` and the marking's `Quader-Bastion-Limits` of a
token subject name its key and the rule the replica's index of the limits resolves at the registration's place (`bastionmain.SubjectLimits`,
`limits.Index.ResolveBastion`), from the principal the authentication stage accepted and the installed authorization index, without a
statement; a registration whose place the index does not hold yet names none, and the Bastion then charges by the kind rule.
*Built on 2026-11-26 by E9a, the flood protection's part:* the per-address figures, the failed-authentication timeout, the blocks and the
exempt networks come from the configuration (R-BAS-093) and change without a restart; the class `gui` is `guard.Page` with a bucket of its
own per address (`bastion.requests_gui`), which no route asks until W-35's pages exist.

*Built on 2026-11-26 by E9b, the budgets:* the package [internal/bastion/budget](../../internal/bastion/budget/budget.go) charges every request
to its subject at the Bastion's place (`budget.SubjectOf`: the key and rule of the answer, else the users' kind rule under the principal,
[Q-BAS-470](#q-bas-470--a-signed-in-caller-whose-answer-names-no-limits-is-charged-by-the-users-kind-rule-under-its-principal); an
anonymous caller by its address prefix with the address rule of the longest prefix or the kind rule, `settings.Place.Anonymous`), after the
credential is decided (`stepBudget` in [budget.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/budget.go)): a block, the request rate with its burst (a
limiter per rule, `bastion.budget_rate_<hash>`), the requests of the hour. A request to the main installation is an upstream request
(`chargeUpstream`, before the forward and the check). A download (an entry of the class `artifact` or a file below `/files/`, a fill's caller,
an artifact passed through) is checked before its first byte against the hour figure of its bytes and the day's, then takes a lease of the
subject's parallel transfers ([Q-BAS-329](#q-bas-329--a-transfer-at-a-bastion-takes-a-lease-that-waits-at-most-10-s-and-the-waiting-leases-hold-at-most-a-quarter-of-a-replicas-request-slots))
and is paced ([Q-BAS-330](#q-bas-330--a-hit-is-paced-by-the-callers-cached-bytes-per-second-never-below-64-kib-a-second),
[Q-BAS-473](#q-bas-473--a-fills-own-caller-is-checked-when-the-answer-names-the-class-artifact-and-paced-as-it-receives-not-as-the-fill-reads));
every byte written to the caller is counted, from the cache as cached, every other as uncached. An answer `403`, and a `401` to a presented
credential, is a refused request of R-LIM-008 (the challenge of a request without one is not; a `404` that hides existence is not told
apart from a name that does not exist at the Bastion and is not counted) and blocks the subject past `refusedPerHour`
([Q-BAS-472](#q-bas-472--a-block-at-a-bastion-holds-for-the-rest-of-the-quarter-hour-it-began-in-and-the-next)). A caller the Bastion learns
from the main installation's answer is counted then and refused by nothing of that request
([Q-BAS-471](#q-bas-471--a-caller-learned-from-the-main-installations-answer-is-counted-for-that-request-and-refused-by-nothing-of-it)).
The counters are `shared.State.Budget` (the Valkey key family `budget`, windows of an hour and a day counted from the epoch with the
sliding estimate of the throughput's hour, R-BAS-097) and the limiters; the usage goes to the replica's buffer
([internal/bastion/usage](../../internal/bastion/usage/usage.go), Q-LIM-308). The mode is `settings.Applied.Enforce`: in Audit every figure
is counted and reported as `wouldLimit`, nothing is refused, paced or blocked; the guard, the ceiling, the slots and the throughput hold in
both (Q-LIM-309). A refusal is `refuseBudget`: 429 (503 for Ansible Galaxy, Q-BAS-451) in the format's shape with the code of R-LIM-020, the
members `figure`, `limit`, `windowSeconds`, `retryAfterSeconds` where the shape carries members, the RateLimit policy of the figure, one wait
rounded once and capped by the format, and no place (R-BAS-099); `quader_bastion_refused_total{reason="budget"}`,
`quader_bastion_budget_events_total{figure,mode}` and `quader_bastion_limits_mode` count it. Each request asks the shared state about three
more times (block, rate, hour; a download three more and its lease) where the figures are set.

**The defaults of the flood protection and of the slots** (R-BAS-093's table, the Internet preset of R-LIM-046, the built-in configuration
of Q-BAS-327; [Q-BAS-448](#q-bas-448--the-defaults-of-the-anonymous-ceiling-and-of-the-slots)):

- The flood figures are R-BAS-092's, unchanged (measured there to hold one normal command of every client from one address): anonymous 50
  a second with a burst of 1,000 and 1,000 misses a minute; signed-in 200, 4,000 and 4,000; `gui` 20 a second with a burst of 100
  (Q-LIM-307, until W-35 measures a page); the timeout 20 failures in 10 minutes, then 15 minutes; blocks at 3,000 refusals a minute, 15
  minutes doubling to 24 hours.
- The slots are 64 across the replicas, an anonymous share of 0.25 and a wait of **5 s** (2 s before). Measured on 2026-11-26: one
  anonymous `dotnet restore` of 200 packages sends 200 requests at once, and the 16 anonymous slots of a whole Bastion (64 × 0.25, whatever
  the number of replicas) answered 31 to 40 of them `503 busy` after the 2 s wait. Derived: the main installation served the other 160 to
  170 within the 2 s, about 85 a second through the 16 slots, so the 200 need about 2.4 s; a wait of 5 s holds one restore with twice that room, and two restores of
  different callers at once (400, about 4.7 s) only just. The other clients send at most 15 requests at once (npm), within the slots. The
  wait, not more slots, is the figure raised: slots are what the main installation carries at once, and when it is the bound (as on the
  measuring workstation) more slots only make every answer slower, whereas a longer wait costs the main installation nothing and holds the
  caller at the Bastion, which bears its own load (the owner, 2026-11-26).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/guard`, 0.01 s, as built by E9a): the class `gui` has a bucket of its own per address
  (`TestR_BAS_096_PagesOfTheWebInterfaceAreAClassOfTheirOwn`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, `internal/bastion/shared`, about 2 s): a subject over `cachedBytesPerHour` is refused a hit before it
  starts and served a document; a hit is paced to the subject's per-second figure; the 65th transfer of a subject at 64 waits and is refused
  after 10 s; a technical token's two secrets share one budget; an anonymous `/64` is one subject; Audit refuses nothing of the budgets and
  keeps the blocks.
- Integration (area `bastionshared`, about 2 s): two replicas share the budgets through Valkey. Integration (area `bastion`, about 5 s): a
  signed-in caller with a rule of its own at the Bastion place is limited by that rule's figures, and the same caller at the main installation
  by its rule there.
- *As built by E9b:* unit (`internal/bastion/budget`, 0.3 s, counters only, a clock the test drives):
  `TestR_BAS_096_EachBudgetRefusesInEnforce` (each figure with its code; a refused request counts in no window),
  `TestR_BAS_096_TheSixtyFifthTransferWaitsAndIsRefusedAfterTenSeconds`, `TestR_BAS_096_TheWaitingLeasesHoldAtMostAQuarterOfTheSlots`,
  `TestR_BAS_096_AHitIsPacedToItsSubjectsFigureNeverBelowTheFloor`, `TestR_BAS_096_RefusedRequestsAboveTheirFigureBlockTheSubject`,
  `TestR_BAS_096_TheSubjectsOfARequest` (a technical token's two secrets, a token without limits, one `/64`, an address rule) and
  `TestR_BAS_096_TheBudgetsFiguresAreTheInterfaces`; unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, 0.05 s, an artifact of 64 bytes):
  `TestR_BAS_096_ASubjectOverItsCachedBytesIsRefusedAHitBeforeItStartsAndServedADocument` and
  `TestR_BAS_096_ATokenWhoseCallerIsLearnedFromTheAnswerIsCountedThenAndChargedByItsKey`; integration `bastionshared`
  `TestR_BAS_096_WithValkeyTheReplicasShareTheBudgets` (0.2 s, counters); integration `bastion`
  `TestR_BAS_096_ASubjectOverItsBudgetIsRefusedInItsFormatsShapeAndItsUsageAndStateReachTheMainInstallation` (about 4 s with its world, one
  npm document): an anonymous caller over two requests an hour refused in npm's shape while another address is served, its usage at the
  Bastion's place of the usage API and the replica's state on the registration. The case of a signed-in caller with a rule of its own at the
  place is not run end to end: the rule the main installation names is `limits.Index.ResolveBastion`'s, tested by
  `TestR_LIM_043_ABastionsPlaceResolvesAlone`, and the Bastion charges whatever rule it is named (`TestR_BAS_096_TheSubjectsOfARequest`).

### R-BAS-097 · The throughput between the main installation and a Bastion
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's choice (a) of [Q-BAS-331](#q-bas-331--the-maximum-throughput-is-enforced-at-the-bastion-on-every-byte-it-reads): the maximum
throughput is enforced at the Bastion, on every byte it reads.

- **What is paced.** One pacing reader wraps every body the Bastion reads: a fill from the main installation, an answer passed through, a
  handover's read from the object store (R-BAS-074), a forwarded document, the continuation of a fill (R-BAS-075), and W-35's catalogue
  pull, which counts as the registration's own traffic. The handover's direct read crosses the network to the object store; where that is
  not the network to the main installation (an object store reached over another link than the main installation's), it still takes from
  the same cap, which then bounds both links together: the owner's choice of one figure for every byte the Bastion reads (Q-BAS-331). The
  Bastion's own calls of the interface (handshake, feed, check, downloads) carry bodies of kilobytes and are not paced.
- **Two buckets per registration**
  ([Q-BAS-332](#q-bas-332--the-throughput-has-two-buckets-the-total-and-the-anonymous-share)): the total, and the anonymous share of it
  (`limits.throughput.anonymousShare`, default 25 %). A read an anonymous caller started takes from both; a signed-in caller's read and the
  catalogue pull take from the total only, the catalogue below the callers' misses in priority: it reads from a slice only while the slice
  is less than half used ([Q-BAS-458](#q-bas-458--the-catalogue-reads-from-a-slice-only-while-it-is-less-than-half-used)). An anonymous
  share of 0 admits no anonymous miss; a share of 1 is the total alone.
- **The figures**: `limits.throughput.bytesPerSecond`, the card's row "Maximum throughput" in MB/s, **200 MB/s by default**, of
  which the anonymous share is 50 MB/s ([Q-BAS-455](#q-bas-455--the-throughput-is-200-mbs-by-default-a-quarter-for-anonymous-callers));
  `null` is unlimited. On demand `bytesPerHour` per class (`anonymous`, `signedIn`, `catalogue`), unlimited by default. The card says that
  the figure is the Bastion's share of the real link between the two networks and that only misses cross it (R-UI-240). A new figure holds
  for the next bytes every transfer reserves, also for one that runs (R-BAS-093).
- **How it paces** ([Q-BAS-456](#q-bas-456--a-bucket-counts-in-slices-of-100-ms-and-a-read-reserves-its-next-bytes-in-the-first-slice-with-room)):
  a bucket counts in slices of 100 ms, each holding a tenth of its second's figure. A read reserves its next bytes (a quarter of the total's
  slice, at least 4 KiB and at most 1 MiB) in the first slice from now on that has room in each of its buckets, waits until that slice
  begins, and reads at most what it reserved; what it does not read (the end of a body, a `304`) is given back. The reservations queue in the
  order they were made, so N transfers at the cap read about an N-th of it each; a running transfer is slowed and never cut. The time a read
  waits for the cap is no stall of a fill (its stall bound of 60 s) and does not count against the floor of a pass-through (R-BAS-025).
- **Across replicas**: with Valkey a slice is one counter of the Bastion's prefix (`throughput:v1:<bucket>:<slice>`, raised by `INCRBY` and
  the part above the limit given back at once), so the replicas share one cap; without, and while Valkey cannot be used, each replica takes
  `bytesPerSecond ÷ bastion.replicas`, so two replicas without Valkey read 2 × 100 MB/s = 200 MB/s together at the default
  ([H-2360](../security/bastion.md#h-2360--without-valkey-the-throughputs-replicas-hold-their-shares-as-bastionreplicas-says)).
- **At the cap** ([Q-BAS-457](#q-bas-457--a-miss-at-the-cap-is-refused-at-once-when-its-first-bytes-would-come-after-its-queue-time)): a
  new miss is admitted after its slot when its first bytes (at most 64 KiB) find room in a slice that begins within
  `limits.slots.queueTimeoutMillis` of when it asked for its slot; otherwise it answers `503 busy` at once, with the wait until the first slice
  with room as `Retry-After` (at least 1 s) and the format's shape. Fills slow down, so their slots stay taken longer, and the slots' own wait
  (R-BAS-025) answers the rest. When a class's hourly volume is used up, its next miss answers `429 upstream_limit_reached` (or the format's
  status, R-BAS-057) with the time to wait and the members `figure` (`bytesPerHour`), `limit`, `windowSeconds` and `retryAfterSeconds`; a
  transfer that runs is never refused by the hour
  ([H-2361](../security/bastion.md#h-2361--the-throughputs-hourly-volume-is-checked-when-a-miss-is-admitted-not-while-it-reads)).
  A revalidation (the Bastion's own conditional request) is a miss of this kind; hits are always served.
- **Metrics**: `quader_bastion_throughput_limit_bytes_per_second{bucket="total|anonymous"}` (the configured figure, 0 while unlimited),
  `quader_bastion_throughput_wait_seconds_total{class="anonymous|signed_in|catalogue"}` and
  `quader_bastion_throughput_refused_total{class,reason="busy|hour"}` beside R-BAS-090's byte counters; a refused miss also counts
  `quader_bastion_refused_total{reason="throughput"}` and `quader_bastion_main_requests_total{outcome="busy"}`.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (package E10).* [internal/bastion/throughput](../../internal/bastion/throughput/throughput.go): `Pacer` (the buckets,
the reservation per slice, `Admit`, `Running`, `Reader` for a handover's direct read, `CatalogueReader` for W-35's pull, which no package
calls yet); the counters `shared.Bytes` ([bytes.go](../../internal/bastion/shared/bytes.go)) over `cluster.BastionStore.ClaimBytes`,
`ReleaseBytes` and `AddBytes` ([valkey_bastion_bytes.go](../../internal/cluster/valkey_bastion_bytes.go)); the client of the main
installation admits every forward after its slot and paces its body (`mainclient.Throughput`, `ThroughputError`, `Response.Pacing`); the
engine paces a handover's direct read, answers the refusals (`refuseThroughput` in [respond.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/respond.go)),
and lets neither the fill's stall bound nor the pass-through's floor count the cap's wait. The default is the built-in configuration's and
a new registration's (`settings.DefaultThroughputBytesPerSecond`, `bastionmain.DefaultLimits` since E8, which a test holds to it).

Acceptance criteria (as built):

- Unit (`internal/bastion/throughput`, a clock the test drives, 0.3 s together, endless bodies of zeros read by the kilobyte): at 1 MB/s
  with an anonymous share of 25 %, an anonymous fill reads 250 KB in a second while a signed-in fill takes the other 750 KB
  (`TestR_BAS_097_AnAnonymousFillReadsAtMostItsShareWhileASignedInFillTakesTheRest`); a new miss of either class at the cap is refused at
  once with the wait until the first slice with room, while a running transfer of 300 KB is slowed and completes
  (`TestR_BAS_097_ANewMissAtTheCapIsBusyWhileARunningTransferSlowsAndCompletes`); an unread reservation is given back; a class whose hour is
  used up is refused its next miss with the hour, a signed-in one is admitted; without Valkey one replica of two reads half; an unlimited
  throughput paces nothing; the catalogue waits first.
- Unit (`internal/bastion/mainclient`, 0.02 s): a forward is admitted after its slot and its body paced, a continuation paced without an
  admission, a refused miss not sent and its slot given back (`TestR_BAS_097_AForwardIsAdmittedAfterItsSlotAndItsBodyIsPaced`).
- Unit (`internal/bastion/engine`, 0.03 s, bytes and a blob of 192 KiB): a refused miss answers `503 busy` or `429 upstream_limit_reached`
  and a hit is served (`TestR_BAS_097_AMissTheThroughputRefusesIsBusyOrUsedUpAndAHitIsServed`); a handover's direct read is paced
  (`TestR_BAS_097_AHandoversDirectReadIsPaced`).
- Integration (area `bastionshared`, 2.3 s): with Valkey one replica alone reads the whole 1 MB/s, and two replicas at once read 500 KB each
  (`TestR_BAS_097_WithValkeyTheReplicasShareOneThroughputCap`).

### R-BAS-098 · The cache protects what was served twice
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's choice (b) of [Q-BAS-333](#q-bas-333--what-was-served-twice-is-protected-in-the-cache). Built on 2026-11-26 (package E11) in
`internal/bastion/cache` ([core.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/core.go) `Sweep` and `rankProtected`,
[sweep.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sweep.go), [store.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/store.go) `Touch`) with the decisions
[Q-BAS-460](#q-bas-460--the-access-marker-is-the-protection-because-a-fill-writes-none) to
[Q-BAS-464](#q-bas-464--a-replicas-own-commit-lets-the-next-serve-write-the-marker-again).

- **Served twice.** A fill counts as the first access and writes no marker; its object's own time is the access. A serve of the entry from
  the cache writes its access marker (R-BAS-031, at most once per `access_resolution` per replica). An object with an access marker was
  therefore served twice, and the marker is its protection: no second marker is written
  ([Q-BAS-460](#q-bas-460--the-access-marker-is-the-protection-because-a-fill-writes-none)). A commit of this replica lets the next serve of
  the bytes write the marker again, so bytes evicted and filled again are protected at their next serve
  ([Q-BAS-464](#q-bas-464--a-replicas-own-commit-lets-the-next-serve-write-the-marker-again)).
- **The order.** In each sweep the protected objects of an area are ranked by last access, newest first; those that fit in 80 % of the
  area's limit are protected, the first that does not fit and every older one are ranked with the objects served once by their last
  access. The sweep evicts the unprotected, oldest access first, then the protected; because 80 % is below the sweep's target of 85 %, a sweep
  never reaches a protected object ([Q-BAS-461](#q-bas-461--the-protected-share-is-a-rank-in-each-sweep-not-a-marker-taken-away)).
- **What the bound and the order prevent.** A flood of single requests for distinct artifacts evicts only what was served once: the working
  set stays. An attacker who requests every artifact twice protects it, but never more than 80 % of an area, ranked by recency: the rest of
  the area (at least 5 % after a sweep, 15 % before the next) keeps what is fetched once, so a new artifact is kept at its first fetch and
  survives the sweeps after it, and a working set that is read twice after the attack takes the place of the attacker's oldest objects.
  What it does not prevent: such an attacker displaces a working set read longer ago than its own reads, at twice the requests and twice the
  bytes from the cache ([H-2290](../security/bastion.md#h-2290--the-protected-markers-are-neither-signed-nor-hard-to-earn)).
- **Across replicas** ([Q-BAS-462](#q-bas-462--served-twice-means-filled-once-and-served-from-the-same-store-once-more)). On the volume,
  served twice means on that replica's volume (with routing by path, R-BAS-033, the replica that holds the path). On a shared bucket it means
  filled by any replica and served from the bucket by any replica: the markers lie in the bucket, and the replica that sweeps reads all of
  them at its listing. Two replicas that miss the same artifact at once both fill it, and neither fill protects it.
- **Layouts.** The encrypted layout (R-BAS-061) keeps the same marker under its tree (`x/<m>`); R-BAS-089's admission at a commit is
  unchanged; documents and artifacts are ranked each in their own area.
- `quader_bastion_cache_protected_bytes{area}` shows the protected share
  ([Q-BAS-463](#q-bas-463--the-protected-bytes-are-counted-by-the-sweep-and-shown-by-the-replica-that-swept)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/cache`): with an area of 20 objects, 4 read twice and 40 distinct fills after them, the 4 stay and the flood's
  last fill is kept; with 18 read twice, 16 are protected after a sweep, and the sweep evicts the two read once and the oldest of the two
  that lost their protection; the volume and the bucket layout and the encrypted layout alike. An attacker who reads 40 objects twice
  holds 16 protected, a new single fetch survives the sweeps after it, and a working set of 4 read twice afterwards is held and protected
  in place of the attacker's oldest; an object filled by one replica of a bucket and served by the other is protected, one filled by both is
  not; bytes filled again are protected at their next serve.

Built: `TestR_BAS_098_*` in [protect_test.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/protect_test.go) (five tests, objects of 64 bytes, 0.9 s
together on a machine at a load of 13 to 21, of which the encrypted layout takes 0.5 s). The planner's area of 100 entries is scaled to 20 so
that 95, 85 and 80 % fall on whole objects and the run stays short. What each leg gains: the unit job about 1 s; no integration shard, no
end-to-end leg; nothing grows with the number of formats. Measured once, not a test: the flood of E4 against a cache of 2 GiB turned a warm
`npm ci` of 475 packages into 475 misses before the change and left it at 475 hits after it
([developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-flood-again-with-the-protection-of-what-was-served-twice-measured-2026-11-26)).

### R-BAS-099 · A Bastion names nothing of the main installation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's rule ([Q-BAS-338](#q-bas-338--a-bastion-reveals-nothing-of-the-main-installation)): "Der Bastion verrät keine internen
Informationen über die Hauptinstanz." Nothing a Bastion answers, in a body, a header or a page, names, links to or identifies the main
installation: not its host, base URL or address; not a repository name the caller did not address; not a request ID of the main
installation; not its policy or rule structure (a place, a rule, a profile); not a version string. What a caller addressed (its repository,
its package) and content that authors put into a package are not the main installation's and stay.

The places, read in the code on 2026-11-26, and what each shows once its package has landed:

| # | Place | What a client sees today | What it sees then | Package |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The refusal of a write (`Marker.readOnly` in [mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go), reached through the probe) | `403 bastion_read_only` "This is a read-only Bastion of https://quader.example.com; publish to https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/", for OCI the image prefix `quader.example.com/web/docker-local`; "This is a read-only Bastion; publish to the main installation." where the base is unknown | `403 read_only` "This address is read-only: it serves downloads and accepts no uploads." | E16 the text at the main installation's backstop; E15 the refusal at the Bastion; E7 the code |
| 2 | The Bastion's own texts and codes ([respond.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/respond.go), `request.go`, `probe.go`) | `main_unreachable` "The main installation is not reachable; retry later."; `bastion_busy` "The Bastion is at its limit of requests to the main installation; retry."; `main_timeout` "The main installation did not answer in time."; `main_failed` "The main installation did not answer."; `bastion_not_served`; texts of `405`, `413` and `421` that say "Bastion" | the codes and texts of [Q-BAS-321](#q-bas-321--the-bastions-own-codes-are-named-by-their-status-its-texts-name-no-party-and-its-problem-type-is-aboutblank) | E16 the texts; E7 the codes (they are the interface's, `iface/problems.go`) |
| 3 | The member `type` of problem details (`errs.ProblemTypePrefix`) | `/api/v1/problems/<code>`, a path of the management API, which the Bastion does not serve | `about:blank` on every problem the Bastion renders and on every problem the main installation renders for a recognized forward (Q-BAS-321) | E16 |
| 4 | The RateLimit policy names of the Bastion's guard (`policyOf` in `request.go`) | `bastion:requests`, `bastion:misses`, `bastion:failed_auth`, `bastion:blocking` | `requests`, `misses`, `failed-auth`, `blocking`; the budgets' policy names of R-LIM-020 since E9b (`requests`, `requests-hour`, `cached-hour`, `uncached-hour`, `upstream-hour`, `day`, `parallel`, `refused-hour`) | E16 |
| 5 | Headers of a forwarded answer (`replayHeader` and `neverReplayed` in `respond.go`; the Bastion's client strips only `Quader-Bastion-*`) | on a miss `Quader-Resolved-From` (the member repository of a virtual repository that served it), OCI's `Quader-Annotations-Cut`, and the main installation's `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` | an allowlist: the core's representation headers, the format's declared replay headers, `Content-Length`, `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Retry-After`, `WWW-Authenticate`, `Allow`, `Link`, `Docker-Distribution-Api-Version`, and `Location` under row 6; no `Quader-*` header and no RateLimit field of the main installation | E16 |
| 6 | `Location` of a `3xx` from the main installation (passed by `replayHeader`) | whatever the main installation set; whether a route answers a forward with an absolute URL on its own host is not verified | passed only when relative or on the Bastion's own host; otherwise `502 bad_gateway`, counted | E16 |
| 7 | Problem bodies of the main installation's refusals passed through (`errs.Write`; the limits' refusal in [errors.go](../../internal/limits/errors.go)) | the main installation's `requestId`; for a signed-in caller "Your limits: <response base URL>/ui/profile/usage", which for a forward is a path of the Bastion's host that the Bastion does not serve; the member `place` | for a recognized forward: no `requestId`, no "Your limits" sentence, no `place`; `figure`, `limit` and `retryAfterSeconds` stay | E16, the main installation's side |
| 8 | The registry token's payload ([token.go](../../internal/auth/registrytoken/token.go); its claims are readable base64url JSON) | the endpoint's name `e`, the principal kind and ID `pk`, `p`, the underlying token's ID, type and hash `t`, `tt`, `th`, and the key ID; until E14a every anonymous caller of a Bastion received such a token | an anonymous caller gets the Bastion's own token (R-BAS-094); a signed-in caller payload version 2: `a`, `exp` and `g` readable, the rest sealed (Q-BAS-339) | E14a; E7 the readers; E17 |
| 9 | Challenges: the Bastion's own (`registryChallenge` in `family.go`; `Basic realm="quader"`) and the main installation's on a forwarded `401` | the Bastion's own host; the main installation's realm is its response base URL, which for a forward is the Bastion's host (R-BAS-017) | unchanged, held by a test | E16 |
| 10 | URLs in documents: npm's `dist.tarball`, NuGet's service index and `@id`, Galaxy's `href`, OCI's `Link` | rendered on the response base URL, which the handshake holds equal to the Bastion's (R-BAS-010); only the npm and NuGet e2e runs check it | unchanged; every format's integration replay asserts that no byte and no header names the main installation's host, another of its base URLs or `/api/v1/` | E16 |
| 11 | Debian's `Release` fields ([settings.go](../../internal/formats/deb/settings.go)) | `Origin` from the repository's settings (default `quader`); a remote passes on its upstream's; no host | unchanged: an administrator's or an upstream's content (H-2296) | — |
| 12 | Client set-up for a Bastion (`client-setup?bastion=`, R-BAS-007) | served by the main installation to its own users, on the Bastion's host, without publish snippets | unchanged; W-35's web interface renders its own on its host | — |
| 13 | Version strings | no `Server` or version header in the Bastion's answers; `User-Agent` only on its outbound requests; `/metrics` only on the ops listener | unchanged | — |

| 15 | Problem texts of a remote's fill that a forward relays (`classify.go` of `internal/proxy`; found while writing this table, not in the planner's list) | "The upstream of web/npm-remote answered 503." and "… cannot be reached." / "… did not answer in time.", which name the member repository of a virtual repository the caller addressed as `web/npm-all` | for a recognized forward, a text without a repository the caller did not address ("The package could not be fetched right now."); the codes stay | E16, with the inventory of W-35's P8 (H-2295) |

Where the code differs from what the planner read: `Quader-Error-Code` is not a header of a package route (only the image scanning's pull
sets it, `internal/vuln/scanner/pull.go`), so row 5 does not list it; the allowlist covers it either way.
