### R-BAS-114 · A forward's problems name nothing of the main installation
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's rule of R-BAS-099 for the texts and codes the main installation's formats and core write on the routes a Bastion forwards
(W-35's P8). The main installation decides a problem's text for a caller of a Bastion when it renders the problem, never where the error
is made, since one error can answer a forward and an ordinary caller at once (a fetch collapsed for every caller of a replica). For a
recognized forward (`errs.WithBastionForward`, R-BAS-099 row 3) `errs.ProblemFor`
([Q-BAS-385](#q-bas-385--a-forwards-text-is-chosen-at-rendering-from-what-the-error-carries)):

- gives the problem the detail its error carries for a forward (`errs.WithForwardDetail`), where the error's own text names something of
  the installation: a repository the caller did not address, a page of the web interface, the place to ask;
- else the neutral detail of a failure of the remote engine (R-BAS-099 row 15);
- else, for a status of 500 or more that is no rate limit, the neutral text of the status, and drops the field errors
  ([Q-BAS-386](#q-bas-386--every-5xx-of-a-forward-reads-the-neutral-text-of-its-status-unless-its-error-vouches-for-its-own)): what failed
  inside the installation is nothing a caller of a Bastion can act on, so a text written later fails closed; an error whose 5xx text
  names only what the caller asked for vouches for it with the same option;
- leaves out every extension member that names only the installation (`errs.WithInstallationExtension`: a finding's ID);
- and keeps every other 4xx text, code, status, header and member.

What each format and the core write, and what a caller of a Bastion reads instead, is the table of what a forward relays in
[R-BAS-029](#r-bas-029--responses-of-the-bastions-own) ([Q-BAS-387](#q-bas-387--a-refusal-loses-its-link-into-the-installation-and-names-this-repository)).

*Built on 2026-11-26 by W-35's P8:* the options in [errs.go](../../internal/errs/errs.go), the rendering in
[problem.go](../../internal/errs/problem.go), the texts of rows 1 to 6 where they are made, and the ClamAV definitions' rate limit, which the
endpoint answers `503`, vouched for in `clamav.Rendered`. The Bastion's own `502`, `503` and `504` read the same texts
(`errs.DetailBadGateway`, `errs.DetailUnavailable`, `errs.DetailGatewayTimeout`).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit, one case per rule and per row of R-BAS-029's table (about 0.4 s in all): `TestR_BAS_114_AForwardReadsATextOfTheInstallationOnlyWhereTheErrorVouchesForIt`
  (`internal/errs`), and the tests the table names in `internal/remotecuration/rules`, `internal/vuln/enforce`, `internal/signatures/gate`,
  `internal/malware/gate`, `internal/repository`, `internal/formats`, `internal/formats/npm` and `internal/formats/clamav`; each renders
  the site's own error for an ordinary caller and for a forward.
- Integration: the replays' scan of R-BAS-099 row 10 meets every text of them a replay reaches.

### R-BAS-115 · A registry token a Bastion relays names nothing of the main installation
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

A signed-in caller's token request below `/v2/` is forwarded, and the main installation's token reaches the caller through the Bastion
(R-BAS-052). Read in the code on 2026-11-26: the token's payload was readable JSON that named the endpoint `e`, the principal's kind and ID,
the Quader token's ID, type and hash, the issue time, the catalog entry and the ring's key ID; it named no host (the realm and the
`service` a client is told are the response base URL's, R-BAS-099 row 9). The main installation issues payload version 2 alone
([formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-005, [Q-BAS-339](#q-bas-339--a-registry-token-reads-only-its-anonymity-its-expiry-and-its-grant)):

- readable: `a`, `exp` and `g`, the three claims a Bastion reads without a key (R-BAS-052), and on a token of a system subject `s`, which
  no forward carries ([Q-BAS-389](#q-bas-389--a-system-tokens-subject-stays-readable-and-version-1-is-read-until-its-tokens-expire));
- the key ID: 8 bytes of an HMAC of the ring key's ID under its MAC key, in hexadecimal, which names no key of the ring;
- sealed: every other claim, under AES-256-GCM with a key derived from the ring's key with the info `quader registry token seal v2`
  ([Q-BAS-388](#q-bas-388--the-sealed-part-of-a-registry-token-is-encrypted-under-a-key-of-the-ring-not-a-reference)).

The verifier reads versions 1 and 2, so a token issued before stays valid until it expires (at most `oci.token_lifetime`, one hour); no
other path of migration is needed. The Bastion's own anonymous token stays version 1 with the key ID `bastion` and the claims `a` and `exp`
(R-BAS-094). The interface stays at version 8: its readers read both versions since E7.

*Built on 2026-11-26 by E17 with W-35's P8:* [token.go](../../internal/auth/registrytoken/token.go); the replays' scan of R-BAS-099 row 10
decodes every registry token in an answer of a Bastion.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/auth/registrytoken`, milliseconds): a token of a principal is version 2 with an opaque key ID and the readable claims
  `a`, `exp` and `g` alone; no byte of its payload names the endpoint, the principal, the Quader token, the issue time or the key ID; two
  tokens of the same claims seal apart, and a sealed byte changed under a valid MAC does not verify; the verifier reads the sealed claims
  back and a token of version 1 until it expires; an anonymous token reads `a` and `exp`, a scan token keeps `s`
  (`TestR_BAS_115_ARegistryTokenReadsOnlyItsAnonymityExpiryAndGrant`). The Bastion's readers read an issued token of version 2
  (`TestR_BAS_052_*` of `internal/bastion/iface`).
- Integration (area `bastion`, about 0 s more): every registry token in an answer of a replay is of version 2 with an opaque key ID and
  the readable claims `a`, `exp` and `g`, or the Bastion's own anonymous token (`tokenNames` in the scan of `replica.do`; the docker and
  containerd pulls of `TestR_BAS_051_R_BAS_053_ADockerAndAContainerdPullThroughABastion` relay a signed-in caller's token).

## The interface version 8: the shared wire

The wire of this section and of W-35's web interface, built by one package (E7 of [developer/bastion-limits.md](../developer/bastion-limits.md)
together with W-35's package P5), which raises `iface.InterfaceVersion` once, from 7 to 8
([Q-BAS-322](#q-bas-322--both-topics-raise-the-interface-version-once-to-8)). Since E8 the main installation sends each registration's
own configuration (Q-BAS-327's built-in configuration is the one a Bastion falls back to, E9a's), and the Bastion ignores what no package
of its side uses yet. *Built on 2026-11-26* (E7 with W-35's P5):
`InterfaceVersion` is 8, and every member below is in [internal/bastion/iface](../../internal/bastion/iface), read and written as this
section says; what each side does with it after E7 is said per member.

**The handshake's member `configuration`** (R-BAS-093), beside the members of R-BAS-010 and R-BAS-057; the top-level `handover` goes into
it:

```json
{
  "configuration": {
    "revision": 17,
    "switches": {"handover": false, "gui": false, "docs": false},
    "limits": {
      "mode": "enforce",
      "preset": "internet",
      "place": {
        "rules": {
          "0193a0c4-…": {"requestsPerSecond": 50, "requestsBurst": 1000, "requestsPerHour": 20000, "cachedBytesPerSecond": 100000000,
                          "cachedBytesPerHour": 30000000000, "uncachedBytesPerSecond": 50000000, "uncachedBytesPerHour": 20000000000,
                          "upstreamRequestsPerHour": 3000, "parallelTransfers": 64, "bytesPerDay": 200000000000, "refusedPerHour": 300}
        },
        "addressRules": [{"prefix": "198.51.100.0/24", "rule": "0193a0c5-…"}],
        "kindRules": {"anonymous": "0193a0c4-…", "user": "0193a0c6-…", "technicalToken": "0193a0c6-…", "ci": "0193a0c6-…",
                      "administrator": "0193a0c6-…"}
      },
      "flood": {
        "anonymous": {"requestsPerSecond": 50, "burst": 1000, "missesPerMinute": 1000},
        "authenticated": {"requestsPerSecond": 200, "burst": 4000, "missesPerMinute": 4000},
        "gui": {"requestsPerSecond": 20, "burst": 100},
        "failedAuth": {"maxFailures": 20, "windowSeconds": 600, "timeoutSeconds": 900},
        "blocking": {"threshold": 3000, "windowSeconds": 60, "durationSeconds": 900, "maxDurationSeconds": 86400},
        "exemptNetworks": []
      },
      "slots": {"maxConcurrent": 64, "anonymousShare": 0.25, "queueTimeoutMillis": 2000},
      "throughput": {"bytesPerSecond": 200000000, "anonymousShare": 0.25,
                     "bytesPerHour": {"anonymous": null, "signedIn": null, "catalogue": null}},
      "anonymousCeiling": {"requestsPerSecond": 100, "burst": 1000, "requestsPerHour": 100000}
    }
  }
}
```

*(example member; the figures of `rules` are the profile Anonymous of R-LIM-010 standing in for "Bastion: anonymous", whose figures E4's
measurement sets, and the ceiling's figures are examples for the same reason)*

- Every member is always present; a figure is a positive integer or `null` (unlimited); a share lies in 0 to 1; `preset` is `internet`,
  `partnerNetwork`, `internal` or `custom`; `mode` is `audit` or `enforce`; `kindRules` names a rule for each of the five kinds of R-LIM-011 (a certificate takes the kind rule of the technical tokens, Q-LIM-96);
  `addressRules` holds canonical prefixes (R-LIM-002) and names rules of `rules`. `Validate` refuses anything else, and a refused member
  fails the handshake.
- The flood figures are positive integers, never `null`: flood protection is never unlimited, and an address that is to meet none is an
  exempt network; a block's `durationSeconds` is not above its `maxDurationSeconds`; a ceiling's `burst` is set only with its rate.
- The types are `iface.Configuration`, `iface.Switches`, `iface.Limits`, `iface.PlaceTable`, `iface.Figures`, `iface.Flood`, `iface.Slots`,
  `iface.Throughput` and `iface.Ceiling` in [configuration.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/configuration.go), with `iface.FloodClass`,
  `FloodRate`, `FailedAuth`, `Blocking`, `AddressRule`, `KindRules` and `ThroughputHours` for their members.
- *After E7:* the main installation answered `bastionmain.InterimConfiguration` ([Q-BAS-352](#q-bas-352--until-e8-the-main-installation-sends-an-interim-configuration-that-equals-todays-behaviour)) until E8. *After E8:* it answers the
  registration's configuration from its snapshot (Q-BAS-440). The link refuses a handshake whose configuration `Validate` refuses and
  applies `switches.handover`. *Since E9a* the Bastion applies the whole member (R-BAS-093): the flood figures, the slots and the anonymous
  ceiling; *since E9b* `mode` and `place` (R-BAS-096). *Since E10* the Bastion applies the throughput (R-BAS-097), a new registration's the
  default of 200 MB/s with an anonymous share of 25 % (Q-BAS-455).

**The subject's limits** (R-BAS-096). The check answer's `subject` gains `limits: {"key": "<limits_subject>", "rule": "<rule ID>"}` for a
usable subject (`token`; for `anonymous` the member is absent, since the Bastion decides an anonymous caller's key and rule itself), and the
marking gains the header `Quader-Bastion-Limits: key=<limits_subject>; rule=<rule ID>` on every answer that carries
`Quader-Bastion-Subject: token=…`. The key is percent-encoded as `Quader-Bastion-Package` is (R-BAS-013); the rule is the rule of the
Bastion place the main installation resolved for the caller, or the kind rule's ID where no single-caller or group rule matched. The member
and the header are optional on the wire: since E8 the main installation sends both for every token subject whose rule its index resolves at
the Bastion's place, and a marking that names limits for a subject other than a token, twice, or malformed is refused (`iface.SubjectLimits`,
`ParseSubjectLimits`).

**The reporting batch** (R-BAS-016, R-LIM-045). `POST /api/v1/bastion/downloads` gains two members, always present:

```json
{
  "events": [],
  "dropped": 0,
  "usage": {
    "bucketSeconds": 300,
    "rows": [
      {"bucketStart": "2026-11-26T12:05:00Z", "subject": "user:0191…", "credential": "0192…", "repository": "web/npm-all",
       "rule": "0193a0c6-…", "requests": 812, "refused": 0, "cachedBytes": 431000000, "uncachedBytes": 2100000,
       "upstreamRequests": 14, "limited": {"cachedBytesPerHour": 0}, "wouldLimit": {}}
    ],
    "overflow": [{"bucketStart": "2026-11-26T12:05:00Z", "subjectKind": "anonymous", "repository": "web/npm-all", "subjects": 3112,
                  "requests": 41000, "refused": 120, "cachedBytes": 9000000000, "uncachedBytes": 0, "upstreamRequests": 0}]
  },
  "status": {
    "replica": "quader-bastion-7d9c-x2k4q", "at": "2026-11-26T12:05:10Z",
    "cache": {"bytes": 15032385536, "capacityBytes": 21474836480, "hits": 120400, "misses": 3100, "evictions": 12,
              "protectedBytes": 9663676416},
    "throughput": {"limited": false, "bytesPerSecondByClass": {"anonymous": 1200000, "signedIn": 41000000, "catalogue": 0}},
    "limited": 4, "blocked": 1,
    "blocks": [{"address": "203.0.113.0/24", "until": "2026-11-26T12:20:00Z", "reason": "refusals"}]
  }
}
```

*(example request)*

- `usage.rows` holds at most 100,000 keys per batch window and the rest in `overflow`, per repository and subject kind (Q-LIM-308);
  `status.blocks` at most 100, the newest. `events` and `dropped` keep their meaning; the Bastion sends a batch every flush whether or not
  `recordDownloads` is true, and with it false `events` is empty.
- The types are `iface.UsageReport`, `iface.UsageRow`, `iface.UsageOverflow` and `iface.ReplicaStatus` (with `CacheStatus`,
  `ThroughputStatus`, `ThroughputClasses`, `StatusBlock`) in [usage.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/usage.go); `MaxUsageRows` and
  `MaxStatusBlocks` are the bounds, and the keys of `limited` and `wouldLimit` are the figures' names (`iface.FigureNames`).
- *After E7:* the main installation refuses a batch whose usage or status breaks a bound (`422`); the Bastion sends both empty, with the
  lists as `[]`, and sends a batch only when it holds events, as before. *Since E9b* every flush sends the usage and the state
  ([Q-BAS-474](#q-bas-474--a-replica-reports-its-usage-as-deltas-with-every-flush-and-its-state-says-of-each-figure-whose-it-is)).
- **Whose each figure of `status` is** (Q-BAS-474), so that a reader adds only what is each replica's own: `cache.bytes`,
  `cache.capacityBytes` and `cache.protectedBytes` are the replica's view of its cache backend: its own on a volume, and the whole Bastion's
  on a bucket, which every replica of a shared bucket reports alike (take one, never the sum); *since interface version 9
  ([Q-BAS-480](#q-bas-480--a-replicas-status-says-whether-its-cache-is-the-bastions-and-the-card-adds-up-only-caches-of-their-own))* `cache.shared` says which: `true` on the bucket backend, `false` on the volume backend, so that a
  reader adds the replicas' own caches and takes the shared one once; `cache.hits`, `cache.misses` and
  `cache.evictions` are the replica's own since its start; `throughput.limited` and `throughput.bytesPerSecondByClass` the replica's own,
  the rate since its previous status; `limited` the subjects a budget refused on this replica within the last five minutes (a subject
  refused at two replicas counts at each); `blocks` the blocks this replica set that have not ended, the newest first, at most 100;
  `blocked` the larger of their number and of the addresses the replica's block list holds (with Valkey the blocks every replica learned of).
- **The reasons of a block** are a closed list (Q-BAS-474): `refusals`, an address that collected more than `flood.blocking.threshold` of
  the Bastion's refusals (R-BAS-037); `failed_auth`, an address in the failed-authentication timeout (R-BAS-036); `refused_requests`, an
  anonymous caller's address past its `refusedPerHour` at the Bastion's place (R-LIM-025, Q-BAS-472). A block's `address` is a canonical
  prefix: an IPv4 address as its `/32`, an IPv6 caller as its `/64`.
  *After E8:* the main installation stores the usage rows at the place `bastion:<id>` and the status in `bastion_status`, whether or not
  downloads are recorded, and bounds a batch's body at `max_batch` × 10 KiB + 100,000 × 640 bytes + 256 KiB, about 71 MiB with the
  defaults ([Q-BAS-442](#q-bas-442--a-batchs-body-is-sized-for-100000-usage-rows-and-its-usage-is-stored-after-every-refusal-was-decided)).

**The format table** (R-BAS-057) gains, per format:

- `errorShape`: `problem`, `npm`, `text`, `distribution` or `galaxy` (R-BAS-095,
  [Q-BAS-337](#q-bas-337--a-bastions-own-refusals-take-one-of-five-error-shapes-a-format-declares)), always present;
  `catalog.Facts.Bastion.ErrorShape` of the format (`problem` where a format declares none; kit check 19 requires the declaration).
- `readWithBody`: a list of `{"method": "POST", "path": "<pattern>"}`, the format's routes with a writing method whose kind is a read, as
  paths from the host root whose `{name}` segments stand for one non-empty segment each; `[]` where there are none ([Q-BAS-353](#q-bas-353--a-format-declares-its-read-routes-with-a-body-below-the-repository-and-kit-check-19-holds-the-list-to-its-routes)). A request
  matches by its method and its escaped path, a literal segment byte for byte, so a spelling the table does not name is a write and fails
  closed (`HandshakeFormat.ReadsWithBody`). As built: npm's `POST /api/npm/{project}/{repo}/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk`,
  `…/-/npm/v1/security/audits` and `…/-/npm/v1/security/audits/quick` (the legacy audit npm falls back to, found in the route table beside
  the bulk one), and the registry root's `POST /v2/_token`; no other format has one.

**The problem codes** (R-BAS-029, Q-BAS-321): `bastion_read_only` becomes `read_only`, `bastion_not_served` `not_found`,
`main_unreachable` `unavailable`, `main_failed` `bad_gateway`, `main_timeout` `gateway_timeout`, `bastion_busy` `busy`. The constants of
`iface/problems.go` and the code registry of `internal/errs` change with them; `bastion_token_invalid`, `bastion_interface_mismatch`,
`bastion_base_url_unknown` and `bastion_not_implemented` stay, since they concern the Bastion and never reach a caller. The headers
`Quader-Bastion-Probe` and `Quader-Bastion-Route` and the value `read-with-body` leave the interface (R-BAS-095); E15 removed the probe,
which [Q-BAS-351](#q-bas-351--until-e15-a-probe-is-recognized-by-its-form-and-a-read-route-with-a-body-is-the-format-tables) had the main
installation recognize by its form until then, without a change of the wire.

**The contact** (R-BAS-010) gains two request headers of the handshake, recorded with the replica's contact:
`Quader-Bastion-Edge-Limit: rps=<n>; connections=<n>` (either member alone) or `off` (R-BAS-093) and W-35's
`Quader-Bastion-Catalogue-Kept: true|false` (`iface.EdgeLimit`, `ParseEdgeLimit`, `ParseCatalogueKept`). Both are optional: a replica that
does not know the value sends none ([Q-BAS-354](#q-bas-354--the-contact-headers-are-optional-and-recorded-in-the-contacts-event-until-e8)).

**The registry token's readers** (Q-BAS-339): `iface.RegistryTokenAnonymous`, `RegistryTokenExpiry` and `RegistryTokenGrant` read payload
versions 1 and 2; E17 then issues version 2. Version 2 is `2:<opaque key id>:<readable claims>:<sealed claims>`: the readable claims are one
JSON object, followed by `:` and at least one byte of the sealed part, which a Bastion never reads.

**W-35's catalogue** (that plan's package P5, built in the same change; its requirements are R-BAS-101 to R-BAS-103): the routes
`PathCatalogue`, `PathCatalogueDocument`, `PathCatalogueDocuments` and `PathCataloguePublic`, the types `CatalogueChanges`,
`CatalogueChange`, `CatalogueBatch`, `CatalogueFrame`, `CataloguePublic` and `CatalogueRepository`, the path grammar `CataloguePath` with
`ParseCataloguePath`, the frame functions `WriteCatalogueFrame` and `ReadCatalogueFrame`, and the feed kind `catalogue`, in
[catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/catalogue.go); R-BAS-101 says what each is.

**What a Bastion of version 7 and a main installation of version 8 do with each other** (R-BAS-009's rule, unchanged): they do not talk.
The Bastion's handshake answers `400 bastion_interface_mismatch` with `"interfaceVersion": 8`; the Bastion treats the main installation as
unreachable, serves cached content to callers with live answers for the grace period and `503` afterwards (R-BAS-027), and fires
`QuaderBastionInterfaceMismatch` (R-BAS-028). A Bastion of version 8 and a main installation of version 7 do the same the other way round.
Main installation and Bastions are upgraded together, and the release notes say so.

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_009_TheInterfaceChangesOnlyWithItsVersion` with the regenerated surface at version 8; unit tests of every new member's
  `Validate` and round trip, and of the catalogue's path grammar; under 0.5 s in all. *As built* (`internal/bastion/iface`, 0.13 s for the
  package, data of bytes): `TestR_BAS_093_TheConfigurationTravelsWholeAndItsRulesHold`,
  `TestR_BAS_096_TheSubjectsLimitsTravelInTheCheckAndTheMarking`, `TestR_BAS_016_ABatchCarriesUsageAndStatusWithoutADownload`,
  `TestR_BAS_093_TheContactReportsTheEdgeAndTheCatalogue`, `TestR_BAS_103_TheCataloguePathGrammarRoundTrips`,
  `TestR_BAS_101_TheCatalogueChangeListHoldsItsOrder`, `TestR_BAS_101_TheBatchReadIsFramed`,
  `TestR_BAS_095_AReadRouteWithABodyIsMatchedAsTheRouterMatchesIt`, `TestR_BAS_052_AVersion2RegistryTokenReadsOnlyItsReadableClaims`,
  and the format table's members in `TestR_BAS_057_TheHandshakeCarriesTheFormatTable`.

## The interface version 9: a HEAD is no download, and a replica says whose cache it reports

Package W34-E19 (2026-11-26) raises `iface.InterfaceVersion` from 8 to 9 for two gaps of the day's packages
([Q-BAS-479](#q-bas-479--a-get-a-bastion-sends-for-a-head-says-so-in-a-header-of-the-request), [Q-BAS-480](#q-bas-480--a-replicas-status-says-whether-its-cache-is-the-bastions-and-the-card-adds-up-only-caches-of-their-own)): the `GET` a Bastion sends to answer a `HEAD` was counted at the main
installation as a download (H-2375), and the card could not tell a replica's own cache from the Bastion's shared one (H-2364 of
[api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md)). Before the first stable release a raise costs nothing but the lockstep upgrade every raise needs.

**The request header `Quader-Bastion-For-Head: true`** (`iface.HeaderForHead`, `iface.ForHeadValue`, `iface.ForHead`) on a forwarded
`GET`: the Bastion sends it on the `GET` that fills a `HEAD` miss of a document and on the conditional `GET` that revalidates a kept
document or the caller's copy for a `HEAD` (`rq.asGet`, `mainclient.Forward.ForHead`), and on nothing else; it is set after the caller's
headers were copied, which drop every `Quader-*` header, so a caller's own value never reaches the main installation.

- The main installation's recognition stage reads it on a recognized forwarded `GET` into `Recognition.ForHead`: exactly one value, `true`;
  anything else is no statement. It removes the header, as it removes the handover's offer, so no stage behind it reads it; on a request
  that is no recognized forward it is removed and means nothing.
- The statement holds only once the request matched a route of a document, a metadata or a computed route (`bastionmain.ForHead`,
  [Q-BAS-482](#q-bas-482--the-main-installation-honours-the-statement-of-a-head-on-a-documents-route-only)); on a download route, the route of an artifact, which a Bastion never sends it for, the `GET` counts as the
  download it is.
- Where it holds, the answer is the `GET`'s, marking included (`Counted` where the core counts that document, so a later serve from what
  the Bastion kept is reported, R-BAS-059), and the main installation records nothing a `HEAD` would not record
  ([Q-BAS-481](#q-bas-481--the-get-of-a-head-records-nothing-a-head-does-not-and-is-charged-at-the-main-installation-as-the-head)): no download statistics, no repository activity, no `artifact.downloaded` (`items.Options.NoDownload`),
  and at the limits no cached bytes, no pacing, no download admission and no parallel lease (`limits.Charge.NoDownload`). Its request
  figures, and the upstream request and the uncached bytes of a fill it causes at a remote repository, count as every forward's.

**The status's `cache.shared`** (`iface.CacheStatus.Shared`), always present: `true` when the replica's cache is the Bastion's bucket (the
bucket backend), `false` for the replica's own volume. The card adds `bytes`, `capacityBytes` and `protectedBytes` over the replicas whose
cache is their own and takes the largest of the shared ones once (R-UI-240, Q-UI-1489 as revised).

**What a Bastion of version 8 and a main installation of version 9 do with each other** (R-BAS-009's rule, unchanged): they do not talk;
the handshake answers `400 bastion_interface_mismatch` with `"interfaceVersion": 9`, as for every raise. Main installation and Bastions
are upgraded together.

Acceptance criteria:

- `TestR_BAS_009_TheInterfaceChangesOnlyWithItsVersion` with the regenerated surface at version 9; the tests named in R-BAS-059's
  criteria for the header; `TestR_LIM_045_TheStatusSaysWhetherItsCacheIsTheBastions` (`internal/bastion/server`, milliseconds, gauges
  only) for the member; the card's two cases in Vitest (R-UI-240).

## The Bastion's imprint and privacy notice

### R-BAS-100 · A Bastion's own imprint and privacy notice from its chart
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner, 2026-11-26, 11:51, of a company that runs a public web interface: "Wird von der Instanz selbst ausgeliefert. Der Text beider
Links kann über ein Markdown frei bestimmt werden. Eingestellt wird es bei der Installation über Helm, der Administrator des Bastion ist
verantwortlich für die Einhaltung dieser Werte." With his rule that "Der Bastion verrät keine internen Informationen über die
Hauptinstanz" and "Je kleiner der Footprint, desto besser".

- **Values.** `config.ui.legal.imprint.en`, `.de`, `config.ui.legal.privacy.en`, `.de` of the chart `quader-bastion` (R-BAS-046):
  Markdown, empty by default, at most 64 KiB each, rendered into the configuration file like every key of `config`; a change is a
  rollout (R-BAS-002). They are the configuration of this Bastion, set by its administrator, who answers for what they say; they are
  never read from the main installation, never a Secret, and nothing in them is derived from the main installation's configuration.
- **Rendering.** At start, by the README renderer of the main installation's packages ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-008) in an
  instance of its own (`internal/bastion/legal`): no external image origin, so an image becomes a link and an image of the Bastion's own
  origin (`server.base_url`) is dropped; no script, style, SVG or frame; links `http`, `https` and `mailto` with
  `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"`. The pages are held in memory; the rule of the languages is the main installation's
  ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-225): a locale without its own text shows the other language's, marked with its `lang`; a page
  that no language has a text for is none.
- **Serving.** This requirement adds no listener and no route
  ([Q-BAS-342](#q-bas-342--the-pages-are-rendered-at-start-and-served-by-no-route-until-the-bastions-web-interface)); `/api/v1/…` answers
  `404 not_found` (R-BAS-003). *Built by W-35's P9 on 2026-11-26:* the web interface serves the pages from `Pages(locale)` of
  `internal/bastion/legal`, which the replica holds from its start (`Server.Legal`), at `/ui/data/v1/legal` (R-BAS-118), while `gui` is on,
  also while the replica holds no catalogue yet, and links them in its footer
  ([H-2304](#h-2304--a-bastion-serves-its-imprint-and-privacy-notice-only-with-its-web-interface)).
- **Imports.** `internal/bastion/legal` imports `internal/packages/readme` and `internal/legaltext` by a scoped allowance of the
  architecture test ([Q-BAS-341](#q-bas-341--the-bastion-renders-with-the-readme-renderer-through-a-scoped-allowance)); neither
  imports a package of this module, so they bring nothing of the main installation into the role (R-BAS-001).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([legal_test.go](../../internal/bastion/legal/legal_test.go), milliseconds, an imprint of a kilobyte): a script, a style, an
  SVG, a frame, an event handler and a `javascript:` link are dropped; an image of another site is a link, one of the Bastion's origin
  is gone; the address block, the table and the three kinds of link stay; the German locale shows the English text marked `en`.
- Unit ([server_test.go](../../internal/bastion/server/server_test.go), a second): a replica started with a German imprint holds it
  for both locales, `/ui/data/v1/legal` answers them, and `/api/v1/legal` answers `404 not_found`
  (`TestR_BAS_100_TheLegalPagesAreRenderedAtStartAndServedByTheWebInterface`).
- Configuration ([ui_test.go](../../internal/config/ui_test.go)): the role takes `ui.legal`, refuses a text above 64 KiB naming the
  key, and refuses `ui.readme` as a key of another section
  ([bastion_role_test.go](../../internal/config/bastion_role_test.go)).
- Chart ([legal_test.go](../../test/chart/legal_test.go)): the texts reach the configuration file as given, a new text rolls the pods,
  and the values schema refuses a text above 64 KiB.
- Architecture ([bastion_test.go](../../internal/archtest/bastion_test.go)): the renderer and the language rule are allowed in
  `internal/bastion/legal` only, and an import of a module package by the renderer would be named.

## The public catalogue: the wire of the Bastion's web interface

W-35, the owner's answers of 2026-11-26, 11:51 to its working paper: "über die Hauptinstanz kann ich die GUI vom Bastion aktivieren um dem
Nutzer zum Beispiel verfügbare Public-Images und die gefundenen Vulnerabilities anzuzeigen" (Q-BAS-14 revised). A Bastion's read-only web
interface for anonymous visitors is served from a public catalogue that the main installation builds per registration and the Bastion
mirrors whole, so that no page view reaches the main installation. This section is the catalogue's wire, built with the interface
version 8 by W-35's package P5 together with E7 ([ADR-303](../decisions.md#adr-303--the-public-catalogue-travels-on-the-bastion-interface-as-compressed-documents-under-a-change-list));
the builder (P6), the store and sync at the Bastion (P7) and the pages (P9 to P11) follow it.

### R-BAS-101 · The catalogue's routes: a change list, documents and the public set
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The priority is the one of R-BAS-100, the other requirement of W-35's web interface on this page.

- **Routes** of the Bastion interface (R-BAS-008), with the Bastion token as `Authorization: Bearer` and nothing else
  ([Q-BAS-350](#q-bas-350--the-catalogue-routes-answer-the-bastion-token-alone-by-the-registrations-switches)):

| Route | Answers | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/bastion/catalogue?after=<seq>&limit=<n>` | the changes after the cursor `after` (0 for the start), at most `limit`, clamped to the main installation's page | `iface.CatalogueChanges` |
| `GET /api/v1/bastion/catalogue/document?path=<path>` | one document, gzip-compressed, `application/gzip`, the SHA-256 of its raw bytes as the `ETag` | the document's bytes |
| `POST /api/v1/bastion/catalogue/documents` `{"paths": [...]}` | several documents in one answer of frames, `application/vnd.quader.catalogue-batch` ([Q-BAS-347](#q-bas-347--the-batch-read-answers-frames-of-a-json-line-and-the-compressed-bytes)) | `iface.CatalogueBatch`, `iface.CatalogueFrame` |
| `GET /api/v1/bastion/catalogue/public` | the public set: the projects (key, display name, description; R-BAS-128) and the repositories (name, format, class, description, whether the wiki is public; R-BAS-130) the catalogue shows | `iface.CataloguePublic` |

- **The change list.** Every entry names a document path (R-BAS-103), its `sha256` and `size`, or `deleted`, and a `seq` above the cursor and
  above the entry before it; `cursor` is the last `seq` answered, `more` says the limit cut the answer, and `reset` that the cursor is no
  longer valid (the catalogue was rebuilt, a restore reset it): the Bastion reads the list again from 0 and keeps serving what it holds
  (`CatalogueChanges.Validate`).
- **Compression and the address** ([Q-BAS-346](#q-bas-346--a-document-travels-gzip-compressed-and-is-addressed-by-its-raw-bytes)). A document travels and is kept gzip-compressed, each document compressed alone.
  Its `sha256` and `size`, in an entry, in a frame and in the single read's `ETag`, are those of the raw bytes: a document's address does
  not change with the compressor. The Bastion decompresses what it receives, to at most the size it was told, and verifies the SHA-256
  before it keeps the compressed bytes.
- **The batch read** ([Q-BAS-347](#q-bas-347--the-batch-read-answers-frames-of-a-json-line-and-the-compressed-bytes)). One to `cataloguebounds.BatchMaxPaths` paths of the grammar, none twice (else `400`). The
  answer holds one frame per path in the request's order: a line of JSON (`path`, `sha256`, `size`, `gzipSize`, `missing`) and the
  document's `gzipSize` compressed bytes; a path the catalogue does not hold, or a documentation path while `docs` is off, is a frame
  with `missing: true` and no bytes. The main installation stops before the frame that would take the answer's compressed bytes above
  `cataloguebounds.BatchMaxBytes`, and answers at least one frame; the Bastion asks again for the paths the answer did not reach.
- **The feed** ([Q-BAS-349](#q-bas-349--a-catalogue-entry-of-the-feed-names-no-registration-and-neither-does-a-configuration-change)). A change of the catalogue writes a feed entry of the kind `catalogue` (R-BAS-015), which names no
  registration: every Bastion whose web interface is on reads its change list at once instead of at its next poll. A change of `gui`,
  `docs` or `hideRepositories` is a change of the configuration and travels as `settings` (R-BAS-093).
- **The bounds** ([Q-BAS-345](#q-bas-345--the-catalogues-bounds-are-figures-outside-the-interfaces-shape)) are figures of `internal/bastion/cataloguebounds`, outside the interface's shape, set from the
  measurement of the catalogue's size of 2026-11-26 ([developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md)): a change list's page of 5,000
  entries without a limit and 10,000 at most, a batch of 5,000 paths and 8 MiB of compressed bytes, a document of 16 MiB raw at most.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P5 with E7), the wire and the routes:* [catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/catalogue.go),
[bounds.go](../../internal/bastion/cataloguebounds/bounds.go), [bastion_catalogue_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_catalogue_api.go)
and the four operations of the OpenAPI tag `bastion`. *Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6):* the routes serve what the builder keeps
(R-BAS-104 to R-BAS-108): the change list after the cursor with `reset` for a cursor the catalogue does not continue, a document with the
SHA-256 of its raw bytes as its `ETag`, the batch's frames up to the bound, and the public set of the last build. *Built on 2026-11-26
(W-35's P7):* the reads of the change list, the public set and the batch at the Bastion, paced in the throughput's class `catalogue`
([catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/mainclient/catalogue.go), R-BAS-109), and what a Bastion does with an entry of the kind `catalogue`
(R-BAS-112). *Not built:* the writer of the feed kind `catalogue` at the main installation
([Q-BAS-369](#q-bas-369--the-builder-writes-no-feed-entry-yet-a-bastion-learns-a-change-at-its-poll), kept by
[Q-BAS-378](#q-bas-378--no-feed-entry-of-the-kind-catalogue-the-follow-up-round-after-the-builders-debounce-carries-a-change)).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/iface`): the change list's order and cursor, the frames written and read back with their bounds, a batch of
  one to the bound of paths (`TestR_BAS_101_TheCatalogueChangeListHoldsItsOrder`, `TestR_BAS_101_TheBatchReadIsFramed`).
- Unit (`internal/api/v1`): the four routes answer by the switches and as the grammar says
  (`TestR_BAS_102_TheCatalogueRoutesAnswerByTheSwitches`), and serve the kept documents (`TestR_BAS_101_TheCatalogueRoutesServeTheKeptDocuments`,
  `TestR_BAS_101_TheBatchStopsAtItsBound`).

### R-BAS-102 · The switches gui and docs
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

A third switch of the web interface, `hideRepositories`, is R-BAS-131's; it is effective only with `gui`, as `docs` is.

- `switches.gui` and `switches.docs` are members of the registration's configuration (R-BAS-093), set on the card in its section **Web
  interface** in plain view (R-UI-240, [Q-UI-1616](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1616--a-bastions-web-interface-is-a-section-of-the-cards-plain-view-not-a-detail-of-its-limits)), off for a new
  registration, delivered with the handshake and changed by a `settings` entry of the feed in about 3 s.
- **gui** switches the Bastion's web interface: while it is off, every catalogue route answers `404 not_found` and the Bastion serves no
  page (its pages answer `404` as every path outside the package families does, R-BAS-003), stops its sync, makes its `catalogue/` tree
  unreadable and lets the sweep delete it; the main installation deletes the registration's catalogue (P6, P7, P9).
- **docs** switches the documentation of the web interface, and is effective only with `gui`: while it is off, a documentation path of the
  grammar (`CataloguePath.Documentation`: the README, the docs tree, its entries and files) answers `404 not_found` on the single read and
  is a missing frame of a batch, and the builder builds none (R-BAS-124).
- The token reads only its own registration's catalogue: the routes take the registration from the recognition of the token, never from
  the request ([Q-BAS-350](#q-bas-350--the-catalogue-routes-answer-the-bastion-token-alone-by-the-registrations-switches)).

*Built on 2026-11-26 (P5 with E7):* the switches on the wire and the routes' answers by them. *Built by E8:* the switches are members of
the registration, off for a new one, set by `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/{name}` with `switches.gui` and `switches.docs` (`endpoints:write`).
*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6):* at the builder, which reads the
stored switches: `gui` on builds the registration's catalogue, off drops it at the next run, `docs` off
builds no documentation and deletes what was built (R-BAS-104, R-BAS-108; `TestR_BAS_102_TheSwitchesDecideWhatIsBuilt`). *Built by E12
(2026-11-26):* the switches on the card, each with its sentence (R-UI-240). *Not built:* the pages the switches start and stop (P9).
*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7):* at the Bastion: `gui` on starts the sync, off makes the catalogue unreadable at once and deletes its
tree; `docs` off hides the documentation at once (R-BAS-112). *Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P11):* the documentation by `docs` and the
wiki at the builder, at the data path and on the pages (R-BAS-124 to R-BAS-126). *Built on 2026-11-27 (W35-P9f):* a change of a
switch starts the builder's run within its debounce (the change area `bastion_configuration`, R-BAS-105), so the first catalogue follows
the switch within seconds and `gui` off deletes the catalogue then. *Since 2026-11-27 (W-39,
[api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1621--a-bastions-main-settings-are-rows-of-name-and-control-a-reader-reads-the-word) Q-UI-1621):*
the switches are the card's first two setting rows, **Web interface** and **Documentation**, each with its help behind the info sign; a
reader reads **On** or **Off**; the line that documentation on does nothing while the web interface is off is gone (the two rows say it).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/api/v1`, `TestR_BAS_102_TheCatalogueRoutesAnswerByTheSwitches`, 0.2 s, no data): with `gui` off the four routes answer
  `404 not_found`; with it on and `docs` off a documentation path answers `404` and names the documentation.
- Unit ([wire_bastion_catalogue_test.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion_catalogue_test.go),
  `TestR_BAS_102_SwitchingTheWebInterfaceOnStartsTheBuilder`, 0.1 s, no data): a change of `bastion_configuration` starts a run, also
  right after the trigger answered that no web interface is on.

### R-BAS-103 · The grammar of a document's path
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

A document of the catalogue is named by a path of this grammar (`iface.CataloguePath`, `ParseCataloguePath`; [Q-BAS-348](#q-bas-348--a-document-path-is-canonical-segment-by-segment-and-names-packages-by-their-catalogue-id)):

| Path | Document |
|---|---|
| `index/<n>` | a page of the index of public packages |
| `projects/<project>/index/<n>` | a page of the index of one project's public packages, the project's own counts (R-BAS-130) |
| `repositories/<project>/<repo>/index/<n>` | a page of the index of one repository's public packages, the repository's own counts; only while the repositories are shown (R-BAS-130, R-BAS-131) |
| `packages/<id>` | a package (`<id>` is the package's catalogue ID) |
| `packages/<id>/versions` | its versions list |
| `packages/<id>/vulnerabilities` | its open findings per version: each version's grade and counts (R-BAS-128) |
| `packages/<id>/images` | an image's list by content: one entry per manifest, led by its highest tag, the other tags as `aliases` (R-BAS-130) |
| `packages/<id>/versions/<v>` | a version |
| `packages/<id>/versions/<v>/readme`, `…/vulnerabilities`, `…/signatures`, `…/contents`, `…/docs` | the version's README, open findings, signatures, contents and docs tree |
| `packages/<id>/versions/<v>/docs/entries/<type>/<name>` | an entry of the docs tree |
| `packages/<id>/versions/<v>/docs/files/<file...>` | a file of the docs tree |
| `packages/<id>/versions/<v>/state` | the times of the version's documents (built, checked, scanned) |
| `state` | the catalogue's state (`iface.CatalogueStateDocument`): the time of the last run that changed a document, today's signatures of the malware scan ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-042) and today's vulnerability database of the image scanning ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-052) |
| `setup/<project>/<repo>/<client>[/<id>[/<v>]]` | the client set-up of a repository, of a package without a version (an image's, the pull by digest; R-BAS-130), or of a package's version (by the package's catalogue ID) |
| `files/<project>/<repo>/folder[/<path...>]` | a folder's listing of a generic repository (the root without a path) |
| `files/<project>/<repo>/file/<path...>` | a generic file's description |
| `files/<project>/<repo>/setup/<client>/<path...>` | a generic file's set-up per client |
| `signatures/objects/<sha256>` | a signature's original (64 lowercase hex) |
| `signing/trusted-root.json`, `signing/chain.pem` | the anchors to verify signatures offline |

- **One spelling.** A path is written segment by segment; every byte of a value outside the unreserved characters of RFC 3986
  (`A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~`) is `%XX` with upper-case hex, and the parser refuses every other spelling: an unreserved character encoded, a
  lower-case hex digit, a `%` without two digits. So a document has exactly one path, and the writer and the parser are each other's inverse.
- **What no value holds.** No value contains `/` (an encoded slash is refused), none is `.` or `..`, none is empty, and each is valid UTF-8
  of at most 512 bytes without a control character; a path is at most 4 KiB. A name that holds a `/`, as npm's scoped names do, is never a
  segment: packages are named by their catalogue ID, and a generic file's path is one segment per path segment. A generic file whose name
  holds a control character or invalid UTF-8 has no path and is not in the catalogue; the builder skips it (P6).
- **Times are not content** (a duty of the builder, P6; [Q-BAS-348](#q-bas-348--a-document-path-is-canonical-segment-by-segment-and-names-packages-by-their-catalogue-id)): a document carries no time of its building or checking
  (`builtAt`, `checkedAt`, `syncedAt`, `scannedAt` and the like). Those times go into the version's `state` document or the catalogue's
  `state`, so that a document changes only with its content: measured on 2026-11-26, every npm vulnerabilities document changed every 15
  minutes with nothing published, and 14,200 Ansible entries were 14,200 distinct documents where 1,264 were left without the time
  fields.
- **Nor what a new signature set or a download changes of a malware state** ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-039,
  Q-MAL-133; revised on 2026-11-26 by W-36's P3): a malware member's `engine`, `scannerInstance`, `age`, `pressure`, `due`,
  `nextCheckInDays`, `downloadsSince` and `currentFiles` are dropped from every document, and its `decidedBy` moves into the version's
  `state` with the check's `scannedAt`, `database` and `databaseBuiltAt`: the engine and the replica are facts of the main installation's
  infrastructure, the rest changes with every set and carries a trace of demand (Q-BAS-358).
- **Nor the database or the analyser's version of a grade** ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-051,
  Q-VULN-296; W-36's P7): a grade's `database` moves into the version's `state` with its `checkedAt`, as a scanned manifest's does with
  its `scannedAt`, since it changes with every rescan under a new database; `scannerVersion` is dropped from every document, as a malware
  state's `engine` is ([H-2407](#h-2407--a-bastions-grade-in-a-list-says-nothing-of-when-and-against-which-database-it-was-checked)).

*Built on 2026-11-26 (P5 with E7):* the grammar as pure functions. *Built on 2026-11-26 (P6):* the builder's documents and its duty
above: every time member goes into the version's state by JSON pointer (R-BAS-106, Q-BAS-359; `TestR_BAS_103_NoDocumentCarriesATimeOfItsCheck`).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit (`internal/bastion/iface`, `TestR_BAS_103_TheCataloguePathGrammarRoundTrips`, milliseconds): every form is written and read back to
  the same value, `+`, `:`, a space, `%`, `?` and non-ASCII letters round-trip, and dot segments, encoded slashes in either case, empty
  segments, other spellings and unknown forms are refused; the forms of the project view (a project's and a repository's index, an image's
  list by content, a package's set-up without a version) among them.

## The builder of the public catalogue

W-35's package P6: the main installation builds, for every registration whose web interface is on (R-BAS-102), the catalogue the routes
of R-BAS-101 serve. The documents are the main installation's anonymous answers (W-35's B.2), stripped of internal identities and
infrastructure (B.10), with every link on the Bastion (B.13), and without a time of their building or checking (R-BAS-103). The Bastion's
side, which mirrors them (P7), and the pages (P9 to P11) follow.

### R-BAS-104 · The builder renders the anonymous answers on the Bastion's base URL
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The priority is the one of R-BAS-101 to R-BAS-103.

- **What it reads.** The builder reads the management API's own reads through its router and handlers, with the declarations of R-API-058
  and the decision point, as the anonymous caller of the default endpoint, outside the edge chain: no limit, no request log, no usage record
  (the renderer of `internal/app/wire_bastion_catalogue.go`, [Q-BAS-355](#q-bas-355--the-builder-is-the-workers-job-and-reads-the-management-api-through-a-router-of-its-own)).
  What an anonymous visitor reads through the default endpoint is what the catalogue shows, and nothing else: every public repository of
  every class, public remotes included, the open findings of P3's anonymous answer.
- **The default endpoint refuses anonymous requests.** The renderer's chain has no authentication stage, so the builder applies the
  default endpoint's `auth.anonymous` itself, as the handshake's `anonymousReads` does (R-BAS-019): while it is `false` (explicitly, or
  because the listener requires a client certificate, R-EP-010) an anonymous visitor reads nothing there, and the builder builds nothing
  for any registration. It empties a registration's catalogue once (its rows and state go, and the state it records starts its numbers
  above every number before, so a Bastion's cursor answers `reset` and its copy empties at its next round, R-BAS-108) and records
  `anonymous_requests_refused` in the state for the registration's card; a later run leaves it as it is. The setting is the configuration
  file's and applies when a replica starts; a replica that claims jobs starts a run then when the stored state differs from what a run
  would leave (R-BAS-105), so opening the endpoint again builds the catalogues within seconds of the restart
  ([Q-BAS-495](#q-bas-495--while-the-default-endpoint-refuses-anonymous-requests-every-catalogue-is-empty-with-its-reason)).
- **The base URL.** A registration's documents are rendered on the base URL it reported at its last handshake, provided it is an entry of
  `server.additional_base_urls` (the rule of client-setup with `bastion=<name>`, R-BAS-007, `catalogue.BaseURL`); a registration that
  reported none, or one the installation does not list, is not built: the builder records `bastion_base_url_unknown` in its state for the
  registration's card and keeps what it built before. A disabled registration builds nothing.
- **The outcome on the registration.** `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` and the list carry the member `catalogue`, the builder's last
  outcome read from its state: `built`, `stopped` with its `reason` (`bastion_base_url_unknown`, `anonymous_requests_refused`), or
  `pending` while no run completed, with the times of the last run (`checkedAt`) and of the last run that changed the catalogue
  (`builtAt`); null while the builder holds no state for the registration. The card says it in words, a stop's reason with what to do
  in plain view (R-UI-240, [Q-BAS-497](#q-bas-497--the-registration-carries-the-builders-last-outcome-and-the-card-says-a-stop-in-plain-view)).
- **What it builds, per format** (W-35's section C; W-40's section 2): the index of public packages (`index/<n>`, pages of 100 in the
  list's order, name), the index of every project and, while the repositories are shown, of every repository of the public set, each
  the main installation's answer with the scope (R-BAS-130),
  per package its summary, its versions and its open findings per version (R-BAS-128), per version the version, its README (`docs` on and a public wiki, R-BAS-124), its open findings, its signatures, the
  Debian contents (the changelog and the copyright only with `docs` on), the Ansible documentation tree with every entry that has
  documentation and every file (`docs` on), the set-up of every client of the format for the version in every public repository that
  holds it ([Q-BAS-502](#q-bas-502--a-versions-set-up-is-built-in-every-public-repository-that-holds-it)), and its state; per image its
  list by content and its set-up without a version per holder and client (R-BAS-130); per public repository the set-up of every
  client; per generic repository (a format whose items are paths) every folder's
  listing, every file's description and its set-up per client; the signature objects the signatures name; `signing/trusted-root.json` and
  `signing/chain.pem` where the installation has a signing identity; and the catalogue's `state` with today's malware signatures
  ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-042). A set-up is rendered with
  `credentials=none` and `bastion=<name>`: the Bastion's addresses, no login line, no publish snippet; an OCI repository's Docker, Podman
  and Helm set-ups have no configure snippet at all, since a public image pulls without a login and a Bastion takes no push
  ([Q-OCI-277](formats/oci.md#q-oci-277--a-bastions-set-up-of-a-public-image-repository-has-no-login)). The public set of the routes is the
  projects and repositories the anonymous caller lists, with the wiki public where the repository's wiki level is `public`, each
  project with the display name and the description the anonymous caller reads (R-BAS-128), and each repository with its description,
  its links rewritten (R-BAS-130).
- **Bounds.** A document above `cataloguebounds.DocumentMaxBytes` is left out and named in its version's state (`omitted`); a path the
  grammar does not admit (a generic file's name with a control character) is left out (R-BAS-103).

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6):* [builder.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/builder.go),

integration suite may set them instead (`app.Options.BastionSwitches`, tests only). *Built on 2026-11-27 (W35-P9f, H-2330):* the default

[bastion_registrations_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_registrations_api.go)) and the card's lines.

### R-BAS-105 · When the builder runs: triggers, the hourly reconciliation by fingerprints
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The job.** `bastion-catalogue`, on the queue `default`, in the Coalesce mode with one key: one run at a time in the installation, and
  the changes that arrive during a run wait as the one job behind it. A replica that claims jobs (`worker`, `all`) runs it; it renders the
  packages of a registration with four workers in parallel.
- **Triggers.** A run starts 5 s after a change that can change a catalogue (the debounce: one publish arrives as several signals and change
  areas): the signals `metadata_changed`, `malware_verdict` and `signature_verdict`, and the change areas `repo_config`, `authz`,
  `vuln_data`, `malware_database` and `malware_settings` (a new signature set in use and a change of the rescan settings, which change
  the catalogue's state, [Q-BAS-491](#q-bas-491--a-new-set-and-a-change-of-the-rescan-settings-start-the-builder-and-only-the-state-changes)),
  and `bastion_configuration`, which a change of a registration's switches `gui`, `docs` and `hideRepositories` raises (R-BAS-102,
  R-BAS-131): switching the web interface
  on builds its first catalogue within the debounce and a run, off deletes it, without waiting for the hourly run. That change also drops
  the trigger's cached answer to whether some web interface is on, since the switch it carries may be what turned one on. And the signal
  `bastion_base_url`, which a Bastion's contact raises when it brings the registration a base URL the builder does not read yet (R-BAS-010):
  a Bastion that first connects after its web interface was switched on, or whose base URL changed, has its catalogue built within seconds
  of that contact ([Q-BAS-499](#q-bas-499--a-contact-that-brings-a-new-base-url-starts-the-builder-through-a-signal)).
  A replica enqueues only while some registration's web interface is on or some registration still holds a catalogue, so an
  installation without one queues nothing ([Q-BAS-361](#q-bas-361--every-change-starts-the-same-run-after-5-s-and-the-hourly-run-is-the-reconciliation)).
- **At a start.** What a run reads of the configuration file (the default endpoint's `auth.anonymous`, `server.additional_base_urls`)
  changes only with a restart, which no trigger hears. A replica that claims jobs therefore compares, once when it starts, the stored
  state of every registration with what a run would leave (`Builder.Drift`: a catalogue to build or to drop, a stop reason that no longer
  holds or newly does, a base URL that moved) and starts a run when they differ, none when they agree
  ([Q-BAS-496](#q-bas-496--a-replica-that-claims-jobs-starts-a-run-at-its-start-only-when-the-store-differs-from-what-a-run-would-leave)).
- **The reconciliation.** The task `bastion-catalogue` runs the same job every hour (`41 * * * *`, `maintenance.tasks.bastion-catalogue`,
  R-OPS-019), so a change a trigger missed stays at most an hour. A run renders only what changed: a unit (a package, a generic repository)
  is rendered again only when its fingerprint differs from the one it was rendered at. The fingerprint is read from the database in one
  statement per run, not rendered: the package's revision and versions, its findings (status, severity, what the page shows of them), its
  files' verdicts and releases, the Debian contents' state, its signatures with their trust, the Ansible documentation built for it, and its
  image scans' outcome, never a time of a check; with the package's index entry and a salt of what changes every document at once (the
  public set, `docs`, the base URL, the README renderer's policy, the builder's revision). The documents of the registration as a whole
  (the index, the set-up per repository, the anchors, the signature objects, the state) are rendered in every run and written only where
  their bytes changed ([Q-BAS-360](#q-bas-360--a-unit-is-rendered-again-only-when-its-fingerprint-of-database-facts-changed)).
- **Writing.** A document is written only when its bytes changed; a path the unit no longer has is marked deleted; a unit gone from the index
  is deleted whole. A run that changed nothing writes nothing.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6):* [builder.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/builder.go),
[wire_bastion_catalogue.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion_catalogue.go), the statements `BastionCataloguePackageFacts` and
`BastionCatalogueRepositoryFacts` of [bastion_catalogue.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/bastion_catalogue.sql). *Not built:* the
feed entry of the kind `catalogue` (R-BAS-101): a Bastion learns of a change at its poll or at the round it runs after the builder's

[H-2314](../security/bastion.md#h-2314--a-narrowing-reaches-a-bastions-pages-only-at-its-next-poll-after-the-run)). *Built on 2026-11-27
(W35-P9f):* the run at a start (`Builder.Drift`, the trigger's `drift`); the change area `bastion_configuration` among the triggers.
*Built on 2026-11-27 (batch I):* the signal `bastion_base_url` of a contact among the triggers (Q-BAS-499).

### R-BAS-106 · The strip: no internal identity, no infrastructure, no time of a check
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

Every JSON document passes the strip (`catalogue.Prepare`, W-35's B.10) before it is kept:

| Member | What the strip does |
|---|---|
| `builtAt`, `checkedAt`, `syncedAt`, `scannedAt`, `computedAt`; `database` and `databaseBuiltAt` beside `scannedAt` (a malware check) | taken out and kept in the version's state document by JSON pointer and document kind (R-BAS-103, [Q-BAS-359](#q-bas-359--the-times-of-a-check-go-into-the-versions-state-by-json-pointer)) |
| `downloadCount`, `downloads`, `lastDownloadAt`, `lastDownloadedAt` | taken out ([Q-BAS-358](#q-bas-358--no-document-carries-a-download-count)) |
| `releasedBy` | `null` |
| `origin` of a signature | `kind` and `at` stay; `principalKind`, `principalName` and the CI job's claims (`ci`) go; `upstreamUrl` only as below |
| `upstreamUrl`, `fetchedFrom` | stays only when its host is one of the formats' well-known public registries (the remote presets: Docker Hub, Quay, ghcr.io, GitLab, npmjs.com, nuget.org, Galaxy, …), `null` otherwise |
| a trust anchor (`id`, `title`, `scope`) | `title` goes unless `scope` is `shipped`; the state words stay |
| `statusChangedBy`, `triagedBy`, `comment`, `history`, `dismissalReason`, `resolvedReason`, `stateCode` | taken out (P3's anonymous answer carries none already) |
| a value that is a principal's reference (`user:…`, `sa:…`, `ci:…`, `bastion:…`), such as npm's publisher of a version published to a local repository | `null` ([Q-BAS-364](#q-bas-364--a-principals-reference-is-no-value)) |
| `nextCursor` of a list | taken out |

The members of a document are written in name order. A Debian package's contents carry no changelog or copyright while `docs` is off.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6):* [prepare.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/prepare.go).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: `TestR_BAS_106_NoDocumentNamesAnInternalIdentityOrTheMainInstallation` (who uploaded, released and triaged, an internal anchor's
  title, a state code, a download count, an upstream that is no public registry: none in any document; the shipped anchor's title and the
  state stay), `TestR_BAS_103_NoDocumentCarriesATimeOfItsCheck` (no time member in any document but the state documents, which hold them by
  pointer), milliseconds.

### R-BAS-107 · Links on the Bastion's base URL and its data path
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The rule of B.13 for what the builder writes:

- An absolute link is rendered on the Bastion's base URL (R-BAS-104). An occurrence of the main installation's own origins in any text
  (`server.base_url`, every entry of `server.additional_base_urls`, every further endpoint's base URL) becomes the registration's base URL,
  in author content too ([Q-BAS-365](#q-bas-365--an-origin-of-the-main-installation-in-any-text-becomes-the-bastions-base-url)).
- A value that is a link of the management API (`/api/v1/…`, relative or on one of those origins) becomes the Bastion's data path
  `/ui/data/v1/…` where the catalogue holds what it names (a signature object, the signing anchors), and `null` where it does not
  ([Q-BAS-363](#q-bas-363--a-link-of-the-management-api-is-the-bastions-data-path-only-where-the-catalogue-holds-it)).
  Inside text (a README's HTML) `/api/v1/` becomes `/ui/data/v1/`.
- A version's file (`PackageFile`) downloads through the Bastion's package routes: its `contentUrl`, the content route only the main
  installation serves, becomes the path of its `downloadUrl` on the Bastion's base URL (`/api/npm/<project>/<repo>/…`, `/files/…`,
  `/v2/…`), which a page's download link takes; a `downloadUrl` on another origin leaves it `null`
  ([Q-BAS-398](#q-bas-398--a-versions-file-downloads-through-the-bastions-package-route)).
- A link of another host (a package's homepage, its repository) stays: public content, readable by pulling the artifact.
- Text answers (a PEM chain) have their links rewritten the same way; bytes that are no text (a signature object) are kept as they are.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6; a file's download through the package route by W-35's P9b):*
[prepare.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/prepare.go).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: `TestR_BAS_107_LinksAreTheBastionsAndItsDataPath`, milliseconds (a file's `contentUrl` the package route's path, and `null` for a
  `downloadUrl` on another origin).
- Integration: every document of `TestR_BAS_104_TheCatalogueFollowsPublishesLevelsAndTheSwitch` is scanned for the main installation's
  base URL, the other entry of `server.additional_base_urls` and `/api/v1/`; `walkWebInterface` of
  `TestR_BAS_109_TheBastionMirrorsTheCatalogueAndServesOnWhileTheLinkIsCut` follows the version page's `contentUrl` through the Bastion's
  client listener without a credential and receives the file of its SHA-256.

### R-BAS-108 · The catalogue's tables: derived, deduplicated, and a reset after a restore
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Tables** (migration 00146, [database.md](../developer/database.md)): `bastion_catalogue` (a registration's change list: path, unit,
  the document's SHA-256 and size or deleted, the change's number), `bastion_catalogue_document` (a document's bytes gzip-compressed once
  for every registration and path that holds the same bytes, addressed by the SHA-256 of the raw bytes), `bastion_catalogue_state` (the
  range of the numbers, the salt, the base URL, why the builder stopped (`bastion_base_url_unknown` or, since migration 00155,
  `anonymous_requests_refused`, R-BAS-104), the public set, the times of the last runs) and
  `bastion_catalogue_unit` (each unit's fingerprint and the signature objects it names). The routes read the documents the builder kept;
  a read renders nothing ([Q-BAS-356](#q-bas-356--the-main-installation-keeps-every-document-compressed-once-per-content)).
- **Numbers.** A run reserves a block of the registration's numbers on its state row in the transaction that writes the rows, so the
  transactions of one registration commit in the order of their numbers and a reader never sees a number below one that arrived later.
  The numbers of a catalogue start at the clock in microseconds when its state is created, above every number a catalogue of the
  registration handed out before: a cursor below a catalogue's first number or above its last answers `reset`
  ([Q-BAS-366](#q-bas-366--a-catalogues-numbers-start-at-the-clock-so-a-cursor-of-an-earlier-one-answers-reset)). A change list read from
  the start leaves the deleted paths out.
- **Derived data.** The four tables are transient for a backup (R-BAK-004): a restored installation holds no catalogue, builds it again at
  the next run, and a Bastion's cursor answers `reset`. `gui` off deletes the registration's rows, units and state at the next run; the
  documents no row names are deleted at the end of every run. A registration deleted takes its rows with it.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P6):* [00146_bastion_catalogue.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00146_bastion_catalogue.sql),
[store.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/store.go), [tables_bastion.go](../../internal/meta/postgres/tables_bastion.go),
[bastion_catalogue_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_catalogue_api.go).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: `TestR_BAS_108_ACatalogueBuiltAgainAnswersReset` (the in-memory store of `cataloguetest`, which keeps the PostgreSQL store's rules),
  `TestR_BAS_101_TheCatalogueRoutesServeTheKeptDocuments`, `TestR_BAS_101_TheBatchStopsAtItsBound` (`internal/api/v1`), milliseconds.
- Integration: the end of `TestR_BAS_104_TheCatalogueFollowsPublishesLevelsAndTheSwitch`: a catalogue switched off and on answers the
  cursor of the one before with `reset`, on PostgreSQL.

## The public catalogue at the Bastion

W-35's package P7: a Bastion replica mirrors its registration's public catalogue (R-BAS-101 to R-BAS-108) into its cache backend and
serves the web interface's reads from it alone, so that no page view reaches the main installation (W-35's B.2), and serves on with its
age while the main installation cannot be reached (the owner's B.2b). The pages themselves are W-35's P9; this section is the sync, the
store, the age, the feed's hooks and the reader they read. The package is [internal/bastion/catalogue](../../internal/bastion/catalogue).

### R-BAS-109 · The sync: the change list, the documents by batch, verified, and one replica of a shared bucket
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The priority is the one of R-BAS-101 to R-BAS-108.

- **A round.** While the switch `gui` is on (R-BAS-102) a replica runs a round every `bastion.gui.poll_interval` (10 s) and whenever the
  feed wakes it (R-BAS-112): it reads the public set; it reads the change list from its cursor to the end, page by page; it reads the
  documents the list names that its store does not hold, one path of each, in batches of at most `cataloguebounds.BatchMaxPaths` paths,
  asking again for the paths an answer did not reach; it builds the index from the pages `index/<n>`; it swaps the new state in and keeps
  it (R-BAS-110). A round that completed is the replica's confirmation: its time is `confirmedAt` (R-BAS-111).
- **Verification** ([Q-BAS-372](#q-bas-372--a-document-that-does-not-verify-fails-the-round-a-missing-frame-takes-its-path-out)). Each
  document is decompressed to at most the size its frame names and held to the SHA-256 of its raw bytes before it is kept (R-BAS-101). One
  that does not verify is not kept and fails the round; what the round fetched before stays in the store, so the next round asks only for
  what is left. A frame that is missing takes its path out of the state (the catalogue no longer holds it; its deletion follows in the
  list); a frame that names newer bytes for its path gives the path those.
- **A reset** (R-BAS-108). An answer with `reset` makes the round read the list from 0 into a state of its own; the old state is served,
  with its `confirmedAt`, until the new one is complete and swapped in, and nothing of the old one stays that the new catalogue does not hold.
- **Throughput and budget** ([Q-BAS-381](#q-bas-381--the-syncs-reads-take-no-slot-are-paced-in-their-class-and-are-bounded-by-the-sync)).
  Every body of the sync is read through the throughput's class `catalogue` (R-BAS-097, `Pacer.CatalogueReader`), from the total only and
  below the callers' misses, and nothing else reads a catalogue body. The reads take no slot of the budget (R-BAS-025), as the handshake and
  the feed do, and are counted as `kind="catalogue"` of `quader_bastion_main_requests_total`; each read is bounded by two minutes, since a
  paced batch of megabytes may take longer than an answer of the interface may.
- **One replica of a shared bucket** ([Q-BAS-371](#q-bas-371--with-a-bucket-and-valkey-a-lease-lets-one-replica-sync-the-others-take-its-state)).
  With the bucket backend and Valkey a lease (`catalogue` in the Bastion's keyspace, three poll intervals) lets one replica sync; the
  others take the state it wrote at their turn when it is ahead of theirs or confirmed later. Without Valkey, and while it is unavailable,
  every replica syncs, which is safe: the documents are content-addressed and the state record is one object, and a replica takes the
  stored record before its round when the record's cursor is ahead of its own. With the volume backend each replica syncs its own volume.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7):* [sync.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/sync.go),
[catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/mainclient/catalogue.go) of the client, the lease `AcquireCatalogue` of
[valkey_bastion.go](../../internal/cluster/valkey_bastion.go) and `State.CatalogueLease` of the shared state.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([catalogue_test.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/catalogue_test.go), against maintest's catalogue, which keeps the builder's
  rules of R-BAS-108): `TestR_BAS_109_ARoundMirrorsTheCatalogueAndReadsOnlyWhatChanged` (a round serves every document verified, a round
  with nothing new reads no document, a new and a deleted document arrive at the next round),
  `TestR_BAS_109_AResetKeepsTheOldStateServedUntilTheNewOneIsComplete`, `TestR_BAS_109_AReplicaOfASharedStoreTakesTheStateAnotherWrote`;
  ([throughput_test.go](../../internal/bastion/mainclient/throughput_test.go))
  `TestR_BAS_109_TheCatalogueReadsArePacedInTheirClassAndTakeNoSlot`. Milliseconds, documents of bytes.
- Integration (area `bastion`, [catalogue_sync_test.go](../../test/integration/bastion/catalogue_sync_test.go), the role all with the
