### R-BAS-110 · The store: a tree of the cache backend with a share of its own, a signed state, a sweep
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The tree.** The documents are kept gzip-compressed, as they travel, by the SHA-256 of their raw bytes in the catalogue's tree of the
  cache backend: `catalogue/documents/<h0h1>/<h2h3>/<64 hex>`, with a cache key (R-BAS-061) objects of the stored format below
  `bc-<id>/g/` under keyed names. A document many paths hold (an Ansible entry over many versions) is kept once.
- **The manifest and the state record** ([Q-BAS-373](#q-bas-373--which-path-holds-which-document-is-a-manifest-of-256-shards-by-unit)).
  Which path holds which document is a manifest of 256 shards, each a document of the same tree, a path's shard chosen by its unit (a
  package, a repository's set-up, a generic repository's files), so that a change of one package rewrites one shard. The state record,
  `catalogue/state.json` (with a cache key `bc-<id>/c/catalogue`, bound to its name), names the shards, the cursor, `confirmedAt`, the
  public set and the switches; it is signed with the signing key in the domain `catalogue` where entries are signed (Q-BAS-98). It is
  written when the cursor, a shard, the public set or a switch changed, and otherwise every minute for its `confirmedAt`
  ([Q-BAS-374](#q-bas-374--the-state-record-is-written-when-it-changed-and-every-minute-for-its-time)).
- **The share** ([Q-BAS-380](#q-bas-380--the-catalogues-share-is-reserved-always-a-catalogue-above-it-is-kept-and-alerted)).
  `bastion.gui.max_bytes` (4 GiB of stored bytes, the measurement's proposal 4) is a share of `cache.max_bytes` reserved whether or not
  the web interface is on: the artifacts are limited to `max_bytes − documents_max_bytes − gui.max_bytes`, and a configuration that leaves
  them less than one `max_object_bytes` does not start and is not rendered by the chart (R-BAS-031's rule, extended). No sweep of the areas
  lists the tree, so the artifacts' and the documents' evictions never take a document of the catalogue; a catalogue above its share is kept
  and `QuaderBastionCatalogueOverBound` fires.
- **The sweep** ([Q-BAS-375](#q-bas-375--a-document-no-state-names-is-deleted-an-hour-after-it-was-written-gui-off-deletes-the-tree)). Every
  five minutes the syncing replica deletes the documents its state does not name that were written more than an hour before; the switch
  `gui` off deletes the whole tree, the state record first.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7):* [catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/catalogue.go) of the cache,
[state.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/state.go), [sync.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/sync.go), the configuration's
`bastion.gui` ([bastion_role.go](../../internal/config/bastion_role.go)) and the chart's room rule.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([catalogue_test.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/catalogue_test.go)): `TestR_BAS_110_TheCatalogueTreeIsSignedSealedAndNeverSwept`
  (plain and sealed: the tree read back, the state record signed and one changed on the volume refused, a sweep of a cache far above its
  limits leaves the tree alone and does not count it, the share comes off the artifacts' limit); configuration
  `TestR_BAS_031_ACacheWithoutRoomForOneLargestObjectIsRefused` with the catalogue's share; chart
  `TestR_BAS_030_TheSpoolFitsTheTemporaryVolume`'s case of the room with `gui.max_bytes`. Milliseconds.
- promtool: `QuaderBastionCatalogueOverBound` (R-BAS-041).

### R-BAS-111 · The age: confirmedAt, serving on without the main installation, a restart with and without a kept state
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's B.2b (2026-11-26, against the development agent's favourite of a grace period): the web interface serves on while the main
installation is unreachable and shows its state's age.

- **confirmedAt** is the time a replica last completed a round (R-BAS-109); a replica of a shared bucket that took the state another wrote
  carries that state's. The reader serves its state whatever its age; `State` answers it with `bastion.gui.stale_after` (1 h) and whether it
  is older, for the pages' "As of" and their notice band (P9). The package answers of the package API keep their grace period (R-BAS-027).
- **A start.** A replica reads the stored state before its client listener binds, after the stored configuration (Q-BAS-327). It serves a
  state it finds with the stored `confirmedAt` and, while it applies the built-in configuration, the stored switches, also while the main
  installation is unreachable. One that finds none answers not ready (`ErrNotReady`, P9's `503 not_ready`) until its first round; so does
  one that knows neither its switches nor a state: such a replica is never off
  ([Q-BAS-379](#q-bas-379--a-replica-that-knows-neither-its-switches-nor-a-state-is-not-ready-never-off)).
- **Kept.** The state survives a restart where the cache does: with the bucket backend and a persistent volume. Every handshake reports it
  in `Quader-Bastion-Catalogue-Kept` (R-BAS-010), from the backend and the chart-managed `bastion.cache.volume.persistent`, which the chart
  renders from `cacheVolume.type` ([Q-BAS-382](#q-bas-382--kept-is-the-bucket-backend-or-the-charts-word-that-the-volume-is-persistent)).
  The chart's default, the ephemeral volume, does not keep it (H-2318).
- **Gauges and alerts** (R-BAS-040, R-BAS-041): `quader_bastion_catalogue_confirmed_timestamp_seconds`,
  `quader_bastion_catalogue_stale_after_seconds` and `quader_bastion_gui_enabled`; `QuaderBastionCatalogueStale` and
  `QuaderBastionCatalogueMissing` per replica.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7):* [reader.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/reader.go), `Catalogue.Load` of
[sync.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/sync.go), the wiring of [server.go](../../internal/bastion/server/server.go), the header in the
client's handshake, the chart's `persistent` and alerts.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: `TestR_BAS_111_AStoredStateIsServedAfterARestartWithItsAge` (a replica restarted with the link cut serves the stored state with its
  `confirmedAt` and switches, stale after `stale_after` and served on; without a state or switches not ready, never off), milliseconds;
  chart `TestR_BAS_111_TheChartSaysWhetherTheCacheVolumeOutlivesItsPod`.
- Integration: `TestR_BAS_109_TheBastionMirrorsTheCatalogueAndServesOnWhileTheLinkIsCut`: with the link cut both Bastions serve with the
  `confirmedAt` of their last round; a replica of the bucket restarted during the cut serves the stored state; a replica whose volume was
  removed answers not ready.
- promtool: `QuaderBastionCatalogueStale` (the stale replica fires, the fresh one beside it does not, nothing with the web interface off),
  `QuaderBastionCatalogueMissing`.

### R-BAS-112 · The switches and the feed's hooks
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **gui and docs** (R-BAS-102). The replica applies the switches of the configuration it applies (R-BAS-093). `gui` on wakes the sync;
  `gui` off makes every read answer off at once (`ErrOff`, P9's `404 not_found`), stops the sync and deletes the catalogue's tree. `docs`
  off hides the documentation (`CataloguePath.Documentation`) at once, before the builder deletes it.
- **A disable** (R-BAS-133, *added on 2026-11-27 by W-41's A2*). While the replica applies a disable of its registration the sync reads
  nothing and the catalogue it holds stays as it is (the main installation answers its catalogue routes `503 bastion_disabled` meanwhile);
  an enable wakes the sync.
- **The public set hides** ([Q-BAS-376](#q-bas-376--the-public-set-hides-a-package-while-none-of-its-repositories-is-in-it)). A round reads
  the public set first and swaps it in before it reads anything else. A package is shown while one of its repositories (the index's
  `repositories`) is in the public set, its documentation while one of them has a public wiki and `docs` is on; a repository's set-up and
  files while the repository is in it; the anchors, the signature objects and the catalogue's state always. The pages of the catalogue's
  own index are the reader's own and are never answered as documents; a project's index is shown while the project is in the public set,
  a repository's while the repository is and the repositories are shown (R-BAS-130, R-BAS-131).
- **hideRepositories** (R-BAS-131). The switch hides every repository's index at once, before the builder's next run deletes it: no
  document of one is answered and no search reads one. The state record keeps the switch beside `gui` and `docs`, so a replica that
  starts without its configuration applies it with them.
- **The hooks** ([Q-BAS-377](#q-bas-377--a-narrowing-of-the-feed-runs-a-round-at-once-and-again-after-the-builders-debounce)). The link
  hands the catalogue every feed entry it applied, and after a reset one of the kind `grants`. An entry of the kinds `grants`, `settings`,
  `principal` and `content` runs a round at once and a second one 8 s later, after the builder's debounce of 5 s and its run, since the public
  set and the change list the main installation answers are those of its last build (R-BAS-101, R-BAS-105); an entry of the kind
  `catalogue` runs a round at once. No feed entry of the kind `catalogue` is written by the main installation
  ([Q-BAS-378](#q-bas-378--no-feed-entry-of-the-kind-catalogue-the-follow-up-round-after-the-builders-debounce-carries-a-change)).

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7):* `SetSwitches` and `Feed` of [catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/catalogue.go),
`Link.OnFeed` of [link.go](../../internal/bastion/link/link.go). *Built on 2026-11-27 (W-40's P2):* the indexes' show rule and the
switch hideRepositories, `shows` of [reader.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/reader.go) and `hidden` of
[catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/catalogue.go).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit: `TestR_BAS_131_TheReaderHidesTheRepositoryIndexes` ([project_view_test.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/project_view_test.go)).
- Unit: `TestR_BAS_112_TheFeedHooksHideAndResyncWithoutWaitingForThePoll` (with a poll of an hour: a `grants` entry hides a package whose
  repository fell out of the public set, a `content` entry brings a withdrawal), `TestR_BAS_112_DocsOffHidesTheDocumentationAtOnce`; the
  switch `gui` off in `TestR_BAS_111_AStoredStateIsServedAfterARestartWithItsAge` (off at once, the state record and every document
  deleted). Milliseconds.
- Integration: the end of `TestR_BAS_109_TheBastionMirrorsTheCatalogueAndServesOnWhileTheLinkIsCut`: a project lowered to private is gone
  from both Bastions' pages within the builder's debounce, its run and the round after it (measured 7 s).

### R-BAS-113 · The reader
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

`catalogue.Reader`, which the web interface (P9) and W-34's anonymous answers read, held by the replica (`Server.Catalogue`):

| Method | Answers |
|---|---|
| `State()` | `gui`, `docs`, `hideRepositories` (R-BAS-131), whether the switches are known, whether a state is served, `confirmedAt`, `stale_after` and whether it is older, whether the state is kept |
| `ConfirmedAt()` | the time of the state served; zero without one |
| `PublicSet()` | the projects and repositories the catalogue shows, each repository with its description (R-BAS-130) |
| `Search(Query)` | the public packages by `q` (a substring of the name, the description or a keyword, without regard to case), `formats`, `project`, `repositories`, `deprecated`, sorted by `name` (the default), `createdAt`, `updatedAt` or `relevance` (a leading `-` descending), in pages of 50, at most 100, with the cursor of the page before ([Q-BAS-383](#q-bas-383--the-search-runs-over-the-index-in-memory-with-a-cursor-of-the-last-entrys-sort-key)); from the narrowest index that answers it ([Q-BAS-507](#q-bas-507--a-search-reads-the-narrowest-index-that-answers-it)): exactly one repository its own index while the repositories are shown, a project (or one repository while they are hidden) the project's index filtered by the repositories, neither the catalogue's own; an entry of a scope's index is listed only while the catalogue's own index shows its package |
| `Package(id)` | a public package of the index: the summary's members that are the same for every format, and the summary as the main installation answered it |
| `Lookup(format, name)` | a public package of the format by its name, else by its key, as a page's address names it (R-BAS-118, [Q-BAS-395](#q-bas-395--the-lookup-finds-a-package-by-its-name-then-by-its-key); added by W-35's P9) |
| `Versions(id, after, limit)` | a page of the package's versions list, as the main installation answered it |
| `Document(path)` | a document of the grammar (R-BAS-103) that the state shows (R-BAS-112), raw and compressed, verified against its SHA-256 on every read |
| `Packages()` | every public package of the index by name, each with its public repositories only, and a revision that stays exactly while the index's pages, the pages of the projects' and the repositories' indexes, the public set and the switches `docs` and `hideRepositories` do: the sitemap's source (R-BAS-122, R-BAS-132, [Q-BAS-414](#q-bas-414--the-reader-lists-the-public-packages-under-a-revision-for-the-sitemap); added by W-35's P10) |
| `SearchDocs(DocQuery)`, `DocEntries()` | the documentation of the public packages' newest versions searched across packages, and every entry of it for the sitemap (R-BAS-125; added by W-35's P11) |

- While the switch `gui` is off every method answers `ErrOff`, while no state is served `ErrNotReady` (R-BAS-111).
- **Integrity on read** (W-35's D6, [Q-BAS-372](#q-bas-372--a-document-that-does-not-verify-fails-the-round-a-missing-frame-takes-its-path-out)).
  A document the store lost, or one whose bytes do not verify, is answered as not found, deleted, counted in
  `quader_bastion_cache_corrupt_total` and fetched again by the next round, which it wakes.

- **The indexes of the project view** (R-BAS-130). Besides the catalogue's own index the replica builds the index of every project and
  repository of the public set from their pages, each page read and parsed once whichever index names it (two scopes of the same
  packages share a page and its entries), and an index whose pages did not change is kept as it is.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P7):* [reader.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/reader.go), [index.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/index.go).
*Built on 2026-11-27 (W-40's P2):* the scoped indexes (`indexesOf`, `scopedIndexes` of [index.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/index.go)),
the search's choice of index (`searchIndex` of [reader.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/reader.go)), the state's switch and the
revision's new parts.

## The Bastion's web interface

W-35's package P9 (the owner's g1 to g13, 2026-11-26): a Bastion whose registration's switch `gui` is on serves a read-only web interface
to anonymous visitors from the internet, "die sich über die publizierten Inhalte informieren wollen", so that they see the public images,
packages and their open findings and trust what the company delivers. It is a second, small Angular application of the main
installation's views ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-223), served by the Bastion itself from the public catalogue it mirrors
(R-BAS-109 to R-BAS-113), never by a request to the main installation, and it names nothing of the main installation (W-35's B.13). The
Go side is [internal/bastion/gui](../../internal/bastion/gui); the application is `web/src/bastion`.

### R-BAS-116 · The web interface is a bundle of the Bastion's own, mounted before the engine, that reaches nothing behind the Bastion
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Mounted before the engine** ([Q-BAS-390](#q-bas-390--the-web-interface-owns--ui-and-everything-below-ui-before-the-engine)). The
  client listener hands `/`, `/ui` and every path below `/ui/` to the web interface, and since W-35's P10 `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and
  every path below `/sitemap/` (R-BAS-122), and every other path to the engine as before (R-BAS-018). No path of the engine's families is the web interface's, and no address of the web interface is a family of the engine.
- **Read-only by construction** (W-35's B.7). Every address of the web interface answers `GET` and `HEAD`; every other method is answered
  `405 method_not_allowed` with `Allow: GET, HEAD` before anything else, its body unread and the catalogue not read. Its data come from the
  replica's catalogue reader (`Server.Catalogue`) and its legal pages (`Server.Legal`) alone: a document the catalogue does not hold is a
  `404`, never a fill, a forward or a check.
- **Never behind the Bastion.** An architecture rule holds the dependency closure of `internal/bastion/gui`: it holds neither the client
  of the main installation (`internal/bastion/mainclient`), nor the link client of a handover (`internal/bastion/handover`), nor the engine
  (`internal/bastion/engine`), directly or through another package of the Bastion's tree.
- **A bundle of its own** ([Q-BAS-391](#q-bas-391--the-main-installations-bundle-is-a-package-of-its-own-the-bastion-embeds-its-own)).
  The application is built from `web/` as a project of its own (`bastion-gui`) and embedded into the binary in
  `internal/bastion/gui/dist`, beside the main installation's in `internal/webui/dist`, which is now a package of its own that only the
  main installation's composition root imports. The Bastion serves its bundle with the handler of `internal/webui` (the locales, the hashed
  files, the nonce of a page), which a scoped allowance of R-BAS-001 admits for `internal/bastion/gui` alone; the main installation's bundle
  is not allowed, so its bytes never enter the Bastion's closure (R-BAS-001, R-ARCH-004). A binary built without the web build serves the
  committed placeholder page of each.

`CheckBastionGUIImports` and the scoped allowance of [bastion.go](../../internal/archtest/bastion.go).

### R-BAS-117 · The web interface's state, headers and request class
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The state decides first** (W-35's B.2b, B.6a; [Q-BAS-392](#q-bas-392--not-ready-a-page-is-served-with-503-the-data-answer-not_ready)).
  While the switch `gui` is off (R-BAS-112), every address of the web interface answers `404 not_found` ("Nothing is offered at this
  address."), its bundle's files and its legal pages included. While the replica holds no state to show, or knows neither its switches nor
  a state (Q-BAS-379), a data address answers `503 not_ready` ("This page is not available right now. Try again in a few minutes.") with
  `Retry-After: 30`, and a page is served with that status and that header, so that a person reads the application's sentence and a
  crawler indexes nothing; the bundle's files and the legal pages are served, since they come from the binary and the chart. Serving, `/`
  and `/ui` answer `302` to `/ui/`, and `/ui/` and an address without a locale `302` to the locale of `Accept-Language` (English
  otherwise), with `Vary: Accept-Language` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **Headers** (W-35's B.7). Every answer carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`,
  `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. A page carries the policy
  `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self';
  base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types angular angular#bundler`
  with a nonce of its own; every other answer `default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. No answer sets a cookie or carries a `Server`
  header or a header of the product's own (`Quader-…`, the chain's `ReplicaNever`).
- **Problems** (Q-BAS-321). Every problem of the web interface is problem details of type `about:blank` with `Cache-Control: no-store`,
  its texts name no party: `not_found`, `not_ready`, `method_not_allowed` ("This address only reads: it answers GET and HEAD."), the
  guard's refusals below, and `malformed_request` for a parameter the data do not answer (R-BAS-118). The code `not_ready` (503) is
  registered with the core's codes.
- **The request class** (W-35's B.14, [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-307). Every request of the web interface, a page,
  a file of the bundle and the data alike, asks the guard's block list (R-BAS-037) and then the class `gui` (20 requests a second, a burst
  of 100, per address by default), never the anonymous class's budget and never a miss. A refusal is `429` (`rate_limited`,
  `address_blocked`) with `Retry-After` rounded up to whole seconds and the RateLimit fields under the policy name `pages`
  ([Q-BAS-394](#q-bas-394--a-refusal-of-the-class-gui-names-the-policy-pages)); a refusal of a blocked address is not logged one by one.
  *Revised by W-35's P10:* a page's address answers the refusal as a page of its own (R-BAS-123); the data, the bundle's files, `robots.txt`
  and the sitemap keep the problem.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P9):* [gui.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/gui.go), `webui.Options.CSP`, `ReferrerPolicy`, `OnIndex` and
`Problem` of [webui.go](../../internal/webui/webui.go), `errs.CodeNotReady`, `engine.MarkQuiet`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([gui_test.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/gui_test.go)): `TestR_BAS_117_EveryAnswerCarriesTheHeadersAndNoCookie` (thirteen
  addresses by `GET`, `HEAD` and `POST`: the headers, the page's policy and its nonce in the page, no cookie, no `Server`, no `Quader-`
  header), `TestR_BAS_117_TheStateDecidesOffNotReadyAndServing` (off, undecided, on without a state, serving; the redirects and the
  locale), `TestR_BAS_117_EveryRequestCountsInTheClassGui` (a page, a file and the data ask the class once each; the refusal's fields; a
  blocked address marked quiet; a refused request reads nothing).
- Unit ([server_test.go](../../internal/bastion/server/server_test.go)): a replica that knows neither its switches nor a state answers
  `/ui/data/v1/state` `503 not_ready` (`TestR_BAS_001_TheRoleServesItsTwoListenersAndAnswersWithItsOwnProblems`).

### R-BAS-118 · The data a page reads: the main installation's shapes below `/ui/data/v1/`
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The application reads everything below `/ui/data/v1/`, the path the catalogue's builder rewrote the main installation's `/api/v1/` links
to (R-BAS-107), in the main installation's JSON shapes, so that the shared views read them as they read the management API
([Q-BAS-393](#q-bas-393--the-data-are-the-catalogues-grammar-below-uidatav1-and-five-addresses-of-their-own)):

| Address | Answers |
|---|---|
| `state` | `{confirmedAt, staleAfterSeconds, stale, docs, hideRepositories, timeFormat}`: the time of the state served, `bastion.gui.stale_after`, whether the state is older, the switches `docs` (W-35's B.2b) and `hideRepositories` (R-BAS-131), and the installation's default form of a time of the configuration the replica applies (R-BAS-128) |
| `legal?locale=en\|de` | the Bastion's own imprint and privacy notice (R-BAS-100) in the shape of `GET /api/v1/legal` (R-UI-225); also while the replica is not ready |
| `projects` | `{items}`: the projects the catalogue shows (the reader's `PublicSet`) that hold a package it lists or a repository with files, each `{key, displayName, description}` (R-BAS-128), for the start page that leads a visitor into a project ([Q-BAS-399](#q-bas-399--the-start-page-offers-a-project-only-while-it-shows-a-package), [Q-BAS-400](#q-bas-400--the-repositories-with-files-are-an-address-of-their-own-and-they-count-for-the-start)) |
| `repositories` | `{items}`: the public set's repositories, each `{name, format, class, description}`, for a project's repositories and the page Set up client of a repository (R-BAS-129, R-BAS-132, [Q-BAS-404](#q-bas-404--the-public-repositories-with-their-format-are-an-address-of-their-own-for-the-page-set-up-client)); `404` while the repositories are hidden (R-BAS-131) |
| `repositories/<project>/<key>` | one repository of the public set, `{name, format, class, description}`, for a repository's page and its page Set up client (R-BAS-132); while the repositories are hidden `{name, format}` alone, which the commands and the files still need ([Q-BAS-504](#q-bas-504--hide-repositories-hides-every-repository-a-visitor-reads-and-keeps-the-key-a-client-needs)); `404` for one outside the public set (added by W-40's P2) |
| `files` | `{items}`: the qualified names (`<project>/<key>`) of the public repositories whose root folder the catalogue holds (`Reader.Files`, in the public set's order), for a project's page that leads a visitor to a generic repository's folders and files ([Q-BAS-400](#q-bas-400--the-repositories-with-files-are-an-address-of-their-own-and-they-count-for-the-start)) |
| `packages?q&format&project&repository&deprecated&sort&cursor&limit` | the search of the reader (R-BAS-113, W-35's B.8) in the envelope of R-API-010 (`items`, `nextCursor`), each item the package summary as the main installation answered it, from the narrowest index (Q-BAS-507: one `repository` its own index's summaries, a `project` its index's), so the counts and the latest version are the scope's as at the main installation; `include` is accepted and changes nothing (the summaries carry the counts of open findings); any other parameter is `400 malformed_request` |
| `packages/lookup?format&name` | the public package of the format by its name, else by its key ([Q-BAS-395](#q-bas-395--the-lookup-finds-a-package-by-its-name-then-by-its-key)), or `404` |
| `packages/<id>/versions?cursor&limit` | a page of the package's versions in the main installation's order; the application sorts, searches and groups them in the browser, as the main installation's view does ([Q-BAS-396](#q-bas-396--the-versions-are-paged-in-the-main-installations-order-and-sorted-in-the-browser)) |
| `search/documentation?q&project&cursor&limit` | the documentation of the public packages' newest versions searched across packages, in the shape of `GET /api/v1/search/documentation` (R-BAS-125; added by W-35's P11) |
| `malware/signatures` | today's signatures of the malware scan from the catalogue's state, in the shape of `GET /api/v1/malware/signatures` with `importedAt` and `engine` null and `stale` false, or `404` while the state holds no set ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-042, [Q-BAS-492](#q-bas-492--the-bastion-answers-todays-signatures-in-the-main-installations-shape-from-its-catalogue); added by W-36's P8) |
| `vulnerabilities/database` | today's vulnerability database of the image scanning from the catalogue's state, in the shape of `GET /api/v1/vulnerabilities/database` with `syncedAt` null and `stale` false, or `404` while the state holds none ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-052, Q-BAS-492; added by W-36's P8) |
| every other path of the grammar (R-BAS-103) | the document as the builder stored it, by `Reader.Document`: a package, its open findings per version, an image's list by content, a version, its README, findings, signatures, contents, documentation, a set-up (a package's without a version too), a generic folder or file, a project's or a repository's index while the reader shows it (R-BAS-112), a signature object, `signing/trusted-root.json` and `signing/chain.pem` (the last three as attachments); a page of the catalogue's own index and the catalogue's own `state` are not answered |

- **One spelling.** A path is read segment by segment and written in the grammar's one spelling before it is looked up, so a browser that
  escapes less than the grammar (`+` of a version, `encodeURIComponent`'s `!'()*`) reaches the same document; a decoded `/` in a segment
  stays encoded and is refused.
- **Caching** ([Q-BAS-397](#q-bas-397--a-document-is-answered-compressed-as-stored-with-its-sha-256-as-its-etag)). Every data answer is
  `Cache-Control: no-cache` with an `ETag`: a document's the SHA-256 of its raw bytes (with `-gzip` for its compressed form), a computed
  answer's the SHA-256 of its bytes; `If-None-Match` answers `304`. A document is answered compressed, as the catalogue keeps it, to a
  client that takes `gzip` (`Content-Encoding: gzip`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`).
- While the replica is not ready, every address but `legal` answers `503 not_ready` (R-BAS-117); the reader's off and not ready are
  answered as `404` and `503`, a query it refuses as `400`.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P9; `files` by W-35's P9d):* [data.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/data.go), `Reader.Lookup` and
`Reader.Files` of [reader.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/reader.go). *Built on 2026-11-27 (W-40's P2):* `repository`,
`repositoryPath` and the state's switch of [data.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/data.go).

### R-BAS-119 · The Bastion's bundle is built, checked and embedded beside the main installation's
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Two applications of one workspace** ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-227). `npm run build:embed` (`make web-embed`) builds the
  main installation's application (project `web`) and the Bastion's (project `bastion-gui`, `web/src/bastion`) in production, both
  locales, and copies them to `internal/webui/dist/<locale>/` and `internal/bastion/gui/dist/<locale>/`. Each tree keeps its committed
  placeholder `index.html`; a binary built without the web build serves the placeholder of each.
- **The same checks for both.** The nonce placeholder in every `index.html`, the hashed names of R-UI-001 (Q-UI-140), no script naming
  DiceBear's service, the compressed initial bundle within R-UI-001's 400 kB (the Bastion's: 158 kB in English, measured 2026-11-26), and
  every locale's `3rdpartylicenses.txt` with the notices of Q-UI-144 (DiceBear's only for the main installation, whose avatars the
  Bastion does not draw).
- **What the Bastion's bundle may hold** (R-UI-228). The Bastion's build writes its metafile (`--stats-json`) and fails when a module of
  the main installation's client, its session, a screen of its own that no page of the Bastion composes, or a dialog put a byte into an
  output file ([Q-UI-1437](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1437--what-the-bastions-bundle-holds-is-checked-over-its-builds-metafile)).
- **The image.** The `web` stage of the `Containerfile` builds both and the `build` stage copies both trees; `.dockerignore` keeps a
  locale directory of a local build out of both.

### R-BAS-120 · No page of the Bastion names the main installation
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's rule (W-35's B.13): "Der Bastion verrät keine internen Informationen über die Hauptinstanz." For the web interface:

- **Its own texts.** The problems of R-BAS-117, the not-ready sentence, the band of an old state ("This information is from <date, time>.
  Newer information is not available right now.") and the footer ("As of …") name no party.
- **Its bundle.** It has no environment file and no compiled address: it reads the relative `/ui/data/v1/` of the host it was loaded from
  (R-BAS-118), and the main installation's bundle is not in it (R-BAS-116, R-BAS-119).
- **Its headers.** No `Quader-…` header, no `Server` header (R-BAS-117).
- **Its data.** The documents are the builder's, which strips internal identities (R-BAS-106) and rewrites the main installation's
  addresses to the Bastion's (R-BAS-107); the web interface adds nothing of its own to them.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P9):* the texts of [gui.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/gui.go) and of the application's shell
(`web/src/bastion/app.ts`).

## Search engines find the Bastion's pages

W-35's package P10 (the owner, 2026-11-26: the Bastion is "für anonyme User aus dem Netz die sich über die publizierten Inhalte informieren
wollen", and people find such pages through search engines; the design is W-35's B.11, [ADR-306](../decisions.md#adr-306--search-engines-read-a-bastions-pages-through-a-head-and-a-text-the-bastion-fills-from-its-catalogue)).
A crawler reads a page's head and text that the Bastion fills from its catalogue, `robots.txt` and a sitemap at the host's root; all of
it from the Bastion's own catalogue and on its own `server.base_url`, none of it by a request to the main installation and none of it
naming the main installation (R-BAS-120). The Go side is [seo.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/seo.go),
[crawl.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/crawl.go), [refusal.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/refusal.go) and
[internal/bastion/gui/page](../../internal/bastion/gui/page); the application's part is [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-231.

### R-BAS-121 · A page's head and text for a reader that runs no script
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Two slots** ([Q-BAS-405](#q-bas-405--the-bastion-fills-the-pages-head-and-text-from-its-catalogue-into-the-applications-indexhtml)).
  The application's `index.html` holds `<!--QUADER_HEAD-->` in its head and `<!--QUADER_PAGE-->` in its root element after the spinner;
  the committed placeholder of a binary without the web build holds them too. A page's address is answered with the document, its two
  slots filled after the nonce went in, so that nothing a slot carries can take the page's nonce. The application replaces the root's
  content when it starts.
- **The head.** `<title>` as the application writes it ("<page> – Quader Bastion", R-UI-231's words, [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md)
  Q-UI-1617), `<meta name="description">` (the package's
  description, cut to 300 characters), `<link rel="canonical">` and `<link rel="alternate" hreflang>` for `en`, `de` and `x-default` (the
  address without a locale, which redirects by the visitor's language), all on the Bastion's own `server.base_url`; `<meta name="robots"
  content="noindex">` where the address is not to be indexed; JSON-LD in `<script type="application/ld+json">`: `SoftwareApplication` for
  a package's and a version's page (`name`, `softwareVersion`, `description`, `license`, `keywords`, `datePublished`, `url`), `TechArticle`
  for a documentation entry's (`?tab=documentation&doc=<type>/<name>` that the version's tree holds), `WebPage` for the start, a project's
  list, the versions and the legal pages. The encoder escapes `<`, `>` and `&`, so no member closes the script element; the policy of
  R-BAS-117 is unchanged (JSON-LD is a data block).
- **The text.** Inside the root element, `<div class="quader-page">`: the way from the start, the heading, the description, the facts every
  format has (the newest version, when it was published, its licences and keywords), the README as the catalogue keeps it (only while the
  catalogue shows it: `docs` on and a public wiki, R-BAS-112), the links to the projects, a project's packages or a package's versions (the
  first 100 each), and the footer's legal links. The start links the projects its application offers, those with a package or with files
  (Q-BAS-399, Q-BAS-400), each to its repositories or, while they are hidden, to its packages (R-BAS-132), and under **Files**, only while
  the repositories are shown, every public repository whose files the catalogue holds, by its qualified name, to the root
  of its files; a project's list links its own such repositories by their keys above its packages, in both modes, and answers `200` for a project with
  files and no package ([Q-BAS-498](#q-bas-498--the-start-the-projects-lists-and-the-sitemap-lead-to-a-repositorys-files),
  [Q-BAS-508](#q-bas-508--a-projects-list-keeps-its-repositories-with-files-in-both-modes)). The project view's pages, a project's own
  address and the way from the start are R-BAS-132's. A browser that runs the application does not show it: a rule under the page's nonce hides
  it and the application's spinner shows until the application starts (R-UI-217); `<noscript>` shows it and hides the spinner
  ([Q-BAS-406](#q-bas-406--the-text-is-hidden-from-a-browser-that-runs-the-application-and-shown-without-script)). Its few fixed words
  are a table in both languages in Go, the application's own words.
- **No format knowledge** (W-35's B.11). The head and the text read only the members of the main installation's shapes that are the same
  for every format: the summary's `name`, `description`, `latestVersion`, `keywords` and `updatedAt`, a version's `version`, `publishedAt`,
  `licenses` and `keywords`, the README's `html`, the documentation tree's entry `name` and `shortDescription`, and the versions list's
  `version`. A format's `metadata` is never decoded. There is no install command in the text
  ([Q-BAS-409](#q-bas-409--the-text-carries-no-install-command)).
- **Status and indexing** ([Q-BAS-407](#q-bas-407--an-address-the-catalogue-does-not-show-is-404),
  [Q-BAS-408](#q-bas-408--what-is-indexed-the-pages-themselves-never-the-findings-or-a-list-of-results)). An address the catalogue does not
  show is `404` with `noindex` and no canonical address: no route of the application, a package not public in the address's project, a
  version it does not hold, a project's list without a package and without files, a legal page without a text. An address that opens the findings
  (`tab=vulnerabilities`, a `severity`) and a list with a search, a filter, a sort or a cursor are `noindex`, canonical without their
  query; every other query is dropped from the canonical address; a documentation entry's keeps `tab` and `doc`. A repository's page Set
  up client is found while the public set holds the repository, titled "Set up client", and never indexed (R-BAS-129,
  [Q-BAS-401](#q-bas-401--a-page-set-up-client-of-the-bastion-is-found-and-never-indexed)). A public generic repository's folder or file
  (`projects/<project>/repositories/<key>`, the root, and `…/files/<path…>`, R-UI-229) is found while the catalogue holds its listing or
  its description, titled by its name (the root by the repository's key, its description the repository's while the repositories are
  shown, R-BAS-132), indexed, its canonical address the one spelling of the path
  without a query; a folder's text links its entries, the first 100
  ([Q-BAS-483](#q-bas-483--a-public-generic-repositorys-folders-and-files-are-pages-a-crawler-finds-and-indexes)). While the replica holds
  no state a page is `503` with `Retry-After: 30`, `noindex` and the title "Quader" alone (R-BAS-117).
- **Cost** ([Q-BAS-410](#q-bas-410--a-pages-head-and-text-are-written-per-request-without-a-cache)). Two or three documents of the
  catalogue per page, as a person's browser reads them a moment later; nothing is kept per address.

### R-BAS-122 · `robots.txt` and the sitemap at the host's root
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **`/robots.txt`** ([Q-BAS-411](#q-bas-411--robotstxt-keeps-a-crawler-off-the-package-api-and-the-findings-documents-and-lets-it-render-the-pages)).
  While the web interface is on: `Allow: /ui/`, `Disallow: /ui/data/*vulnerabilit`, `Disallow: /api/`, `Disallow: /files/`,
  `Disallow: /v2/` and `Sitemap: <server.base_url>/sitemap.xml`. The data of the pages stay allowed, so that a crawler that renders the
  application can render a page; they answer `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (every answer below `/ui/data/`). While the web interface is off:
  `Disallow: /` for every crawler. While the replica knows neither its switches nor a state: `503 not_ready`, which a crawler takes as
  "try again later" rather than as a rule. `text/plain`, `no-cache` with an ETag; answered also while the switch `gui` is off.
- **The sitemap** ([Q-BAS-412](#q-bas-412--the-sitemap-lists-the-start-the-projects-the-packages-and-the-legal-pages-split-at-50000-and-kept-per-revision)).
  `/sitemap.xml` is a sitemap index of the files `/sitemap/<n>.xml`, each of at most 50,000 addresses. It lists, each in both languages with
  `xhtml:link` alternates for `en`, `de` and `x-default`: the start, every project's list that holds a package or files, the root of every
  public repository's files the catalogue holds (its folders and files are linked from there,
  [Q-BAS-498](#q-bas-498--the-start-the-projects-lists-and-the-sitemap-lead-to-a-repositorys-files)), every package's page in every
  project whose public repository holds it, its documentation pages (while `docs` is on, the entries of R-BAS-125's `DocEntries` in the
  project whose repository the tree was read from, each as its page's canonical address `…?doc=<type>/<name>&tab=documentation`; W-35's
  P11), and the imprint and the privacy notice that have a text; while the repositories are shown also each such project's repositories
  and the page of each of its public repositories (R-BAS-132). `lastmod` is the package's `updatedAt` (a list's and the start's the newest of theirs; none for a legal page, a root of files or a project's list without a package). A version's
  own page is not listed: a package's page links its versions. The set is built from the reader's `Packages()` and `Files()` once per
  revision of both and of the switch `hideRepositories` (a repository's files that arrive change no revision of the packages) and every
  file is kept compressed with it; a crawler that takes `gzip` gets those bytes, `no-cache` with an ETag of the revision and the file.
  Off: `404`; not ready: `503 not_ready`.
- Every request of both counts in the class `gui` (R-BAS-117).

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P10):* [crawl.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/crawl.go), the hook [crawl_docs.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/crawl_docs.go),

## The documentation of the Bastion's web interface

W-35's package P11, the owner's B.5 (2026-11-26): "Eine weitere, separat zuschaltbare Option ist das Ausliefern von Docs pro Repo", and of
Ansible (2026-11-25): Quader replaces Galaxy completely and as an equal, so the documentation a format regularly carries is stored, shown,
and shown first. A Bastion whose switch `docs` is on (R-BAS-102) shows a public package's documentation as the main installation shows
it to an anonymous visitor: the README of an npm, a NuGet and a Helm package and of an Ansible collection or role, an Ansible collection's
documentation tree with its entries, files and changelog, and a Debian package's changelog and copyright. The repository's wiki level
decides per repository (R-AUTHZ-034); there is no setting of its own. The builder's part is R-BAS-124, the Bastion's R-BAS-125, the pages'
R-BAS-126 and [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-232.

### R-BAS-124 · The documentation travels in the catalogue only with docs on and a public wiki, with the words of the main installation's search
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The priority is the one of R-BAS-101 to R-BAS-120.

- **What travels.** A version's README, its documentation tree, the tree's entries and files (R-BAS-104) are built while the
  registration's switch `docs` is on **and** a repository of the public set that holds the version has a public wiki
  ([Q-BAS-415](#q-bas-415--the-builder-asks-the-public-set-for-the-wiki-besides-the-anonymous-answer)): the anonymous answer of the main
  installation already holds none for a wiki that is not public (R-AUTHZ-034), and the builder asks its public set again, so a level the
  answers have not caught up with builds none either. A Debian package's changelog and copyright follow the switch `docs` alone: they are
  no wiki of R-AUTHZ-034, and an anonymous reader reads them at the main installation
  ([Q-BAS-416](#q-bas-416--a-debian-packages-changelog-and-copyright-follow-the-switch-docs-alone)).
- **No wiki member without it** ([Q-BAS-417](#q-bas-417--a-version-without-its-documentation-carries-no-wiki-member)). A version whose
  documentation does not travel carries `hasReadme: false` and no `metadata.docs`, R-AUTHZ-034's answer to a caller who may not read the
  wiki; a Debian package's contents carry no `changelog`, `changelogFile`, `changelogTruncated`, `copyright` or `copyrightTruncated`.
- **The search words** ([Q-BAS-418](#q-bas-418--the-tree-carries-the-lexemes-of-the-search-vector-less-those-another-begins)). Every
  entry of a tree the catalogue keeps carries `searchWords`: the lexemes of its search vector at the main installation
  (`tsvector_to_array` of `ansible_doc_entries.search`, the statement `BastionCatalogueDocSearchWords`, one per version), lower case,
  sorted, each once, without a word that begins another (a prefix of it is a prefix of the longer one), joined by a space. The member is
  the catalogue's alone; the main installation's answer has none. A tree that the words would take above `cataloguebounds.DocumentMaxBytes`
  is kept without them, and its search finds by the names alone.
- **What renders it again** ([Q-BAS-419](#q-bas-419--what-else-decides-the-documentations-html-is-in-the-salt-and-the-fingerprint-reads-the-documentation-built)).
  The salt of every unit (R-BAS-105) holds, besides the README renderer's policy hash, the renderer's version and the Ansible markup
  converter's (`docgen.MarkupVersion`): the main installation converts on every read, so no stored fact changes with them, and a change
  renders every document again (W-35's D1). A package's fingerprint reads the documentation built for each version (its generator, its
  entries and its bytes), so a rebuild that changes the search words renders the package again. The builder's revision is
  `catalogue/2`.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P11):* `publicWiki`, `withoutWiki`, `TreeWithSearchWords` and `SearchWords` of
[builder.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/builder.go), `DocSearchWords` of [store.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/store.go),
the statements `BastionCatalogueDocSearchWords` and `BastionCataloguePackageFacts` of
[bastion_catalogue.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/bastion_catalogue.sql), `docsPolicy` of
[wire_bastion_catalogue.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion_catalogue.go), `MarkupVersion` of
[markup.go](../../internal/formats/ansible/docgen/markup.go).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([docs_test.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/docs_test.go), a fake management API of one collection, milliseconds, bytes):
  `TestR_BAS_124_TheDocumentationTravelsOnlyWithDocsOnAndAPublicWiki` (docs on and a public wiki: the README, the tree, an entry and a file,
  the version announcing them; docs off and an internal wiki: none of them, the version announcing none, its other members kept),
  `TestR_BAS_124_TheTreeCarriesTheSearchWordsOfTheMainInstallation`, `TestR_BAS_124_SearchWordsKeepTheWordsThatNoOtherBegins`.
- Integration (area `bastion`, inside `TestR_BAS_104_TheCatalogueFollowsPublishesLevelsAndTheSwitch`, no world of its own): the npm

### R-BAS-125 · The documentation is searched at the Bastion: a version in the browser, across packages at the Bastion
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Inside a version** (R-ANS-036 at the Bastion, [Q-BAS-420](#q-bas-420--a-versions-search-runs-in-the-browser-over-the-whole-tree)).
  The Bastion has no search route per version: the application reads the version's whole tree once and narrows it in the browser by the
  rule of the main installation's statement `AnsibleDocsTree`, the function `narrowDocTree` of
  [docs-model.ts](../../web/src/app/views/packages/docs-model.ts): the text without control characters, split on white space into at
  most 8 terms of at most 64 characters; an entry matches when every term is a part of its name, whatever the case, or its letters and
  digits in lower case begin a word of the entry's `searchWords`; a file matches when every term is a part of its title, the changelog
  when every term is a part of "changelog"; the groups, types and counts stay those before the search and `matchCount` is the entries
  left; a text of fewer than 2 characters is refused (`422`), as the main installation refuses it.
- **Across packages** (R-ANS-058 at the Bastion, [Q-BAS-421](#q-bas-421--the-search-across-packages-is-a-data-address-over-the-newest-versions-trees)).
  `GET /ui/data/v1/search/documentation?q&project&cursor&limit` answers the entries of the documentation tree of every public package's
  newest version (the index's `latestVersion`, the version the package's page opens on, R-UI-218) in the main installation's shape of
  `GET /api/v1/search/documentation` (`DocumentationHit`: format, package ID, the package's name, version, project, repository, type, name,
  short description, the package's deprecation) in a list of R-API-010, pages of 50, at most 100. A hit is an entry each of whose words of
  the text (the runs of `a` to `z` and `0` to `9`, `rows.ViewQuery`'s) begins a word of its `searchWords`; the best first: a name equal to
  the text, then one that starts with it, then one that holds it, then a match of the words elsewhere, within that by the entry's name,
  the package, the repository and the type. A text of 2 to 100 characters after its control characters are taken out; any other parameter,
  text or limit is `400 malformed_request`. A hit is found only while `docs` is on and the repository its tree was read from is public
  with a public wiki; otherwise the list is empty, as for a reader who may read no wiki. The replica builds the index of the trees with
  each round, reading only a tree it has not parsed before; a tree it cannot read is left out and fetched again by the next round.
- **For the sitemap.** `Reader.DocEntries` lists every entry the search could find, nothing while `docs` is off: the source of the
  sitemap's documentation entries (W-35's B.11, R-BAS-122): `docRoutes` lists each entry in the project whose repository its tree was read
  from, as its page's canonical address, the package's route with `doc=<type>/<name>` (`DocHit.Doc`) and `tab=documentation`. The
  revision of `Reader.Packages()`, by which the sitemap is kept, includes the trees of the documentation, so a changed tree builds the
  sitemap again.

*Built on 2026-11-26 (W-35's P11):* [docs.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/docs.go) (`SearchDocs`, `DocEntries`, the index built in
`sync` and `take`), `searchDocs` of [data.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/data.go), `narrowDocTree` and `docEntryMatches` of
[docs-model.ts](../../web/src/app/views/packages/docs-model.ts), `docs` of [reads.ts](../../web/src/bastion/data/reads.ts),
[crawl_docs.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/crawl_docs.go) (the sitemap's entries) and the revision of `Packages` in
[reader.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/reader.go).

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit ([docs_test.go](../../internal/bastion/catalogue/docs_test.go), against maintest's catalogue, milliseconds):
  `TestR_BAS_125_TheDocumentationIsSearchedAcrossThePackagesNewestVersions` (the newest version's entries by every word's prefix, the name

- Unit ([gui_test.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/gui_test.go), microseconds): `TestR_BAS_125_TheDocumentationIsSearchedInTheMainInstallationsShape`

- Unit (web, [docs-model.spec.ts](../../web/src/app/views/packages/docs-model.spec.ts), milliseconds): `R-BAS-124 the browser narrows the

### R-BAS-126 · The pages show the documentation while docs is on, and lead with it
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **Docs on.** The Bastion's pages show the documentation as the main installation's views show it (R-UI-218, R-UI-060, R-UI-008): an
  npm and a NuGet package's address opens its newest version on its README, an Ansible collection's on its documentation; the tab
  Documentation has its tree, its entries with their anchors and its files; a deep link (`?doc=<type>/<name>#parameter-<path>`, R-ANS-048)
  opens that page at that anchor; a Debian version has its tab Changelog with the changelog and the copyright.
- **Docs off** ([Q-BAS-422](#q-bas-422--with-docs-off-a-packages-address-stays-its-newest-versions-page-and-opens-on-its-first-other-tab)).
  The application reads the switch from the state (`/ui/data/v1/state`, `docs`) at the live idle cadence (R-UI-213): the tabs README,
  Documentation, Contents and Changelog are gone at its next read, and a version opens on its first other tab; a package's address stays
  its newest version's page, so a link, a canonical address and a sitemap entry stay valid whatever the switch. The data path answers at
  once: the README, the tree, its entries and files `404` (R-BAS-112), the search across packages nothing (R-BAS-125), and a Debian
  package's contents without its changelog and copyright, before the builder's next run takes them out of the document.
- **Nothing of the main installation.** The documentation is the builder's documents (R-BAS-106, R-BAS-107): its links are the Bastion's
  and the README renderer's, its in-page links page-relative (R-ANS-048), and the application adds nothing of its own to them (R-BAS-120).

`VersionPage` of [package-pages.ts](../../web/src/bastion/pages/package-pages.ts), `withoutDocumentation` of
[data.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/data.go).

## What a visitor of the web interface still missed: the interface version 10 and the page Set up client

W-35's package P9e (2026-11-27), the owner's reason for the web interface (2026-11-26): it shows anonymous visitors the public images and
the vulnerabilities found "um Vertrauen in die ausgelieferten Images zu schaffen". The builders of P9b, P9d and UI-1126 left four things a
visitor met: no grade column in a package's versions table, no page Set up client (a generic file's command calls a function only its
set-up defines), projects named by their keys, and the factory form of a time. Three of them change the interface between the Bastion and
the main installation, which rises to version 10 (R-BAS-009); before the first stable release a raise costs nothing but the lockstep
upgrade every raise needs.

### R-BAS-128 · The interface version 10: a package's grade per version, the projects' names and the installation's form of a time
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The priority is the one of R-BAS-116 to R-BAS-126, whose pages these complete.

- **A package's open findings per version** ([Q-BAS-403](#q-bas-403--a-packages-open-findings-per-version-are-a-document-of-their-own-without-the-time-of-their-check)).
  The document kind `packageVulnerabilities`, path `packages/<id>/vulnerabilities` (`iface.CataloguePackageVulnerabilities`, R-BAS-103), is
  the main installation's anonymous answer of `GET /api/v1/packages/{id}/vulnerabilities`: per version its grade with the counts of the open
  findings (`needs_triage`, `confirmed`, `blocked`; no dismissed or resolved finding, W-35's B.4b), the fixable count, the end of life, the
  public state, over every public repository that holds the version, the worst first (R-VULN-038). The builder renders it with the package
  (R-BAS-104); the strip (R-BAS-106) takes each grade's `checkedAt` out and keeps it nowhere, since the column does not show it and the
  version's own report keeps its time in the version's state. The package's fingerprint already reads the findings and the image scans'
  outcome (R-BAS-105), so the document follows a triage or a scan within a run. The Bastion serves it while the package is public
  (R-BAS-112) at `/ui/data/v1/packages/<id>/vulnerabilities`, and `BastionVulnerabilityReads.packageReport` reads it: the versions' table of
  the shared view gets its column with no change of the view (R-UI-229).
- **The projects' names** ([Q-BAS-423](#q-bas-423--the-public-set-names-a-project-by-its-key-display-name-and-description)). A project of
  the public set (`iface.CatalogueProject`) is `{key, displayName, description}`, the members the anonymous caller reads of it in
  `GET /api/v1/projects` and nothing else of it (no owner, no member count); the description is `""` for a project without one, and both
  texts have their links rewritten as a document's (R-BAS-107). The data path's `projects` answers them (R-BAS-118); the start lists a
  project by its display name with its description, a project's packages are headed by them, and the head and title a crawler reads name
  the project so (R-BAS-121: "Packages in <display name>"). The state record a replica keeps holds the public set; its form is raised to 2,
  so a record of the form before is refused and the replica reads the catalogue again (R-BAS-110).
- **The installation's form of a time** ([Q-BAS-402](#q-bas-402--the-installations-form-of-a-time-is-the-configurations-display-and-changes-without-the-registrations-revision)).
  The configuration (R-BAS-093) has the member `display`, `{timeFormat}`: the installation's default form of a time (api-and-ui.md R-UI-251),
  one of `iface.TimeFormats()` (the main installation's `sysstate.TimeFormats()`, a test holds them equal), the factory form `dmy-weekday` in
  a replica's built-in configuration. The composition root sets it from the replica's copy of the system state where it answers a
  handshake; it is the installation's, no member of the registration, and changes without the registration's revision: a replica applies a
  configuration that differs in any member (`settings.Holder.Apply`). A change (`system.time_format_changed`) is an entry of the feed of the
  kind `settings`, so every Bastion handshakes again within the feed's seconds. The data path's `state` answers it (R-BAS-118), and the
  application writes every time in it (api-and-ui.md R-UI-250, closing [H-2390](api-and-ui.md#h-2390--the-bastions-pages-write-the-factory-form-of-a-time-not-the-installations-default)).
- **What a main installation and a Bastion of different versions do** (R-BAS-009's rule): they do not talk; the handshake answers
  `400 bastion_interface_mismatch` with `"interfaceVersion": 10`.
- **Nothing of the main installation** (R-BAS-120): the new document is the builder's, through the strip and the link rewrite; a
  project's names are what an anonymous reader of the main installation reads.

### R-BAS-129 · The page Set up client at the Bastion
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

W-35's P9d left a generic file's command calling a function (`quader_curl`, `quader_wget`, `$QuaderHeaders`) that only its repository's
set-up defines, and every format whose install command relies on a configuration (npm's registry, NuGet's source, APT's source list) had
the same gap, since the Bastion had no page Set up client and its panels of commands offered no link to one (Q-UI-1456).

- **The page** (api-and-ui.md R-UI-120 at the Bastion, [Q-UI-1468](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1468--the-bastion-has-the-page-set-up-client-of-a-public-repository)).
  At the main installation's address, `/projects/<project>/repositories/<key>/setup?client=<client>`, the target of **Set up client** in every
  panel of commands of the Bastion's pages. Its header names the repository (a link to its files for a generic repository, to the project's
  packages otherwise), its format and its class, the client address of the set-up; a select **Client** where the format has several (the
  Bastion's format table, now with the server's clients); one line that the snippets need no credentials; the steps Configure (where the
  set-up has configure snippets: an OCI repository's has none, so its page starts at Install, Q-OCI-277), Install and, where the
  installation signs, Verify, from the shared view `views/setup/setup-steps.ts` (Q-UI-1469). No token, no **More options**, no
  Bastion to choose, no Publish and no guide: the guide describes the main installation (R-BAS-120).
- **Its data.** The snippets are the catalogue's set-up document of the repository and the client (`setup/<project>/<repo>/<client>`,
  R-BAS-103), which the builder renders for every public repository and every client of its format with `credentials=none` and
  `bastion=<name>` (R-BAS-104): the Bastion's address, no login, no publish line, and no configure snippet of an OCI repository
  (Q-OCI-277). So a generic repository's Configure defines the function
  its files' commands call, without the header that would carry a credential. The repository's format and class come from the data path's
  `repositories` (R-BAS-118, [Q-BAS-404](#q-bas-404--the-public-repositories-with-their-format-are-an-address-of-their-own-for-the-page-set-up-client));
  a repository the public set does not hold says "This address offers no repository of that name." and asks for no set-up.
- **For a crawler** (R-BAS-121): the address is found while the public set holds the repository, titled "Set up client", and `noindex`
  ([Q-BAS-401](#q-bas-401--a-page-set-up-client-of-the-bastion-is-found-and-never-indexed)).
- **Nothing of the main installation** (R-BAS-120): the snippets are the builder's documents, scanned by R-BAS-104's tests; the page's own
  words name no party.

## The catalogue of the project view: the interface version 12

W-40 (the owner, 2026-11-27): a Bastion's project opens on its repositories, as the main installation's does, each repository lists what
it holds with the command of every row, and a switch on the Bastion's card turns the Bastion into the flat view of packages alone. The
main installation's side of it, W-40's package P1: the catalogue the pages read and the switch, which change the interface between the
Bastion and the main installation, so it rises to version 12 ([Q-BAS-506](#q-bas-506--the-project-view-raises-the-interface-to-version-12-and-the-bastions-state-record-to-form-3)).
The Bastion's reader, data path and crawler, W-40's package P2, are R-BAS-132 and the Bastion's parts of R-BAS-130 and R-BAS-131; the
views (P4a, P4b), the pages (P5), the card (P6) and the texts (P7) follow.

### R-BAS-130 · The catalogue of the project view: the indexes per project and repository, an image's list by content, the set-ups of every holder
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The priority is the one of R-BAS-116 to R-BAS-129, whose pages these feed.

- **A repository's description.** A repository of the public set (`iface.CatalogueRepository`) carries the description the anonymous caller
  reads in `GET /api/v1/projects/<p>/repositories`, its links rewritten as a document's text is (R-BAS-107); `""` for none. The state
  record a replica keeps holds the public set, so its form rises to 3 and a record of the form before is refused: the replica reads the
  catalogue again after the upgrade (R-BAS-110).
- **A project's and a repository's index** ([Q-BAS-500](#q-bas-500--a-projects-and-a-repositorys-list-read-indexes-of-their-own)).
  `projects/<project>/index/<n>` (kind `projectIndex`) is the main installation's anonymous answer of
  `GET /api/v1/packages?project=<p>&include=vulnerabilities`, built for every project of the public set; `repositories/<p>/<r>/index/<n>`
  (kind `repositoryIndex`) the answer of `GET /api/v1/packages?repository=<p>/<r>&include=vulnerabilities`, built for every repository of
  the public set, and only while the repositories are shown (R-BAS-131): ClamAV's lists its databases, which are packages although its
  format's items are paths; a generic repository's is an empty page (`{"items":[]}`), its files being documents of their own. Each in pages of 100 in the list's order, page 0 also for an empty list. The main installation
  aggregates per scope (`internal/packages/view/topology.go`), so a scope's `latestVersion`, `versionCount` and grades are its own: a
  local repository's index does not count the version a virtual repository over it holds besides. The indexes are documents of the
  registration as a whole (unit `""`, R-BAS-105), rendered at every run and written only where their bytes changed.
- **An image's list by content** ([Q-BAS-501](#q-bas-501--an-images-list-by-content-is-the-main-installations-answer-with-groupcontent)).
  `packages/<id>/images` (kind `packageImages`) is the anonymous answer of `GET /api/v1/packages/<id>/versions?group=content&include=kind`:
  one entry per manifest, led by its highest tag, the image's other tags as `aliases`, the leading tag and the order the server's
  (api-and-ui.md Q-UI-1130, Q-API-432). Built for every package of a format whose lists are lists by content (OCI), with the package's unit.
- **The set-up in every holder** ([Q-BAS-502](#q-bas-502--a-versions-set-up-is-built-in-every-public-repository-that-holds-it)). A
  version's set-up per client (`setup/<p>/<r>/<client>/<id>/<v>`) is built in every repository of the public set that the version's
  document names, each once, a local one and a virtual one over it alike, so the command through any repository a page offers finds its
  document. A repository the main installation answers no set-up for (`404`) has none.
- **The set-up of an image without a version** ([Q-BAS-503](#q-bas-503--the-pull-by-digest-reads-a-packages-set-up-without-a-version)).
  `setup/<p>/<r>/<client>/<id>` is the anonymous answer of the client set-up with `package=<name>` and no `version`, per public holder of
  the image and client of the format: the pull by digest appends `@<digest>` to the image's name, which only this set-up names. OCI only.
- **Cost** (W-40's section 2.2, derived from the measurement of 2026-11-27 on the render seed: a summary of an index 117 B compressed, a
  set-up 440 to 455 B, a versions list 354 B): a package of 10 versions in one public repository adds about 23 B per version; an image of
  10 tags about 150 B per tag; a version held by a further public repository adds its clients' set-ups (0.45 to 1.8 KiB). The measured
  figures of the catalogue after the change are in [developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-catalogue-of-the-project-view).
- **Nothing of the main installation** (R-BAS-120): every new document is the builder's, through the strip (R-BAS-106) and the link
  rewrite (R-BAS-107); the scans of R-BAS-104's and R-BAS-106's tests run over them.

*Built on 2026-11-27 (W-40's P1):* the kinds and the path forms of [catalogue.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/catalogue.go),
`publicSet`, `scopedIndexes`, `images`, `holders` and `setups` of [builder.go](../../internal/bastionmain/catalogue/builder.go).
*Built on 2026-11-27 (W-40's P2):* the Bastion's reader of the scoped indexes, which its search reads (R-BAS-113, Q-BAS-507), and its
show rule (R-BAS-112); the images list and the set-up without a version are a package's documents, which the reader answered already;
the data path and the crawler (R-BAS-118, R-BAS-132). *Not built:* the pages (W-40's P5).

### R-BAS-131 · Hide repositories
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner (W-40): a Bastion may show its projects and their packages without the repositories that hold them. The switch names no
repository anywhere a visitor reads; a client's address still carries the repository's key, since the Bastion mirrors the main
installation's address space ([Q-BAS-504](#q-bas-504--hide-repositories-hides-every-repository-a-visitor-reads-and-keeps-the-key-a-client-needs)).

- **Stored.** The column `hide_repositories boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` of `bastion` (migration `00157`), a member of the
  registration's switches beside `gui` and `docs` (R-BAS-102), off for every registration, new and existing, so a missing member is the
  default ([Q-BAS-505](#q-bas-505--the-switch-is-hide-repositories-off-by-default-behind-the-details-of-the-web-interface)).
  `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}` answers it as `switches.hideRepositories`; `PATCH` with `{"switches": {"hideRepositories": true}}` sets it
  (`endpoints:write`, as the other switches, Q-BAS-325; `If-Match` with the registration's revision, `412` for a stale one), absent and
  `null` unchanged. A change raises the registration's revision and records `bastion.configuration.changed` with the part
  `switches.hideRepositories`.
- **To the Bastion.** `iface.Switches.HideRepositories` (`hideRepositories`) in the handshake's configuration (R-BAS-093), changed by a
  `settings` entry of the feed within about 3 s.
- **To the builder.** `catalogue.Registration.HideRepositories`, read from the stored row as `gui` and `docs` are, is part of the salt
  (R-BAS-105), so a change renders every unit again; the change area `bastion_configuration` starts a run within the debounce. While it is
  on the builder renders no repository's index (the run that hides them deletes the ones built before), and its rewrite treats no
  upstream as a well-known public registry: every `upstreamUrl` and `fetchedFrom` is `null` (R-BAS-106's rule with an empty
  `PublicRegistries`), so a version's page names no remote's upstream. A project's index, the set-ups in every holder (the pages offer
  the first then) and an image's list are built as while shown.
- **Still named, and why** (Q-BAS-504): the key inside a command, a download address, Set up client's snippets and address (a client needs
  them); a generic repository's files under their root folder, which is the key as every download address of them has it; the data a
  browser reads keep a version's holders with their keys and classes, which the shared views' rules read.
- **On the card** (api-and-ui.md R-UI-240): the switch **Hide repositories**, the first row of the card's closed **Details**, under the
  group's heading **Web interface** (W-41's plan, D24: not a fold of its own in the plain view, so the default card gains no line); its
  sentence is the row's help.

### R-BAS-132 · A crawler finds the project view
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

W-40's P2: what a reader that runs no script reads of the project view (R-BAS-121's head and text, R-BAS-122's sitemap), from the
catalogue of R-BAS-130 alone. The application's own pages are W-40's P5; until it lands a browser that runs the application shows its
"Page not found" at the two new addresses, while a crawler reads the text below.

- **The addresses** (the application's routes of W-40's plan, 4.1). `projects/<project>` is the project's own address: its text and
  canonical address are its repositories' page, or its packages' while the repositories are hidden (W-40's D1). `projects/<project>/repositories`
  is the project's repositories; `projects/<project>/repositories/<key>` and its spelling `…/<key>/files` are a repository's page;
  `…/<key>/files/<path…>` a folder or a file below the root of a generic repository's files; `…/<key>/setup` Set up client, as before.
- **A project's repositories.** Titled "Repositories in <display name>" ("Repositories in …" in German), headed by the display name, its
  description as the lead and the page's description; its text links every public repository of the project, the first 100 in the public
  set's order, each by its key with its description as the note. Indexed; `404` for a project the public set does not hold and while the
  repositories are hidden.
- **A repository's page** ([Q-BAS-509](#q-bas-509--a-repositorys-page-in-the-text-is-its-files-root-where-the-catalogue-holds-one-and-its-indexs-packages-otherwise)).
  Where the catalogue holds the root of the repository's files, it is that root (R-BAS-121, R-UI-229), in both modes; its description is
  the repository's while the repositories are shown. Otherwise it is titled and headed by the key, its description as the lead, and its
  text links the packages of the repository's index (R-BAS-130), the first 100, each to its page in the project, under **Images** for an
  image repository (format `oci`, the application's word for its items) and **Packages** for any other; a repository without a package
  has the page without a list. Indexed; `404` for one outside the public set, and for every repository but a root of files while the
  repositories are hidden.
- **The way from the start** (W-40's D20, [Q-BAS-510](#q-bas-510--a-link-that-names-a-project-leads-to-its-repositories-or-to-its-packages-while-they-are-hidden)).
  Every page of a project starts at Projects › the project's display name, which leads to the project's repositories, or to its packages
  while the repositories are hidden. A project's repositories and its packages end there; a package's page goes on › Packages (› its name
  on a version's or the versions' page); a repository's page › Repositories; Set up client › Repositories › the key; a folder or a file
  › Repositories › the key › its folders. While the repositories are hidden there is no step **Repositories**, Set up client ends at the
  project and names no repository, and a file's way goes Projects › the project › the key › its folders: the key is the root folder's name,
  as every download address of the files has it (Q-BAS-504). No step is `<project>/<key>`.
- **The start** links each project to where its way leads; its section **Files** stands only while the repositories are shown. A project's
  packages keep their section **Files** in both modes ([Q-BAS-508](#q-bas-508--a-projects-list-keeps-its-repositories-with-files-in-both-modes)).
- **The sitemap** (R-BAS-122). While the repositories are shown, each project the sitemap lists has its repositories (before its list, the
  `lastmod` of its list) and each public repository of those projects its page, in the order of their names: a root of files without
  `lastmod` as before, any other with the newest `updatedAt` of its index, none for one without a package. Hidden, the set is the one
  before W-40: no project's repositories and no repository's page but the roots of files. The set's revision includes the switch.

*Built on 2026-11-27 (W-40's P2):* the kinds `Project`, `Repositories` and `Repository` of
[address.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/page/address.go) and the words of [texts.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/page/texts.go);
`repositoriesPage`, `repositoryPage`, `projectTrail`, `repositoryTrail` and `projectRoute` of [seo.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/seo.go);
`repositoryPages` of [crawl.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/crawl.go). The project Upstream's description and the well-known repositories'
names stay the stored English text until W-40's P7 gives the Go table its words.
