## Disabling a Bastion

The owner's words of 2026-11-27, looking at the dialog that disabled a Bastion by refusing its tokens: "Es muss eine Möglichkeit geben,
bei voller Konnektivität zwischen Hauptinstanz und Bastion den Bastion sekundenschnell zu deaktivieren. Nicht wie hier über einen
synthetischen Timeout. Ich klicke auf Deaktivieren des Bastions und diesem wird direkt mitgeteilt: Arbeit einstellen. Zwei Wege, Soft
und Hard: Soft lässt noch alle Downloads, die bereits begonnen haben, weiterlaufen, aber keine neuen mehr zu. Hard bricht auch aktuelle
Downloads ab." Plan W-41, D3 and D5 to D10.

### R-BAS-133 · Disabling a Bastion: soft or hard, told over its connection
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: DIST-025

- **A member of the configuration** ([Q-BAS-512](#q-bas-512--disable-is-a-member-of-the-configuration-told-over-the-connection-the-token-is-not-touched)).
  A registration carries `disabled`: `null` while the Bastion works, `soft` (no new request is admitted; every request in flight, a
  download that started and the fill it reads, finishes) or `hard` (the same, and every request in flight and every fill is cut), with
  the time it was set (`disabled_at`, set again by a change from soft to hard). It is a member of the configuration the handshake sends
  (`iface.Configuration.disabled`, R-BAS-093), raises the registration's revision, and is stored with the configuration a replica keeps
  (`configuration/current.json`), so a replica restarted during an outage keeps it. The registration's principal and its tokens are not
  touched: the Bastion keeps its line to the main installation.
- **The API and the command line.** `PATCH /api/v1/bastions/{name}` `{"disabled": "soft"|"hard"|null}` (`endpoints:write`, no recent
  authentication: a disable narrows, and an enable restores a state the administrator had); absent is unchanged, `null` enables, any
  other value is `400` at `/disabled`. Soft to hard is allowed at any time; hard to soft changes nothing that runs. `quader admin bastion
  disable <name> [--hard]` and `quader admin bastion enable <name>` do the same from a `web` pod (R-AUTH-015's pattern). The
  registration reads `disabled` `{mode, at}` or null, `state` and `running`; `state` and `running` also for a holder of `limits:read`.
- **Told within seconds.** `bastion.disabled` and `bastion.enabled` map to the feed's `settings` entry (R-BAS-015): every replica
  handshakes again within one poll of the feed (`bastions.feed.poll_interval`, 2 s, plus a round trip: about 3 s) and applies its
  registration's configuration whole. The change area `bastion_configuration` brings it into every main replica's snapshot of the
  registrations within the bound of R-ARCH-018 (2 s).
- **The main installation refuses the disabled Bastion's work** ([Q-BAS-513](#q-bas-513--while-disabled-the-main-installation-refuses-the-bastions-work-and-keeps-its-line-open)).
  From its snapshot, the recognition stage (R-BAS-008) answers a forward, the check and the four catalogue routes of a disabled
  registration `503 bastion_disabled`, a problem of the interface that the Bastion never passes on; the handshake, the feed and the
  download intake answer as before, so the Bastion learns the disable, confirms it and reports the downloads a soft disable lets finish.
  A hard disable cancels the registration's forwards in flight on every main replica as its snapshot takes it.
- **The Bastion's answer** ([Q-BAS-514](#q-bas-514--a-disabled-bastion-answers-503-in-the-formats-shape-and-names-no-disable)). While
  disabled, every new request gets `503` with `Retry-After: 300` capped per format (R-BAS-091), in the format's error shape with the code
  and the detail of the Bastion's own `503 unavailable` (R-BAS-029, R-BAS-099: it names nothing of the main installation and does not say
  "disabled"); the web interface's pages a `503` page in its shape ("Not available at the moment. Try again later."); its data path,
  `robots.txt` and the sitemap `503`. Readiness is unchanged, so the ingress keeps answering in the Bastion's shape. A replica sends the
  main installation nothing but the handshake, the feed and its status batches: the catalogue's sync pauses, the cache stays as it is.
  A `503 bastion_disabled` to a forward or a check (a request that raced the disable) makes the replica handshake at once.
  `quader_bastion_disabled{mode}` is 1 while it applies a disable. *Built on 2026-11-27 (W-41's A2):* `stepDisabled`, `operation` and
  `Operation` of [disable.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/disable.go) (the gate after the path's family, the requests counted, a hard
  disable's cut of every request and of the request a fill holds, `newHold`), `ErrDisabled` of the client and the link's handshake at
  once ([client.go](../../internal/bastion/mainclient/client.go), [link.go](../../internal/bastion/link/link.go)), `unavailable` of the
  web interface ([refusal.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/refusal.go)) with its words in [texts.go](../../internal/bastion/gui/page/texts.go),
  the catalogue's `Paused`, the status's `operation` ([status.go](../../internal/bastion/server/status.go)) and the gauge of the
  [holder](../../internal/bastion/settings/holder.go).
- **The confirmation and the state** ([Q-BAS-511](#q-bas-511--the-bastions-state-is-one-of-six-computed-by-the-main-installation),
  [Q-BAS-515](#q-bas-515--the-bastion-confirms-with-its-status)). Every replica's status (`iface.ReplicaStatus`, sent with every flush, 1 s)
  carries `operation` `{disabled, running}`: the way of the configuration it applies and the requests of its callers it has in flight. A
  replica confirms when a status reported after the disable names the same way. The main installation computes the state once
  (`bastionmain.StateOf`), for the API and the command line:

| `state` | When |
|---|---|
| `connected` | not disabled; a replica was heard (a contact or a status) within 5 minutes |
| `noContact` | not disabled; no replica was ever heard |
| `contactLost` | not disabled; no replica was heard within 5 minutes |
| `disabling` | disabled; a replica heard since has not confirmed it yet, within 15 s of the disable, or the confirming replicas still run requests (`running` is their sum) |
| `disabled` | disabled; every replica heard since confirms it and runs nothing |
| `disableUnconfirmed` | disabled; 15 s after the disable a replica heard since has not confirmed it, or none was heard since; at once when no replica was heard in the 5 minutes before the disable |

- **Audit, journal and restore** ([Q-BAS-516](#q-bas-516--audit-journal-and-restore-of-a-disable)). `bastion.disabled` carries
  `details.mode` and the journal entry `{principalId, name, mode}`; `bastion.enabled` none. The replay of `bastion.disabled` disables
  the registration in the entry's way and never more lightly than it is (a hard one stays hard); the replay of `bastion.deleted` disables
  it hard, and the deletion's own `token.revoked` entries revoke its tokens. An enable after the restore point is not replayed.
- **The token is not the Bastion** ([Q-BAS-517](#q-bas-517--the-declared-token-is-invalidated-on-the-api-and-no-token-is-issued-beside-it)).
  A disabled registration's token stays valid. Revoking a token is the last resort and works on every token, the declared one of
  R-BAS-127 included; a declared registration gets no token issued on the API (`409 managed_by_config`).
- **The fallback while the connection is down.** Nothing reaches a Bastion that cannot reach the main installation: it is unreachable
  already (R-BAS-027), serves its cache for its grace period and then nothing; the disable is stored on the registration and applied at
  its first handshake, before it serves a request through the main installation, which refuses those anyway. The state reads
  `disableUnconfirmed` meanwhile.
- **Upgrade** ([Q-BAS-518](#q-bas-518--a-registration-disabled-by-its-principals-status-becomes-disabled-hard)). Migration 00158 turns a
  registration disabled before by its principal's status into one disabled hard, with its principal active again.

*Built on 2026-11-27 (W-41's A1), the main installation's part:* migration
[00158_bastion_disable.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00158_bastion_disable.sql); `BastionSetDisabled` and
`BastionReplayDisable` of [bastion_registration.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/bastion_registration.sql); `setDisable`,

[bastion-card.ts](../../web/src/app/features/bastions/bastion-card.ts),

card is disabling or not confirmed.

## What a Bastion may distribute

The owner's words of 2026-11-27, looking at his Bastion's card: "Was mir hier auch noch fehlt, ist die Möglichkeit, die Nutzung des Bastion
administrativ einzuschränken bzw. freizugeben. Ich wäre für Whitelisting: Ein Admin muss also freigeben, welche Projekte ihre Repos über den
Bastion zur Verteilung freigeben dürfen. Die Visibility eines Repos „öffentlich" war von Anfang an auf die Hauptinstanz bezogen, meistens
im Intranet der Firma. Eine Verteilung eines öffentlichen Repos über die interne Verteilung hinaus, z.B. über einen Bastion, muss separat
vom Project Owner konfiguriert werden." They supersede [Q-BAS-6](#q-bas-6--a-caller-reads-what-its-token-may-read-there-is-no-release-step)'s
"there is no release step of its own".

### R-BAS-134 · What a Bastion may distribute: the administrator's projects and the owner's choice
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

What leaves the main installation's network through a Bastion is granted twice
([Q-BAS-519](#q-bas-519--an-administrator-allows-projects-per-bastion-and-a-new-bastion-allows-none)): an administrator allows projects
per Bastion, and a project's Owner chooses per repository the Bastions that distribute it, among those that allow the project. A level
stays the main installation's: `public` means public on its network, and a repository of any level is distributed through a Bastion only
while it is chosen there ([Q-BAS-520](#q-bas-520--every-level-needs-the-choice-not-only-public)).

- **The administrator's list.** The rows of `bastion_project` (migration `00159`): a project per Bastion, since when and by whom. A new
  Bastion allows none. `GET /api/v1/bastions/{name}/projects` (`endpoints:read`) lists them by project key, each with its display name,
  `allowedAt`, `allowedBy` and the keys of its repositories that chose the Bastion, `q` filtering by key or display name, paged by
  cursor, with `totals` of the whole list (the projects allowed and the repositories distributed). `PUT …/projects/{projectKey}`
  (`endpoints:write`, idempotent, no `If-Match`: it binds one pair) allows a project and records `bastion.project.allowed`; a repeat records
  nothing. `DELETE …/projects/{projectKey}` (`endpoints:write`) takes it off and, in the same transaction, deletes its repositories'
  choices of that Bastion: allowing it again distributes nothing until the Owner chooses again. `404` for a registration or a project that
  does not exist, and for a removal of a project the Bastion does not allow.
- **The Owner's choice** ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004, Q-REPO-491). The repository document's
  member `bastions`, rows of `repository_bastion`: written with the document by the project's Owner or a holder of
  `repositories:write-config` (the people who set its levels, [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033), never a Maintainer. A
  name of a Bastion that does not allow the project answers `422 validation_failed` with `bastion_not_allowed` at `/bastions/<i>`.
  `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectKey}/bastions` (the Owner, or `repositories:read-config`) lists what may be chosen: each Bastion that
  allows the project with whether it is disabled, whether its web interface is on, and its `addresses`. Every reader of a repository reads
  the member, in the full document, the consumer view and the list of repositories (R-REPO-012); the search and the package views do not
  carry it yet (W-41's D1): `{name, addresses, disabled}`, `addresses` being the base URLs its
  deployments reported within the last 24 hours that are entries of `server.additional_base_urls` (as R-BAS-007 holds a client setup's).
  A write takes a name or that object, whose `addresses` and `disabled` are ignored; the repositories of the project `upstream` take it
  from an administrator as their other open members (R-REPO-069).
- **The database holds the rule.** A choice exists only while its Bastion allows the repository's project: a row written around the API
  is refused (SQLSTATE `AI011`), a project taken off a list takes its choices with it, and a repository that moves to another project
  loses its choices (R-REPO-060), each in the statement's transaction.
- **Events, journal, feed** ([Q-BAS-521](#q-bas-521--a-narrowing-of-the-distribution-is-journaled-and-tells-every-bastion-at-once)).
  `bastion.project.allowed`, `bastion.project.removed` (with the repositories whose choice went), `repository.bastion.added`,
  `repository.bastion.removed` (cause `owner` or `move`). The two removals are journaled, `{bastionId, projectId}` and
  `{repositoryId, bastionId}`, and the replay deletes the rows again after a restore to a point before them. The feed maps a widening to
  `settings` and a narrowing to `grants` and `settings` (R-BAS-015). Every change announces the change area `bastion_distribution`, after
  which the public catalogue's builder starts a run (R-BAS-105).

*Built on 2026-11-27 (W-41's B1):* the tables and their guards ([00159_bastion_distribution.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00159_bastion_distribution.sql)),
the statements of [bastion_distribution.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/bastion_distribution.sql), the list's service in
[distribution.go](../../internal/bastionmain/distribution.go) and the replays of [distribution_replay.go](../../internal/bastionmain/distribution_replay.go),
the feed's mapping of [feed.go](../../internal/bastionmain/feed.go), the member of [bastions.go](../../internal/repository/bastions.go),
the move's part of [move.go](../../internal/project/move.go), [bastion_projects_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_projects_api.go)
and the OpenAPI document, the events of [events_bastion_distribution.go](../../internal/audit/events_bastion_distribution.go).
*Not built:* the ceiling (W-41's B2, [authorization.md](authorization.md)): nothing decides a request through a Bastion on the
distribution yet, so a Bastion serves what it served before; the card's section **Projects** (W-41's C2) and the repository's group
**Bastions** with its mark (W-41's D1).

  without its IDs, the two widenings not); `TestR_BAS_134_TheFeedTellsTheBastionsOfADistributionChange` (settings for a widening, grants and
  settings for a narrowing); `TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified` covers the new events.
- Unit ([bastions_test.go](../../internal/repository/bastions_test.go)): `TestR_BAS_134_TheMemberBastions` (a name or the read's object,

- Unit ([bastion_projects_test.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_projects_test.go)): `TestR_BAS_134_WhoChangesWhatABastionMayDistribute`
  (the list's writes refused with `endpoints:read`; the declarations of the six operations); `TestR_BAS_134_TheAddressesAreTheListedOnes`.
- Integration (area `bastionreg`, [distribution_test.go](../../test/integration/bastionreg/distribution_test.go), about 5 s, a handful of
