### Q-BAS-152 · The ID of an applied entry is kept until a read behind which it lies no longer returns it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: finding F-116. `TestBastion_R_BAS_049_RoutingByPath` failed in the runs 42530616876, 43401661890 and 43578163061: every tarball request of the measurement went to the main installation as a revalidation. The Bastion kept the
ID of an applied entry for at least 5 minutes and 15 seconds after its receipt (Q-BAS-126), on the assumption that the feed sends an
entry again for its lookback after it was first received. The lookback is measured behind the cursor (R-BAS-015), and the cursor names
the last entry, so while no entry is committed every read returns the same window, for as long as the feed stays quiet. 5 minutes and
15 seconds after the first receipt the replica forgot the IDs, the next read applied the same `grants` and `content` entries again with a
new receipt time, and every URL answer and cache entry validated within 15 s before that was unusable (R-BAS-020 rule 3, R-BAS-022);
with the IDs recorded again, the cycle would repeat while the feed stayed quiet. In the e2e suite the fixture's packages are
the last entries, and the test runs about 5 minutes and 30 seconds after them. The replica logs of the runs show it: in 43578163061 every
tarball validated before 09:14:43.66 was revalidated and every later one was a hit, which puts a re-application at about 09:14:28.6, some
5 minutes and 17 seconds after the npm packages the fixture published from 09:09:10.6 were first received as `content` entries of
the repository (the time is inferred from the boundary; the Bastion logs no applied entry); in 43401661890 the npm publishes of 09:41:41.5 to 42.2
were applied again at about 09:46:58, and the measurement ran from 09:47:11.3 to 12.1. The two content entries the diagnostics saw
during that measurement were the NuGet pushes of 09:41:53, applied again in the same way. The baseline run 44186978088 failed the same way: npm publishes at
22:22:00.5 to 01.1, every request of the test from 22:27:29.8 to 32.9 revalidated, and the re-application at about 22:27:17 lay before
the warm-up, so the count since the warm-up was 0. A re-application counts in `quader_bastion_feed_entries_applied_total` like a first
one (`link.applyEntries` counts every entry `FeedLog.Record` accepts): each failing run shows 88 content entries applied by the time of
the test, the first run with this decision (44191314996) shows 44, every entry once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A read whose cursor lies after an entry and that does not return it ends the entry's ID; the cursor never moves backwards (chosen) | The behind part of a read is complete (R-BAS-015 resets rather than cut it) and the window only moves forward, so an entry that left it cannot come back | Exact for any `bastions.feed.lookback`, no clock is compared, no interface change; H-470 goes | The IDs of a quiet feed's window stay in memory, at most one window |
| (b) Keep the IDs for the longest lookback the configuration allows (1 hour) | A time again | One constant | Still wrong for a feed that is quiet for longer than an hour; a re-application then repeats every hour |
| (c) Measure the window behind the time of the read at the main installation | The feed re-sends an entry for the lookback after it was committed | The Bastion's time rule would hold | A Bastion that was cut off longer than the lookback misses a late commit the cursor-relative window catches |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** the main installation already returns, on every read, the complete set of entries the Bastion could see again; the
Bastion only has to stop forgetting what that set still contains. A content or grants entry that a replica applies for the first time
still makes the entries validated in the 15 s before unusable, as R-BAS-022 specifies: that is the margin of R-BAS-020 and not a defect.
The synthetic cursor of an empty read moves to the time of the read only when that is later than the cursor (Q-BAS-76), so a Bastion clock
behind the main installation's cannot widen the window again.

**Paging.** The rule holds for every page, also one that says `more`, because `limit` never cuts the entries behind the cursor:
R-BAS-015 reads them in a query of their own that returns all of them within the lookback (`BastionFeedBehind`, bounded at four times
`max_page`, beyond which the answer is `reset: true` and the log is emptied), and only the entries after the cursor are cut by `limit`
(`BastionFeedAhead`, ordered by `(occurred_at, id)`). An entry before the cursor that a page leaves out therefore lies outside the
lookback; entries after the cursor that the page cut away lie at or after the cursor's time, which Settle never forgets. A synthetic
cursor (the start, or after an empty read) is the same with the nil ID: the entries before its time within the lookback are all sent. At
the start the log holds no ID, so the first read forgets nothing; each later page's cursor is the last entry of the page before, and
the IDs of start-read entries that fall more than the lookback behind it go, which they may, since the window does not move back.
`TestR_BAS_015_MoreEntriesBehindTheCursorThanFourPagesResets` pins the main installation's side (eight entries behind a cursor with
`max_page: 2` are all returned), `TestR_BAS_026_PagesWithMoreEntriesThanTheLimitInsideTheLookbackApplyEachEntryOnce` the Bastion's: a
start read of 150 entries and a burst of 120 within a second, pages of 50, every entry applied once through ten quiet minutes, and the
log keeping exactly the IDs of the window behind the last cursor; with a feed that cut the entries behind the cursor at the limit the
test applies 25 entries twice. The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-026; code: `answers.FeedLog.Settle`, `link.pollOnce`;
`TestR_BAS_026_AQuietFeedThatReSendsAnEntryPastItsLookbackDoesNotApplyItAgain`, `TestR_BAS_026_AnAppliedIDIsKeptWhileTheFeedSendsItsEntry`,
`TestR_BAS_026_PagesWithMoreEntriesThanTheLimitInsideTheLookbackApplyEachEntryOnce`.

### Q-BAS-153 · A stale answer in a replica's memory does not hide the one Valkey holds

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `TestBastion_R_BAS_049_FailedAuthenticationTimeout` failed once (run 43698804297): `$FULL`, used from the address before the
timeout, answered `429 auth_timeout`. The replica logs show why. Replica `x2nsv` had obtained `$FULL`'s credential answer at 09:43:13.8,
seven seconds before; the last request reached replica `ldx5d`, whose memory still held its own answer of `$FULL` from 09:42:38, older
than the e2e period of 30 s. The store found that copy in memory, judged it expired and returned no answer without reading Valkey, so
the replica had no usable answer for `$FULL` and the timeout of R-BAS-036 refused it, although the Bastion as a whole held a usable one.
The same lookup made a stale shape or URL answer cost a request to the main installation that a shared answer would have saved.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A memory copy that fails a rule is dropped and Valkey is read (chosen) | Memory is a cache of the shared store and never hides a newer record | Every replica sees what any replica obtained; one Valkey read per stale copy | None found |
| (b) Refresh the credential answer of a caller in the background before it expires | No stale copy for a caller who keeps coming | Fewer misses | A request per caller and period to the main installation; a replica that did not see the caller still has no answer |
| (c) Accept it | A replica decides by its own memory | Nothing to change | A colleague behind an address in the timeout is refused depending on which replica the ingress picks, which R-BAS-036 rules out |

**Choice:** (a).

**Rationale:** R-BAS-034 shares answers so that a replica does not ask what another one knows; reading Valkey only on a miss in memory
defeated that for exactly the callers a replica had seen before. The rules of R-BAS-020 judge the record from Valkey as they judge the copy,
so nothing becomes usable that is not. The development agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-034, R-BAS-036; code: `engine.answerStore.get`;
`TestR_BAS_036_AStaleAnswerInMemoryDoesNotHideTheFreshOneAnotherReplicaShares`.

### Q-BAS-154 · Routing by path hashes the path alone, so HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 clients meet

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: found while reading F-116 (the HAProxy Ingress logs of run 43578163061). The chart rendered `balance-algorithm: uri`, which
HAProxy hashes over the URI as received. An HTTP/1.1 request carries the path alone; an HTTP/2 request carries the scheme and the
authority as well (HAProxy logs it as `https://bastion-volume…:8093/api/npm/…`). The npm clients of the cold runs sent HTTP/1.1, `curl`
of `TestBastion_R_BAS_049_RoutingByPath` HTTP/2, and 18 of the 36 tarball paths reached the other replica, which did not hold them: the
warm-up round of the test was 18 misses and 18 revalidations. Both HAProxy Ingress pods agreed on the slots (`srv001`, `srv002`), so the
request form, not the controller, split the paths. HAProxy 2.8, the version in the controller image `v0.16.3`, documents `path-only`:
"the hashing key starts at the first '/' of the path ... to make sure that HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 URIs will provide the same hash".

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `balance-algorithm: uri path-only` (chosen) | The hash covers the path up to the query, whatever the HTTP version | One word; R-BAS-033 holds for every client | None found |
| (b) Keep `uri` | Each path may live on two replicas, one per HTTP version | Nothing to change | Twice the volume for clients of both versions, and a miss for the second |

**Choice:** (a). The controller copies the value verbatim into `balance` and checks no list of algorithms (`annotations/updater.go`
and `haproxy.tmpl` at `v0.16.3`).

**Rationale:** R-BAS-033 promises one replica per artifact; the HTTP version of a client is not part of the artifact. The development
agent records no revisit condition.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-033, R-BAS-045; code: `deploy/helm/quader-bastion/templates/ingress.yaml`; `TestR_BAS_033_RouteByPath`,
`TestBastion_R_BAS_049_RoutingByPath` (the warm-up finds every path on the replica the cold runs filled).


### Q-BAS-164 · The malware scanning's events in the feed: a find and a withdrawn release are `content`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The owner decided
on 2026-11-20 that a later find reaches the Bastions as a feed entry ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) Q-MAL-12).

Context: a verdict belongs to a blob, and a blob may be held by many repositories; the journal's entries of `malware.found` and
`malware.release.withdrawn` name the digest, not a repository.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `content` for every repository that holds the blob when the feed is read, and their virtual repositories (chosen) | The main installation resolves the digest to repositories as it resolves virtual repositories today | Only the caches that may hold the bytes are touched | A blob held by many repositories names them all |
| (b) `grants` | Every answer of the Bastion is asked again | Simple | Empties the Bastion's whole cache for one find |
| (c) A new kind `blob` with the digest | The Bastion drops entries by digest | Exact | A new kind in the Bastion's interface, and the Bastion's cache is keyed by URL, not by digest |

**Choice:** (a); the switch turned on maps to no entry (H-1102). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-015.

### Q-BAS-165 · The registry root is a path family of the Bastion at its own host root

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. That a Bastion
serves images is the owner's (2026-11-22, [Every format](#every-format)).

Context: Docker and OCI clients fix the API at `/v2/` on the root of a host (R-OCI-001). The Bastion serves no web interface, so its
host root is free; the deferred table assumed a Bastion host per host-root binding, which is a different case (R-OCI-029).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/v2/…` is a family of the Bastion at the host root of its `server.base_url`, mirrored like `/api/<format>/` (chosen) | `packages.example.com/web/docker/library/nginx:1.29` | The main installation's address scheme on the Bastion's host; one `docker login` for every repository; the snippets of R-BAS-007 already render this prefix | A family the Bastion has to classify beside `/api/` and `/files/` |
| (b) A Bastion host per bound repository only | One repository per Bastion release | No new family | Every repository a partner pulls needs a release and a binding; not "like the main installation" |
| (c) A Bastion of its own per format | Format releases | Narrow | A second chart configuration per format; the owner's "alles" in several pieces |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the registry root is a family of INV-6 like `/files/`, not a format: the Bastion learns one more
family and no format. The planner would revisit this if a second format ever needed a host-root family of its own.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-003, R-BAS-018, R-BAS-050, R-BAS-051; [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) Q-OCI-23.

### Q-BAS-166 · The token service at a Bastion is the main installation's, reached by a forward

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: the registry's token flow (R-OCI-004) sends a client to the realm of the challenge, which the main installation renders on the
host it answers for, the Bastion's (R-BAS-017). A registry token is signed with a key derived from the main installation's key ring
(R-OCI-005); a Bastion holds none and must hold none (Q-BAS-1, Q-BAS-7).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `/v2/_token` is forwarded with the caller's credential; the main installation's token service issues the token (chosen) | The realm is the Bastion's `/v2/_token`, answered by the main installation | One issuer; every rule of R-OCI-004 and R-OCI-005 holds unchanged; the Bastion holds no key | Each pull costs the main installation a token request |
| (b) The Bastion issues registry tokens | A key at the Bastion | No round trip | A minting key in the DMZ (H-579's power at the internet's edge); the Bastion would decide who gets which grant |
| (c) A `Basic` challenge instead of the token flow | Clients send the Quader token on every request | No token requests; stable credential keys | An anonymous Docker client cannot pull behind a `Basic` challenge; the long-lived token crosses the wire on every request; the Bastion would rewrite the main installation's challenge |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the token service decides grants, which is a decision about a caller and the main installation's alone.
The planner would revisit (c) never, and (b) only with asymmetric registry tokens whose public key a Bastion could hold to verify, not to
sign.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-051.

### Q-BAS-167 · A registry token is checked by the main installation, and its read shape is at most partial

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-22**, after the owner's word that its favourite is built and not what was built
first: option (b); built as (a) until R-BAS-080 to R-BAS-088 are. *Superseded in place on 2026-11-22: decided by the planner in the
owner's absence, put to the owner as a question the same day, with (a) recommended and built meanwhile.*

Context: almost every image client reads with registry tokens of five minutes (R-OCI-005). A grant names image names and is checked by the
enforcement point in front of `/v2/`, not by the decision point that computes a read shape ([mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go)
lines 169 to 185, Q-OCI-56); a `full` answer computed without the grant would let a token granted one image read every cached image of
the repository.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An opaque credential checked by forwards and the check, its shape capped at `partial` (built) | Every cached artifact is served after a conditional request with the token (`304`, no transfer) | Exact; no change of the decision point or the interface beyond the cap; every byte of a warm pull comes from the Bastion | A warm pull costs the main installation one request per manifest and blob, and counts against the address's miss limit ([H-1242](#h-1242--every-pull-with-a-registry-token-costs-the-main-installation-its-token-request-and-one-check)) |
| (b) Read shapes per package: the marking names the package of a response and the caller's shape on it, the check answers per package (chosen) | A token granted `library/nginx` is `full` on that image, served from the cache without a request | Takes the requests off the main installation for images, and for every reader narrowed by package patterns (npm's `$PART`) | A new shape in the decision point, a new member of the interface, entries keyed by package; the larger change |
| (c) Asymmetric registry tokens the Bastion verifies | The Bastion reads the grant and keys answers by the Quader token behind it | No request for a token's warm reads | A change of the token's signature; the Bastion would need the registry's path grammar to read the grant, format knowledge it must not hold |

**Choice:** (b), specified in [Read shapes per package](#read-shapes-per-package) and decided in detail in Q-BAS-240 to Q-BAS-254; (a)
stays built until R-BAS-080 to R-BAS-088 are. **Rationale:** the first use of a public Bastion is a cluster pulling images behind one
address, and under (a) each warm pull of an image of ten layers costs the main installation twelve requests against that address's miss
limit of 300 a minute, so a rollout of about twenty pulls a minute reaches it; (b) brings a warm pull to its token request and one check
(about 100 pulls a minute behind one address) and keeps correctness, because a package answer is the main installation's statement about
the caller, limited to the grant on both sides. With a single platform, a config and ten layers, a warm Docker pull falls from 14 requests
to 3 (derived from the read flow, not measured; R-BAS-088's measurement writes the numbers down). *Superseded in place on 2026-11-22: the choice was (a), with (b) as the revisit once
a measurement showed the conditional requests matter; the rationale was correctness first and the smaller change.*

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-052, R-BAS-053, R-BAS-080 to R-BAS-088; Deferred (its row removed).

### Q-BAS-168 · An anonymous registry token is the anonymous caller at the Bastion

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: an anonymous client gets an anonymous registry token from the token service and pulls with it (R-OCI-004). Keyed by its string,
every anonymous pull would be a stranger to the Bastion: no shared answer, no shared document, the anonymous share of the budget spent
on each pull. At the main installation such a token "stands for a request without a credential" (`byRegistryToken` in
[stage.go](../../internal/auth/stage.go)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Bastion decodes the payload without verifying it; a token whose claims name the anonymous principal is dropped and the request is anonymous (chosen) | Answers under `anonymous`, forwards without `Authorization` | Every anonymous pull of a public image shares one set of answers and documents; trusting the bit can only lower what is read | The Bastion reads the payload format of R-OCI-005 (core, not a format) |
| (b) An opaque token like any other | No reading of the payload | Nothing to learn | Each anonymous pull costs the main installation its requests; the anonymous budget fills with pulls of public images |
| (c) The Bastion answers anonymous token requests itself with a marker | A token of its own | No token request reaches the main installation | An answer of the Bastion's own that imitates the token service; `quader_oci_registry_tokens_total{outcome="anonymous"}` misses them |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a request without a credential is always possible, so treating a token that claims to be anonymous as
none grants nothing. The planner would revisit it if the anonymous registry token ever carried something the main installation decides
on beyond its grant.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-052.

### Q-BAS-169 · The Bastion's own answers below /v2/ are in the distribution's error shape

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Below `/v2/` the Bastion's own answers carry `Docker-Distribution-API-Version` and the distribution's error body, the Quader code in `detail` (chosen) | A renderer per family | What R-OCI-003 promises of every answer below `/v2/`; clients print a message they understand | A second shape in the Bastion, by family |
| (b) Problem details as on every other family (R-BAS-029) | One shape | Simple | A client reads `unknown` errors; the API version header missing on a refusal |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the shape belongs to the family, which the Bastion knows, not to a format. **Applied in the spec:**
R-BAS-029, R-BAS-051.

### Q-BAS-170 · A format's facts reach the Bastion in the handshake

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: a few facts of a format matter to the Bastion before or without a response of the main installation: which headers a cached
answer replays, which status its own rate-limit refusal takes (the ClamAV definitions never answer `429`, R-CLAMAV-005), which format
serves the registry root and which prefixes a bound host has.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The handshake carries a table of the formats' facts (chosen) | `formats` and `boundRepository` in R-BAS-010's answer | Known before the first request of a format; a format to come brings its facts as data, no code of the Bastion changes | The interface rises to version 4 |
| (b) A header on every marked response | Per response | No table | The Bastion's own refusals happen before any response of the format; the facts arrive too late |
| (c) Code per format in the Bastion | A table compiled in | No interface change | Format knowledge in the Bastion; a format to come needs a Bastion change and a release of both sides |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-057.

### Q-BAS-171 · A cached answer replays the headers its format declares, held by the kit

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: a cached entry replays the representation headers only ([respond.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/respond.go) lines 142 to
155), so `Docker-Content-Digest` and `Link` are lost on a hit and present on a miss.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The core's representation headers and the format's declared `ReplayHeaders`; kit check 19 fails a content route that sets an undeclared header (chosen) | An allow-list per format | A header that names the caller can never be replayed to another; an omission is found by the kit, not by a client | A declaration per format that has protocol headers |
| (b) Replay every header but a deny list | Keep all | No declaration | A per-caller header of the core that is added later is replayed to every caller of a shared document |
| (c) Representation headers only (as built) | — | — | A hit differs from a miss |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-053, R-BAS-057, R-BAS-058.

### Q-BAS-172 · A ranged miss streams from the spool and a caller of a running fill follows it on its own permission

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: a layer of gigabytes takes minutes to fill. A caller's `Range` on a miss waits for the whole fill before its first byte, and a
second caller of the same key waits 30 s and is then answered `503 busy` ([fill.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/fill.go)
`waitFill`, [readflow.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/readflow.go) `waitLeader`). A rollout whose pods pull one new image through a
Bastion is exactly that.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A range streams from the spool with its tail withheld until the commit; a second caller asks its own permission and follows the spool; across replicas a waiter waits while the lock is extended, up to `fill_wait_max` (chosen) | The leader's way for every caller of the replica | One transfer from the main installation for any number of callers; first bytes at once; no `503` for a large layer | A second reader of a spool that is still written; across replicas a waiter still gets no byte until the other fill commits (H-1245) |
| (b) As built | — | Nothing to build | Large layers answer `503` to every caller but one for their whole fill; clients retry into the same answer |
| (c) A waiter fetches itself after the wait | No `503` | Simple | As many transfers of the layer as callers |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-021, R-BAS-025, R-BAS-054.

### Q-BAS-173 · A shared answer above the memory bound is spooled by its content address

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: a document is held in memory up to 64 MiB and passed through above it, without the caller's `Range`
([forward.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/forward.go) lines 21 and 386 to 395). A ClamAV container is a document (Q-CLAMAV-2), and
R-CLAMAV-006 says a run of the three files fetches about 110 MiB; whether `main.cvd` alone passes 64 MiB was not measured here.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A shared answer above the memory bound whose strong `ETag` is a content address is filled through the spool like an artifact, kept in the documents' area and revalidated like a document (chosen) | One rule for every format | A large document is served from the cache, `Range` included; no format knowledge | A second way into the documents' area |
| (b) Pass through as built | — | Nothing to build | Every `freshclam` check of a large container transfers it whole from the main installation |
| (c) Raise the memory bound | Larger buffers | Simple | Memory per replica for one document; the next format's larger file passes again |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-021, R-BAS-056.

### Q-BAS-174 · Debian: the release documents are documents of the metadata period, and by-hash keeps an apt update consistent

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: an `apt update` reads an `InRelease` and then the indexes it names. A Bastion that holds an `InRelease` of an older generation
must not hand out indexes that disagree with it. Every release Quader writes announces by-hash (R-DEB-011), the main installation keeps
the by-hash files of three generations and `by_hash_keep` (R-DEB-012), and the Debian and Ubuntu archives announce by-hash too.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The release documents and the plain indexes are documents of the metadata period; by-hash files are immutable artifacts (chosen) | The kinds of R-DEB-003 decide, no rule of the format | An `apt update` storm costs the main installation one conditional request per suite and period; APT fetches by hash, which cannot disagree | A plain index path (an upstream without by-hash, a flat repository) can disagree with the `InRelease` for up to the period ([H-1243](#h-1243--a-plain-index-path-of-a-debian-remote-without-by-hash-can-disagree-with-the-inrelease-a-bastion-serves)) |
| (b) The release documents are revalidated on every request | A conditional per `apt update` | Exact for every client | The main installation answers every `apt update` of every client; the Bastion takes no load off for metadata |
| (c) Plain index paths are never kept | `pass` for them | Exact for clients without by-hash | A whole index transfer per such request; needs a route-level rule of the format |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** by-hash is what APT uses against exactly this race, also at the main installation between two of its
replicas. The planner would revisit (b) for the release documents if a "Hash Sum mismatch" through a Bastion is reported.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-055.

### Q-BAS-175 · The withdrawals of OCI, Debian and Ansible Galaxy are content entries

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `oci.manifest.deleted`, the four `deb.*` events and `ansible.version.deleted` are `content` for the repository and its virtual repositories; `ansible.tombstone.cleared` none (chosen) | As `package.deleted` | Withdrawn content ends at every Bastion within the feed's bound | A promotion of a Debian key also ends the service of the repository's cached entries, which then revalidate (`304` for the pool files) |
| (b) `grants` | Every answer | Simple | Empties every Bastion's answers for one deleted manifest |
| (c) None (as built) | — | — | A deleted image or a withheld package stays servable for up to `artifact_revalidate_after` |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-015, R-BAS-055.

### Q-BAS-176 · The ClamAV definitions through a Bastion: anonymous and tokens, no client certificate

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below. **Put to the owner as a question on
2026-11-22** (he decided the certificates on 2026-11-21, Q-REPO-415); the recommendation (a) is built in meanwhile.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: the certificate subject exists only on an endpoint whose TLS ends at Quader (Q-CLAMAV-8); a Bastion's TLS ends at the Bastion,
and its forward reaches the default endpoint, which admits no certificates (R-CLAMAV-010).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The endpoint is served through a Bastion to the anonymous caller and to tokens; the certificate admission stays a further endpoint of the main installation (chosen) | `PrivateMirror https://packages.example.com/api/clamav/upstream/clamav` at `public` | Nothing new to trust; a ClamAV outside the company updates from the Bastion at the default level | An installation outside that must use a certificate reaches the main installation's certificate endpoint, not the Bastion ([H-1247](#h-1247--the-certificate-admission-of-the-clamav-definitions-does-not-reach-a-bastion)) |
| (b) The Bastion verifies client certificates and vouches for them to the main installation | A header signed with the Bastion token | Certificates through a Bastion | The main installation would take a certificate's identity from a header, which Q-CLAMAV-8 excludes; the Bastion would decide who is a reader |
| (c) TLS passthrough through the Bastion to the main installation's certificate endpoint | A relay | Certificates end at Quader | No cache; the main installation's endpoint carries the load and must be reachable through the Bastion |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-056.

| (b) Artifacts only (as built) | — | Nothing to build | A warm pull of a single-platform image is reported without its manifest |
| (c) Every hit, documents included | — | Simple | An npm packument would be a download, which it is not at the main installation |

### Q-BAS-178 · A host the main installation binds is served by a Bastion whose base URL is that host

### Q-BAS-181 · The core's representation and per-request headers are two lists of the catalog, and the content headers of R-ARCH-007 are representation headers

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: R-BAS-058's header duty and Q-BAS-171 speak of "the core's representation headers" and "a header of the core's own (a
request ID, a rate-limit field)" without listing them. The Bastion keeps ten names in `keepHeader` and drops `X-Quader-Replica`,
`Cache-Status`, `Set-Cookie` and `X-Request-Id` in `neverReplayed` ([respond.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/respond.go)). The kit, the
catalog's rule for a declaration and the Bastion need the same lists; the Bastion may not import the catalog (R-BAS-001) and the kit
may not import the interface (Q-ARCH-216). Read in the code: `keepHeader` does not keep the content headers of R-ARCH-007 that
`formats.ServeRoute` puts on every content answer, so a hit from a Bastion's cache carried none of them (gap H-1250, closed with the
Bastion's side: the engine replays `catalog.RepresentationHeaders()`, held by `TestR_BAS_053_TheEnginesHeaderListsAreTheCatalogs`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Two functions of the leaf `catalog`: `RepresentationHeaders` (the ten of `keepHeader` and `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`) and `PerRequestHeaders` (`Content-Length`, `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Date`, `Age`, `X-Request-Id`, `X-Quader-Replica`, `Cache-Status`, `Retry-After`, `Quader-Resolved-From`) (chosen) | One place the kit, the catalog and a test of the engine read | A cached answer carries the headers every content answer of the main installation carries; a format cannot declare a header of the core | The engine keeps its list in code, held to the catalog's by a test (a test may import the catalog) |
| (b) The lists in the interface `iface` | The wire contract both sides import | Nothing to keep in step on the Bastion's side | Neither the kit nor the catalog may import the interface: a second copy |
| (c) The ten of `keepHeader` as built; the content headers per answer | Nothing changes at the Bastion | No change of the engine | A hit carries no `nosniff`, no sandbox policy and no resource policy |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the lists are facts about the core that every format meets, and the catalog is the leaf every layer
reads. The content headers are the same for every caller of a Bastion, since no session cookie reaches the main installation through it
(R-BAS-021), so replaying them hands no caller another's answer. The builder would revisit (b) if the Bastion's tree were allowed to
import the catalog.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-053, R-BAS-058; code: `catalog.RepresentationHeaders`, `catalog.PerRequestHeaders`
([bastion.go](../../internal/formats/catalog/bastion.go)), kit check 19.

| (a) The form of `http.CanonicalHeaderKey`; Register refuses another (chosen) | One spelling per name | An exact comparison in the kit, the catalog and the Bastion; the spelling net/http puts on the wire | The table's spelling is not the distribution specification's prose |
| (b) Any case, folded where compared | The specification's spelling | Readable declarations | Every reader folds; two declarations that differ in case both pass |
| (c) The specification's spelling, canonicalized when read | Two forms of one name | Readable declarations | The handshake and the code disagree in spelling |

### Q-BAS-184 · Kit check 19 judges what a Bastion keeps, and a route is exempt from two duties only, with a reason

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: R-BAS-058 lists the duties; open were the answers they judge, whether a document without a validator fails, and the form of
an exemption ("listed in the fixture with its reason"). The check run over the seven formats found five document routes without an
`ETag`: npm's root, dist-tags, keys and attestations, and OCI's tags list; every `Download` route and every header passed.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The header duty judges the `200`, `206` and `304` of `Download`, `Metadata` and `Computed` routes; a `Download` answer needs `Content-Length` and a content address equal to its body's SHA-256; a served document needs an `ETag` and `304` to it; `Fixture.NoBastion` exempts a route from these two duties with a reason, never from the header duty, and refuses a stale entry; the five routes are listed with H-1249 (chosen) | Strict for every format to come | The gap of today is named in the fixtures and in the specification | Five entries in two fixtures until the handlers carry validators |
| (b) A document without an `ETag` passes; only one that ignores its own fails | Lenient | No entry | A format to come without validators passes: the cost the duty exists to find |
| (c) The five routes get validators in this package | No exemption | No gap | Format handler code outside the package's directories and scope |

**Choice:** (a). The in-memory host of the kit answers `If-None-Match` with an item's content address `304`, as the production Host does
(`edge.ServeItem`), so a document a format serves from the item store meets the duty as in production. A format that writes a download
itself fails check 19 as well as check 16 (`testformat.WritesOwnDownload`). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-058; code: kit check 19
([checks_bastion.go](../../internal/formats/formattest/checks_bastion.go)), `Fixture.NoBastion`.

### Q-BAS-185 · A registry token's form is checked as the token service decodes it, and the anonymous principal is its claim a

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: R-BAS-052 names the form (the prefix, base64url, one `.`, base64url, at most 4 KiB) and the unverified reading of
`1:<key id>:<claims>`. Open were how strict base64url is, whether the length of the MAC is checked, and which claim names the anonymous
principal. The token service writes the member `a` true into the token of a request without a credential
([token.go](../../internal/auth/registrytoken/token.go)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Both parts decode as base64url without padding and with strict trailing bits, as the token service's `Verify` decodes them; the MAC's length is not checked; the anonymous principal is `a` true in the claims of payload version 1, unknown members ignored (chosen) | `iface.RegistryTokenWellFormed`, `iface.RegistryTokenAnonymous` | What the main installation refuses for its encoding is refused without a request; a new member of the claims does not hide the anonymous claim | The interface reads one member of the token service's own JSON; a test issues tokens with the real encoder to hold the two together |
| (b) The alphabet only | Simpler | Fewer rules | A value that cannot decode costs the main installation a request |
| (c) Also the MAC's 43 characters and strictly decoded claims | Closer to `Verify` | Fewer forwarded failures | Every change of the token's MAC or claims becomes a change of the interface |

**Choice:** (a). Trusting the unverified claim can only lower what is read (Q-BAS-168). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-052; code:
[regtoken.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/regtoken.go), `TestR_BAS_052_AnAnonymousRegistryTokenReadsAsTheAnonymousCaller`.

### Q-BAS-186 · A counted download is noted at the status line of the serve that counts it

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: R-BAS-059 says the item store's download recording notes `Quader-Bastion-Counted`, as its lookups note `absent`. Read in the
code: the recording (`items.Store.Served`) runs after the body is written (`edge.ServeItem`'s `Served`, the remote engine's `Streamed`,
the raw file handler, OCI's `recordTagFetch`), and the marking writes its headers with the status line, so a note there reaches no
response. The three serves that count all start their answer through a writer the core holds; OCI's tag of a remote repository is
written by the format itself, which counted it after the body through `ItemStore.RecordDownload`. Package C reports only the entries
the marking calls counted, so a counted download the marking misses is missing from the audit trail of a Bastion's warm pulls.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The writer of a counting serve notes the count when it writes the status line of a download it counts once complete: a `GET` answered `200`, or `206` from byte 0 (`bastionmain.CountingWriter`, at the item store's serve, the remote engine's artifact answer and `/files/`) (chosen) | A statement of the rule's verdict, made when the answer starts | Every format's stored artifacts and documents and `/files/` are marked without format code; the condition is R-STOR-015's, read from the status line; an ordinary request pays nothing (the writer is returned unwrapped); `RecordDownload` notes as well, and OCI records a remote tag before its status line | A format that counts a download of an answer it writes itself must record it before its status line; an answer that starts as a counted download and is then not counted is marked ([H-1290](#h-1290--a-miss-passed-through-during-an-outage-of-the-object-store-is-marked-as-counted)) |
| (b) The note where the recording counts | As the sentence of R-BAS-059 reads | Exact | After the status line: no response is ever marked |
| (c) A trailer `Quader-Bastion-Counted` after the body | The note when the count happens | Exact, also for an aborted body | A content answer always carries `Content-Length` (R-STOR-012), and HTTP/1.1 sends trailers only with chunked framing; proxies drop trailers; the interface defines the member as a header (A's version 4) |
| (d) The marking derives it from the route kind and the status | `artifact` means counted | No note at all | The rule of what a download is would live in the marking, and a document that counts (the manifest of an OCI tag, Q-OCI-222) would not be marked |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the core's serves already decide the count on R-STOR-015's condition; the writer reads the same
condition from the status line and needs no knowledge of a format. Every call of `items.Store.Served` is preceded by the note: the item
store's serve, the remote engine's streamed miss, `/files/`, and `RecordDownload`, which OCI's remote tag now calls before
`writeStoredDocument` writes its `200` (it counts the same requests: `recordTagFetch` leaves out a `HEAD` and the `If-None-Match` that
answers `304`, and the bytes are already in memory; only a write the client abandons mid-body is counted now). The builder would revisit
it if a format needs to count an answer it writes itself only after the body (then a method of the host that notes at the status line
and counts after the body).

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-013, R-BAS-059; code: [absence.go](../../internal/bastionmain/absence.go),
[ingest.go](../../internal/formathost/ingest.go), [remote.go](../../internal/formathost/remote.go),
[handler.go](../../internal/api/rawfiles/handler.go), `recordTagFetch` in [remote_handlers.go](../../internal/formats/oci/remote_handlers.go),
`TestR_BAS_059_ACountedDownloadIsNotedAtItsStatusLine`, `TestR_BAS_059_ARemoteTagIsCountedBeforeItsStatusLine`.

### Q-BAS-187 · A token answer names the caller the token service accepted

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: the chain's authentication stage does not evaluate the credential of `/v2/_token`; the token service presents it itself
(R-OCI-004, `Stage.AuthenticateTokenRequest`). The marking's subject is the caller the chain's stage accepted, which for every token
request is the anonymous caller. The Bastion records the subject of every marked response as the answer for the credential it sent
(`recordAnswers` of the engine).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The token service tells the marking the caller it accepted (`bastionmark.NoteCaller`); its refusal is a `401` and `invalid` like every other (chosen) | The subject is the token of the Basic password or the form's password, with its expiry | The marking states the truth about the credential the request carried, as on every other route | A call of the edge package of the marking from the token service |
| (b) The chain's caller | `anonymous` on every token answer | Nothing to build | A false statement about a request that carried a credential; a Bastion that kept it as the credential's answer would serve a narrowed token as `anonymous` |
| (c) No subject on a token answer | A marking without `Quader-Bastion-Subject` | No statement | The header is always written (`iface.Marking.Set`); an interface change |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-013, R-BAS-051; code: `NoteCaller` in [mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go),
[token.go](../../internal/api/registry/token.go), `TestR_BAS_051_TheTokenServiceAndTheCatalogTellTheMarkingTheirKind`.

### Q-BAS-188 · The bound repository is named as the match of /v2/ reads the binding

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: R-BAS-057 names `boundRepository` "the qualified name the default endpoint's `host_roots` binds the Bastion's host to", and the
Bastion classifies a path matching "a bound-host prefix of that repository's format" as that repository. The handshake does not name the
repository's format. The match of `/v2/` treats a binding to a repository that does not exist, or that is not of the format that declares
the registry root, as no binding (`Dispatcher.BoundRepository` in [registry_target.go](../../internal/api/dispatch/registry_target.go)).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The dispatcher's reading: the repository is named only when the match of `/v2/` honours the binding (chosen) | `BastionServices.BoundRepository` is `Dispatcher.BoundRepository` | The Bastion classifies a bound path exactly when the main installation serves it as the bound repository; today only the registry root has bound prefixes, so the format is the one whose entry has them | A second format with bound prefixes needs the format in the handshake |
| (b) The raw value of `host_roots` | Every binding | Literal | A binding of an npm repository would make a Bastion send `/v2/library/alpine/…` as that repository, which the main installation then reads as an unbound path |
| (c) The binding and its format in the handshake | A member `boundFormat` | Ready for a second format | An interface change (version 5) that nothing needs before a second format with bound prefixes |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** one reading of the binding for the Bastion and the main installation. The builder would revisit (c)
with the first format other than the registry root that declares bound-host prefixes (Terraform's discovery).

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-057; code: [bastion_handshake_api.go](../../internal/api/v1/bastion_handshake_api.go), `bastionBoundRepository`
in [wire_bastion.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion.go), `TestR_BAS_057_TheHandshakeCarriesTheFormatTable`.

### Q-BAS-189 · The core routes below /v2/ tell the marking their kind only for the methods they answer

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

| (b) For every method | One call | Simple | A `PUT /v2/_token` would be answered `204`, and the Bastion would forward its body only to receive the `405` |

### Q-BAS-190 · The check's paths count as served on every replica

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

| (a) The check's stage counts every family as served (`bastionCheckStage`), the chain's stage is unchanged (chosen) | The check decides as a replica that serves the package families decides the Bastion's forward | A registry token is verified on every replica; an anonymous check is decided as the forward of the same caller is | The check's rules differ from the chain's of the answering replica in one member |
| (b) The process's surface, as the chain applies it | No change | Nothing to build | On a replica of the role `api` every registry token's check answers `invalid`, and the Bastion refuses a token it holds content for |
| (c) The Bastion sends its check to a replica that serves the package families | A second address for one operation | The rules of the forward's replica | A further configuration value of the Bastion and a split of the interface |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-011, R-BAS-052; code: `bastionCheckStage` in
[wire_bastion.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion.go), `TestR_BAS_052_TheCheckDecidesItsPathsAsAReplicaThatServesThePackageFamilies`.
### Q-BAS-195 · On a bound host every path below /v2/ but the core routes is the bound repository, as the main installation reads it

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. Where the specification and the code
disagreed: the criterion of R-BAS-057 said `/v2/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…` keeps its unbound meaning on a bound host, while
formats/oci.md R-OCI-029 and the dispatcher (`matchRegistry` in [registry_target.go](../../internal/api/dispatch/registry_target.go)) read
every path below `/v2/` on a bound host as the bound repository, the whole path after `/v2/` the image name; the unbound meaning stays
only for a binding to a repository that does not exist or is not of the format, which the handshake does not name.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) With `boundRepository` the Bastion classifies every path below `/v2/` but `/v2/`, `/v2/_token` and `/v2/_catalog` as the bound repository (chosen) | `/v2/web/docker-local/app/manifests/1` is the image `web/docker-local/app` of the bound repository | The Bastion keys its answers, checks and entries by the repository the main installation serves the request from | `/v2/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…` names no other repository on such a host, at the Bastion as at the main installation |
| (b) The unbound reading first when the path parses as one | The criterion's wording | A host serves both | The Bastion would key `web/docker-local` while the main installation serves the bound repository: a `full` answer of one repository applied to another |
| (c) No bound host at the Bastion | Defer | Nothing to classify | Against Q-BAS-178 |

**Choice:** (a); the criterion of R-BAS-057 is corrected. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-057; code: `classifyRegistry` in
[family.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/family.go).

### Q-BAS-196 · The Bastion's own registry challenge names no scope

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: the main installation's challenge below `/v2/` names the scope its route needs (`scope="repository:<image>:pull"`, R-OCI-004);
the image name is read by the format's grammar, which a Bastion does not hold (Q-BAS-17). The Bastion answers a `401` of its own below
`/v2/` for the version check without a credential, a malformed registry token and one past its reported expiry (R-BAS-051, R-BAS-052).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `Bearer realm="<base>/v2/_token",service="<host>"`, with `error="invalid_token"` for a refused credential, no scope (chosen) | The challenge of the version check, which the main installation renders without a scope too | No format knowledge; Docker and containerd ask for the scope of the operation they run | A client that takes the scope only from the challenge asks for a token without one, and its next request draws the main installation's challenge with the scope |
| (b) The scope read from the path by a rule of the family | `repository:<rest before /manifests/ or /blobs/>:pull` | The main installation's challenge | The registry's path grammar in the Bastion |
| (c) Forward such a request and replay the main installation's challenge | No answer of its own | Exact | A malformed token costs the main installation a request and counts nothing at the Bastion |

**Choice:** (a). What the real clients do with it is recorded with their measurement ([developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-real-clients-through-a-bastion)).
**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-051, R-BAS-052; code: `registryChallenge` in [family.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/family.go).

### Q-BAS-197 · A range shorter than the withheld tail is served after the commit

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. The rule of R-BAS-054 withholds "the range's
last 64 KiB" until the commit, while its criterion asked a range of 1 KiB to receive its first byte before the fill ends: both cannot hold
for a range shorter than the tail.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The rule: the last 64 KiB of the range stay back while the fill runs, so a range of at most 64 KiB is served whole after the commit; the criterion uses a range of 128 KiB (chosen) | `bytes=0-131071` of a running fill gets its first 64 KiB at once and the rest after the commit | No byte of a range reaches the caller as a complete answer before it is verified, whatever its length | `freshclam`'s check of 512 bytes on a cold container waits for the container's fill, as every ranged miss did before |
| (b) At least one byte held back | `bytes=0-1023` gets 1023 bytes at once | The criterion as written | A short range is complete but for one byte before it is verified: a client that reads the range as it arrives acts on unverified bytes |
| (c) The object's last 64 KiB, not the range's | A range far from the end streams whole | Simple | A range that ends before the object's last 64 KiB is complete before the commit |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-054; code: `streamFill` in [fill.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/fill.go).

### Q-BAS-198 · The Bastion caps a registry token's shape and reads insufficient_scope itself

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: R-BAS-052 caps the read shape of a registry token at `partial` at the main installation's marking and check, and has the marking
say who a `401 insufficient_scope` was for. Both are the main installation's side.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Bastion also records at most `partial` for a registry token, and does not keep an `invalid` answer or count a failed authentication for a `401` whose challenge says `insufficient_scope` (chosen) | Defence in depth on the Bastion's side | A main installation that marks a registry token `full` or `invalid` by mistake cannot let one image's token read every cached image of the repository, nor put a puller into the timeout | Two places hold one rule |
| (b) Rely on the main installation | One place | Smaller | A defect of the main side opens the Bastion's cache |
| (c) Refuse a registry token below `/v2/` that the main installation marks `full` | A check | Finds the defect | A refusal of a pull for a defect of the other side |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-052; code: `capRead` and `insufficientScope` in [registry.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/registry.go).
*Extended on 2026-11-22 to package answers, built on 2026-11-23 ([Q-BAS-246](#q-bas-246--the-bastions-own-guard-for-registry-tokens),
R-BAS-084):* the cap on the repository stays, and a package answer `full` for a registry token is recorded only where the token's
unverified grant names the repository and the package with pull; otherwise `partial`, whatever the main installation marks (`capPackage`
in [registry.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/registry.go)).

### Q-BAS-199 · A format table the Bastion cannot rely on fails the handshake

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A table that fails `iface.HandshakeFormats.Validate` (an ID twice, two registry roots, a status other than 429 or 503, a replay header outside the rules) is a broken answer: the handshake fails and the replica is unreachable (chosen) | Like a body that does not decode | The request flow acts on the table (which headers a cached answer replays, which status a refusal takes); a broken table is a defect of the main installation that shows at once | A defect of one format's facts makes the replica unreachable for every format |
| (b) Drop the entries that fail and keep the rest | Partial table | The other formats are served | A defect is hidden, and a dropped registry root silently stops `/v2/` |
| (c) Keep the previous table | Stale | Serves on | A main installation's change never arrives |

**Choice:** (a); the main installation's catalog refuses such facts at registration (R-BAS-058), so the case is a defect. **Applied in the
spec:** R-BAS-057; code: `Link.handshake` in [link.go](../../internal/bastion/link/link.go).

### Q-BAS-200 · A caller follows a running document fill only on a full shape

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: a shared document above the memory bound is filled through the spool (Q-BAS-173), and its waiters could follow it as the waiters
of an artifact fill do (R-BAS-054). A document is shared only with full readers (R-BAS-023); a partial reader's version is filtered.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A waiter follows a document fill with a usable `full` shape answer or a check that says `full`; any other waits for the commit and decides again; an artifact fill is followed after a conditional request as R-BAS-054 says (chosen) | One permission rule per kind | No partial reader is served a shared document from a spool | A partial reader of a large document waits for the fill |
| (b) A conditional request for documents too | As for artifacts | No wait | A `304` to a shared document's validator is not the partial reader's own answer (Q-BAS-107) |
| (c) No following of documents | Wait for every document | Simple | A `freshclam` storm of a cold container answers `503 busy` after 30 s |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-054; code: `followFill` in [fill.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/fill.go).
*Extended on 2026-11-22, built on 2026-11-23 (R-BAS-085):* a usable `full` answer for a document fill also means a package answer `full`
on the fill's package, which the leader's marking supplies; such a document is the same bytes for a reader of that package in full as for
a reader of the whole repository (kit check 21, R-BAS-086). The fill keeps the repository and the package of the leader's marking
(`fillRun.repo`, `fillRun.pkg`), and `followFill` asks the caller's package answer on them.

### Q-BAS-201 · The engine's tests of Every format run over the engine's double of the client

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. The criteria of R-BAS-050 to R-BAS-054 named the

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

| (a) The engine's tests run over `fakeMain` of the engine's tests, which every engine test of the role uses, and the link's over `maintest` with its format table and bound repository (chosen) | The double answers byte by byte what a case needs | A body in 16 KiB steps behind a gate, a request count per kind, no TLS per test: the engine's tests stay at about 5 s | `maintest`'s TLS path is not under these cases; the role's scenario and the integration suite are |
| (b) Every case over `maintest` and the real client | As the criteria said | One more layer per case | Each case needs a handler written for `maintest`; the cases of the large fill need control of the body the fake does not offer |

### Q-BAS-202 · A registry token's expiry is the one the main installation reported, remembered per replica

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

Context: R-BAS-052 refuses a request with a registry token past "the expiry the Bastion holds" without a request and without a count.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The expiry of the subject the marking or the check reported for the token, kept by the replica for the token's credential key, bounded (100,000 tokens) (chosen) | The main installation's statement, as for every answer | No interface change; the expiry is the one the main installation verified | A replica that did not see the token, or forgot it, forwards it and counts the main installation's `401` as a failure (H-1295, closed on 2026-11-23 by Q-BAS-252) |
| (b) The `exp` of the token's unverified claims | Read like the anonymous claim (Q-BAS-185) | Every replica knows it; trusting it can only refuse | A new reader in the interface, which raises its version again |
| (c) The answers' own expiry only | No memory | Nothing new | Every expired token costs a request and a counted failure |

**Choice:** (a). The builder would revisit (b) with the next change of the interface. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-052; code:
`noteRegistryToken` and `registryTokenExpired` in [registry.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/registry.go). *On 2026-11-22 that change
came: [Q-BAS-252](#q-bas-252--option-b-of-q-bas-202-is-bundled) bundles (b) with the read shapes per package. **Superseded in place on
2026-11-23** (package P4 of the read shapes per package): (b) replaced (a). `registryTokenExpired` reads `iface.RegistryTokenExpiry` of the
token itself; the per-replica memory (`engine.expiries`, `noteRegistryToken`) is gone, since the expiry the main installation reports for a
registry token is the same member of the same claims (`Credential.ExpiresAt` in [stage.go](../../internal/auth/stage.go)).*

### Q-BAS-203 · The Galaxy clients' scheme Token is a credential of the protocol family, keyed apart

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. Found with the real client: `ansible-galaxy`
sends `Authorization: Token <Quader token>`, which the main installation reads on every route of Ansible Galaxy (R-ANS-006,
`credentialHeader` in [stage.go](../../internal/auth/stage.go)), and which the Bastion refused as an unreadable credential, so no
collection was installable through a Bastion with a token.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Bastion reads the scheme Token on `/api/<format>/…`, checks the token like any, forwards the header unchanged and keys its answers by the SHA-256 of `Token <token>` (chosen) | The main installation decides whether the scheme is a credential on the route | No format knowledge; a refusal of the scheme on a route that does not declare it never becomes the same token's answer as Bearer, and a full answer under the scheme is only used for requests that send it | A `Token` request on a route that does not declare it costs the main installation a request before its `401` is kept |
| (b) The formats that declare the scheme in the handshake's table | A fact per format | Refused at the Bastion where the main installation would refuse | A new member of the interface, which raises its version |
| (c) Read the scheme as Bearer | Same key as Bearer | Simple | The main installation's refusal of the scheme on another route would be kept as the token's answer and refuse its Bearer requests |

**Choice:** (a). The builder would revisit (b) with the next change of the interface. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-050, R-BAS-019;
code: `authorization` and `parseCredential` in [credential.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/credential.go),
`TestR_BAS_019_TheGalaxyTokenSchemeIsACredentialOfTheProtocolFamily`.

| (b) The Bastion's settings in `values-scatter.yaml` | Every scatter set carries them | No new profile | The sets npm, NuGet, Debian, Ansible and the access tests trust the pod range for Bastion tokens and list a host none of them uses |

### Q-BAS-205 · The Bastion of the set oci is one replica of the volume backend on an emptyDir, installed and removed by its case

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. R-BAS-060 names one release with the volume
backend, one replica and no Valkey, and asks for it as cheap as it can be.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-238](../decisions.md#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `bastion.sh install oci`: one replica, the volume backend on an emptyDir, no Valkey, no PodDisruptionBudget, `minReadySeconds: 0`, the namespace holding only the dev CA and the edge certificate; the case installs it beside the build and push of its image and uninstalls it at its end (chosen) | `deploy/dev/oci-bastion.yaml`, `oci-bastion-chart.yaml` | Ready about 5 s after the install started (measured): no claim to provision, no minimum ready time; every run installs the release as CI does | A second Bastion layout in `deploy/dev` beside the two of the set `bastion` |
| (b) The Bastions of the set `bastion` (`bastion.sh infra`) | Two releases, a Valkey of five pods, a bucket | One layout | Minutes of set-up for what images do not need |
| (c) The chart's defaults | Two replicas, an ephemeral volume per pod | Closer to an installation | A claim per pod, a PodDisruptionBudget and 10 s of minimum ready time; the second replica adds nothing the case asserts (the wait across replicas is a unit test, R-BAS-054) |

**Choice:** (a). The case waits after the release is ready until the edge routes the Bastion's host to it: HAProxy Ingress takes a new
Ingress into its configuration a moment after the pod is ready, and a run that did not wait met the edge's default certificate. **Applied
in:** R-BAS-060.
