### Q-BAS-210 · The cache key is one file in the Bastion's chart, and the format's keys derive from it

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. That the Bastion's cache is
encrypted in the same format once its chart gives it a key, off by default, is the owner's (2026-11-22, decision 13 (a)).

Context: the Bastion has no database and no key ring (R-BAS-001); the main installation's storage keys lie sealed in its database
([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-083). A lost cache costs a refill, never data.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One 32-byte key file from a Secret of the Bastion's chart; the storage key, the key's identifier, the name key and the entries' key derived from it (chosen) | One secret | Nothing to store or rotate beside the file; a new file is a new key identifier and an empty tree | Replacing the key empties the cache (a refill) |
| (b) A storage key drawn by the Bastion and kept sealed in its bucket under the file's key | The main installation's hierarchy | A key change without a refill | A key in the bucket it protects, and the volume backend per replica would draw one per pod |
| (c) The Bastion's signing key used for it | No new Secret | One Secret fewer | One key for two purposes; the signing key is also required without encryption |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the cache is disposable, so the simplest key that rotates by refilling is the right one.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-061.

### Q-BAS-211 · With a cache key, every object of the cache store is encrypted or sealed and named without a digest

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-245](../decisions.md#adr-245--the-bastions-cache-is-encrypted-in-the-stored-format-under-one-key-from-its-chart).

Context: the cache store holds artifact bytes, documents, signed entries (whose names are a hash of the cache key, so of the request path),
access markers named by the content address, and the audit spool of download events (R-BAS-030, R-BAS-039).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Artifacts, documents and the audit spool in the format; entries sealed under a derived key; every name a keyed name; only sizes, counts and times stay visible (chosen) | Nothing readable or confirmable in the store | The DMZ's copy reveals neither content, nor which packages are cached, nor who downloaded what | Every object of the store changes its layout when a key is set |
| (b) Only artifact bytes and documents | The content | Less to change | Entry names confirm which paths are cached; access markers carry digests; the spool carries personal data in the clear |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** an encryption that leaves the list of cached packages and their downloaders readable protects the content and
gives away the interest in it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-061.

### Q-BAS-212 · The record of a cached object lies in front of its body, in the same object

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. Found while building R-BAS-061: R-STOR-077 puts the
record in the object's metadata, and neither backend of the cache keeps any. The volume is files; the bucket backend writes through the plain
methods of `internal/blob/s3` ([Q-BAS-89](#q-bas-89--the-bucket-backend-reaches-s3-through-a-plain-adapter-and-fails-fast), R-BAS-030's five
operations), which carry no user metadata.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The record as a frame in front of the body, `FMT ‖ u8(len(id)) ‖ id ‖ W ‖ C` (182 bytes with a cache key's identifier), read before the body and checked with R-STOR-077's steps in their order (chosen) | One object, one write, one read, the same on the volume and in the bucket | The record cannot drift from its body, the owner's reason for decision 2 (e); the format's body is unchanged; no change to the S3 client | A reader of the main installation's objects (the offline tool) reads a cached object only after cutting the frame; a range costs one small request for the frame before the request for its segments |
| (b) The record in a second object beside the body | Two objects per artifact | Each object keeps the format's form | Two writes that can drift apart, which decision 2 (e) rejects; two requests per read |
| (c) Object metadata in the bucket, extended attributes on the volume | R-STOR-077 as written | Cached objects look like the main installation's | The cache's S3 client has no metadata (a change of another package's client and of R-BAS-030's adapter), and not every volume keeps extended attributes |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the cache is disposable and private to the Bastion, so a frame of its own costs nothing that a second reader
needs, while it keeps one object per write on both backends. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-061; code: `encodeFrame` and `readFrame` in
[crypt.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/crypt.go), [sealed.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sealed.go).

### Q-BAS-213 · Entries and the spool's files are objects of the format bound to their names

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. R-BAS-061 sealed the entries under an entries' key
derived from the cache key, `nonce ‖ Seal(entries' key, nonce, entry, FMT ‖ " bastion entry" ‖ name)` with a random 96-bit nonce per seal,
and named them `e/<k0k1>/<HMAC-SHA-256(name key, cache key)>`. Found while building: a Bastion writes an entry again at every revalidation (a
shared document every `metadata_revalidate_after`, one minute by default), so one entries' key seals without a bound over the life of a cache
key, while random 96-bit nonces under one key are good for 2^32 seals (NIST SP 800-38D §8.3; the format allows a data key 2^31 segments,
R-STOR-076). The backend names an entry by the SHA-256 of its cache key and never sees the cache key.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every entry, every file of the audit spool and the probe an object of the format with a data key of its own, its plaintext the object's name, a line feed and the payload, so that an object moved to another name or family fails; an entry named by the keyed name of area `e` over the SHA-256 of its cache key, `e/<m0m1>/<m>` (chosen) | One construction for every sealed byte, the format's, whose vectors an independent implementation checked | No bound on the writes under one key (each data key seals one object); an entry is authenticated even without a signing key; one naming function for the three areas | About 280 bytes more per entry (the frame and the final segment) and three derivations per write and read |
| (b) The seal as specified, under one entries' key | 28 bytes per entry beyond the record | Cheaper | A bound of 2^32 seals under one key that a busy Bastion approaches within the life of its key; a second construction beside the format, checked by no vector |
| (c) (b) with a key per seal derived from a salt, as the format's wrap does | No bound | Cheaper than (a) | A construction of its own, checked by no vector |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the cache's own seal would be the one construction of the feature that no independent implementation checked,
and its bound is reached by the Bastion's normal work; the bytes it saves are not worth either. The entries' key of R-BAS-061 is dropped.
**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-061; code: `putSealedBytes` and `readSealedBytes` in [sealed.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sealed.go),
`bound`, `unbind` and `sealer.name` in [crypt.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/crypt.go), `sealedLayout` in
[layout.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/layout.go).

### Q-BAS-214 · With a key, the volume backend spools its fills on the pod's temporary volume

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. R-BAS-061 leaves "the spool of fills in progress
on the pod's temporary volume" in the clear. The volume backend spooled its fills to `tmp/` of the cache volume so that a fill was committed by
a rename ([Q-BAS-131](#q-bas-131--the-bytes-of-the-fills-in-progress-are-bounded-and-the-chart-sizes-the-volumes-from-the-bound)), which
leaves the plaintext of each fill on the cache volume, a persistent one with `cacheVolume.type: persistent`, and that of an interrupted fill
until a later start removes it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-245](../decisions.md#adr-245--the-bastions-cache-is-encrypted-in-the-stored-format-under-one-key-from-its-chart).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) With a key, spool to the pod's temporary volume (`/tmp`), write the sealed object to `tmp/` of the cache volume and rename it into place; the chart sizes `tmp` as for the bucket backend (chosen) | The cache volume holds ciphertext only | The commit seals, so it is a copy anyway; what R-BAS-061 says stays in the clear is where it says | The pod's ephemeral storage grows by `spool_max_bytes` (2 GiB by default) |
| (b) Keep the spool on the cache volume | No chart change | — | Plaintext of fills in progress, and of an interrupted fill, on a volume that may be persistent and backed up with the cluster |
| (c) Seal the spool as it is written | Nothing plain anywhere | Closes the last plaintext at rest | A key per fill, held in memory for the fill and its followers' reads; the bucket backend's spool lies in the pod already |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-061, R-BAS-030, R-BAS-045, the values reference (`tmp.sizeLimit`); code: `New` in
[store.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/store.go), `quader-bastion.spoolInTmp` in the chart's
[_helpers.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader-bastion/templates/_helpers.tpl).

### Q-BAS-215 · The sweep of other layouts deletes them in a replica's first hour and while it still finds some

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. R-BAS-061 has the sweep delete the trees of other
identifiers and the plain layout "in its first runs after the change", which leaves open which runs, how much per run, and whether a cache
without a key deletes the trees a key left. The cache's store lists by prefix only (the plain methods of the S3 client have no delimiter), so
finding other trees lists everything below `bc-`, the replica's own tree included.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) With a key, the plain layout and the trees of other identifiers; without a key, every tree; in every sweep of a replica's first hour after its start and in each later sweep that follows one that found something; at most 10,000 deletions per sweep, so that the eviction of its own layout is not held back (chosen) | Other layouts appear only while replicas of two configurations run, a rollout | A key that is changed, set or removed leaves nothing behind; the own tree is listed once per sweep only while it matters | What a replica of the old configuration writes after the first hour of every new replica stays until the next start ([H-1326](#h-1326--after-a-key-change-the-old-tree-stays-readable-to-a-holder-of-the-old-key-until-the-sweep-has-deleted-it)); on a shared bucket, while replicas of both configurations run, each deletes what the other fills, which costs refills until the rollout ends (performance only) |
| (b) In every sweep | Always | Catches every other layout within one interval | Lists the whole own tree every `sweep_interval` for the life of the replica |
| (c) In the first sweep after the start only | Once | Cheapest | Misses what the old replicas write during the rest of the rollout |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-061; code: [foreign.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/foreign.go).

### Q-BAS-230 · The handover is an answer to the forward of a miss

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. That a Bastion gets a link
and the data key per released blob is the owner's (2026-11-22, decision 12 (b)).

Context: a handover must be decided as the caller's own request, with the gates, the limits and the counting, which is what the main
installation does with a forward today (R-BAS-013). The Bastion holds the caller's credential for the length of the request only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The forward of a miss carries an offer, and the main installation answers it with the handover instead of the bytes where the conditions hold (chosen) | One round trip | Every rule of a forward holds unchanged: authentication, the decision, the gates, `Admit`, the counting, the marking; no second decision path | The handover rides on the package routes; a class and two headers raise the interface's version |
| (b) A new interface operation `POST /api/v1/bastion/handover` with the caller's credential and the path | An interface call of its own | The key only on an interface route | The operation would decide a download outside the route that serves it: a second decision path beside every format's |
| (c) The forward answers with a ticket, and a second call with the Bastion token fetches the link and the key | Two steps | The key never on a request that carried a caller's credential | Two round trips per fill and a ticket kept between them, for nothing: the caller's credential is the Bastion's to see anyway |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the forward is where the main installation already decides a download for this caller; the handover is a
different answer to the same decision. The planner would revisit this if a handover had to be given without a caller's request (a prefetch).

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-070, R-BAS-072, R-BAS-073; [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095.

### Q-BAS-231 · The handover rides in a marking header of the item's own 200 with an empty body

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: a format sets headers of a stored file at its status line (OCI's `validatorWriter` writes `Docker-Content-Digest`, the `ETag` and the
content type, [handlers_manifest.go](../../internal/formats/oci/handlers_manifest.go) lines 46 to 66), and the Bastion keeps those headers with
its entry (R-BAS-057). The Bastion's client removes every `Quader-Bastion-*` header from an answer before the engine sees it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The item's `200` with every header it would carry, `Content-Length: 0`, the class `handover` and the value in `Quader-Bastion-Handover` (chosen) | The answer the file would get, without its bytes | The file's headers arrive as with the bytes, through the format's own writers; the value travels in a header the existing strip keeps from every caller; a defect that passed the answer on would give a client an empty `200` whose digest check fails, not a key | A secret in a response header, which no request log keeps and the redaction rule must name |
| (b) A JSON body of a media type of its own with the value and the file's headers | No secret in a header | | The formats' writers rewrite the content type at the status line; the file's headers would be copied into a body per format; a body passed on by a defect would hand a client the key |
| (c) A `307` to the link with the key in a header | A client's answer | | A `307` is what a client follows: a defect would send a caller to the store, and the key would stand beside a `Location` |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the failure of a defect is what decides: with (a) it is a broken download, with (b) and (c) a key or a link
in a caller's hands.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-073.

### Q-BAS-232 · The switch is per registration at the main installation, and the Bastion's chart has none

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: what leaves the main installation is its own decision. Several Bastions of one installation can stand in zones of different trust (a
partner's network, the company's DMZ), and the Bastions screen has a card per registration (Q-BAS-95). Simple by default: one switch in the
plain path, details on demand.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A member `handover` of the registration, off by default, on its card; no value in either chart (chosen) | The administrator who registers a Bastion decides what it receives | Per Bastion, in one place, one switch | A Bastion's operator who knows his network cannot reach the store has no switch of his own; the cooldown bounds the cost (R-BAS-075) |
| (b) One switch of the installation | Every Bastion or none | One switch | Every Bastion receives keys once one should |
| (c) The installation's switch and the registration's | Two levels | A stop for all at once | Two switches where one does the job; the cards are turned off one by one, at most `bastions.max_registrations` |
| (d) A value of the Bastion's chart | The DMZ opts in | The DMZ's operator decides | The DMZ would decide that keys leave the main installation |

**Choice:** (a). The `PATCH` asks no recent authentication: the switch hands nothing to anybody but the operator's own Bastion, it is
audited, and its switch-off is journaled. **Rationale:** the decision belongs to the side the keys leave. The planner would revisit (c) if an
installation ran many Bastions.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-071, R-BAS-078.

### Q-BAS-233 · Only artifacts the Bastion keeps are handed over

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-250](../decisions.md#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward).

Context: the Bastion keeps an artifact under its content address within `max_object_bytes` and the spool (R-BAS-021, R-BAS-030); a document is
shared or private by the caller's shape (R-BAS-023), and a private one is kept in memory only.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A whole `GET` of a `Download` route or of a file of `/files/`, up to the size the Bastion offers (chosen) | The fills the Bastion keeps | The bytes a handover moves are the large ones; every handed blob is kept and served from the cache again; one class to handle | Layers above `max_object_bytes` still pass through the main installation on every request until the operator raises the bound |
| (b) Documents too (an image's tag, the ClamAV containers) | A few large documents | | A private document is never kept, so a handover would move it once per caller; a document's rendition is not always the stored blob |
| (c) Also files the Bastion passes through, verified while they stream | The largest layers too | | A pass-through with a verification and a hold-back of its own beside the fill, and every pull of such a layer contacts the store again |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a handover is worth its round trips where the bytes stay at the Bastion. The planner would revisit (c) once a
measurement shows layers above the bound.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-070, R-BAS-072; [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-095.

### Q-BAS-234 · The Bastion opens the object with the handed data key alone

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: the format's reader opens an object with a data key, its digest and its size (`blobcrypt.NewReader`); the record's wrap opens only
under the connection's storage key, which never leaves the main installation; the main installation opens the record in `CopyDataKey` (steps 1
to 6 of R-STOR-077). The segment key derives from the data key (R-STOR-076). Gap H-1302 asked the planner of the handover whether a
commitment in the body is needed.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The data key with the digest and the sizes; the Bastion checks every segment, the final segment and the digest, and reads no record (chosen) | The format's reader as built | Nothing the Bastion cannot open; a body under another key fails at its first segment | The Bastion cannot tell a changed record from a changed body, and needs neither |
| (b) The segment key derived from the data key instead | A key that opens the segments only | Less than the data key | The data key opens nothing more of a released blob (the staging tails it also opens are gone once the blob exists, R-STOR-081); a reader entry and vectors of their own for no gain |
| (c) The data key, and the Bastion also compares the record's commitment | A second check | | The commitment binds a record to a key; the Bastion reads under the key the main installation took from the record, so no body is read under two keys |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** what protects the bytes is the authentication of the segments under the one key the record names; the
handover adds no second key, so H-1302 stays dormant and no commitment in the body is needed for it.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-074; [security/stored-content-format.md](../security/stored-content-format.md) H-1302.

### Q-BAS-235 · A failure before the first byte is a forward, after it a continuation by a range

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: a direct read of a large layer can fail at its start (the Bastion's network does not reach the store, a refused link) or in its middle
(a cut connection, a stall), while other callers follow the fill (R-BAS-054).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Before the first byte the forward again without the offer; after it a forward with the Bastion's own `Range` from the spooled length and `If-Range`, which continues the spool; a digest that fails at the end fails the fill and marks the key (chosen) | The main installation finishes what the store did not | No caller sees a failure of the store's path while the main installation can serve; a continued fill fetches no byte twice; on an encrypted copy the main installation's ranged read meets the failed segment and marks a damaged copy | A failed handover is counted or charged again (H-1342); a fill has a second source |
| (b) Every failure fails the fill, and the client's retry is a new miss | | Simple | A cut at 90 % of a gigabyte cuts every follower and costs a second transfer; a network that cannot reach the store fails every first pull |
| (c) The direct read resumes with a range of the store | | The main installation stays out | A link's life spent or a second link; the failure that cut the read may persist |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the handover is a way to spare the main installation, never a new way to fail a download.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-075.

### Q-BAS-236 · A replica that cannot read the store offers no handover for a minute

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Per replica and for every connection, 60 s after a failure of the network or the store before the first byte (chosen) | A pause | A Bastion whose network does not reach the store costs one more forward per replica and minute | One unreachable connection pauses the handovers of the reachable ones on that replica |
| (b) Per connection: the offer names the connections to avoid | Precise | | A list in the offer, another member of the interface, state per connection at the Bastion |
| (c) No pause | | | Every miss waits for a connect timeout first |

**Choice:** (a); the 60 s are a field of the engine, which a test shortens, not a value of the chart. **Rationale:** a store unreachable from
the DMZ is a configuration fault that the alert of R-BAS-075 reports; the pause only keeps its cost low until it is fixed. *Amended on
2026-11-23:* a value the Bastion refuses starts it too ([Q-BAS-293](#q-bas-293--a-value-the-bastion-refuses-starts-the-cooldown)).

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-075.

### Q-BAS-237 · The store is trusted with the chart's trust bundle

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The system roots and `bastion.main.ca_file`, the chart's `trustedCA` (chosen) | One bundle for the main installation, its store, Valkey and the bucket | No value; an operator's own CA is added once, an in-cluster gateway's CA as well | A CA added for the main installation also vouches for the store |
| (b) A bundle of its own (`trustedStoreCA`) | Separate trust | | A value for an expert case in the plain path |
| (c) The system roots only | | | A store under the operator's own CA could never serve a handover |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the integrity of the bytes does not rest on it (a body under another key fails at its first segment, a plain
body at its digest); TLS keeps a plain body and the link from the network, and the operator's CAs are trusted for that already.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-074, R-BAS-078.

### Q-BAS-238 · A blob withdrawn during a fill is treated as in a forwarded fill

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The running fill completes, and the feed's entry refuses the entry to every later caller (chosen) | The rule of a forwarded fill | No new window: a forwarded fill has the same one today | The callers of the running fill receive a blob withdrawn during its transfer |
| (b) A feed entry for the repository aborts its running fills | A shorter window | | Callers cut; a `grants` entry would cut every fill |

### Q-BAS-239 · The tests: once at the cheapest tier, one integration case, no end-to-end case

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Context: the owner's rule "Tests stay runnable" of 2026-11-20. A client sees an artifact from the Bastion as before; what changes is between
the Bastion, the main installation and the store.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (a) Unit tests for the wire, the main installation's conditions, the Bastion's read and its failures; one integration case in the area `bastion` against the stack's object store; no end-to-end case (chosen) | Each behaviour once | Nothing a real client does differs; about 5 s in one integration shard | The store of an owner's installation is not exercised; the measurement and the test link are |
| (b) An end-to-end case with `docker pull` through a Bastion with the handover on | The real path | | A Bastion release with the switch and a public address the kind pods reach: about 100 s in the leg `oci` for what the integration case shows |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-079.

### Q-BAS-240 · What "full on a package" means

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Context: a package shape must never let the Bastion serve a byte the main installation would refuse the caller
([Read shapes per package](#read-shapes-per-package)). The decision point decides a version on the package's path and on its file's path
(Q-AUTHZ-255), and through a virtual repository it resolves to different members for different callers.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every version and path of P in every member, the wiki, the populate right, no path pattern on the repository, an endpoint that exposes everything (chosen) | The decision point's rule of a `full` repository shape, made per package | Agrees with the decision point by construction; one test proves it | Conservative: any path-pattern grant on the repository makes every package `partial` |
| (b) Judged per member, where the item lies | `full` on P where the member that holds it is readable | More readers gain | Through a virtual repository the main installation resolves to different members for different callers, so the same path may hold other bytes |
| (c) Send the grant patterns to the Bastion | The Bastion matches names itself | No check needed | A copy of policy at the Bastion (against Q-BAS-1); package-name matching would be format knowledge |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** it is the decision point's own rule, made per package. The development agent would revisit it if a
measurement showed that path-pattern grants take the gain away from real installations.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-080. *As built:* `authz.Engine.PackageReachOn`; the fill of a package is decided without a path
([Q-BAS-260](#q-bas-260--the-fill-of-a-package-is-decided-without-a-path)), and the rule's agreement with the decision point is
`TestR_BAS_080_PackageShapeAgreesWithTheDecisionPoint`.

### Q-BAS-241 · How the main installation learns a response's package

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The core notes the package of every rights decision the host makes; the response has a package when exactly one was named and no package-less decision was made (chosen) | `bastionmain.NotePackage` from `Host.Authorize`, `WikiReadable`, `PathsAllowed` and the read scope | No format code; every format already decides through the host; a format to come gets it for free | Relies on decisions coming before the status line, which kit check 21 holds ([H-1383](#h-1383--per-package-sharing-rests-on-the-cores-notes-and-kit-check-21)) |
| (b) A route declaration naming the package parameter, checked by the kit | Explicit per route | Explicit | A declaration per route of every format; the declaration and the actual decision can drift apart |
| (c) The format's `Classify` of the request path, or the enforcement point's image | No notes | No notes needed | Request paths are not item paths; works for OCI only |

([Q-BAS-265](#q-bas-265--the-read-scope-a-format-meets-has-mayread-rows-only)).

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

### Q-BAS-243 · Package shapes have two values, and absent stays per repository

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `full` or `partial`; `none` folds into `partial`; negative entries stay for full readers of the repository (chosen) | No local refusal per package | A local refusal would happen only for cached entries, which is a timing signal (Q-BAS-124) | A reader who can read nothing of a package pays a conditional request per read |
| (b) Three values with a status | A `none` per package refused at the Bastion | Fewer requests for refused readers | Tells which hidden packages the Bastion holds |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-080, R-BAS-082, R-BAS-083. *As built* at the decision point: `PackageReachOn` answers
`ReachFull` or `ReachPartial` only, and `ReachPartial` for every package of a repository whose reach is `none`. *As built on the wire
(package P3):* the marking and the check answer `partial` for a repository the caller reads none of without asking the decision point, and
`bastionmain.CapRegistryPackage` turns any other value into `partial`; `absent` stays tied to `Read: full`. *As built at the Bastion on
2026-11-23 (package P4):* a package answer holds `full` or `partial` (`capPackage` records every other value as `partial`), and the negative
cache still serves only callers whose shape on the repository is `full` (`fromNegative` asks no package answer).

### Q-BAS-244 · Documents are shared per package

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built. It changes
[Q-BAS-18](#q-bas-18--metadata-shared-for-confirmed-full-readers-filtered-documents-per-caller)'s condition from a full read of the
repository to a full read of the repository or of the package the document belongs to; named to the owner on 2026-11-22.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A caller `full` on a package is served the `shared` document of that package (chosen) | The main installation marks it `shared`, the Bastion serves it on a `full` package answer | A warm pull costs no conditional request for the tag; npm's package documents are served from the cache | Q-BAS-18 says "a full read of the repository"; this becomes "of the repository, or of the package the document belongs to" |
| (b) Artifacts only | Documents stay per caller for a narrowed reader | Q-BAS-18 untouched | One conditional request per tag and package document per use; a warm pull costs about 4 requests instead of 3 |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** kit check 21 makes the document of a reader of the package identical to the repository reader's, so the
reason behind Q-BAS-18, that nobody sees another's view, still holds.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-013, R-BAS-023, R-BAS-082; Q-BAS-18 (a dated sentence). *As built on 2026-11-22 (package P3):* `classOf` in
[mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go). A Bastion whose engine has no answers per package (before package P4) keeps such a
document as the shared entry of its key and serves it from the cache only to callers whose shape on the repository is `full`
(`TestR_BAS_022_R_BAS_024_NegativeCacheOnlyForFullReaders` in the integration area `bastion`, run); the caller who was `full` on the package
alone keeps sending a conditional request per read, which the main installation answers `304`, marked `shared`, while the document is
unchanged (read in `onShared` and `fromEntry`, not run). *As built on 2026-11-23 (package P4):* `fromEntry` serves the shared entry
without a request to a caller whose package answer on the entry's package is `full`, under the entry's freshness; in the integration area
`bastion` `$PART`'s second `npm ci` of `@acme/sdk` through `npm-local`, its package document included, sends nothing
(`TestR_BAS_022_R_BAS_024_NegativeCacheOnlyForFullReaders`).

### Q-BAS-245 · When the Bastion asks

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built. It qualifies the
wording of Q-BAS-167's option (b), "served from the cache without a request": a warm pull keeps one check per new registry token.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A check with the entry's package only when the shape on the repository is unknown; a conditional request when it is known and `partial` (chosen) | R-BAS-085's steps 4 and 5 | 3 requests per warm pull; no new timing signal | Each new registry token's first read still costs one check |
| (b) A check whenever a package answer is missing | One rule | Simpler | An extra round trip only for cached entries: a timing signal per package |
| (c) Markings only, the check unchanged | No member of the check | No change of the check | 4 requests per warm pull (a check, then a conditional request) |
| (d) The token service's answer carries the new token's answers | Answers arrive with the token | 2 requests per warm pull | A second way for answers to enter; the Bastion would have to take the token's key from a header or read the token service's body |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the fewest requests that add no timing signal. The development agent would revisit (d) once a measurement
shows that the check matters (Q-BAS-167's own criterion).

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-022, R-BAS-085. *As built on 2026-11-23 (package P4):* `fromEntry` in
[readflow.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/readflow.go) asks `checkShape` only without a usable shape answer, with the entry's package
when the entry is of the request's repository; a caller whose shape is known goes to the conditional request. A late caller that reaches
the check's collapse after another check stored the shape is answered by `storedCheck`, which never sends a check while a shape answer is
usable, so step 5 holds through the collapse as well (`TestR_BAS_085_NoRoundTripTellsACachedPackageFromAnUncachedOne`).

### Q-BAS-260 · The fill of a package is decided without a path

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-080 — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is
built.

Context: condition 5 of R-BAS-080 asks the populate right "for P". The populate check of R-AUTHZ-008 decides `read` and, for a frozen mirror,
`deploy` on a coordinate. A `deploy` grant may be narrowed by package and by path, and the build found that `ReachOn` asked it on a
coordinate without a package and a path, which every narrowed grant matches (R-AUTHZ-005).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Decided on P without a path (chosen) | `populate` on `Coordinate{Package: P}`: a grant or a scope with a path pattern does not match a coordinate without a path (Q-AUTHZ-250), so a fill narrowed by path is `partial` | Covers every path of P: without a path pattern the decision comes from the package patterns alone, as conditions 2 and 3 argue for the read | A fill narrowed by path is `partial` on every package, as a read narrowed by path is |
| (b) On the package document's path | `populate` with `atPackage` | A fill narrowed to the document's folder could be `full` | A fill pattern that admits the document's path and not a tarball's would be `full` while the tarball's fill is refused |
| (c) On the repository alone | As `ReachOn` did | No new coordinate | Every narrowed `deploy` grant matches it: `full` where a fill is refused |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** it fails closed exactly where a path pattern could tell two paths of P apart, the argument condition 2 makes
for the read. `ReachOn` asks a frozen mirror's action on every package and path (`actsEverywhere`) for the same reason.

**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-080 (as built).

| (b) `VersionsByPath` true, as for every other `Allow` | The kit's default | Nothing new in the host | Fails NuGet for a caller the marking never calls `full` on a package; the repair would change a validator Q-NUGET-120 chose against leaking hidden versions |

### Q-BAS-270 · A package answer that ended with its shape answer is renewed by the check

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-084 and R-BAS-085 (package P4) — selected from the options below;
the owner sees it when it is built.

Context: R-BAS-084 renews a package answer by use: "once the answer has expired, the next read sends one conditional request, and its
marking renews the answer" ([Q-BAS-248](#q-bas-248--package-answers-renew-by-use)), and
[H-1381](#h-1381--the-main-installations-limits-and-blocks-do-not-reach-hits-from-per-package-answers) counted on that conditional request
meeting the main installation's limits and blocks within one period. The build showed that a package answer and the shape answer it rides
on are obtained together, from one marking or one check, and so end together: the next read then holds no usable shape answer, which is
step 4 of R-BAS-085, a check with the entry's package, and the check consults no limit.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Step 4 asks for the entry's package whenever the shape answer is missing, whether the credential is new or its answers ended (chosen) | One rule; a renewal costs one request, the check, which renews the shape and the package answer together | The gain stays: a new registry token's pull costs one check, and so does a long-lived narrowed token's renewal; nothing has to remember a credential whose answers ended | A blocked or limited subject keeps its package answers through checks, as a full reader keeps its shape answer through the background refresh: H-1381's finding holds for both |
| (b) Step 4 without the package for a credential seen before, so the renewal is the conditional request | A memory of credentials whose answers ended, beside the answers | H-1381's bound of one period holds for readers of a package | A renewal costs two requests (a check, then a conditional request); a second structure to keep, bound and share between replicas; a new registry token cannot be told from an old one by anything the Bastion holds |
| (c) Shape answers of partial readers refreshed in the background, so they outlive the package answers | The package answer ends first and the next read is the conditional request | H-1381's bound holds | A background check per partial reader and period, which Q-BAS-248 rejected for package answers for the same reason: the check consults no limit |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** what (b) and (c) would protect is a bound the check itself takes away from full readers today; the fix
belongs in the check (consulting the subject's block and request figures), which closes both cases at once. **Applied in the spec:**
R-BAS-084 (as built), H-1381; code: `fromEntry` and `checkShape` in [readflow.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/readflow.go).

### Q-BAS-271 · The end-to-end warm assertion counts what a warm pull asks about artifacts

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-085 (package P4) — selected from the options below; the owner sees it
when it is built.

Context: R-BAS-085 asked the warm assertion of `TestOCI_R_BAS_051_ThroughABastion` to allow at most one request below `/v2/` besides the
token step. The first run on a kind cluster (2026-11-23) showed that the real clients send requests the package answers are not about.
Docker 29.9.3, which resolves through its containerd image store, sends its first `HEAD` of the tag without a credential, which the Bastion
forwards while the main installation admits anonymous reads (the set `oci` has a public repository) and whose `401` it keeps nothing of
([H-1420](#h-1420--while-the-main-installation-admits-anonymous-reads-a-clients-first-head-of-a-tag-without-a-credential-is-forwarded-on-every-pull));
Docker and the kubelet `HEAD` the tag and never `GET` it, so the tag has no entry until another client fetches it (a `HEAD` miss keeps
answers only, R-BAS-021) and its `HEAD` is forwarded once per pull; Docker asks the referrers list of an index with attestations
(`Volatile`, never kept, R-BAS-053); Podman sends its version check with the token. A warm Docker pull of the set's image cost three such
requests besides the token step. And the set-up's own feed entries (the push's claim, a content entry; the fixture's policies, `grants`
entries) were younger than the skew margin when the cache filled, so every cached entry was stale for the warm pulls and each was
revalidated whatever answer its caller held (R-BAS-020, R-BAS-022).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A warm pull asks the main installation nothing about an artifact (a manifest by digest or a blob), and the cold pull starts once the Bastion received the set-up's feed entries more than the skew margin before (chosen) | `noArtifactRequest` on the warm Docker pull, the Podman pull and the kubelet's pull; the case waits `ociFeedQuiet` (16 s) after the push or the replica's readiness, whichever is later: a replica that starts reads the feed's lookback at once, so it receives the set-up's entries then | Exactly what R-BAS-085 removes: before, one conditional request per artifact; it holds whatever a client sends about the tag, its version check, the referrers or its anonymous challenge | The leg waits about 16 s more |
| (b) The criterion as written, with the set run without anonymous reads and with images without attestations | Fewer requests to count | The count the planner derived | Changes the set's other cases (its anonymous pull reads a public repository) and hides what real clients send |
| (c) The criterion as written, with the anonymous challenge, the referrers and the version check counted apart | One number per pull | Close to the text | The tag's `HEAD` still costs a forward or a check depending on which client fetched the tag first, so the count depends on the subtests' order |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** it asserts the mechanism the requirement adds and nothing the clients decide; the measurement of
[developer/bastion.md](../developer/bastion.md#the-real-clients-through-a-bastion) gives the whole count per client. **Applied in the
spec:** R-BAS-085 (the end-to-end criterion, as built), H-1242, H-1420; code: `noArtifactRequest` and `ociFeedQuiet` in
[oci_bastion_test.go](../../test/e2e/oci_bastion_test.go).

Context: R-BAS-073 lists `storedSize` equal to `S(size)` on an encrypted copy among the checks of the value, and its criterion has the unit

### Q-BAS-281 · The wire's checks are narrower than the list of R-BAS-073

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-073 (package 1 of the handover) — selected from the options below; the
owner sees it when it is built.

Context: the list of R-BAS-073 says what a handover's members must be; it does not say what of a URL, a base64 text or a JSON object is
refused beyond that, nor how the offer is spelled. The Bastion acts on the value: it fetches the link with a client of its own that sends no

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Refuse the user information and a fragment of the link; compare the host by name, case-insensitively and whatever the port; lower-case digits; no negative size; strict base64url without padding for the value and the key; one JSON object without an unknown member or trailing data; one spelling of the offer, any other value no offer (chosen) | Each value has one form, and a link carries nothing the client would send | A link with user information would make the link client send a credential, which R-BAS-074 forbids; a refused host on another port still leads back into Quader; the main installation writes the value, so a narrower reader refuses nothing it writes | Rules the list did not name |
| (b) Only the list | | Nothing beyond the requirement | The link client would have to refuse user information itself, and a host could be reached back on another port |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** every addition refuses a value the main installation never writes, and a refusal ends in the bytes through
the main installation (R-BAS-075), never in a failed download. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-073 (amended); code:
[handover.go](../../internal/bastion/iface/handover.go).

### Q-BAS-285 · Only the journaled switch-off is listed as yielding no feed entry

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-071 (package 2 of the handover) — selected from the options below;
the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-250](../decisions.md#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward).

Context: R-BAS-071 says that both events of the switch are listed in `noFeedEntry` with their reason. That list holds the journaled events
that yield no entry of the feed (R-BAS-015): the feed reads journaled events only, and `TestR_BAS_015_EveryJournaledEventIsClassified`
refuses an event in the list that is not journaled, so that no stale or mistyped entry hides there. `bastion.handover.enabled` is not
journaled (R-BAS-071: switching on widens).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `bastion.handover.disabled` in `noFeedEntry` with its reason; `bastion.handover.enabled` nowhere, since an event outside the journal never reaches the feed (chosen) | The list stays the journaled events | The test keeps refusing an event the feed can never read | The requirement's sentence is narrower than written |
| (b) Both, and the test accepts an event that is not journaled | The sentence as written | | The list would hold events the feed never reads, and the test's guard against a stale entry is gone |
| (c) Journal the switch-on too | Both in the list | | A journal entry that widens, which R-HA-054's replay never applies |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** what the sentence wants, that the feed is classified for both events, holds for the switch-on by
construction. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-071's as-built note; code: `noFeedEntry` in [feed.go](../../internal/bastionmain/feed.go).

### Q-BAS-293 · A value the Bastion refuses starts the cooldown

Status: **Decided by the development agent** while it joined the two sides in one integration case (2026-11-23) — selected from the options
below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Context: Q-BAS-236 starts the cooldown after a failure of the network or the store before the first byte, and H-1342 rests its bound on it:
"a Bastion that cannot reach the store causes at most one such double count per replica and minute". As built by package 3 a value the
Bastion refuses (a link on a host of the Bastion or of the main installation, an expiry its clock has passed, a blob above the offer, a
digest that is not the `ETag`'s, a value the interface cannot decode) fell back without the cooldown. Each of those comes from the main
installation's configuration, its clock or its code, not from one blob, so it is refused at every miss, and every miss then cost a second
forward and a second counted download, unbounded. The integration stack shows the first case by itself: without a public address the
links name the store's endpoint on `127.0.0.1`, which is the host of the Bastion's `bastion.main.url` (the front), and the check refuses
every one of them by name (Q-BAS-281).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A value refused before the read starts the cooldown like a failure of the network or the store; a fill the cache cannot start, a spool without room, a file whose `Vary` the Bastion cannot key on and a first segment that does not open do not (chosen) | The cooldown covers every refusal that would repeat at the next miss | H-1342's bound holds for every cause; a misconfigured public address or a skewed clock costs one more forward per replica and minute; the alert still fires | One refusal of a defect pauses the handovers of the replica for a minute |
| (b) The main installation refuses to hand over when its link's host is one of the Bastion's hosts | The cause at its source | No round trip for a refused link | The main installation does not know the host of a Bastion's `bastion.main.url` (a Service name, a front); clock and code defects stay unbounded |
| (c) As built | | | H-1342's bound is false for a refused value |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-075 (amended, as built), H-1342's bound
([security/bastion-handover.md](../security/bastion-handover.md#h-1342--a-handover-whose-direct-read-fails-is-counted-or-charged-again));
code: `onHandover` and `checkHandover` in [engine/handover.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/handover.go); test:
`TestR_BAS_075_ADirectReadThatFails`, "a value R-BAS-073 refuses falls back without a read and starts the cooldown", which fails without the
change.

### Q-BAS-290 · A handover counts one outcome, by the path it took

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-075 (package 3 of the handover) — selected from the options below; the
owner sees it when it is built.

Context: R-BAS-075 names four values of `quader_bastion_handovers_total{outcome}` (`read` "read from the store and committed", `fallback`
"failed before the first byte", `continued` "finished through the main installation", `refused` "the bytes failed verification") and the
request log's `bastion_handover`, without saying what a handover that meets two of them counts: a later segment of an encrypted copy that does not
open is a failed verification and a continuation; a continuation whose commit then fails is both; a small plain body whose digest fails before
anything was spooled is a refusal and a fallback (Q-BAS-291). The fill outlives its caller (Q-BAS-123), so a caller's request can end before
the read does.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One outcome per handover, by the path the bytes took: `fallback` when the forward without the offer replaced it, whatever the reason; `continued` when the fill turned to the main installation after its first byte, counted when the continuation is sent, whatever it answers; `refused` when the read delivered its bytes and they are not the blob (the plain digest, the encrypted plaintext's digest) or the commit refused a fill read wholly from the store; `read` when that commit passed. The log names the outcome, and `reading` while the read runs after its caller left (chosen) | Each handover is one event | The counters add up to the handovers; the alert's sum counts each failing handover once; the log of each request says what happened to its bytes | A refusal before the first byte counts `fallback`; a continuation that the commit then refuses counts `continued`, and the key is marked all the same |
| (b) Every value that applies | Several counts per handover | Each fact is counted | The counters no longer add up to the handovers; the alert counts one failure several times |

**Choice:** (a). Every commit that fails after a direct read, continued or not, marks the key for `artifact_revalidate_after`, so that the
main installation's verifying read meets the copy. **Rationale:** the operator's question is where the bytes came from; one count per handover
answers it, and the mark does not depend on the count. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-040 (the note under the table), R-BAS-075 (as built);
code: `directFill.finish`, `turnToMain`, `committed` in [engine/handover.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/handover.go).

### Q-BAS-291 · A blob of one segment is verified whole before its first byte

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-074 (package 3 of the handover) — selected from the options below; the
owner sees it when it is built.

Context: R-BAS-075 decides by the first byte: before it the forward without the offer replaces the read, after it the fill continues or fails.
On an encrypted copy the format's reader releases the plaintext of the last segment only after the final segment and the digest, so for a blob of
one segment the first byte is the whole verified blob. On a plain copy the bytes arrive as the transport delivers them, so whether a plain body of
a few kilobytes whose digest fails is "before" or "after" its first byte would depend on how the network cuts it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `Open` reads the first 64 KiB of plaintext, or the whole body and its digest when it is not longer, before it returns; a digest that fails there is a failure before the first byte: the forward without the offer replaces it, and the key is marked (chosen) | The first byte of a direct read is the first verified segment, for both kinds of copy | One rule for both; a small damaged plain object costs the caller nothing but a delay, and the main installation's read meets the copy at once | 64 KiB held in memory per open read |
| (b) The first bytes as the transport delivers them | | No buffer | A small damaged plain object cuts its caller or falls back depending on the network |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-074, R-BAS-075 (as built); code: `Read.first` in
[handover/read.go](../../internal/bastion/handover/read.go).

### Q-BAS-292 · The forward that replaces a handover counts no second miss, and a core route carries no offer

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-072 and R-BAS-075 (package 3 of the handover) — selected from the
options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Context: every forward of the read flow first asks the guard's miss limit of the caller's address (R-BAS-035). R-BAS-075 says the forward that
replaces a failed handover "goes on as for a miss today". R-BAS-072 puts the offer on every `GET` the Bastion forwards; the core routes of the
registry root (`GET /v2/_token`, the catalog, the version check with a credential) are forwarded as well, and their answers are passed on and never
kept (R-BAS-051).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The replacing forward is sent without asking the guard again, as a plain forward (no validator, no offer) even when the first was the Bastion's own conditional request; a core route of the registry root carries no offer (chosen) | One miss per caller's miss; no offer where no handover can be used | A failure of the store's path never costs the caller a second miss of its limit; a `200` answers a conditional request whose validator failed anyway; the main installation never hands over on those routes (they are no `Download` route, R-STOR-095 step 2), and the engine could not keep such an answer | The engine has a second way to send a forward (`send` behind `forward`) |
| (b) The replacing forward through the guard, the offer on every `GET` | The text as written | | A Bastion whose network does not reach the store spends two misses of every caller's limit per cold miss until the cooldown |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-072, R-BAS-075 (as built); code: `send` in
[engine/forward.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/forward.go), `offerFor` and `fallback` in
[engine/handover.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/handover.go).

### Q-BAS-295 · The card names the connections a Bastion cannot read, and only those

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-071's screen (package 5 of the handover) — selected from the
options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-250](../decisions.md#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward).

Context: R-BAS-071 says that while the switch is on "the card lists each connection with whether it can serve a handover and its reason
where not". The owner's rule "simple by default, details on demand" (the repository's working rules, R-UI-067) wants the plain path to be
the switch and its sentence; which connections a Bastion reads from matters to an administrator when one of them cannot be read. The
states come from `GET /api/v1/download-links/settings`, which needs `settings:read`, while the screen needs `endpoints:read` (a repository
administrator holds the one and not the other).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Nothing of the connections while every one can serve a handover; a line per connection that cannot, its reasons in words, and one link to the storage settings' **Details**, where an address is set and tested (chosen) | The detail shows where it helps | The plain path stays the switch and one sentence on every installation that works; a fault is named where the switch is, with the place to fix it | An administrator does not see which connections a Bastion reads from while all can |
| (b) As written: every connection with "can" or its reasons | | Complete | A list on every card that is on, of facts nobody acts on |
| (c) A count ("1 of 3 connections cannot be read") and the link | | Shortest | The reason needs a second page |

**Choice:** (a). The states are read once per load of the list, only while a registration's switch is on and the viewer holds
`settings:read`; without it, or when the read fails, the card shows the switch and its sentence alone. The link is offered only where a
plain connection is among the lines: for an encrypted one nothing on that page changes what happens to its files today (Q-BAS-296).
**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-071 (amended, as built); code: `handoverLines` and `BastionHandover` in
[bastion-handover.ts](../../web/src/app/features/bastions/bastion-handover.ts), `loadConnections` in
[bastion-list.ts](../../web/src/app/features/bastions/bastion-list.ts).

### Q-BAS-296 · Until the data keys are handed, the card's sentence names no key and an encrypted connection has its line

Status: **Decided by the development agent** during the build of R-BAS-071's screen (package 5 of the handover) — selected from the
options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-250](../decisions.md#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward).

Context: R-BAS-071's sentence reads "Large files go from the object store to this Bastion by a link per file, and for an encrypted store
with that file's key; the main installation decides and counts every download as before." Package 4 (the data keys) is not built: the main
installation never names an encrypted copy (`case c.Encrypted(): continue` in
[downloadlinks/handover.go](../../internal/downloadlinks/handover.go)), so the files of an encrypted connection go through the main

decides by the address and the link check alone.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (c) As written, and an encrypted connection judged by `handoverUsable` like a plain one | | One rule | An encrypted connection the answer calls usable shows nothing, and its files pass the main installation unnamed |

when package 4 landed.*
