### Q-BAS-301 · A commit is admitted against a running estimate of its area, and a fill without room is passed through unkept

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E1 (2026-11-26), a defect that needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options
below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: R-BAS-031 promised that the cache stays below `max_bytes`, and only a sweep every `sweep_interval` held it there (R-BAS-089 says what
that let through). A bound at every commit needs the bytes of the area at that moment. A listing gives them and costs one request per thousand
objects on a bucket, or a walk of the directory on a volume; the volume's file system could say how full it is; the replica knows what it
commits itself. The engine already treats a refused commit as a backend failure: the fill's callers are answered from its spool, nothing is
kept (R-BAS-030, `Fill.Keep`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An estimate per area, set by every listing and raised by every commit of the replica; a commit that would pass the limit is refused with `ErrNoRoom` unless the store holds its address already, and a sweep is asked for; the first commit of a replica waits for, or makes, the first listing (chosen) | The bound is checked in memory at every commit; the store is asked only when the answer is no | No request per commit; the area stays below its limit on a volume at every moment; one code path for both backends and the sealed layout; the engine's existing path for a refused commit serves the caller | Between listings the replica does not see other replicas' writes (Q-BAS-302); the estimate errs high after an eviction until the next listing, so a few fills may be passed unkept that would have fit |
| (b) A sweep inside the commit when the area is above its mark, the commit waiting for it | The commit makes its own room | Every fill is kept | The fill's callers wait for the withheld tail for the length of a listing and an eviction (seconds on a bucket of many objects); a burst of commits runs one sweep each |
| (c) Ask the volume's file system for its free space at each commit | — | Sees what else fills the volume | Not for a bucket, which has no fixed size; not by area; a second rule beside the areas the sweep keeps |
| (d) Shorter `sweep_interval` only | — | Nothing new | Still unbounded between two sweeps; listings every few seconds on an idle Bastion |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the attack R-BAS-089 closes is fills arriving faster than a timer; only a check at the commit bounds it, and
only a check in memory keeps that check out of the path of every fill. A refusal costs one fill that is not kept, which is the outcome the
owner's case calls for: under a flood of distinct artifacts the volume does not fill and the pod is not evicted. **Applied in the spec:**
R-BAS-089, R-BAS-031; code: `estimate`, `Cache.admit`, `Cache.committed`, `Cache.firstListing` in
[room.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/room.go), `Fill.Commit` in [fill.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/fill.go).

### Q-BAS-302 · A replica on a shared bucket counts each of its commits once per replica

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E1 (2026-11-26), a defect that needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options
below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: with the bucket backend every replica writes into one bucket (R-BAS-030) and the estimate of Q-BAS-301 is a replica's own. A replica
sees what the others wrote and evicted only when it lists: at its own sweeps without Valkey, and with Valkey only the holder of the sweep lease
sweeps (R-BAS-031). The repository's rule for figures kept per replica is Q-BAS-11 and Q-BAS-34: without shared state a replica takes its share
by `bastion.replicas`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Each commit counts `bastion.replicas` times in the replica's estimate; a replica without the sweep lease lists, deleting nothing, at its sweep's turn when it committed since its last listing (chosen) | A replica assumes every other one fills as much as it does | The rule of Q-BAS-34 applied to bytes; with fills spread evenly the estimate is the bucket's; a replica that fills alone lists sooner, which costs listings, never evictions (a sweep evicts by the listing alone); works with and without Valkey | A bucket filled unevenly can pass its limit by what the other replicas wrote beyond their share between two of a replica's listings (H-2270) |
| (b) A shared counter per area in Valkey, raised at every commit and set by the lease holder's listing | One estimate for the release | Exact across replicas while Valkey answers | A Valkey round trip per commit; without Valkey the same question again; a counter that the lease holder's listing and the others' increments race on |
| (c) Each replica counts its own commits once | — | Nothing to configure | With N replicas the bucket can hold up to N times the headroom past its limit between listings |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a bucket has no fixed size, so passing `max_bytes` by a share costs storage and not a pod; what must not happen
is a bound that grows with the replicas, and (a) keeps it at one share of the headroom. (b) is the way to close H-2270 if a measurement shows
the gap matters. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-089; code: `Options.Replicas` and `build` in
[store.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/store.go), `Cache.relist` in [sweep.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sweep.go), `buildDeps` in
[server.go](../../internal/bastion/server/server.go).

### Q-BAS-303 · At once is one sweep at a time, asked for by any number of commits, at most one a second

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E1 (2026-11-26), a defect that needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options
below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: R-BAS-089 starts a sweep when an area passes its high mark between two timed sweeps. Under a burst every commit above the mark asks
for one, and a sweep lists the area twice (before and after it evicts) and the markers once: on a bucket of 18 GiB of objects of 100 KiB, about
180 requests of `ListObjectsV2` per listing. A sweep that cannot bring the area below its mark (a failing backend, fills faster than the
eviction) would be asked for again by the next commit at once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The replica's one sweeper loop takes a request from a channel that holds one: a request while a sweep runs or waits is one more sweep after it; a sweep the size asked for starts at least a second after the last one ended (chosen) | One sweep at a time per replica, coalesced, at most one a second | A burst of a thousand commits costs one or two sweeps; a failing backend is listed at most once a second; between two triggered sweeps the area must fill by the 10 % between the marks, so under normal load they are rare | Under a sustained flood above the eviction rate a replica lists once a second (H-2271); fills are refused for up to a second after the area is full |
| (b) A sweep per commit above the mark | — | Simple | Hundreds of concurrent listings under a burst |
| (c) A sweep at once and then none for `sweep_interval` | — | Cheapest | A flood fills the area within the interval again, and every fill after is refused until the timer |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the second bounds the cost of the case where sweeping does not help, and costs nothing where it does: the band
of 10 % between the marks (1.8 GiB of the default artifact area) takes seconds to fill even at the planner's 320 MB/s. **Applied in the
spec:** R-BAS-089; code: `Cache.wantSweep` in [room.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/room.go), `RunSweeper` and `waitGap` in
[sweep.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/sweep.go).

### Q-BAS-304 · The marks are R-BAS-031's: a sweep at 95 %, a refusal only at the limit

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E1 (2026-11-26), a defect that needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options
below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: R-BAS-031 sweeps an area above 95 % of its limit down to 85 %. R-BAS-089 needs a point that starts a sweep between the timed ones and a
point past which a commit is refused.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A sweep is asked for above 95 %, the sweep R-BAS-031's own; a commit is refused only when it would pass 100 % (chosen) | The band from 95 % to 100 % takes the fills that arrive while the sweep runs | No new figure; a fill is refused only where the bound itself is at stake; the sweep's eviction is unchanged | — |
| (b) Refuse above 95 % | — | A margin below the limit | Fills refused while the area still has room, at every sweep's start |
| (c) Marks of their own in the chart | — | Tunable | Two more figures for a defect's repair, against "simple by default"; nothing measured to set them from |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-089; code: `Cache.limitOf` in [room.go](../../internal/bastion/cache/room.go).

### Q-BAS-305 · The spool of fills does not count in the areas

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E1 (2026-11-26), a defect that needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options
below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: a fill is written to the spool while it streams, on the cache volume (the volume backend without a cache key) or on the pod's `tmp`
volume (the bucket backend, or a key), and is renamed into its area at the commit (Q-BAS-131). The spool has its own bound,
`spool_max_bytes`, and the chart refuses a `cacheVolume.size` below `max_bytes` plus the spool.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The areas count committed bytes only; the spool keeps its own bound (chosen) | A volume holds at most `max_bytes` plus `spool_max_bytes` plus entries and markers | The two bounds the chart already sizes the volume from; a rename moves bytes from the spool into the area without changing the volume's level | A cache volume sized exactly to the two still holds entries and markers beyond them (H-452) |
| (b) Count the fills in progress in the artifact area | — | One figure | A cold burst would refuse commits for bytes that are still in flight and may never be kept; the bucket's spool is not on the cache store at all |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-089; the chart's check is Q-BAS-131's, unchanged.

### Q-BAS-306 · The main installation counts the body bytes the marking stage writes, by registration and the caller's class

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E5 (2026-11-26), which needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options below;
the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: W-34 asks for the bytes the main installation sends to a Bastion, per registration and per class of caller. The request log has
`response_bytes` per request but no metric; the marking stage (R-BAS-013) is the one place that sees every recognized forward, its
registration and its caller, and it already counts the requests by the marking's class. That label `class` means the marking's class
(`artifact`, `shared`, `private`, …); the label list of R-OPS-007 holds `class` and no label for a caller's kind.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A counter of its own, `quader_bastion_forwarded_bytes_total{bastion, class}`, raised by the marking stage's writer with every body byte it passes, `class` the caller's: `anonymous` or `authenticated`, the values of the Bastion's budget (chosen) | Bytes by registration and by who asked | One place, every forward; the two sides' figures use one vocabulary (`quader_bastion_main_in_flight{class}` at the Bastion); no new label | The label `class` means the marking's class on the request counter and the caller's on the byte counter, which the specification and the help texts say |
| (b) A third label on the request counter and the bytes in a histogram | — | One family | A histogram per registration and class and marking class: more series for a sum nobody reads by bucket |
| (c) Read the request log's `response_bytes` | — | Nothing to build | Not a metric; per request, not per registration over time |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the question is how much a Bastion draws and on whose behalf, and the budget's classes are what the Bastion
divides its slots by. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-090, R-BAS-008; code: `markWriter` in
[mark.go](../../internal/api/bastionmark/mark.go), `ForwardedBytes` in [metrics.go](../../internal/bastionmain/metrics.go).

### Q-BAS-307 · The class of a fill's bytes is the class of the request that started it

Status: **Decided by the builder** of W-34's package E5 (2026-11-26), which needs no decision of the owner — selected from the options below;
the owner sees it when it is built.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-298](../decisions.md#adr-298--a-bastions-cache-is-bounded-at-every-commit-and-the-bytes-between-a-bastion-and-the-main-installation-are-counted).

Context: a fill reads its source once, whoever follows it (R-BAS-054): callers of either class may be served from one fill, and a fill goes on
after its caller left (H-472). The request that started the fill took the budget slot of its class (R-BAS-025).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The class of the request that started the fill, the class of its slot (chosen) | Each byte read once, under one class | The sum over classes is the bytes read; the anonymous share of the fills is what the anonymous slots let in | A fill an anonymous caller started and signed-in callers follow is counted anonymous |
| (b) Each follower's class for the bytes it is served | — | Says who was served | Counts the bytes served, not read: `quader_bastion_bytes_served_total`'s job |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-090, R-BAS-040; code: `fillRun.class` in [fill.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/fill.go).

### Q-BAS-310 · The longest wait a format's client is told is a fact of the format; zero tells the true wait

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-299](../decisions.md#adr-299--the-longest-wait-a-formats-client-is-told-is-a-fact-of-the-format).

Context: the main installation tells NuGet's and Ansible Galaxy's clients at most 30 s (`maxRetryAfter` in each format's `WriteError`),
because their clients count a wait against the timeout of the whole command. A Bastion renders its own refusals without the format's
code and told them the whole wait: up to 24 hours for a block (W-34, the planner's finding E2, reproduced by
`TestR_BAS_058_TheBastionsOwnRefusalsKeepTheFormatsLongestWait` on the unchanged code: `Retry-After: 900` and `t=900` on both formats'
paths). The question is where the cap lives so that both sides apply the same one, for every format to come.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A member of `catalog.BastionFacts`, 0 for the true wait; the handshake's table carries it; kit check 19 holds `WriteError` to it for every format (chosen) | The format's constant is declared once in its descriptor and used by its `WriteError`; the Bastion reads it as data | One place per format; a format that caps without declaring, or declares without capping, fails its kit run; the Bastion stays without knowledge of a format; the format to come answers it by its `WriteError` | The interface rises to version 7 |
| (b) As (a), with an explicit value for every format (a sentinel for "uncapped") | Every descriptor names it | Nobody can forget it | Five formats write a value that says nothing; the kit's check already shows what each format tells, so a forgotten cap fails anyway |
| (c) The cap in the Bastion's code for the IDs `nuget` and `ansible` | Two special cases | No interface change | The Bastion learns two formats, against Q-BAS-179; a format to come is forgotten |
| (d) The main installation caps centrally for every format, and the Bastion copies the same constant | One cap for all | Simple | OCI must not be cut (formats/oci.md R-OCI-008), and npm and podman wait honestly what they are told |

**Choice:** (a). The cap is `catalog.Facts.Bastion.RetryAfterMax` and `HandshakeFormat.RetryAfterMaxSeconds`; NuGet and Ansible Galaxy declare
their `maxRetryAfter`, every other format declares nothing. The Bastion caps every `Retry-After` of its own and the `t` of its guard's
RateLimit field; the detail keeps the true wait (R-BAS-029, R-BAS-091). The main installation's caps and the Bastion's come from one
place, the format's constant; the main installation's RateLimit field `t` is not capped by it
([H-2275](#h-2275--the-main-installations-ratelimit-field-tells-a-nuget-or-galaxy-client-the-whole-wait)).

**Rationale:** the format knows what its clients do with a wait, the Bastion does not; a declaration checked against the format's own
writer is the one form that cannot drift. The development agent would revisit it when a format's clients need a floor as well as a cap.

### Q-BAS-311 · A refusal of the Bastion's guard names its wait in words and rounds it once

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: with a cap of 30 s a NuGet client that is blocked for an hour comes back every 30 s; what it, and its user with `curl`, can
read of the true wait is the body. The Bastion's detail was "Too many requests; retry after the period in the Retry-After header.", which
under a cap sends the reader to a value that is not the wait. The main installation's refusals round once and name the wait in their
detail ([usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-291).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The main installation's rule: round up once, to seconds below two minutes and to minutes from there; the detail names it in words, `Retry-After` and `t` carry it, capped (chosen) | "Too many requests from this address. Try again in 15 minutes." | One wait per answer, as at the main installation; the reader of a capped answer sees the truth; a client that waits is never early | A wait of 2 min 1 s is told as 3 minutes |
| (b) A member `retryAfterSeconds` with the true wait in the problem body | Machine-readable | — | Not in the distribution's error shape below `/v2/`; no client reads it; a member of the interface's bodies more |
| (c) Keep the detail | — | No change | Under a cap the detail points at a wrong value |

**Choice:** (a), in `refuseVerdict` of [request.go](../../internal/bastion/engine/request.go) (`oneWait`, `refusalDetail`): a block says
requests from the address are refused for a while, a failed-authentication timeout that a credential the Bastion cannot check now is
refused, every other refusal that there were too many requests; each ends with "Try again in <wait>.".

**Rationale:** the answer a person reads must carry what the capped header no longer does. The development agent would revisit it if a
client is found that reads the problem body's members.

### Q-BAS-312 · The Bastion's request figures are the main installation's profiles Anonymous and Standard

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's decision 18 (usage-and-limits.md Q-LIM-59) set the main installation's request figures from a measurement so that
normal use never meets them, and his rule of 2026-11-26: built-in defaults are generous and derived from what real clients do, for large
companies. The Bastion's figures (10 a second with a burst of 40 anonymously, 50 and 200 with a credential) were estimates from before the
measurement and refuse one anonymous `docker pull` of 40 layers and one `npm ci` of 475 packages with a credential (R-BAS-092). The Bastion
counts per address, not per subject: an address can be a NAT of several people.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The request figures of the profiles Anonymous (50/s, 1,000) and Standard (200/s, 4,000) (chosen) | The Bastion admits from one address what the main installation admits from one caller | Q-LIM-59's normal use holds, with its room for two commands at once; one rule for both doors; the windows are 20 s, as at the main installation | One address may send 1,000 anonymous requests at once |
| (b) The smallest figures that hold one command (burst 50 anonymously, 500 with a credential) | Tight | Least room for a flood | A NAT of two people, or a second command, is refused; docker exits at the first `429` |
| (c) The profile Technical with a credential (1,000/s, 20,000) | Room for a CI fleet behind one address | — | Five times Standard for any credential from the internet, valid or not; an address is not a system |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-035, R-BAS-046, R-BAS-092; code: the defaults of `config.BastionLimitAuthenticated` and
`config.BastionLimitAnonymous`, the chart's values.

**Rationale:** the measurement gives the commands and the profiles give their room; the Bastion's own figures exist to stop a flood, which
they still do within seconds (Q-BAS-314). The development agent would revisit them with the measurement of a Bastion per format (W-34's E4).

### Q-BAS-313 · The miss figures hold in a minute what the request burst holds at once

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: on a cold Bastion every request of a command is a miss; a cold pull of 40 layers is 48 misses within 0.3 s, which met the 30
anonymous misses a minute. The misses are what costs the main installation; they are bounded there per caller as well (R-BAS-017) and per
Bastion by the slots (R-BAS-025).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The burst of the class per minute: 1,000 anonymously, 4,000 with a credential (chosen) | A command the request figures admit is not refused for being cold | One rule; a cold cache refuses nothing a warm one serves | One address can send 1,000 anonymous misses a minute to the slots |
| (b) One command per minute: 500 and 1,000 | Tighter | Less load from one address | Two installs at once on a cold Bastion are refused |
| (c) The rate per minute: 3,000 and 12,000 | As wide as the requests | — | The minute of misses is the main installation's load; the slots already decide what reaches it |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-035, R-BAS-046, R-BAS-092; code: the defaults of `config.BastionMisses`.

**Rationale:** what is refused as a miss and served as a hit is a refusal of whoever comes first after a restart or an eviction. The
development agent would revisit it if a measurement shows that the slots let a thousand addresses load the main installation more than its
own per-caller figures do.

### Q-BAS-314 · The block threshold is the anonymous class's minute: 3,000 refusals

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a block follows refusals (R-BAS-037), and with the figures of Q-BAS-312 a client over its figure collects more refusals per
second than before: three anonymous installs of 475 packages at once from one NAT collect about 300 in 2.5 s, which the former threshold of
300 a minute turned into a block of 15 minutes. A block is the answer to a flood, never to normal use (Q-BAS-127).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 3,000 a minute, what the anonymous class admits in a minute (chosen) | Blocked at twice the anonymous rate sustained, or 1.25 times the rate with a credential | A NAT over its figure is refused and not blocked; a flood at the ingress's 1,000 a second is blocked in about 4 s | A flood just below twice the rate is refused, not blocked |
| (b) Keep 300 | — | Blocks sooner | Three commands at once block an office for 15 minutes |
| (c) A threshold per class | Two values | Exact per class | One more key for one rule; the refusals of an address mix both classes |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-037, R-BAS-046, R-BAS-092; code: the default of `config.BastionBlocking.Threshold`.

**Rationale:** a refused request costs the Bastion one counter; a block saves it nothing for an address that is refused cheaply anyway, and
costs an office its access. The development agent would revisit it if refusals themselves are shown to load a replica.

### Q-BAS-315 · The edge defaults hold the fastest normal command: 1,000 requests a second and 256 in flight

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: HAProxy Ingress's `limit-rps` counts HTTP requests also on a kept-alive connection and has no burst (R-BAS-038, read from the
template of v0.16.3 and HAProxy 2.8's source on 2026-11-26; a measurement on the kind cluster was not run: the cluster is shared with the
other builders of the day, and the reading leaves no doubt the measurement would settle). An `npm ci` of 475 packages is about 190 requests
a second, so the default of 100 refused it at the ingress before the Bastion saw it. The chart requires the value above the Bastion's own
rate with a credential (now 200).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 1,000 a second and 256 in flight (chosen) | The anonymous burst can arrive within a second; a quarter of one replica's `server.max_in_flight` | Two `npm ci` at once (about 380 a second) and a pull pass; the edge still cuts a flood at 1,000 a second per address | A single address may hold 256 of a replica's 1,024 requests in flight |
| (b) 400 a second, 100 in flight | Just above two commands | Tighter | The busiest second of an `npm ci` is not measured; a `dotnet restore` on Linux is not bounded by its client |
| (c) Turn the edge limit off by default | The Bastion's own stage only | Nothing to tune | The Bastion pays for every request of a flood; the owner chose two stages (Q-BAS-16) |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-038, R-BAS-046, R-BAS-092; code: the chart's `edgeLimit` and the fallback of its check in
`_validate.tpl`.

**Rationale:** the edge exists to cut what would overload the Bastion itself; a figure a normal command meets makes it a limit of its own,
with no burst and no `Retry-After`. The development agent would revisit it with a measurement of the busiest second of `npm ci` and of the
requests in flight of a large `dotnet restore` (H-2276).

*Revised on 2026-11-26 by the owner's [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation):* the
Bastion's own figures move to its registration, so the chart's check of the edge figure against them goes (R-BAS-093); the edge's defaults
of this decision stay, and the card warns where a configured figure lies above the edge figure the Bastion reports. *Built by E9a
(2026-11-26):* the check in `_validate.tpl` is gone and the edge figure is reported; the card's warning is E12's, built on 2026-11-26 in plain view
(R-UI-240, [Q-UI-1486](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1486--the-edge-warning-stands-in-plain-view-not-under-the-flood-figures-in-details)).

### Q-BAS-320 · The configuration travels as one member with each rule's effective figures, and its revision is the registration's

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's [Q-BAS-323](#q-bas-323--a-bastion-is-configured-on-its-card-at-the-main-installation) puts a Bastion's
configuration on its registration and delivers it with the handshake. The Bastion holds no profile model and no group (R-BAS-001); the
rules of its place name profiles, and an administrator changes a profile at the instance without touching a registration.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One member with the effective figures of each rule, the revision the registration's, raised also by a change of a rule of the place or of a profile such a rule names (chosen) | The Bastion compares one integer and applies one value | The Bastion needs no profile model and no resolution of overrides; one revision for the card's `ETag` and the metric | A change of a profile used by many Bastion places raises every such registration's revision and makes every Bastion handshake |
| (b) Profiles and rules as the main installation holds them, resolved at the Bastion | A second copy of the model at the Bastion | Smaller when many rules share a profile | A second implementation of R-LIM-010's overrides and R-LIM-016's caps in a DMZ |
| (c) A content hash as the revision | The revision follows the member's bytes | No trigger on profiles | Two revisions of one registration (the `ETag` and the hash); a gauge cannot carry a hash |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the configuration is the main installation's word and should arrive decided; the handshakes a profile change
causes are bounded by `bastions.max_registrations` times the replicas. The development agent would revisit it if a profile change ever made
the handshakes a load. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-093, the wire of [The interface version 8](#the-interface-version-8-the-shared-wire).

### Q-BAS-321 · The Bastion's own codes are named by their status, its texts name no party, and its problem type is about:blank

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's rule of [Q-BAS-338](#q-bas-338--a-bastion-reveals-nothing-of-the-main-installation). The two plans of W-34 and W-35
named the Bastion's own codes and texts differently (W-34: `unavailable`, `busy`, `timeout`, `not_found`, with `main_failed` and
`main_timeout` both under `timeout`; W-35: `unavailable`, `bad_gateway`, `gateway_timeout`, `busy`, `not_found`), and one kept the
problem type `/api/v1/problems/<code>` while the other set `about:blank`. One set is built.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Codes by their status (`unavailable` 503, `bad_gateway` 502, `gateway_timeout` 504, `busy` 503, `not_found` 404, `read_only` 403), texts that say "this service" or "this address", the type `about:blank` (chosen) | A client reads the status's meaning and nothing behind it | Names no party and no structure; keeps 502 and 504 apart; `not_found` and `unavailable` are the core's codes already; `about:blank` is RFC 9457's type for "no more than the status" | Three new codes in the registry (`bad_gateway`, `gateway_timeout`, `busy`) beside `read_only` |
| (b) W-34's four codes | `timeout` for 502 and 504 | Fewer codes | A `502` called a timeout |
| (c) The core's codes of an upstream (`upstream_failed`, `upstream_timeout`, `server_busy`) | No new code | Reuse | "Upstream" tells a caller there is an installation behind the address |
| (d) Keep the type `/api/v1/problems/<code>` | Unchanged | No change | A path of the management API on the Bastion's host, which answers `404` there |

**Choice:** (a), with these texts: `unavailable` "This service is not available right now; try again later.", `bad_gateway` "This service
could not answer; try again later.", `gateway_timeout` "This service did not answer in time; try again later.", `busy` "Too many requests
are waiting; try again in a moment.", `not_found` "Nothing is served at this address.", `read_only` "This address is read-only: it serves
downloads and accepts no uploads." (the text told to the owner on 2026-11-26), `method_not_allowed` "This address serves GET and HEAD.",
`misdirected_request` "This address does not answer for the host of the request.", `payload_too_large` "The body is too large.". The type
is `about:blank` on every problem the Bastion renders and on every problem the main installation renders for a recognized forward.
**Rationale:** a code is a contract with clients and an operator; one named by its status carries no more than the status line does. The
development agent would revisit it if a client is found that reads a code. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-029, R-BAS-099, the wire.

### Q-BAS-322 · Both topics raise the interface version once, to 8

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-34 (limits, throughput, writes, names) and W-35 (the web interface's catalogue and switches) both change the interface; equality
of versions is the owner's rule (Q-BAS-20), so every raise is a lockstep upgrade of the main installation and every Bastion.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One package lands the whole wire of both topics at version 8; the packages behind it change no wire (chosen) | E7 with W-35's P5 | One lockstep upgrade; the sides are built against a fixed contract | The wire lands before the behaviour; members are carried that nobody reads yet |
| (b) A raise per package | 8, 9, 10, … | Each raise carries what is built | Up to six lockstep upgrades in a week; each side's packages wait on each other's raises |

**Choice:** (a). The registry token's version 2 is read from 8 on and issued later by E17, which changes no wire. **Rationale:** the
upgrade, not the code, is what a raise costs an operator. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-009, the wire.

### Q-BAS-323 · A Bastion is configured on its card at the main installation

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-26** — option (a) of his working paper (k1), stored at 11:51.

Context: a Bastion's limits are chart values and a change is a rollout (R-BAS-002, the owner's Q-BAS-15); at the main installation only the
handover can be switched per Bastion. His task of 10:40 asks that "die Download-Limits … sich durch den Administrator detailiert
konfigurieren lassen" and that a configuration per Bastion be possible.

|---|---|---|---|
| (a) On its card at the main installation (chosen) | Limits, flood protection, throughput, mode and the switches (handover, GUI, docs) belong to the registration and reach the Bastion with the handshake; the chart keeps what the installation sizes: the cache's size, the periods, TLS | One place for every Bastion, audited, in force in about 3 s without a rollout; before the first contact the strict preset holds with every switch off | Changes the owner's earlier "chart values only" (Q-BAS-15); the interface version rises |
| (b) In the chart values, as today | Nothing changes | GitOps | Against his task; a rollout per change; the administrator sees nothing |
| (c) Both, the stricter value wins | The chart as a floor | The operator of the DMZ keeps a lever | Two truths; the card shows values that do not hold |

**Choice:** (a), the owner's decision. It supersedes his Q-BAS-15 for every value the table of R-BAS-093 names. **Applied in the spec:**
R-BAS-002, R-BAS-010, R-BAS-035 to R-BAS-038, R-BAS-046, R-BAS-071, R-BAS-093;
[ADR-300](../decisions.md#adr-300--a-bastion-is-a-place-of-the-download-limits-configured-from-the-main-installation-and-names-nothing-of-it).

### Q-BAS-325 · The limit members of a registration need limits:write, the others endpoints:write

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: a registration is changed with `endpoints:write` (R-BAS-004); limits are changed with `limits:write` everywhere else
([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-040). The card now holds both.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|

### Q-BAS-333 · What was served twice is protected in the cache

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-26** — option (b) of his working paper (k9), stored at 11:51.

Context: the sweep evicts what was touched longest ago, and a fill counts as a touch; the planner derived that four addresses exchange a
cache of 18 GiB in about five minutes. That the cache overflowed between sweeps is fixed (R-BAS-089).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) As today | The overflow fix only | Nothing new | An attacker keeps evicting what is really used |
| (b) What was served twice is protected (chosen) | The sweep first evicts what was fetched once; at most 80 % of the cache is protected | Single fetches of many artifacts cannot evict the working set; a new artifact is still kept at its first fetch; no setting | One more marker per entry |
| (c) Keep only at the second miss | | Churn never enters the cache | Every new artifact crosses the transfer network twice |
| (d) A fixed share of the cache for anonymous fills | | Bounds anonymous churn | Public content is read by signed-in callers too |

**Choice:** (b), the owner's decision. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-031, R-BAS-098; H-2272. Built on 2026-11-26 (package E11) with the
builder's [Q-BAS-460](#q-bas-460--the-access-marker-is-the-protection-because-a-fill-writes-none) to

### Q-BAS-348 · A document path is canonical segment by segment and names packages by their catalogue ID

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-35's P5 asks for pure functions with a round-trip parser that refuses dot segments and encoded slashes; the measurement found no
paths for generic files and documents that changed with their times alone.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every byte outside RFC 3986's unreserved characters percent-encoded upper-case, one spelling read; no `/` in a value; packages by their catalogue ID, generic files segment by segment; the times in a `state` document (chosen) | One path per document; a scoped npm name needs no slash in a segment | A store, a cache and a sitemap key on the text; no traversal | A generic name with a control character has no path |
| (b) `url.PathEscape` and the router's decoding | Lenient | Familiar | Several spellings of one document; `%2F` as a slash or not by reader |

### Q-BAS-351 · Until E15, a probe is recognized by its form, and a read route with a body is the format table's

### Q-BAS-374 · The state record is written when it changed, and every minute for its time

| (c) Only when something changed | Fewest writes | — | A restart after a quiet day shows the age of the last change, not of the last confirmation |

### Q-BAS-385 · A forward's text is chosen at rendering from what the error carries

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

(`not_found` of a placeholder), and one error can answer a forward and an ordinary caller at once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The error carries the text a forward reads (`errs.WithForwardDetail`) and the members only the installation reads (`errs.WithInstallationExtension`); `errs.ProblemFor` picks them for a forward (chosen) | Six places say their sentence twice | Exact per text, also under a generic code; correct for an error shared by a forward and an ordinary caller; the format's error shapes need nothing, since they render through `ProblemFor` (kit check 19) | A new 4xx text that names something passes until someone gives it its forward text (H-2323) |
| (b) A neutral detail by code in `ProblemFor`, as Q-BAS-426 did for the remote engine | One table | Nothing at the sites | `not_found` and `forbidden` cannot be told apart from their harmless uses; a caller would lose every useful 4xx text of those codes |
| (c) The place that makes the error reads the forward from the context, as the limits engine does (R-BAS-099 row 7) | A branch per site | No new option | Wrong for an error made once for several callers; the limits engine's refusal is made per request, a gate's or a remote's not necessarily |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a sentence is best rewritten by the code that wrote it, and carrying both keeps one error right for every

### Q-BAS-386 · Every 5xx of a forward reads the neutral text of its status, unless its error vouches for its own

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-114. The texts of a status of 500 or more tell what failed inside the installation: "on this replica", its database, its
object store, an upstream's document, the key that signed an upstream's release (Debian's field errors). A caller of a Bastion acts on
the status and `Retry-After` alone.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |

| (a) Every 5xx of a forward that is no rate limit reads the neutral text of its status and loses its field errors; an error whose text names only what the caller asked for vouches for it with `errs.WithForwardDetail` (chosen) | Fails closed, as the header allowlist (Q-BAS-425) | A text written later names nothing; the Bastion's own 502, 503 and 504 read the same sentences | The pending answers of the malware and the signature gate and the ClamAV definitions' 503 of a rate limit must vouch, which they do |
| (b) Inventory each 5xx text and neutralize the ones that name something | As the 4xx | Each useful text stays | Every new text of a replica or a store reaches the internet until someone lists it |

**Choice:** (a). The texts: 501 "This operation is not served at this address.", 502, 503 and 504 Q-BAS-321's, 500 and every other status
"The server failed to process the request."; the remote engine's failures keep Q-BAS-426's. **Rationale:** the owner's rule is about what a
caller may learn, and the failures of a server are where the installation's structure shows. The development agent would revisit it if a
format's client is found that prints a 5xx detail it needs. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-029, R-BAS-114.

### Q-BAS-388 · The sealed part of a registry token is encrypted under a key of the ring, not a reference

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-115, Q-BAS-339 left open what the sealed part is. R-OCI-005 verifies a registry token without a lookup, on every replica,
and a token lives at most an hour.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) AES-256-GCM of the sealed claims under a key derived from the ring's key with the info `quader registry token seal v2`, a random nonce, the readable part as additional data; the key ID an HMAC of the ring key's ID under its MAC key (chosen) | Self-contained, as version 1 | No lookup and no store; a rotation of the ring rotates it; every replica opens it; the MAC still covers the whole token | 28 bytes more per token (the nonce and the tag) before base64; a holder of the ring reads the claims, as before |
| (b) An opaque reference: a random handle, the claims kept in Valkey or PostgreSQL | The token names nothing at all | Smallest token | A lookup per request below `/v2/`, against R-OCI-005; a shared store the verifier depends on; a lost store refuses every token |
| (c) The ring's own sealing of stored secrets (`secrets.KeyRing.Seal`) | One mechanism | Reuses code | Its form names the ring's key ID in clear and binds a database column and row, neither of which a token has |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the token stays what R-OCI-005 makes it, a credential verified by the MAC alone, and what a caller reads
shrinks to what a Bastion needs. The development agent would revisit it if a token must name nothing at all, the grant included (H-2297).
**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-115, [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-005.

### Q-BAS-389 · A system token's subject stays readable, and version 1 is read until its tokens expire

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-115. A scan or blob token (R-OCI-037, R-MAL-006) carries the system subject `s`, which the Bastion's reader of the grant
reads to refuse a token that reaches one manifest or blob (Q-BAS-246); the tokens issued before E17 are version 1.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `s` readable on a system token beside `a`, `exp` and `g`; the verifier reads versions 1 and 2, the token service issues 2 alone (chosen) | The reader's rule holds unchanged | `s` names a kind of token (`scan`, `blob`), nothing of the installation, and no forward carries such a token; a token issued before the upgrade stays valid for its few minutes | Two versions to read for at most an hour after an upgrade |
| (b) `s` sealed | Fewer readable claims | — | The Bastion would read a scan token's grant as a full pull grant |
| (c) The verifier reads version 2 alone | One version | Simplest | Every pull in progress during an upgrade fails once with `401` and asks for a new token |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a token issued before an upgrade stays valid for the minutes it lives, at the cost of one branch of the
verifier; pre-alpha needs no other path of migration. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-115, [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-005.

| (a) A document kind `packages/<id>/vulnerabilities`, the anonymous answer, its grades' `checkedAt` taken out and kept nowhere (chosen) | One document per package | The view gets its column unchanged; one read per page; the document changes only with the findings, not with every rescan | The column has no time of a check, which it does not show anyway |
| (b) The application reads every version's report and builds the grades | No interface change | — | One read per version: a package of 400 versions is 400 reads per page view |
| (c) The grades as a member of the versions list | — | One document fewer | The versions list is the main installation's shape; a member of its own there is a shape the main installation does not answer |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-103, R-BAS-104, R-BAS-128.

### Q-BAS-483 · A public generic repository's folders and files are pages a crawler finds and indexes

| (b) Found and never indexed, as Set up client (Q-BAS-401) | — | Nothing new in an index | A public file is the content a visitor looks for; its page holds no commands per client that would make it empty for an index |

### Q-BAS-425 · The headers of a forwarded answer pass an allowlist, and a format's need is a replay header

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-099 row 5. The Bastion passed every header of the main installation's answer on but a deny-list (the interface's, the
replica, the cache state, cookies, the request ID), so `Quader-Resolved-From`, OCI's `Quader-Annotations-Cut` and the main installation's
RateLimit fields reached the caller, and every header a component adds later would too. Read in the code: the one header a format's
client reads on an answer the Bastion only passes on is npm's `npm-notice` of an audit that left names out (R-NPM-038); every other is a
representation header of the core, OCI's four declared replay headers or a header of the fixed list below.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An allowlist: the core's representation headers, the format's replay headers of the handshake's table and a fixed list of the framing, the wait, the challenge, the methods, the links, the distribution's version and `Location`; npm declares `Npm-Notice` (chosen) | One rule for a cached and a forwarded answer; a format's need is its declaration | A header nobody listed never reaches a caller; no change of the interface (the table already carries the replay headers); a format to come declares what its client needs where it declares the rest | A header a client needs on a refusal and that is no replay header must be declared as one |
| (b) A deny-list extended by `Quader-*` and `RateLimit*` | Today's mechanism with two more prefixes | Nothing a client reads can go missing | Every header added later at the main installation reaches the internet until someone lists it |
| (c) A second list per format of the headers of passed-on answers | A new fact `PassHeaders` | Exact | A change of the interface and of the contract for one header of one format |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the owner's rule is about what a caller may learn, and an allowlist fails closed; a declared replay
header is a header every reader of the format's answers may receive, which is the same promise for an answer passed on. The development
agent would revisit it if a format needs a header on a refusal that must not be replayed from the cache. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-058,
R-BAS-099 row 5.

### Q-BAS-426 · A forward reads a neutral detail for every failure of the remote engine, chosen by the code when the problem is rendered

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-099 row 15 and H-2295. The remote engine's failures name the remote repository that failed ("The upstream of
web/npm-remote answered 503.") and some name an upstream's host ("The certificate of registry.internal is not trusted."); through a
virtual repository the remote is a member the caller did not address. The same error can answer a forward and an ordinary caller at once
(a fetch is collapsed for every caller of a replica), so the error itself cannot be reworded where it is made.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) At rendering, for a recognized forward, every code of the remote engine and its upstream clients takes one neutral detail (chosen) | `errs.ProblemFor` reads the forward from the request's context and the code from the error | One place; every text of those codes is covered, those of the formats' wrappers too as long as they keep the code; the code, the status, `Retry-After` and the headers stay, so a client acts as before | A detail written for an operator of the main installation is lost to a caller who reaches it through a Bastion |
| (b) A neutral detail written beside each text where it is made (`errs.WithNeutralDetail`) | Twenty sites in `internal/proxy` | Each text says exactly what failed | A new text that forgets the option names the member again |
| (c) The virtual engine's `asAddressed` of R-EP-018, applied to a forward as to an endpoint with exposure rules | The failure is the virtual repository's | Reuses a mechanism | It also turns every `404` into the engine's one `404` and drops the absence the Bastion's negative cache reads (R-BAS-024); a direct remote keeps its texts |

**Choice:** (a), with "The package could not be fetched right now." for the failures and "The caller may not bring new content into the
cache of this repository." for `populate_not_permitted`. **Rationale:** a caller of a Bastion needs the status and the code to act; the
member and the upstream are the main installation's structure. The development agent would revisit it if a format's client is found that
prints a detail it must show unchanged. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-099 row 15, H-2295.

### Q-BAS-427 · A Location on another host is answered 502 at the Bastion, whatever the status

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-099 row 6. The main installation renders a forward's URLs on the Bastion's base URL (R-BAS-017), and no route answers a
forward with an absolute URL on its own host (read in the code); the one place a URL on another host is made for a download, a signed link
to an object store, is never the answer to a forward (storage.md R-STOR-070 step 2). A proxy in front of the main installation or a
change of either rule could still put another host into `Location`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `502` for any answer whose `Location` is neither relative nor on the Bastion's scheme, host and port; counted by the reason `foreign_location` (chosen) | The answer is not passed on | Fails closed; a caller never learns a bucket's or the main installation's host; the counter tells an operator at once | A `201` of a write with such a `Location` is a `502` too (writes are refused before, R-BAS-014) |
| (b) Drop the header and pass the rest | The caller gets a `3xx` without a target | No `502` | A redirect without a target is a broken answer that a client retries |
| (c) Rewrite the URL onto the Bastion's host | The path stays | A redirect keeps working | The Bastion would guess what another host's path means, against R-BAS-017's "the Bastion never rewrites" |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** an answer the main installation should not give is a defect, and a `502` is the honest status for it.
The development agent would revisit it if a route is built that answers a forward with a redirect to another host by design.
**Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-040, R-BAS-099 row 6.

### Q-BAS-428 · A forward is marked on the request's context, and every writer of an error renders through one function

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-099 rows 3 and 7. Problems are rendered by `errs.Write` and by every format's own error shape (npm, NuGet, OCI, Ansible
Galaxy read `errs.ProblemOf`); none of them knew whether the request was a forward of a Bastion.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Recognize stage marks a forward's context (`errs.WithBastionForward`), a Bastion marks its own (`errs.WithBastionAnswer`), and `errs.ProblemFor(r, err, requestID)` applies the mark; every writer of an error to a request calls it; kit check 19 holds a format to it (chosen) | One function decides the type, the title, the request ID and the neutral detail | The leaf `errs` needs no knowledge of the Bastion's packages; a format to come is held by the kit; the limits engine reads the same mark | A writer outside the formats that calls `ProblemOf` with a request would bypass it; none exists today |
| (b) The Mark stage rewrites the body of every answer to a forward | One place on the main installation | No change of the writers | A body rewritten after it was rendered: four error shapes to parse, and streamed bodies |
| (c) The Bastion rewrites the bodies it passes on | The main installation unchanged | — | Against R-BAS-017's "the Bastion never rewrites a body"; the Bastion would need every format's error shape |

**Choice:** (a). The title of a problem with the type `about:blank` is the status phrase, as RFC 9457 section 4.2.1 asks. **Rationale:** the
mark costs one context value per request and makes the rule a property of rendering, where it cannot be forgotten by a handler. The
development agent would revisit it if a writer of errors is found that cannot reach the request. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-029,
R-BAS-058, R-BAS-099 rows 3 and 7; [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-API-009 (the member `type`).

### Q-BAS-435 · The anonymous token is the anonymous caller at every replica and every Bastion, and no key signs it

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: Q-BAS-335 gives the Bastion's anonymous token a MAC of random bytes that nobody verifies. The plan of E14a asked what key signs
it so that every replica of one Bastion recognizes it and nobody else, how that key rotates, and what a token of replica A is at
replica B. The Bastion must not hold the main installation's signing key (owner, 2026-11-26: the smaller the footprint, the better).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No key: a token is recognized by its unverified claim `a` alone, wherever it is presented, and dropped (chosen) | Replica A's token at replica B, another Bastion's token and a forged one are each the anonymous caller | No key on an internet-facing node, nothing to share between replicas, nothing to rotate; a client that moves between replicas or Bastions keeps its token | Anyone can mint one, which gains exactly what a request without a credential gains (H-2350) |
| (b) A key shared by the replicas of one Bastion (generated and kept in Valkey, or derived from its cache key) | A foreign or forged token is refused `401` | Only that Bastion's tokens pass | A key to keep, rotate and lose on the edge; without Valkey and a cache key no shared key exists; refusing a token that grants nothing protects nothing, and a client refused there renews it at once |
| (c) A key derived from the Bastion token | Every replica holds the Bastion token already | Shared without Valkey | The Bastion token is the main installation's credential for this Bastion: a derivation of it on the wire of every anonymous caller, and a renewal of the Bastion token ends every anonymous token |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the token carries no scope the Bastion would trust, and the Bastion drops a token that claims to be
anonymous (Q-BAS-168), so its authenticity decides nothing; a request without any credential reaches the same answers. The main
installation knows no key of the ID `bastion` and refuses the token there. The development agent would revisit it if the anonymous token
ever carried something a Bastion decided on. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-052, R-BAS-094; [security/bastion.md](../security/bastion.md)
H-2350.

### Q-BAS-436 · An anonymous token request is one without a credential, and the Bastion reads neither its scope nor its service

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-094 answers "a `GET` or `POST /v2/_token` without a credential" at the Bastion. The token service of the main installation
answers a `POST` without a password `400 invalid_request`, a `HEAD` `405`, a `service` of another host `400`, and more than 16 scope
entries `400`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A `GET` without an `Authorization` header and a `POST` whose form holds no password and that carries none are answered with the token; an anonymous registry token presented with either is no credential (Q-BAS-168); an anonymous `HEAD` answers the token service's `405` at the Bastion; scope and service are not read (chosen) | No request to the main installation for any of them | The token grants nothing, so nothing a client asks for has to be checked; a request with any credential goes to the main installation as before | A malformed anonymous request gets a token where the main installation would answer `400` |
| (b) Mirror every `400` of the token service at the Bastion | The service check and the scope grammar at the Bastion | The same answers at both doors | Format knowledge of the token service's grammar at the Bastion, for a token that grants nothing |
| (c) Forward what the Bastion does not answer | An anonymous `HEAD` and malformed requests go to the main installation | Nothing new at the Bastion | A one-for-one path stays open to the internet |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-051, R-BAS-094.

### Q-BAS-437 · The anonymous caller's copy is kept also without a validator, and judged as a cache entry is

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-094 keeps a document the main installation filtered for the anonymous subject for the metadata period. A caller's private
copy was kept only with an `ETag`, since a copy without a validator cannot answer a conditional request; and its validity was judged by the
four rules of an answer, whose fourth (no answer obtained within 15 s of the start of the replica's feed history) a cache entry does not
apply. Which documents count needs no list: a tag's manifest, an npm packument, a NuGet index, an APT `InRelease` and a Galaxy version
list are each a document the main installation marks `shared` or `private`, and the Bastion keeps by the marking's class, never by the
format. Blobs and other artifacts are not documents.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The anonymous copy is kept with or without an `ETag`, served while `metadata_revalidate_after` has not passed since its validation and no `content` or `grants` entry of the feed that names its repository was received after it, judged as a cache entry (`freshFor`); after it a conditional request, or a plain one without a validator (chosen) | One rule for a shared entry and the anonymous copy | A document without a validator spares the main installation as one with it; a replica that just started serves the copy within its first 15 s as it serves a shared entry; a withdrawal the feed carries ends it as it ends a shared entry | A copy without a validator costs a whole transfer after the period |
| (b) Only with an `ETag`, as a token's copy | | Nothing new | A format whose document carries no validator keeps every anonymous request one for one |
| (c) Judged by the four rules of an answer | | The copy is an answer about the anonymous subject | For 15 s after a replica's start every anonymous read of a private document goes to the main installation, where a shared one does not |

**Choice:** (a). The period's default stays `metadata_revalidate_after`, `1m` (R-BAS-023): a narrowing the feed does not carry reaches
anonymous callers within it, as it reaches full readers ([security/bastion.md](../security/bastion.md) H-2292, H-2351). **Applied in the
spec:** R-BAS-023, R-BAS-094.

### Q-BAS-430 · A Bastion is recognized by its token; its reports about its callers count only from its own registration's networks

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (package E13) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: the owner's [Q-BAS-334](#q-bas-334--a-bastions-egress-addresses-belong-to-its-registration) gives each registration its own list; the spec says what counts from the list, not what a
request of a Bastion from outside it is, nor what an empty list means.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The token recognizes the Bastion wherever it connects from; only a request from its own networks has its forwarded address and host and its check's `clientAddress` count; from elsewhere, and with an empty list, the request is the Bastion's own, from its address, and its request line says `bastion_egress: "unlisted"` (chosen) | Recognition and trust apart | A new Bastion works before its list is set, the card's warning names the address to add (R-UI-243); a token used from elsewhere chooses no address; the empty list is the safe reading | Callers pool at the Bastion's address until the list is set (H-2291) |
| (b) A request from outside the list is not a Bastion's at all | | Strict | A new Bastion, and every Bastion after a change of its NAT, stops at once: no marking, no handshake, no warning with the address it came from |
| (c) An empty list trusts every address | | Nothing to set | Q-BAS-334's option (c), which the owner did not choose |

**Choice:** (a). The address compared is stage 5's (R-ARCH-006 with `server.trusted_proxies`), the same the token's last use records.
**Rationale:** the empty list is the default of every new registration; reading it as "nothing counts" keeps a stolen token from choosing
addresses, and keeping the recognition keeps the Bastion working while the administrator adds its address. **Applied in the spec:**
R-BAS-010, R-BAS-011, R-BAS-017; code: `Recognition.FromEgress` ([recognize.go](../../internal/bastionmain/recognize.go)),
`bastionForwarded` ([wire_bastion.go](../../internal/app/wire_bastion.go)).

### Q-BAS-431 · A registration lists at most 32 networks; an address is its own network, and /0 is refused

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (package E13) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An IPv4 or IPv6 address (its `/32` or `/128`) or a network in CIDR form; an IPv4 address in IPv6 form is the IPv4 one; at most 32; refused: `/0`, a network with bits beyond its prefix (the error names the network meant), a zone, a duplicate; answered with the prefix length (chosen) | The rules of `server.trusted_proxies`, stricter | One list a replica's snapshot holds for every registration; a typo is named, not widened silently | A wide prefix such as `/1` is still accepted |
| (b) Allow `/0` with a warning | | An operator who cannot know the address | Anyone holding the token chooses every caller's address (Q-BAS-334's option (c)) |

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (package E13) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the

### Q-BAS-445 · The anonymous ceiling is taken in the slot budget, after the slot

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (package E9a) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-094's ceiling counts every request a replica sends to the main installation on behalf of an anonymous caller, the background
refresh included, which no guard counted; a refused request consumes nothing.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) In the slot budget of the client (`mainclient.SlotBudget`), which every such request passes with its class: a request of the anonymous class takes from the ceiling once it has its slot, and a refusal gives the slot back at once (chosen) | One place for forwards, conditional requests, checks, probes and the refresh | Nothing that reaches the main installation for an anonymous caller can pass by it; a request the slots refuse takes nothing from the ceiling | A request the ceiling refuses waited for a slot first, at most the queue's wait, and only while every anonymous slot is taken |
| (b) At the guard's miss step, beside the per-address miss figure | The engine asks it before a forward | Refused before the slot | The background refresh and the conditional requests of a refresh take no miss step; each new path to the main installation would need the call |
| (c) Before the slot | | No wait for a refusal | A request the slots then refuse has taken from the ceiling |

**Choice:** (a). The hour is read before the second's bucket and counted only after it admitted the request: a refusal by either takes
nothing; requests decided at the same instant may pass the hour by their number (H-2356). A refusal is `mainclient.CeilingError`, which is
`ErrBusy`: the engine answers `503 busy` with the ceiling's wait and counts `reason="anonymous_ceiling"`. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-025,
R-BAS-094; code: [ceiling.go](../../internal/bastion/guard/ceiling.go), [budget.go](../../internal/bastion/mainclient/budget.go).

### Q-BAS-446 · A configuration is applied when it differs, and a request reads it once

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (package E9a) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: R-BAS-093 applies a configuration whole: the guard's figures, the slots, the throughput, the ceiling and the switches change
together. Until E8 the interim configuration (Q-BAS-352) keeps its revision when a main installation's release changes what it holds.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One immutable value swapped in with one atomic store when the configuration differs from the applied one; a request reads it once at its start and carries it on its context, so all its decisions are made with one configuration; the slot budget resizes in a watcher (chosen) | `settings.Holder` | A request never decides with figures of two configurations; a configuration of the same revision but other content (a new release of the main installation) is applied; a handshake that brings the same one costs a comparison | Two requests in flight may decide with two configurations while one is swapped in |
| (b) Apply when the revision differs | One integer | Cheaper by a comparison per handshake | The interim configuration of another release keeps its revision and would not be applied |
| (c) Each decision reads the configuration applied now | No context value | Smaller | One request's steps can see two configurations |

**Choice:** (a). The background refresh, which outlives its request, reads the configuration applied when it starts. **Applied in the

### Q-BAS-451 · Ansible Galaxy answers a rate limit 503, because ansible-galaxy does not survive the retry of a 429

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-26** (package E15) — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: E15 ran ansible-galaxy 2.17.14 against the `galaxy` shape (R-BAS-095's table of E15's run). It reads the shape, but a `429` on
the version list still ended it with exit 250. The cause, from its source (`ansible/galaxy/api.py`): `_call_galaxy` is retried for 429, 502
and 520 (`RETRY_HTTP_ERROR_CODES`); for a document it caches (the version list) it writes an empty entry of its
response cache before the request, valid for a day, and the retry reads that entry as a hit and takes its `results`, which the failed
attempt never wrote: `KeyError: 'results'`. The body is never read again, so no shape helps; a status it does not retry does. ansible-core
2.21.6 has the same retry set and cache code (read, not run) and ended at the main installation with "Missing expected 'results' in
ansible-galaxy cache" (usage-and-limits.md, measured 2026-11-20).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The format declares `RateLimitedStatus` 503, and its `WriteError` answers a rate limit 503 with its code and `Retry-After`, as the ClamAV definitions do (R-BAS-056) (chosen) | ansible-galaxy exits 1 and prints the detail and the code, at a Bastion and at the main installation alike; one fact, held by kit check 19 | ansible-galaxy no longer retries a short limit by itself: a refused request ends the command at once, as it did on every cached document anyway |
| (b) Keep 429, the `galaxy` shape alone | | No change | Exit 250 at a Bastion, measured |
| (c) Users pass `--no-cache` | | The client retries a 429 six times | A switch nobody knows; the default crashes |

**Choice:** (a). A `502` on a cached document crashed the client the same way (H-2358, run on 2026-11-26: exit 250); since the same day a Galaxy route answers a gateway failure `503` as well (R-BAS-095). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-056, R-BAS-095,
[formats/ansible.md](formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-007, [usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) gap 1; code:
[format.go](../../internal/formats/ansible/format.go), [errors.go](../../internal/formats/ansible/errors.go).

| (b) A token bucket with a theoretical arrival time in one counter | One counter per bucket | Exact | Lifting the counter after an idle period needs a compare-and-set: two replicas lifting at once push every read out by the idle time |
| (c) A fixed second | 1 s windows | Fewer round trips | A second's whole figure at its start; transfers race at every boundary |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-097; code: [throughput.go](../../internal/bastion/throughput/throughput.go),
[valkey_bastion_bytes.go](../../internal/cluster/valkey_bastion_bytes.go).

Context: an issued Bastion token always expires (R-BAS-004, Q-BAS-19), so that a forgotten token does not live on and renewal happens by
hand with an overlap. A declared token lives in a Secret both releases read; whoever writes the Secret renews it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No expiry; the token ends when the Secret holds another value or the declaration is removed; the authenticator accepts no expiry only for a registration's declared token (chosen) | | A Bastion run from Git is never cut off by a date; one rule, checked where the token is read | Nothing forces a rotation: H-2366 |
| (b) An expiry of `auth.tokens.bst.max_ttl` from each run of migrate | | A token expires when no release happens for 13 months | Every run writes; an installation without upgrades is cut off; the expiry says nothing about the Secret |
| (c) The expiry of `auth.tokens.bst.default_ttl` from the first run | | As an issued token | The Bastion is cut off after a year although the configuration still declares it |

**Choice:** (a). The handshake's `tokenExpiresAt` is the zero time for it, which the Bastion already reads as no expiry; the interface's
version stays. **Applied in the spec:** R-BAS-127, R-BAS-004; code: `loadBastion` in [token/bastion.go](../../internal/auth/token/bastion.go),
migration [00148](../../internal/meta/postgres/migrations/00148_bastion_declared.sql).
